title: Lee Hunter: 'It feels good to put pads on' | Carolina Panthers
text: Okay, no problem, all right. >> Okay, questions for Lee? >> Lee, what's it been like getting pads on these last three practices and being able to actually play football two days in a row? >> Oh, no, I feel good just getting pads on and and play football again. I I haven't played football fast since that Oregon game in college, so it feel great just getting pads on and put hands on people and and be able to dominate this town. >> First First time walking out into an NFL stadium to play, even though it's Fan Fest, what were your impressions of the bank? >> Just mind-blowing, just blessed to be here. Uh excited, happy, and just ready to play ball. >> With Turk and Bobby out, you're getting a lot of reps. Um is there a guy that you've been impressed by on the opposite side of the ball when you've been rushing them? >> Oh, I just give the give it the uh I give a big shoutout to the whole offensive line as a group. Uh they they play well together. Uh they scrap and they get they get the D-line better off, I feel, and they get me better at two-a-days, so I just give them a I just get after them together as a whole. >> What have you learned from Derrick Brown so far? >> Just just the little things. Uh slow is fast. Uh run to the ball. Uh technique. Uh be physical dominant. Just doing other game aspect. Derrick, he's just a dog and he's just a great person. He give you a lot of good feedbacks. He coach you on film. He was on He was on the sideline coaching me today during the scrimmage, so he's just a great guy, great guy to be around, and shh >> [snorts] >> love his presence. >> Slow is fast, can you expand on that? Can you Can you tell us like slow is fast? What is Can you >> Slow is fast. If you go slow, you get your technique. Slow is fast. I I don't think you can explain slow is fast. >> Well, I just I didn't know, you know, it just I I wanted to know more. >> Yeah. >> Yeah, it's just slow is fast. Like if you're doing a technique cuz normally I'm coming in, I'm like, I got to do this fast, and they just saying just slow down, slow is fast. >> You told us when you were drafted that DB has always kind of been one of your idols. Has there been a moment where you're like, "Dang, I'm sitting here in the NFL learning from Derrick Brown." >> Probably every day, just seeing them. Every day you learn from the best, somebody you just wanted to play like always in high school, college, and you finally get on this team and see what he do every day and see why he the best. >> Granted, it's going to be preseason, but what does it mean to kind of make your debut uh in Canton with all NFL eyes on on this game? >> Just be me. Just be me, believe the technique, and believe the coaching that my coach teach daily, and just stay with the script, the plan, and just just be me and go out there and play football. Just knowing just extra people going to be in the stands watching. >> When you say "be me", what do you want somebody watching to say to take away from watching Leon Hunter? >> Just a dog, someone who physical strength, and and just like to play football, someone who love the game. >> Have you done your rookie performance yet? >> Probably not. >> Who do you think probably Have y'all started those? I mean, I'm just saying in the team. >> Oh, god. Not yet. >> Okay. >> Not yet. >> Are they doing Are y'all doing it as a group or individually? >> We haven't talked about it yet, but probably as a group. >> How close is this rookie group gotten over the last few months? Obviously, Chris goes down. Like, how how have you guys kind of embraced each other and and formed kind of relationships over these last few weeks? >> Just being in the hotel too got us closer. Just going to eat lunch together over the field of guys and just getting to know each other in the locker room. We all was in the back in the room at one point in time getting to know each other. But, the hotel brought us closer, I think, and we got to know each other. Why you play football? What's your why? And why you love to do it? >> Who's the rowdiest in the hotel? Or is it you? >> The [snorts] rowdiest in the hotel is when we When we get to the hotel, it's probably like sleep. I normally when I leave practice, I go home and see my kids. Then I I get to the hotel about 9:40. So, when I when I get back to the hotel I it's I'll be going to sleep. >> Any more questions, Philly? >> Appreciate y'all. >> [music] [music]

He was up there, you know, rocking out on stage and uh the guys were excited about that. >> Dave, this is a big year for Xavier Leette. We've talked about it several times >> with Chris Brazzle now out for the season and that news. >> What does that mean specifically for Xavier? >> Uh it's business as usual for X. You know, we have big plans for him. He's got big plans for himself and he's been working hard at it and again had a great off seasonason and carried it right into training camp and you know you saw made a couple of plays today and the timing is there. Bryce knows him. He understands what we're trying to get done and he's working his butt off and so I'm really proud of where he's at and can't wait to see where where we go from here. >> Can you take us through the Brazle because originally it was reported that it was eight weeks and then you got there was a decision to make a season ending. Yeah, just gathering all the information, going through our normal process and making sure that we got all eyes and we have great people in the building and then we also have great people around the league and specialists um who were able to look at the images and we wanted to make sure we did the right thing for Chris long term. So, let's get all the information and then as the days went on, you know, you kind of what you'd like to do is get initial imaging and then kind of see how it responds the following day and do more testing. And the more information we gathered, you know, with everybody putting their heads together landed on this is the best course for him long term to be able to get the knee stable um to get him on the right track. So, um you know, that was we just kind of were again took us a couple of days to gather the information we needed. Dave, >> last year uh coming into camp, President Tmaine wasn't really talked about a whole lot. Um ended up being a guy you play all three positions, the special teams. with Brazle out, does he become a guy that you kind of look to for that X position or or some of these package spots? >> Yeah, the beauty of Bryson is he's a really smart guy and uh you know, he does a lot of the dirty work. You know, we we asked him to go in and dig out safeties and um do different things in the run game, but in the pass game, he can play all the spots and that's really valuable. You know, we have a couple of guys like that. Bryson's one of them, David Moore is another. Jim Reed has been a guy that we're really trusting right now with just being able to step in at different spots. So, um, we have a great group. This room is a very competitive room to start with, we certainly had high hopes for Chris and the way that we could use him in our offense and, um, and while that it's not going to happen this year, um, we we have a bunch of guys that we really count on and trust. >> Speaking of Bryson, he had a pretty loopy catch from Kenny tonight, Rand. Like, what happened on that play? Why did that work between the two of them so well? Yeah, just I I think you know he made a couple of plays. So there was a there was a the drive before Kenny hit him on a on a boot, you know, and he just he just really just full effort got across the field and presented himself to Kenny as he was flushing out to the right and then in that last two-minute drive, you know, I mean, it's a bang bang play. I wanted to blow it dead right there so we can get a few more plays out of the drive, but uh that timing is there. A guy that the quarterbacks really trust and I'm I'm glad to see him make a couple plays today. >> Tommy Trimble didn't practice. Anything of note about that? Yeah, just soreness, general soreness. And and for this, you know, of course, for for us, this is just another practice. And so, we treated it as such. There were a couple of guys, uh, uh, Derek, uh, Devin Lloyd, both guys just taking vet days, which kind of fell in their normal rhythm and routine of when it was going to happen. And, um, they've had amazing practices up up to now. And so, you know, with just like understanding we were going to like oscillate when those guys are available. Today just happened to be the day that they weren't going to be available. But um we'll turn around and we'll have a couple of really nice days. >> Will he had a couple nice reps against McMillan? Just a word on Yeah. the rookie. >> Yeah, absolutely. Um you know, just the the talent and everything is there and you know, he makes great plays and then a couple plays later he'll give a big one up and that's been kind of you know he's he's minimizing some of those things but when he's right, when he's in the right position, his eyes are right, uh we have a real talent there outside as another option. So um really excited to see where Will heads from here. He had a knee sleeve on his half. >> Yeah, he just got a little bit of soreness and we just wanted to make sure we shut him down. We have a couple of really great days coming up and then of course we're turning around pretty quickly with the uh Hall of Fame games. So, wanted to make sure that we get him um some good work going into these next couple days. >> What have you seen from JT so far this summer maybe compared to last summer where he he had a big summer and then didn't have the production he probably hoped for? >> Yeah, JT's been amazing um going into his third season. So, another guy talked about X. Um, I got to talk about JT the same way. This is a guy who knows what we're trying to do. He understands our concepts. He understands our offense and what we're trying to get done. He did a great job this summer of just working on his routes and and all those things. He's been reliable, making some tough catches in camp. And um that's what we would love to see JT continue to build on. >> Kind of get in the get in the backfield a few times tonight. You challenged him a few days ago to step up. How has he responded to that? Honestly, Princeley since the beginning of camp has really been one of our guys on defense chasing the ball all over the field. And uh this is really cool to watch him and Nick come in at the same time. And we know how Nick plays and with this just relentless effort and Princeley has been that guy. He's chasing everything down. He's working on his craft. Um he's continuing to push himself in different rush packages and um he's a guy that I'm really excited to see where he goes. Was the decision made to uh hold off on signing Kyle Tras at this point or what was the decision? >> Yeah, just general needs uh for our roster right now. Um we just didn't really feel like we had the luxury with a couple of positions. We have some guys down. Uh Robin Doo missing some practices where, you know, we're probably plus one or two on the offensive line to make sure we can throw a good practice. And um and certainly with the tight end position, you know, Mitch had an ankle. He'll be back really, you know, in the next couple of days back practicing with us. And then Tommy getting some soreness. We we really felt like that's a group where the the reps could really build up on that group and we wanted to bring another person in. >> We'll do a couple more. >> For the rookies in particular, did you tell them anything about what stepping out onto the field at Bank of America Stadium is like ahead of tonight? And did you kind of paint the picture to them or did you let them experience it? We tried to, you know, we've shown them highlights of, you know, just kind of down the stretch last year to see the environment, the energy that's in the building. And um really honestly, you know, I heard what what was going to happen and and how the fans were going to show up. Um but I didn't really know what what it was going to look like until we walked into the stadium and sure enough, you know, the energy was right and our guys were able to get a feel for that. Um it means a lot to me. I take a lot of pride in our guys their first time stepping out into the stadium to get that kind of uh reception from our fans and uh and it's just uh I know I don't know it's just a point of pride where it feels good to me that our that our new guys, our free agents, our rookies, the guys who are here for the first time can feel the energy in this building in Bank of America Stadium and um I was really proud of that. So again fans, thanks a lot um because that gives us that gives just a little wind in our sales. We're right into camp mode and that's just the kind of energy that our guys need. The locker room is great right now. The guys are all smiles and they could feel that. So, it was a phenomenal night. >> Dave, you have a lot of versatility with your secondary, whether it's JC moving into the slot, Cory Thornton playing deep, Shaw Smith Wade can move a lot of different spots. How do you balance having a lot of guys that can do a lot of things, but also trying to narrow down the things that work best for you guys? >> Yeah, that's a challenge um in a good way. And uh we'll have to look at, you know, Agerro's his philosophy is let's get our best 11 on the field. That means different packages. Um, and I won't go into specifics of it, but you know, there's it's the front, it's the backers, it's the secondary. How can we use different guys to get the best 11 on the field? Um, and that's all that's going to be the goal is to try to figure out who can help us and uh and it certainly does uh bode well for those guys in terms of, you know, being competitive to make the roster. So, how much more can you do, you know, and can you play more than just an outside spot? Can you go inside to the nickel? Can you play safety? Um, and the guys that have multiple roles that way give themselves a real chance. >> The last one, >> Dave, you talked early in camp about not calling plays. Now that you've been through a week [snorts] of it and Brad's up there calling a lot of tonight, have you noticed any patterns developing or has there been anything now that you're weekend that you kind of notice about it? >> Well, I love where we're at just from a from a rhythm standpoint. Um the the for sure like right off the bat it's like the tempo of which the calls are getting in and making sure they're getting in in a timely fashion so we're organized. Brad's done a great job of that. Um especially tonight trying to simulate some real drives looking at the different situations. I try to move the ball all over the field to just put his head space in a in a different zone, a different area. And he handled that really well. So um I'm excited for that. And uh as far as like patterns and rhythms, I think I'm going to keep that to myself. But he's doing a great job uh organizing the group and making sure that we're pushing our our concepts, adding wrinkles to things, keeping the guys interested, but also having a great feel for what is our group doing well, so we can start to hone in the closer and closer we get to playing these games. >> All right. Thank you. Jaylen crowdf >> Yeah, of course. Of course. I mean, I think um pack the bank, you know, that's our that's our that's our motto and um you know, we continue to win, continue to build up this culture and um show why people need to come out to Carolina football games and you get a result like tonight. >> Tough news where Chris was concerned this week to receiving. >> Yeah, I mean I think just coming from like, you know, I've had injuries and stuff like that, too. So, just to kind of give him my little two cents, you know, just continue to keep his head up, you know, not not get in into his head too much, you know, just um just attack the work. That's all you really can do. Just continue to work every day, get a little bit better every day, and um after that, you know, just just let it rip. So, um but no, of course, I think uh we're going to miss miss him not being out there. He's a different element on the team and, you know, he he's a playmaker, so of course that's we're going to miss that. Jaylen, there are quite a few 18 jerseys out there now. Um, I know you signed your contract, but when you look up and you see guys, kids wearing your jerseys and stuff like that, like what does that mean to you now heading into your third year? >> Yeah. No, I mean that's uh it's surreal really. Um, yeah. I mean, it's it's awesome feeling. It really is. I feel like I've always dreamed of being in the position I'm in now and to be here. I just want to do it justice and make sure I'm doing it the right way. Jaylen, what have you seen from uh Zade really get so far this summer? >> I mean, he's been balling. He's been balling. He really is like a one-of-a-kind athlete and a player and a person, too. So, I mean, can't say enough good things about him. >> You've worked on like scout team and and worked on practice squad and and been a depth guy. Jim Reed's a guy that a lot of people talk about just having a lot of success on the practice squad last year and now he's having a lot of success with Kenny right now. What have you seen from him since he's been here and and why do you think he's found so so much success? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. No, I think it's a lot to do with his confidence, you know? I think um coming in like a little bit late last year, you know, trying to find his bearings, get his footing, and then I feel like he came in here with a clean slate and just let it let it rip. So, I think um yeah, his confidence is through the roof and he he's a great player, too. I mean, what he did at San Diego and everything, like you don't just do that, you know? You're obviously coming in with with talent. So, I mean, he's he's a really good player. Again, great person. I mean, I'm just excited to see him keep working. >> See, you got one on you. >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. Yeah. >> Take us through that cuz >> Yeah. Yeah. Of course. You know, um he shouldn't have been there basically, but no, I I probably just got to throw that out of bounds, but um you know, it's pain to do though. Do you I mean do you like were you excited that that play was called and you were be going to be >> Oh yeah, of course I was excited. I was disappointed with the result definitely. But um but no. Yeah, I think just uh for the coaching staff have to trust me in a position like that. I know it's just FanFest, but you know down the line hopefully we can work some of that stuff in. I I think I still got some some some stuff left in the tank, but um but yeah, no, I think it's just a again just belief in me. >> Did you advocate for that or did they come to you and like hey we want you to run? Well, I I was hoping that my throwing on the sideline would have would have sparked it and it did. And now it's, you know, now we're going to have to rebuild again. But it's all right. It's okay, though. >> I mean, we've seen you throw probably 30 35 yards in practice with the trainer. Like, how how much confidence do you have in that arm? >> Oh, I have a lot of confidence. A lot of confidence, for sure. Played one game of quarterback in high school, so I'm basically like vested. Um, but uh but Oh, yeah. I mean, whatever the team asked me to do. >> How did that one game go? Oh, we lost. >> Oh, I threw for like 300 yards and just couldn't get in the end zone, though. >> Did JC have some words for you after that pick? >> No, no, he didn't say anything, but I eye contact. I could tell. >> You mentioned to us back in January that you really want to be able to make it through a full season after having some of the issues. Did you change anything this off season as far as just your training that in hopes that that will be something you're able to do? >> Uh, not really change anything. I think I just continued on what I was doing from when I got hurt the first time and then when I was able to come back like that whole training process I kind of just continued that and continued to stay around the you know stay around the facility where everyone knows me kind of knows what I need like um so then just kind of built on that and uh I'm feeling good playing fast so it's working. >> Jaylen with with Chris out that obviously leaves some open spots for guys. We saw guys like Bety and Casey Washington tonight kind of make plays. What have you seen from some of those guys as as they've shown that they have the best piece? >> Yeah, I mean I think um our entire room will say that like I our entire room is so competitive. Like everyone can play, everyone can make plays. Um but you know, I'm just I'm just really excited to to continue to work and just see um you know, how much this competition pushes us all to be better. Jaylen, seeing you out there building punts before practice and and such and even during special teams work beginning of practice. Is that still something that's in your in your repertoire even though it's something you haven't really done at this level yet? >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, um, you know, whatever the team asked me to do, I I feel confident being back there. It's just a matter of if they put me back there. So, just got to stay ready. >> How are you feeling physically after you told us in the spring that you had really changed up some things with your regimen to soft tissue stuff? >> Yeah, I'm feeling great. I really am feeling really good. Like I was I was saying, playing fast. Um, you know, I feel like uh we're off to a good start for sure. >> Jaylen, where are you most seeing the benefits of, you know, you team and Bryce just having this full off season together coming off of establishing ourselves together at the end of last >> Yeah, I think it's just again like chemistry, confidence, just kind of knowing where like him knowing where we're going to be in spots and him trusting us to make the 50-50 balls and make those catches that might be harder. So, I think um just as we progress through the summer and stuff, just meeting outside of uh of the facility, you know, getting together, hanging out, just kind of just being friends. Um I think, you know, just as we continue to build, it's just going to flourish. >> You talk about chemistry and confidence. The last time you were in the stadium, you had the big game against the Rams. Of course, you get the contract this off season. Have your expectations for yourself and kind of what you now expect to do changed since the last time you're out there and since everything's happened? this offseason. >> Yeah, I mean, I don't think they've changed at all. I think that I'm going to continue to strive to be a thousand yard receiver. Um, that's what, you know, I always wanted to accomplish. So, I mean, that was my goal coming in as a rookie. That was my goal last year. That'll be my goal this year. Um, and it's just going to whatever I can do to help the team is uh is what I'm is what I'm going to try my best to do. So, if that's, you know, if that looks like 600 yards and it doesn't matter to me as long as I we're winning football games and I'm continue to just put my best foot forward. >> Even though the result may not have been what you prefer, does calling that play create a little spark for guys >> that play. >> Oh. Um, >> just having trick plays in the bag. >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Of course. I mean, I think you have to be ready for anything. So, just, you know, you put a couple deceptive plays in there. I think it always helps. Thanks. >> Okay, questions for Lee. Lee, what's it been like getting pads on these last three practices and being able to actually play football to an extent? >> Oh, no. It feel good to just get pads on and and play football again. I I haven't played football fast since that Oregon game in college. So, it feel great just get pass on and put hands on people and build domin. What were your impressions of the bank? >> Just mind-blowing. Just blessed to be here. Uh excited. happy and just ready to play ball. >> With Turk and Bobby out, you're getting a lot of reps. Um, is there a guy that you've been impressed by on the opposite side of the ball when you've been rushing them? >> I just give the give the uh I give a big shout out to the whole offensive line as a group. Uh they they play well together. Uh they screen, they get they get the D line better, I feel, and they get me better, too, daily. So, I just give them I just get all to them together as a whole. What have you learned from Derek Brown so far? >> Just just the little things. Uh slow is fast. Uh run to the ball. Uh technique. Uh be physical dominant. The student of the game aspect. Derek, he's just a dog and he's just a great person. He give you a lot of good feedbacks. He coach you on film. He was on he was on the sideline coaching me today do the scrimmage. So he's just a great guy. Great guy to be around and I love his presence. Slow. >> Fast. Can you expound on that? >> Can you Can you tell us like slow is fast? What? Can you >> Slow is fast. If you go slow, you get your technique. Slow is fast. I I don't think you can explain slow is fast. >> Well, I just I didn't know, you know, it just I I wanted to know more. >> Just slow is fast. Like if you doing the technique cuz normally I'm coming in, I'm like, I got to do this fast and they just saying just slow down, slow as fast. You told us when you were drafted that DB's always kind of been one of your idols. Has there been a moment where you're like, "Dang, I'm sitting here in the NFL learning from Derek Brown." >> Probably every day just seeing him. Every day you learn from the best, somebody you just wanted to play like always in high school, college, and you finally get on this team and see what he do every day and see why he the best. Granted, it's going to be preeason, but what does it mean to kind of make your debut uh in Canton with all NFL eyes on on this game? >> Just be me. Just [snorts] be me. Believe the technique and believe the coaching that my coach teach daily and just stay with the script, the plan, and just just be me and go out there and play football just knowing just for people going to be in the stands watching. When you say being me, what do you want somebody watching to say to take away from watching Lee Hunter? >> A dog. Someone who physical strength and and just like to play football. Someone who love the game. >> Have you done your rookie performance yet? >> Probably not. >> Have y'all started those? >> Not yet. >> Okay. >> Are they Are y'all doing >> as a group or individually? We haven't talked about it yet, but probably as a group. >> How close has this rookie group gotten over the last few months? Obviously, Krisco's down. Like, how how have you guys kind of embraced each other and and formed kind of relationships over these last few weeks? >> Just being in the hotel too got us closer. Uh just going to eat lunch together with a few of those guys and just getting to know each other in the locker room. We all was in the back in a room at once point in time getting to know each other. But the hotel brought us closer, I think, and we got to know each other. why you play football, what's your why, and why you love to do it. >> Who's the rowdiest in the hotel? Or is it you? >> The rowest in the hotel is me. >> When we get to the hotel, it's probably like sleep. I normally when I leave practice, I go home and see my kids. Then I I get to the hotel by 9:40. So when I when I get back to the hotel, it's I'll be going to sleep. >> Any more questions for Lee? >> Appreciate y'all.

title: Cole Kmet, Jaylon Johnson, Zavion Thomas on Bears’ competitive mindset | Press Conference
text: Cole, your your time here hasn't been exactly defined by continuity with coach or the coordinator here this year. It feels like there's a flow to the offense early in camp. And from your perspective, does it feel a little bit different? >> Oh, it's great. It's great. I was uh I was just talking with Adam outside and and to my wife about this, but like um I was talking to her last night. It's just like it it's a different feel to camp than maybe in years past. Um you know, you spend I've spent a lot of my career kind of wondering what's next and you know, how is how is tomorrow going to to go and um I feel like I kind of know what to expect at this point, especially with this staff and um you know, what they want to get done, what they expect from each individual. So, uh it it's nice coming in getting ready for a season, you know, understanding how you fit in in the scheme of things and then also the direction of this offense and where we want it to go and the the identity that we want to forge. So, um yeah, it's been it's been a good I think first four days for us. Um it's felt good coming in and being operationally pretty sound. But uh you know, next week will be big with us, you know, with with pads coming on. So, that'll be the the next step for it. >> What can you do differently or what can you guys do now that at this time a year ago was either a thought so far in the distance or you guys just weren't equipped to do? >> Yeah, well, I think last year we were just struggling so much operationally uh especially just in the spring and the start of camp. So, now you can just get I think more into the the detail of routes and things and maybe in the run game and um you know, as we as we pluck away our installs, I'm sure there'll be more stuff the coaches will want to add um as we continue to get it. So, that that's all the the exciting stuff I think going forward. Um I still I think that being said, we're still you know, you kind of get through the first 12, whatever, 14 days of camp to kind of get the the base stuff in and then I think from there, you know, if we show this coaching staff that we can that can truly handle all that and execute that at a high level. Um I'm sure I'm sure Ben will have more for us. >> Ben told us yesterday that he tweaked the run install this year and the coaches really like it. What's the player perspective on that? >> Yeah, I like it. Um we're kind of uh we well, I I think he I don't know if he this is why he did it just cuz you know, it's hard to run a lot of gap scheme stuff without pads on. Um so, you know, you run more of the wide zone and and all that uh for these first four days and um I think that's been really good. You kind of get maybe more reps than you'd like, but uh it's a good it's a good thing to work the technique and work the detail of it and um it it's been good for us to get off the snap count, understand our point, all those things. So, um I know guys are itching to kind of get into more of the power and the gap scheme stuff coming up, but um I I I like it so far. I think it's been a cool change up. >> You caught a couple balls from uh Tyson there at the end of practice. You've been here watching him through his time. What what's the impression on you about the way he's gone about his time as a >> Yeah, I mean, I think me and him are very similar in terms of how we come to work every day and um I I I got so much respect for Tyson. I mean, as an undrafted guy to do what he he's done um so far and he's made such a big impression on this this coaching staff, you know, he's he's also had it he's seen changes as well offensively and I think every offensive coordinator or coach that he's he's been with has been super impressed by him. Um but he he's just a joy to be around. I mean, he's great. He's all ball all the time. Um such a locker room guy and um I think I think he's a top 32 quarterback in this league. I think he could start for for some teams in the league and uh we're we're very lucky to have him. >> Why do you think Ben enjoys him as much as he does? >> Well, I think he's a worker, you know, and he's so and Tyson's so hard on hard on himself. He doesn't need anybody telling him um what he did wrong or what he needs to do the next time. Usually if Tyson makes the mistake, it's it's fixed. Like it's it's he's not making that same mistake again. And um uh Ben and and the rest of the coaching staff, I know they really appreciate guys like that. >> Cole, you came in with Jaylon, and we were just talking to him, and he was being honest about how big of a year this is for him coming off the injury. >> Yeah. >> Feeling the way he feels now, which is much better. Just What are you seeing from him? >> Health off the field, on the field so far. >> Yeah, I know I know last year um was hard for him just with his injury, and then coming back. I know he really wanted to be out there, and I'm sure at times he probably didn't feel like 100%. Um but you know, he wanted to be part of the run, and you know, he's a he's a big big piece of the defense, obviously. Um but since seeing him these first few days, he's made some some great plays, and you can see his instincts, and his movement skills are I think back to to what they were a few years ago. Um he's an unbelievable player, unbelievable corner. Um uh it's been awesome to be with him since since we've been uh we've been drafted. I do joke that I I still am the longest-tenured Bear by like 15 minutes, but >> [laughter] >> uh but yeah, that being said, uh Jaylon and I have been on been through a lot together, and um no one's rooting for him more than I am this year. That's for sure. >> Cole, what have you What have you seen between the speed upgrade on the defense with Kobe with Kobe and Dylan and Devon? Just when you guys are playing together, how do you feel that that upgrade that they have? >> Yeah, you can feel that pursuit especially when we're doing our wide wide zone runs, like side to side line to side line, or we're running our our crossers across the field. Like you you you can feel them on your hip. Um yeah, those guys got great lateral speed. Um downhill speed. I think I You know, you see Dylan, too. I think that's really picking up for him as well as he's getting more comfortable with the game, so um it'll be exciting to see those guys this year, for sure. >> What have you seen between Caleb and the offensive line as you guys reset on the line now. >> Yeah. To Yeah. >> Organize >> think I think we were all a little you know, you don't know how it's going to go especially when you lose somebody like Drew who's uh you know, kind of that captain of the offensive line there communication-wise. Um but I mean with Garrett it's it really has been flawless so far and uh I know we haven't had pads on for from a physicality standpoint, but you know, you talked about communication in the walk-throughs that we've had and in practice. Um things have been really clear, concise and I feel like when I've been out there uh especially in the run game and the pass pro, um things have been really clear and uh I think we've we've had a great understanding with one another. So, um yeah, it's a it's a it's a good unit up front for sure. >> You kind of underline how far the offense has come from this point last year to to now and you know, where you guys can go from here. >> Yeah, well, I think I really just think it's just been an operational thing that has really taken over and we've always been talented. Um but now you get guys in you know, going in their second years have have a year under their belt like Luther and Colston and um you get Caleb's second year into a into a system and now you can start seeing the talent just take over cuz uh you know, you're not you're less worried about how to say a play call or remembering what route to run and now you're worried about okay, how am I going to beat this guy on this route versus this coverage. So, you're you're focused on different things not just all right, where do I line up? What route do I have on this play? Things like that. So, um I think that's like the next step forward for us and um but that getting that operation down was was big and um you can see that we started to kind of figure that out here especially in the early part of camp. >> Cole, how do you how do you reconcile or balance, you know, being probably the person who epitomizes what Coach O'Connell wants to do the most in terms of making a lot of things look the same in the run game and the pass game, but also maybe the ball doesn't come your way as much as it has in the past. >> Yeah, I mean you I'd rather win, man. I It's miserable around here when you're not winning. So, Look, I mean I know like when I do get the ball, like it's great and all that stuff, but like they put a heavy value on on the run game and and pass pro, all that stuff. So, that's that that stuff really doesn't concern me. Um you know, like I said, I feel like you do what they ask you to do here and you do it at a high level, um you're not going to have much to worry about. So, that's kind of that's kind of how I go about things. >> Let's go a couple more. >> What's it been like watching Sam sort of get up to speed here with you? >> Yeah, it's been great. Sam's been awesome. Um he he's funny. He's been fun to have in the room and um I mean, so we got Stanford, Michigan, Notre Dame. It's a you would think it would be a smart It's a it it displays as a smarter room than it actually is. Uh >> But uh no, we have a lot of fun. He really fits in with our group really well and um I'm excited to see when the pads go on how how he shows up in in in that way. So, uh it'll be exciting. I hopefully we'll run a a lot of 13 personnel. >> Obviously a vision for how you guys want to play as an offense. There's aspirations also. I've heard the Peyton Manning Broncos mentioned more than once. Did you put your sights on that? The idea of >> Yeah, I mean that that I mean that's what you're chasing. So, um yeah, we want to score a lot of points and we want to be unforgiving about it and um I think we definitely have that potential. So, uh we got a lot of talent across the board and despite who we're going against, uh I think we have the ability to be very multiple throughout the year, whether we got to beat a team in 11, we got to go 12 for the game, if we have to be really heavy and go 13. Um we have we have the guys to do that. So, I don't think there's anybody in the league that we should be afraid to go against defensively. Um we got we got all the guys that we will need this upcoming year and we we definitely have the potential to to to go do that. >> How does the unforgiving part come to life? >> I I think it just I just keep scoring points until they tell you to stop. So, um, yeah, we're trying to score every time we get the ball in our hands and whether that's running it in or or throwing it, we can do it either way. >> I just said oh, sorry. >> You're good. You're good. One more. >> How much do you expect >> Dang it, Pat. >> Is that a reflection of your coach, the unforgiving >> I mean, that that is that's a total reflection and I mean, he's the ultimate, you know, he's our he's our leader for us, uh, on on the football side of things and you know, we we got everyone everyone's bought into what to his messaging and I think that you know, at first when a when a coach comes in, you know, everyone's always a little like, all right, what's going to happen you know, when he gets in front of the team, starts speaking and does an install like, all right, you're like, okay, this guy knows what he's talking about and it's it's easy to buy into that type of stuff. So, yeah, we're excited about it. >> Uh, I mean, I'm a little sore. It's like, I'm good. I feel straight. >> Physically, the difference for you today versus 7 or 8 months ago, how do you describe kind of where you're at? >> Uh, night and day. Night and day. Um, I like I said, I needed a full off season to to get my legs back under me, to get some scar tissue and things like that out, really just work and push my body. So, I feel really good. I feel good with my speed. I feel good with where I'm at, laterally, change of direction and then all of that. So, I just got to keep stacking days. Um, just really just working on my technique and getting consistent and getting back to just being dominant. >> Do you remember mini camp which was shortly after you showed up, you had a practice out there with with two interceptions, I remember that day. Did did you feel like it was you were back on the bicycle again though, like you were at top form? >> I mean, >> pretty quickly? >> I still got some some time to go off of really good where I'm at right now. But, I mean for me two interceptions doesn't make me satisfied like okay, I'm good. I'm back. That's just part of the game sometimes. They come your way, you got to make the plays when they come. But, for me I'm just hungry to to get back 100% get my like I said my eyes, my feet right and just continue to just get better. That's all I'm focused on. I don't really care too much about the happy place. >> So, my bad. Do you look back at last year and think maybe you just pushed yourself too quick to come back? >> Uh at this point no. I mean kind of in in the moment thinking about that. But, at the end of the day I'm a competitor. I feel like I mean I easily could have sat on my ass and not played and just watch it watch it be what it was. But, for me I feel like what I had to give was was enough to contribute to the team. Of course, it wasn't nowhere near who I could be. Um and I feel like people know that. So, I mean for me it was just going out there competing. Just want to be out there. >> You said this morning you're talking 60% 70%? Is there a way to kind of like get across it it exactly how healthy you felt then? >> I mean probably I guess the only time I wasn't in pain playing was probably the Rams, maybe the first Packer or the playoff game. Other than that, I was taking pain medicine, getting numbing shots. I mean, trying to do whatever I can, getting extra work outside of the facility. So, I mean I was doing everything I can. At the end of the day, I was only two three months out of groin core surgery for corner of us. That's a tough position to be in. >> What did your off season look like as far as training? Like how different was it rehabbing from surgery versus like a normal off season before you? >> I wouldn't even say it was too different. I think really just working on the mechanics of running again. I mean, again with core and groin, the knee drive, the knee lift is something that I had to get back. I mean, in the beginning doing a lot of speed work, I can definitely tell that's where I was really weak at. So, just really hitting that, trying to get the the speed, the lift, and the I would say just hip flexors, groin, knee, all that's kind of connected. So, just attacking that early. Um and then really just getting just getting back to myself. I mean, training, lifting, running, sprinting, just the usual stuff. But, I would say there was definitely some areas where I felt weak at and got into Pilates, too. So, Pilates is very is one of the things that I'm going to continue to do. I'm going to get some at the house so I can continue to get my core, get my groin, and things like that strong and and lubricated for this for this year. >> Jaylen, this is really like your first healthy look at at Coach Johnson's offense. What do you see from them? What what makes them challenging and and >> Honestly, this is probably the best offense I've had in 7 years as far as going like against them, for sure. I would say they got a lot of got a lot of speed. Um and then really just Caleb's the best quarterback I've had again since I feel like maybe Nick Foles, if you want to go back that far, but just as far as slinging I feel like he he's definitely doing doing his thing. You can see the accuracy. You can see the the confidence throwing the ball in tight windows. It's something that stood out to me, but I just feel like top to bottom I feel like they're confident group. They believe in each other, believe in what they're doing, and you can see it. And that's what we need to go against on on defense. And they know what we're doing, and they they challenge us. We go we go after them. So, it's going to be a fun camp. >> You you seem pretty fired up with Kobe's interception today. >> What did you see on that play in particular? >> Honestly, I was a little panicked because we were like a two-man. So, I was trailing my guy and I didn't see him. So, I was just like, "Damn, left by myself." And then I looked and he went and got an interception. So, I'm like, "Okay, go make a play then." So, I just like guys that are confident that when they see something they go make it happen instead of "Oh, I thought about it." And this is like no, he went, he read the quarterback, made a good play, and he wasn't even supposed to be there for. So, at the end of the day, things like that make me excited. But, I mean, it was a it was a good day. I mean, we had a lot of energy. So, I mean, somebody make a play you want to celebrate that. >> The quarterback looked pretty good to you guys. He's pretty quick. >> Yeah, no doubt. >> What's it been like just getting to know him over the last few months? >> I mean, honestly, it's like it's easy when somebody comes in that's genuine. Um I mean, we have some mutuals as well, and it's just it's just easy. I feel like we just come in, we gel. I mean, we're the same age, so I mean, a lot of things we just got in common, competitors. He come in and definitely talks about the competitive nature and some of the things that he went through in Seattle, and that's something that you got to take in and respect as um a competitor myself. So, I mean, everything that he's about is what I'm about, so we definitely click easy. >> The The quarterback market has taken off since you got your deal. >> You're set for one more year after this season. Does that make this a pivotal season for you personally? >> this definitely a contract year. I mean, we all know what the cap hit and all that stuff is talking about, so um this definitely a contract year for me. So, I mean, at the end of the day, whether that's here or somewhere else, I got to put it on tape that I'm still a top guy in this league. >> Is that Have you felt that all along knowing like how the deal worked? >> Yeah, no, I mean, I struck I mean, I'm not I'm I'm not a dummy. I think we all we all know that, and I've structured my deal a certain way to put myself back at the table at the age of 27. So, for me, it was always for this point to get here and then show out and do what I do, and be healthy, and be out there doing what I do best, and that's covering, that's making plays, being a difference maker, and then from there, wherever that contract talk goes, it goes. >> Coming off the Coming off the injuries last season, >> does that put added pressure on you, though? >> No, there ain't no pressure. I am who I am, and I do what I do regardless of the circumstance. Um I mean, I'm just happy to be be healthy. I'd much rather it happen last year than this year, for sure. >> Yeah, we we talked to you about expectations during training camp in the past, and you've always pointed out like we haven't won yet. >> You won the division last year. Obviously, you want more, but what's it How's it feel a little different this year, if at all, about just knowing there might be some outside expectation? We talked about hunted versus being the hunter. Like, how does it feel a little different? >> I mean, we're I mean, for me on defense, we're not different. Outside of takeaway, we finished, if I'm not mistaken, bottom 10 or bottom five in a lot of categories, so for me, we we ain't done a damn thing. So, it's a lot of for us to prove on defense. Of course, offense is rolling, but that's not something we can rely on. And okay, offense go put up 40, and then we're holding them to 35. To me, that's unacceptable. So, we still got a lot to work on. We still got a lot to to do and improve. Um I know a lot of I mean, you go down the list. I got a lot to prove. People don't think I am who I am because of a injured year last year. Tarik is on a contract year. He got to prove himself. Um I mean, there's plenty of guys. I mean, Kyler, when he gets back, he has to prove himself. I mean, on the D-line, there's a lot of doubters that don't believe in them. They got to prove they self. I mean, we got If guys aren't hungry, I don't know what's what what what to say or what to do about that. So, we got a lot of people that are motivated, and we got to go out there and play. >> Do you have >> Dillon, >> what does that Dillon get in a conversation? What are your early thoughts on the rookie off and on the field? >> Off the field, I mean, he fits right in. I mean, he's a sponge, as he should be coming in, just really listening and observing. Um and I think he's really smart, too. I think in the communication and times we're talking, he's definitely hasn't said too many other wrong things. He's communicating the right way, saying the right things. So, um I think for him, it's really just getting comfortable, getting confident in what he can do. He's really athletic, but he just has to let his eyes take him to his plays. But he he he'll be he'll be really good. >> What do you tell Kyler, who's going through his own medical thing this year? >> You and him both did last year, and do you have a sympathy for kind of working through that and how hard that is? >> Yeah, I mean, I think his situation is his situation, so I don't want to speak too much on on that. I think it's just more of I would say, if I had to say something to him, just you got to take care of yourself in whatever capacity that looks like, whether that's physically or whether that's mentally. Just make sure you're taking care of your taking care of yourself. I mean, that's the only thing I really could say or speak on with that situation. Um just a nice call by coach Ben. That's all it was and I had to do what I had to do, put my team in a position to win and make a play, so that's what I did. >> How have you felt big picture wise just kind of getting settled within this offense and and really drinking through a fire hose as they like to say? >> Uh, sir, it's been fun. Um, just being around the guys that I'm around, uh, the young guys in the room, uh, they help me every time. If I got a question, I can go to the older guys, I go to Rome, I go to Leaf, I go everybody in the room, so they make me feel comfortable. So, everything been good. >> They've been throwing a lot at you, just about the rules, your work on your units. What's the benefit you think of being as utilized that much this early? >> Uh, yes, ma'am, it's good. Um, at the end of the day, whatever is getting thrown at me, I got to I got to know what I'm doing. I said I got to put my team in the best position to win, so that's what I'm going to do. >> How has working with working with Tyson kind of helped you get acclimated? >> Yeah, it's been good working with Tyson. Um, every time I got a question, even before practice, after practice, I go to him. Uh, whatever it is, he always tell me if you ever need something, you ever want to know something, just come to me, so him making me feel comfortable and building a relationship with relationship with him been good. >> Zay, I've got two questions for you about speed. >> Sir. >> Obviously, I'm sure you've been the fastest player everywhere you've ever been. Does it take an adjustment for the quarterbacks, when you get a new quarterback, to get used to your speed in terms of where that ball may be, where, you know, for you, they want it out here, but because you're so fast, it may end up back shoulder? >> I mean, yes, sir, that's why they got mini camp, that's why they got training camp, that's why we went to Cali, so we can just get the get the timing down, so when we doing that, we we going to get it down. >> The other part is kind of the inverse of that for you, with your speed, do you kind of is there an adjustment period for you to understand when I need to be full throttle, when I need to kind of pull it down a little bit and and when and where to use your speed? >> In a way, but, uh, my position coach, coach Al, he tell me just go. Everybody just tell me just go, so I'm going to just do what they say and just go. >> Seems like a lot of you young guys have latched on to Khalif. What have you kind of from him? >> Everything. Um, he's been a guy that that that's been around for a long time. He's been in the league for a long time. He seen a lot, way more than I ever seen in my life. So, anytime I I want to know something or I got a question with someone I'm second-guessing something like he's a guy that I go to. >> What did you notice about the way he attacks practices? >> Um, Kalif is a guy that that he does everything right. Um, when I first got here I was talking to coach Ben. He was telling me about him. He was like, uh, "We have a guy named Kalif. I want you to follow him around. I want you to do everything he do." So, that's what I've been doing. I've been staying on his hip. >> Same with the with the kickoff returns. I know you guys haven't worked a lot of it in camp yet, but what is the biggest change for you in learning the NFL kickoff return and the way it's structured? >> I mean, there's no change. Uh, it's it's the same objective. Put the offense in a great position to score. So, that's what I'mma do. Understanding where the blocks going and stuff like that. Understanding what things to hit at. Talking talking about it with coach Hightower and stuff. So, it's it's really no change. Just making the right decision and putting the offense in a position to score. >> Coach Taylor was talking to us the other day about how they believe in the fire hose method method here with especially with the young players just throwing kind of everything at you and seeing what you can handle. How do you feel like you've been handling all that so far? >> I've been handling it good. Um, meeting in the morning uh, with the coach and stuff like that. Studying when I get back to the hotel. So, like I said, whatever been thrown at me it's just going to get thrown at me. It is what it is. I got to learn and I got to go out there and execute. >> What nuggets have you been able to pick up from coach Randall Elston so far and how how's that connection kind of formed between the two? >> Uh, everything. Um, coach Al was a guy that that he was a a a great player over there at Indiana. Uh, went to the league and was a great player. So, me just trusting everything he telling me. Understanding he want me to win. He's going to put me in a position to to make plays. So, it all comes down to trust and I trust him. So, I'm just going to go with everything he say every time. >> Same with what you're connecting >> about the balls coming your way or maybe even surprised at how much how many touches you're getting? >> I mean, that's out of my control. Like I said, I just I just go out there, do my assignment. If it come, make the play. If it if it go to somebody else, go make the block. So, that's that's my mindset. >> What have been your impressions of Caleb as you've gotten to know him as a quarterback? >> Caleb crazy. Uh he when I we first got here on uh mini camp, he had made like a throw to Rome. And I'm looking back at the other receivers and like he like scrambling this way, threw it like 60 yards the other way. I look, they looked at me. They was like, "Get used to it." I'm like, crazy. But, I mean, just building a relationship with him, uh talking to him in the locker room, having conversations with him off the field, and uh building that bond. >> What's it like for you when he gets on you a little bit where if there's a mistake? >> I know it's coming from a good place. We all got the same objective. We all got the same goal. We want to win. So, if if if I'm not doing the right thing, anybody can tell me. I I know how to take coaching. I know it's coming from a good place. >> There's been a comparison made between you and how Ben Johnson utilized Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit. Have you watched much of his game or the last couple years? I know you're in college, but do you know much about him? >> I mean, yes, ma'am. I'm I'm familiar with him. Uh watched watched a couple games. Uh played against him when I was at Mississippi State my freshman year when he was over there at Bama, but not as not as much as is just paying attention to his game cuz uh I play for the Bears. I play this certain position, so I'm focusing on what I got to focus on till then. Whatever coach Dawson tell me to do, >> Were the uh slick conditions a little tricky today for you guys as pass catchers? >> Nah, not really. It's really We all We all played in the rain before. Got to catch the ball and make plays. We'll play in snow. Catch the ball and make plays.

title: Richard Hightower says rain presents opportunity to practice ball security | Press Conference
text: Morning, morning. >> Morning. Hey, how's everyone? >> Good. >> Great to see you all. Great day for football. Great weather out there. Chance to get better. Go ahead. >> She, how do you feel about going out here for a few hours in the the squall? >> Yeah, I feel great about going out here in a few hours in the squall. I'm actually excited about it. I think our players are excited about it, too. Uh embrace the opportunity to go out in the wet and rainy weather. You know, we got wet ball Wednesday on a Saturday. So, we're fired up about that because you know why? Because we get to work ball security. The returners get to work that. We get to see if the snappers can snap the ball in this type of weather. We get to see if we can kick in it. Um and we get to see, you know, who is ready to rock and roll no matter what the elements are. Because as you know, we playing soldier and everything's unpredictable. So, I I'm excited to see who's going to respond today. >> Kicking and punting units, is there are there specific things you emphasize or is it just that everything has to be that much sharper because of the the conditions? >> Yeah, I mean, obviously uh the footwear. All right, you got to make sure you have on the proper cleats when the grass is slicker and things like that. But, we also talk about balls being more in play, which uh I think most, you know, all 31 teams talk about balls being in play more um because of the elements. But, it's a chance for for teams to factor in a ball game more so when you have a weather game. Um we we call it a special teams game when we got a weather game. >> HD, what goes into a long snapper competition? Like, what are you looking at specifically day after day? >> Yeah, I mean, I'm just looking at one, I'm looking at how the guys are and do they fit as a Chicago Bear? All right? And they wouldn't be in the building if they didn't. But, I'm looking at that. I'm looking at the way they carry themselves, the way they walk, the way they talk, the way they treat people in the building cuz that's a a very um it's a very unique skill set because you have to deal with the punter and the kicker and you have to be a person of service. So, that's a characteristic that a long snapper must have. He's the glue in the room. But, we got two guys in camp right now that we feel good about, but as I told you all before, we won't know anything until the pads come on. So, you know, in two days or whatever when we put pads on, we'll find out a lot more, but they're both working hard and they're both trying to prove that they belong in this league. >> When the pads come out, how do you scrutinize exactly what you're looking for in that guy? >> Yeah, what I'm looking for is a guy that can snap the ball with accuracy, give us a good clean deliverable ball, and then somebody who can protect and know their assignments and can understand pre-snap communication, post-snap communication, can work well with the guards on both field goal and punt, and can be that that glue for the other two specialists. >> Can you tell us about Cairo's off season and what he worked on? Where do you think he's at right now? >> I can tell you that Cairo came back extremely driven, right? He got another taste of, you know, playoffs, which we know is over, all right, and we got to restart, but he has come back focused. He's hitting the ball really well right now. He really locked in on some things that he wanted to do over off season, and that was really evident when he came back. So, he's in a good place right now, and he'll kick today. So, we'll see how it looks today. >> Coach, watching him hit it, it seems like it's where he's where he's hitting on the net, where he's hitting it from, it seems like he may have another two or three yards. Do you see that or not? >> No, I do. I do see that, Herb. I agree with you. I mean, it's it's crazy to go in year 13 and see the constant improvement, but that's one of the things Coach Johnson talked to us about, you know, I mean, a lot of different core things that we believe in, which I won't divulge all of our what we what we believe in, but but improving is one of those staples, and I think Cairo's taking it to heart. >> You got You obviously got a lot of young guys in the room every year. Having Jaylen and Josh and Elijah and Sanborn, Hardy, so many guys that have been with you for a long time. How much does it help the rookies that are in the room just having that core guys that know you and know the system so well? >> Yeah, I mean I always think it helps having veteran players like a Blackwell like you said or some of those guys that can kind of you know show them the way but it's been stated before and I mean you all know I mean we got a lot of new players totally different roster. We've got a handful of guys on teams that we've worked with before that'll be back but it's going to be critical for Josh and Hardy and those guys to step up in a leadership role and and kind of help those guys along cuz we're teaching a lot of young guys this year. They got new rules, it's a new system for them, new speed of the game for them but that's the excitement about what we do because we have to constantly have moving pieces and changing pieces that we have to it's that's the fun part of the job. So should be should be fun. >> Do you have any communication with Kyle Shanahan after the unfortunate accident? >> Yeah, BZ you're going to try to make me uh you're going to try to make make me get uh you know emotional up here but the one thing I'll say is I'm glad I have had contact with him. And I'm glad he's okay. Okay, you guys know Kyle's we're close. So I'm praying for him and his family. And I I do I do like that the fact that he he sounds like he's getting better. >> John you have three pretty talented options right there back there right now at punt returner. What are you looking for from those guys as you as you sort through that especially with one of them being a rookie? >> Yeah, I mean just coach I just I'm just looking that's the fun part about training camp as we sorting through this stuff. I just want to see who is willing to compete day in and day out. Right? Who's made of what we want and who's ready to step up to the to the challenge and and and take basically take the job, right? We all know we got two a decorated guy in Kalif. We we all know that, right? But the other guys got to compete their tail off every day. All right? So, I'm just looking forward to the competition and it'll sort out. It'll sort out as it goes. >> What stands out for you about Kalif? >> Yeah, I'm going to tell you the one thing that stands out, obviously unbelievable player with unbelievable traits. Okay? On the field. Off the field, I'll give you one nugget that stood out to me. The day one when he got here, he got here, he came up, he came right to my office. Hey coach, I'm looking for the extra 1%. So, how do we do jugs here and and pre-practice and post-practice? Can I get with the equipment guy? Can I talk to them about that? And I like to do a lot a lot more, you know, uh and certain just little knicks and knacks and sec- secrets and trades. I won't divulge all of them, but just that mindset to come in, all right, and and say that I I need this cuz I'm looking for the 1% to get better. All right? It's I mean, that's something that obviously you're not into comparisons here, but we all know Devin was an elite returner here, right? That's something I had a conversation with Devin about. He used to do that all the time. He'd come in on days off, he'd be on the jugs, he'd be doing the work in the dark that nobody saw. And then you saw what happened when it came to the light. So, that's that's something about Kalif that totally stood out to me. Um that he wants to make sure he has every opportunity, not for him, but so he can help the team. >> How much he plays receiver impact at your decision at all as to how much he returns? >> No, I don't think I don't think it does. I don't think it does. I think Ben and I are on the same page on that. In fact, I know we are. Um and uh being wants to see it ball in his He wants ball He wants the ball in playmakers' hands as much as possible. He likes explosive plays. >> You talked in the spring about Zayver getting used to the dynamic kickoff. Where is he? I know it's early in camp, but where is he in the evolution with that? >> Yeah, we've had one kickoff return day uh so far in camp and uh he handled it well, you know. He handled it well. He did a nice job. The traits we like in him, they have shown up. The speed, um the athletic ability to make you miss off of one cut and the vision have showed up again, but he's still a you know, he's still a rookie and he's still got to develop and what a heck of a way to to to come into your rookie year in a system that he can develop under a guy like Khalif and see it. So. >> Richard, is uh is Josh Blackwell one of the better success stories you've seen in your coaching career and what is the lesson that the new undrafted guys can take from >> Yeah, I mean, I think guys, I've been like extremely for- fortunate and blessed and I know that, all right? With Blackwell, he is definitely one of the one of the best stories, right? And his story is still being written. Um and Blackwell's going to be one of those guys a couple years or 5-10 years from now that we show tape of to younger guys. So, as I'll give you example, we show tape to the guys we have now of Raheem Mostert who was here at one point, but was cut by nine teams and came to the team in San Francisco where we were, became one of the best special team players in the league and then became a Pro Bowl running back for coach Scudderfield that's here now. So, I hope that is Josh's story. And I mean, just lucky. List goes on and on on that stuff. In fact, I showed those guys that the other day. Aziz Al-Shaair on the tape, Fred Warner on the tape, George Kittle on the tape, Jack Sanborn when he was a rookie, now he's here. Elijah Hicks, so those are the things I feel like Sam Roush needs to see. You know, those are the things that Malik Muhammad needs to see so that they can see something tangible that they can touch and they can say, "You know what? I can do that." And you can if you put the work in. >> You have spoken about getting more involved in defense and special teams. How have you seen him become more involved in special teams and how have you helped him come along? >> Yeah, I'll tell you what, he has been involved in a major way. Like he has been it's year two, you know, so obviously the continuity in the staff allows us to do some different things. But just meeting with him meeting with him, meeting with coach Blevins on self scout game management, Harry Freed, all of those guys together all right has been phenomenal. And Bean has been so locked in when it comes to special teams and I appreciate him being in the meetings. He's in the meetings people notice that. And you know what that does? That gives us a chance to help the football team because he values it, he knows how important it is and not everybody does that. But he is locked in and and and and we like that on teams. >> When you look at some of the starting battles maybe at linebacker or what's going on with Kalen Ballage at safety and nickel maybe outside corner. How's that impact the reps with teams and and how you start to put your team together? >> Yeah, I mean that's a great question because as you know it's always a trickle down effect of whatever happens wherever. So it just I I put I stated to the guys like this, "Hey guys, we got a lot of opportunity. We got a lot of opportunity and we do. I mean we got a couple returning guys, but we got a lot of opportunity for guys to step up and go take a spot. So there's multiple spots there available in the core. So we just got to see who wants to rise to the occasion and and who wants to go get that done. And that's that's exciting part about training camp, you know? >> With Jaylen Jones specifically, he's been one of your core guys, you know, throughout his time here. I know he was away for a minute, but if he happens to be the nickel going into the season, is he off of teams cuz he's he's one of those guys he's not just a guy on teams. >> Which one you talking about? >> Jaylen Jones. >> Oh, Jaylen Jones. Yeah, you know what? If that happens for Jaylen Jones, great, you know? He'll still play some form of it, but on teams we always, you know, you're dealing with 90 guys right now. I'm really coaching 85 with the quarterbacks or whatever, but you deal with the entire team and you got to make sure you do what's best for the team. So, if Jaylen is playing a lot of defense, then he'll still play special teams, but he won't play as much cuz we want him, you know, fresh. And then that's where a guy like, you know, one of the younger corners got to go in there and got to develop, but that's my hope and my dream for every player that we have on special teams to ascend um to a bigger role. And that's why we coach. Coach Blevins I and and and that's what we want for all of them. >> Coach, we all know that Tory can boom the ball. We saw it in practice the other day. What What are you guys emphasizing right now to take all that talent he has and and hopefully realize it's where he can rise to be one of the better punters in the league. >> Yeah, I think the main thing for him is just taking it day by day and all of the guys. And consistency is what we want. Um we're preaching to him you hit your best ball. All right, you hit your best ball and we'll go cover it for you. But ball contact, ball strike, his hands, where he's dropping the ball, his lines that he's taking so that he's his body is in sync when he strikes the ball much like a golfer, you know? Um but that's why punting and kicking is harder than a lot of people think. Um because it's one time to do it and it's like playing golf. You go out there and can you have a great golf shot every single time? A lot of us in here like to golf, but a lot of us can't do that. So, that's what world they live in. So, we we working on best ball right now.

title: Darnell Wright, D'Marco Jackson, Braxton Jones emphasize consistency | Press Conference
text: Then talked about this morning, putting a focus on it end of half situations. Uh since these practices I've been able to get in that for a touchdown there at the end of practice. >> Uh that's good. Every I mean anytime we uh score the ball in a half, I mean that's big for us. Something we need really need to work on. Something we need to improve on from last year, so it's good that we, you know, starting that and getting getting better. >> Did they identify any reasons why maybe that was a tough spot for you guys to get going? >> Um >> In the game you're great. >> Yeah, I mean you could point to a number of reasons, but uh at the end of day it's just not as good as it needs to be, so whatever the reason is, um it just needs to get better. >> Then also said that he's tweaked the running style for the first time in his career. Can you tell us anything about how it different [snorts] from last year? >> Uh I think it's just more so um instead of um kind of popping from one uh scheme to the next, like wide zone to gap scheme, we just we go maybe 2 days in a row wide zone just to sink our teeth in it a little bit more. Just get more in depth in it. >> [snorts] >> I don't know how you handle only the uh the contract extension part of your life right now. >> Um I mean uh my main focus really is just football, you know, being as best as I can be uh for the team. Um obviously I mean I know I'll be here for a long time. Um hopefully my whole career, so those things kind of handle themselves. Um but I mean I just got to stay focused on uh the main things. That's just getting better consistently every day, so. >> Would it be proper to get that done sooner than later? >> Um I mean I'll be I'll be on the Bears for a long time, so I it doesn't really matter to me, you know, so. >> Ryan has expressed the same desire for you to be here for a very long time. Has your representation communicated with you what's the hold up or how far apart the two sides may be? >> Um I mean [clears throat] I kind of the reason you have representation cuz you let those guys go in and they handle some of those things for you, so, you know, my job is to play football, handle that part of it. Their job is to talk and so, you know, I'm just trying to handle my piece and those things take care of themselves. So. >> Part of your piece, Brian said the other day, is just being more consistent. When you think about areas where you need to be more consistent, what do you identify? >> Uh just consistent in probably just >> [sighs] >> uh showing up every day. I mean, there's little pieces uh sometimes can lapse. Maybe it's my stance on a particular down. I mean, just little things that, you know, everyone has. Just trying to I just everyone has those. So. >> When you look at your higher moments from last year, what what encouraged you about some of the stuff you put on tape? >> Um I think just taking the next step. Um you know, being more being a more dependable guy, being a little bit more of a leader through my actions. Um that sort of thing. >> What was the challenge for you playing through significant discomfort with that? >> Yeah, I mean, obviously it was hard, but you know, it is, you know, everybody's got bumps and bruises. So. >> How do you feel about the prospect of having to restart basically on the offensive line with a new group after you guys really got some continuity last year and now, you know, unexpected changes. >> Um I mean, yeah, that's a big that's a big part of our line. Obviously, all five of us need to gel. And you know, that's why you train. That's why you guys work together. Um that's why, you know, we work together off the field and just uh that that's a growing process, but I mean, it'll get better and it's gotten better. So. >> Particularly in the running game, how much easier is it this time than it was at this time last year knowing exactly where you're going and then what can that mean for you two on the ground? >> Um I'd say the the biggest thing is just, you know, when you see things twice, it's it's easier. You have a little bit more experience in it. Um so, I'd say that's for anybody. That's easier second time around, but yeah. >> You guys [snorts] were the number three rushing attack last year. When you look at being I mean, is the top spot the goal? >> Uh yeah, for sure. >> How And how you get there? >> Uh, just improving. >> In his second year in the in the system, [snorts] how have you seen Caleb get better at helping you do your job in terms of identifying, check, things he's got to do once you got to get up to the line? >> Yeah, I mean, Caleb, he's gotten like he's leaps and bounds better than he was even than me last in OTAs. Uh, you can tell he spent some time with the coaches and spent some time here, you know, during our off season, so. Um, I mean, the I mean, he just just the way he presents himself in the huddle, you know, the clarity he has, um, the tone he demands, uh, it's everything's gotten better and it's better. >> Couple more. >> How was your mentality >> Um, it's tough. Just try to play tough. You know, everybody has stuff, so. >> Did you think at any point you would have to get shut down last year? >> Um, maybe, maybe if it didn't go right, if it wasn't healing correctly or whatever, but it was fine. >> How will your mentality change uh, approaching practice when you guys go to pads next on Monday? >> Um, just uh, I don't know. It won't really change, I guess. >> What's camp like for you having the contract and just so different, obviously, you weren't even here, you know, for for the last year, but I just being in the situation >> Uh, man, you know, I'm blessed to be here. I'm glad they brought me back um, to be a part, you know, Coach Johnson's building here. You know, we out there right now, we're building a foundation, and you know, it's just really like a lot of grit and hard work being taken place, and you know, you just you just a lot of um, work being put in and you just going from my situation last year from New Orleans being cut, you know, you just grateful to be in this league, so I'm great grateful to come in the locker room, work with these guys, and to be here. Yeah. >> Malcolm, given the reps you're getting now, how do you make the most of this camp over the next five or six weeks? >> Uh, man, so like I would say you just go in not really looking at where you at, just working on fundamental techniques. Um you know, when you're playing in, you know, Miami, outdoor stadiums, you just got to you got to train your body um when you get in those situations to depend on your techniques. When you're lining up against, you know, speed or bigs and stuff like that. So, really just homing in on my technique and just improving myself as a player to a better the unit. >> You got to show last year when you got the opportunities and emergency duties there a couple times. >> Yeah, you know, I think we played together well as a unit. Um we we were fast, we were physical, and we just showed like a lot of versatility um out there. So, continuing that on, building on that, building on the physicality, the um the conditioning part, um last and longer than any opponent that we played. Um that's some of the things I honed in on. >> What's the your early learning with with Devin? What have What have you figured out about him so far? >> Oh, man, great dude. Um great locker room guy. Great dude on the field. Um he's a great addition to our linebacker room. He brings in a um you know, everybody's different in this world. So, he brings in a different um type of personality in the room to, you know, just to keep going, the the keep going, to keep driving, and things like that. Yeah. >> What do you say enabled you to thrive last year when you got here? I mean, when you did get the opportunity to play, you had some real big games. >> Yeah, you know, I would say it was just the locker room that we had, you know, the the the players that we had, the coaches that we had. You just really felt that family atmosphere here. And when your name's called, you just up and you don't want to let people down. So, you just go out there and give just give your best, you know? And that goes with the preparation prior to the week, even if you're not starting and you're that backup guy.
