title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski AT&T Training Camp Press Conference | August 01, 2026 | Atlanta Falcons
text: Mhm. >> Come on, Dave. >> All right. Fire away, guys. >> All right, good. >> Same situation with the quarterbacks. Um we have any of them off rest day like he had a work day rest day? >> He will work today. Yeah, all all players are off tomorrow, but uh yes, today is a work day for him. He works on his rest day, too. I should uh clarify. Yeah. >> Is Tua any closer to being full? >> Definitely closer. Getting better and better. So, just going to be smart with the off day coming tomorrow. >> Kevin, it it feels like you've been trying to institute a a certain culture in the weight room specifically. I noticed that you talked about it at your introductory press conference. I've got to ask you about it before and stuff, but why why is that important to you and and what kind of an impact can a good weightlifting culture specifically make on football? >> Well, you know, we want to play a physical brand of football and obviously, if you're going to do that, that means running the football, stopping the run. And in order to do that, you better be strong and and particularly along the front. So, it's it's nothing new to football that that weight room culture. It's what the guys have been raised on and we just feel like it's an important piece to our success is having a physical football team and while I think literally the the the act of getting stronger happens in there, I think there's a lot that can happen from a culture standpoint when it's hard in the weight room and you got a lot of weight on your back and I just think the guys have have really embraced that and again, it's nothing new to football, but they've certainly embraced the idea that we can't just maintain. I don't think you can just maintain. I think you have to get stronger as the days go by. >> Any update on Bijan Robinson? >> No update. >> On coach Callahan's like run scheme, I think in May, I think Bijan called him like legendary. What about those schemes are is unique? What makes it work, do you think? >> Well, I think with coach Callahan, there's not a scheme he hasn't run. So, and I think back to our first time first year together in 2020, that was the COVID year, so no off season and so you have training camp. So, we really leaned into the wide zone scheme in getting ready for the season. And then very early in the season, I remember coach Callahan bringing up some gap scheme, some guard pull stuff that he really liked and that he thought had a chance with the players that we had and we had not repped it prior to that and he installed it, we put it in and it was excellent. So, I think coaches depth of knowledge is so impressive and and he can tap into that uh, to lean into you name it type of run scheme. I mean, he he's truly done it all, including wildcat uh, type thing. So, uh, I I think when I when we thought think about our scheme, what we want to be, uh, obviously it's what we feel like our players do best, and I I do feel very confident that with Coach Callahan, with Tommy, we have an ability to pivot into whatever other schemes uh, we feel like fit our players best. >> What would you say is uh, is kind of taking the reins as far as play calling right now with Brick out? >> We have a really good plan. Uh, you know, Brick and I have spoken about all these type of things, and uh, we have a really good plan of of organization, and and the truth is everybody's uh, pulling a little bit more uh, it with uh, with Brick out. So, we're asking everybody to do a little bit more. >> I'm talking like big picture philosophies. Uh, we talked to you yesterday. He said something that's a little bit different that you've implemented, at least for him in his history, was fully installing practice the night before, not having team meeting the morning of practice, and kind of seeing how guys retain that information. Why is that something that you like doing? When was that first implemented to you? >> Well, I I think this is really my first time in a morning practice schedule. All those years in Minnesota and Cleveland, we practiced in the afternoon, and I think weather-wise everybody understands that you could do that. So, with us practicing more in the morning, you really have to We don't have meetings prior to this practice. So, you have to get the guys ready for this practice the night before. Now, in the And then when the regular season comes around, we'll meet, we'll walk through, we'll practice. Here, we practice, we meet, we walk through, we meet a little bit more. So, it's just the rhythm is a little bit different, but the idea of preparing your team for the next day's practice, that really hasn't changed. It's just the idea idea of we're hitting the you're on the field at 9:05 and [clears throat] you have to have retained a lot of what you learned the evening before cuz you're not going to get a walk-through prior to it. So, you may have a few more mistakes in practice that maybe you wouldn't have if you had had a walk-through prior to practice, but you get to teach off of those mistakes. You get to have a walk-through after practice and and correct those mistakes. So, to me it's just a different teaching progression. It's just a little bit different learning progression when you have a morning practice, but when we get into the regular season that that will really go back to the normal rhythm of afternoon practices. I have no idea if I just answered your question or not. >> Yes, thank you. Also, Michael Penix kind of famously didn't play under center much in the last the two years he's been a pro. How have you observed him in in that aspect? >> Yeah, doing excellent in in that area. Very pleased with how the work he's put into it. I It is something that you see players coming out of college they're less and less under center, so you do have to do more work in the off-season program leading the guys work on it prior to training camp. It sounds simple and some ways it is, but getting that snap and and pushing off the proper foot and getting the proper drop from under center is different. So, you know, there's things that we believe in are best under center. There's certain concepts that you feel like are best under center does not mean that we won't be in the gun, does not mean we won't be in the pistol, but it is a little bit of a quarter turn adjustment if you will for some of our guys and it's just technique and and luckily we got Alex Van Pelt to to help those guys. >> Have y'all made a decision on when the pads come on? >> Uh Monday, we're allowed to have them on Monday, so there's a lot of restrictions in the acclimation leading up to camp, which again we're we're in full uh compliance with if you will, so no pads today. There's a limit to the amount of time you can be on the field in these first few practices, so they'll be on Monday. Uh cannot have pads on Tuesday, then we'll be back on on Wednesday. >> Start going back what you said about the year with coach Callahan and going from wide zone to gap. How often do you go into a year thinking, "Okay, this is one thing." And and you you get a couple of weeks in and you're like, "Nope, you know, we're going to do this." >> Every year. >> Every year. Yeah, because that's that's the NFL and you better be ready to pivot. And that's why if you're worth your salt as a teacher, you're able to do so. And I think this that's offensive system, defensive system. You want to have breadth with everything you do so that in a given game plan, we we want to lean into this or we want to lean into that. I think the bottom line where I give coach Callahan a ton of credit is understanding your players. What do your players do best? What are the things that they can do best? Whether again, in this example, we're talking about wide zone reach, force line reach, backside of blocks being able to cut or being able to down block, being able to pull, being able to pull to the same side of a run in a G scheme, being able to pull on the backside of like a counter scheme, if you will. So, that that's where as these pads come on, we get to know our players and see what they do best. >> Kevin, I know Michael's been limited, but what have you seen as far as glimpses of athleticism when he does maybe move around or pivot and throw? >> Sure. Limited in the sense that not out there for team drills, but as you watch Mike in individual, as you watch Mike in seven on seven, it's hard to watch him and say that there's a limitation, if you will. So, he's doing a very, very good job doing everything that he's been asked to do. All the stuff that he does off to the side with with our group and and in terms of rehab, he he he looks, you know, he's looks explosive and and he looks good and he's doing a great job. Are there days that he feels 100%? Probably not, but he he's stacking days, which I really appreciate. >> Coach, I do want to follow up on about the whole gap scheme versus the scheme. when you know obviously a lot of the guys that they look a little bit different from they have like different body types when in set schemes. So, is it a matter of you coming into and saying hey to those offensive lineman hey guy I need you to add a couple of few more pounds and then make the adjustment if we see that they aren't necessarily you know getting the job done so to speak. >> Right. I think for us we want the guys at all positions as big as they can be and as fast as they can be. So, haven't really adjusted anybody's weight per se because you still everybody you want to be as big that can and they can still move. You know there's there's wide zone, there's gap schemes, there's G schemes, there's toss schemes. So, can your tackles run? Can they move? Can they get out in space? There's there's the zone game wide and and tight. There's just there's so many different things that we can ask of the players but it's finding out what they do best and that's what training camp. But we're still in install phase. So, we're going to try it all. We're going to do it all. We're going to show some of it in the preseason. Probably not all of it in the preseason and just get a good feel for what we want to be as you go into week one and then oh by the way things can change as the season goes on. >> Is One Year One Year Morris been working mostly at left tackle that I've seen. Do you think of him as a left tackle or he's just there for now? >> There for now. I mean everybody's got to be ready to play all across that those five spots. So, not many guys will be one whole players but for now obviously worked him in the left side. >> Michael Jurrell have a what's his progress like at this point looks like he's your starting right tackle. >> Similar getting a lot of the reps with the ones but I wouldn't look into too much of what we're doing in this early stages of camp. We're going to try different combinations of guys really at a bunch of different positions. >> You can say Christian Harris right now is kind of the the guy alongside of the line. >> Yep. Similar conversation. I think Christian's doing a great job and I'm pleased with everybody but we will work in different guys throughout this game. >> So, you talked a lot about like Michael Penix like just being limited and stuff like that. Do you feel like that's enough to like evaluate going into the quarterback battle like down the line? >> Without a doubt. And again, Mike's not cleared for team drills, but he's cleared to do a lot and there's a lot that we're doing out there and I'm pleased with what he's able to put on tape. I'm pleased with the progress he's made in understanding this system and is I'm pleased with the progress he's made from how to command this system and operate in the system and understand all the things that are important to playing this position. So, he's making great strides and we'll again keep a very narrow focus when it comes to what what's what's important right now for Mike. >> Coach, when you talk about Billy Bowman going on to the pup list, does that kind of for you does that open up an opportunity for guys like a Clark Phillips or Natron Brooks or does it mean that you try to see maybe a young Terrell more so as an inside and try to see what he looks like or what is what does that mean for like >> All the above. >> [laughter] >> I mean, cuz that's where we are in camp. That's where you where you are in a depth chart. You're at 90. We know we got to get down to 53 at some point, but we're not even close to that yet. So, let's see what guys can do. Let's let's in this first block where that first block really ends today. We'll we'll we'll circle up and meet as coaches and say, "Okay, let's try this guy here now." So, there's going to be a lot of mixing and matching that that occurs over the next month, but anybody and and Billy who's doing great by the way, anybody in in those type of positions, we're just learning more about them and and so much of this is for our you know, you mentioned some young guys earning a role. You know, there's going to be a lot of earning roles that happens over the next month. >> You have a couple more but >> Considering like the injuries happening at quarterback league wide and you have two that are banged up right now, what appreciation do you have for the fact that it's a long season and you need a strong quarterback room and and a lot of times multiple guys do have to play. >> That's, [clears throat] you know, been my experience and not just me, but a lot of people across the league where uh you better have great depth uh in a bunch of your position rooms and certainly at the quarterback position. Uh this is a uh you got to have guys that that you trust and and I feel confident in the group that we have. I, you know, I love how these guys are are pushing each other. I love how these guys are uh working together and and and you know, that competition thing, it's really you're competing against yourself every single day, but uh the idea that you have to get multiple guys ready to play all these positions because you just can't predict anything in this league. >> I think we're hearing from the Throw Brothers today. What has it been like watching their working relationship? Obviously brothers, that connection, but the way that maybe AJ has taken kind of that leadership role, how he's kind of coaching him. What have you kind of seen from from him in that room and working together as >> Sure. I I think they obviously uh push each other. They they they are uh they're diligent workers. AJ and Avionte have a great attitude in terms of out on that grass, what needs to look like, how it how it I need to push myself, push each other. Uh obviously Avonte this season, you know, a few days into his pro career, so he's still uh learning, but he he's very very lucky to have a brother uh in the room that he can watch and and there's a bunch of veterans in that room which he he again, Mike Hughes, uh Clark Phillips, CJ Like these are guys that that have played in games and have a lot of lot that they can show him and a lot happens in my estimation as I watch it. You learn a lot just by watching and uh sometimes you you may not uh have to No, somebody's not going to pull you aside often times and tell you, "Hey, do it exactly this way." But you have great examples that are doing it on a day-to-day basis that you can watch. So, I think he's learning a lot by watching and and will only continue to get better because he's lucky to have those vets in there. >> All right. Thank you. >> Okay, thanks guys. >> Thank you. Appreciate it. >> Thank you.

Is this like an ongoing thing that he's dealt with previously or just >> believe so. >> Okay. >> With Mike, uh obviously he was off yesterday. How do you guys try to schedule when he's out there, when he's off? Like what is that process? >> I work with medical and they they tell me what they think is the best. Uh so, for instance, yesterday we didn't schedule any seven-on-sevens cuz Mike wasn't practicing. Today Mike's practicing, so had a seven-on-seven. So, just trying to be uh mindful of when he's out there and making sure he's getting great work when he's out there. >> You had mentioned to you that it might be a month until he's completely cleared. I mean, how much of a hindrance is that? And is it is there still a chance he can be the guy week one? >> He and and I are so focused on what's in front of us. Uh I know that there's conversations that happen about, you know, when when uh cleared for team, all those type of things. That's really not the our priority right now. Uh I know when he's available out there at practice and and we're going to get him ready like he's like he's doing. I think you guys see from Mike, um he's continuing to attack his rehab, attack learning a new system, getting around his teammates. So, we're really pleased with what he's doing out there. Uh and we'll just worry about that day-to-day. >> Going back to Mike Glenn, how much did you know about the situation coming in? Was that something that you were aware of? This could be a possibility. >> Well, I think just the NFL, you you understand different things come up uh via all sorts of things and and contracts obviously are part of that. So, uh it doesn't change relationships and those type of things. >> I understand those are private conversations you can't get into What have you talked with him about? Any messages that you have to him or >> I don't Yeah, I don't think it's fair to to share those type of things and again, I think we all trust in in in the process of what what's going on. >> Tua said at the end of OTAs there were certain things that he wanted to work on. Obviously, you know, a little bit limited in what he can do. Have you seen what kind of jump or what kind of improvements have you seen? I know it's only >> Sure. I'd say it's early in the camp and and until he gets fully going, you know, you'll see that as time as time goes on. I think for a player like Tua and and like Mike for that matter, it's a new system. So, you're learning and you're learning the different nuances of each play, if you will. So, I think those come with reps, those come with mental reps, those come with meetings. So, it's just about stacking days, I would say, as you learn a new system. >> How is Jack Skaggs progressing in these last three days with college reps? >> Jack is doing a nice job. Obviously, as a quarterback, you're prepared to be the starter. I mean, just that's how you do it. All whether you're carrying four guys or three guys or five guys, everybody has to prepare themselves as if they're the starter. That's how that that room works. That's that's the nature of that position. So, he's doing a nice job with what's with what Tommy and and coach Van Pelt are asking him to do. It's not perfect as you would not expect any rookie to be perfect, but I think Jack continues to impress with his ability to command the offense, the ability to get in and out of the huddle, get us in and out of run plays to pass plays. He's a very very bright young man. >> Were there a couple of traits that stood out in the draft process that made you identify that that's a guy we'd like to go after if we have the opportunity? >> Sure. I I do think the intelligence piece, which is important when you're playing that position, like we're talking about. And obviously, his size when you see him up close. Jack's a big kid that can that can stand in the pocket and deliver. >> Do we make too much about the Division II II to NFL jump? I mean, any jump from college to NFL is substantial, but is there >> I I think football's football ultimately, but those windows get really small in the NFL and guys are typically not wide open when you're throwing to them. So, I think that's just the natural college to pro type of thing. I don't know if Division 1 AA, 1 A, whatever you want to call it. I just think that's the natural thing. When you get up to this level, these these defense players are are excellent and it's hard to get guys uh really open. You know, you have to throw throw guys open. >> Coach, you heard a lot about the defensive line last year and how well they played, but the secondary is a very important unit to this particular team. How do they look so far? >> Well, I think the secondary and the front feed off of each other. And and I think a good front allows a secondary to flourish. I think a really good secondary allows the defensive line to get home. So, I think those rushing coverage really go together. Very pleased with the back end of players that we have, both young and old. I think it's a really good mix of talent. It's really good versatile mix of talent. So, really pleased with what our coaches are asking of our guys early and and throughout camp will mix and match different players back there, but yeah, really feel good about that back end in total. >> Coach, about that about James Pierce. I know he joined this team in mini camp this OTAs. You talked about him being on a timetable to progress. How do you feel like he's progressing? >> Doing a nice job. Obviously, we're just a few days into camp, so making up for some of the time he missed in the spring from a mental standpoint, but he's doing a nice job with what we're asking of him in the weight room, on on the field and in the meetings. So, he's handling his business and doing a really nice job. >> It seems like you have had a pretty rotation at nickel corner. What's kind of your evaluation of that? >> I would say that that should continue really at a lot of positions. We're going to rotate different players in there in different packages and and understand that once we get to week one you have to have a plan of of who's starting in this package, who's starting that package, but we're going to mix and match a lot of guys so that we get reps and can make an informed decision. >> Now it's only been a few days but what's that what has impressed you the most about Cash Jones so far and what do you hope to see coming? >> Cash has done a nice job just going back to the spring, you know, we bounced him from the wide receiver room to the running back room and in an effort to help him and and understand routes and understand how to get open and use his hands in the pass game with with the wide receiver position. The running back position comes naturally to him but catching the ball out of the backfield is obviously a big part of what he can potentially do so just have felt that he's done a nice job understanding his role, understanding what he can do in the system and then you know, big part for a guy like Cash and a lot of young guys is their ability to help on special teams and and he's taken that very seriously. >> What is your philosophy on playing starters in the preseason? >> I think uh every team is different. What your team needs can be different year to year. I do think in general it's good to play in the preseason. Now the number of plays varies of course and we'll really treat the first game and the third game as games that we'll play some of our starters in. The second game, you know, we're going over to Indianapolis to practice versus the Colts for a couple days so the majority the majority of the reps versus the Colts will go to our starters so those guys will not play in that second game but we'll work through our plan for the first and third game but in general I think guys to get ready to play football you got to play football. >> Could you see Ifedi to uh Mike Boone playing in those games? >> We'll see when we get to those games. Uh but again, we'll have those type of discussions leading into every game, but uh by and large, what we'll have a plan uh that that will vary based on what we feel like that that player needs to get ready for the season. >> I don't believe uh on Kyle Pitts side, we brought up his whole contract last time we talked. I mean, what did he improve to you guys from May, June, that whole process that you guys said, "Hey, I I want you here long term." >> Well, I I think Kyle obviously has been here for a good amount of time where he's established himself as a player on the on the field. He's established himself on on a person in the organization. Uh a player, a teammate in the locker room. So, what he showed me as I just got to know Kyle through the off-season program is somebody that's very serious about his work, that wants to be great, uh wants to work at uh a ton of things with coach Koger, and uh has the right attitude, and and is a really good teammate. >> I'm curious cuz I'm sure you had an idea of who he was and what he can be, but is there just the way that he operates, what's kind of surprised you, what's impressed you? Cuz he's, you know, accomplished quite a bit. >> Sure. >> Sure, you know, only know so much when you're not with him. >> Right. I I think Kyle's a very impressive when you see him initially in person. I think this is Kyle's uh been blessed to have the size and the ability to move at that size. You know, not many people are that height and that weight and can move as fluidly as Kyle does. So, I think that's something that you see when you at the first few times that we're practicing and running routes, you see the ability of Kyle to bend at that size, which I think is very rare. >> Really golf, too. >> Well, he plays a lot of golf. I don't know if I'd say he can really golf. >> Kevin, you talk so much about focus on the day-to-day process. I mean, when you go through these training camp practices and preseason and everything, what is part of the process that you enjoy most and rewards you most as a coach? >> Well, you used the word reward. You know, we uh we don't want to chase the reward, we want to reward the chase is what we're trying to do. So, what that means is all of it is part of the process, whether it's those drills that we just did out there on the field, and even the minutia of football and those drills that seem so simple and and they're everyday drills that you do. They're they're all just trying to get you ready for the the long haul. Uh what we do in the weight room, what we do in the meeting rooms, how we attack uh this off excuse me, how we attack this training camp and and get our minds and our bodies ready for a long season. I just think it's so important for us as coaches, us as players to to keep our head down, keep the main thing the main thing, work like crazy, and and not focus on what comes after uh that. We're just we're going to keep our head down and we're going to work. >> From the outside looking at so many people say, "Okay, best player at this position." You know, that's when it comes to the competition, what separates a guy in your estimation when it comes to an intangible thing versus a skill? How do you How do you go about evaluating that you feel comfortable you know, that guy has earned that opportunity? >> Uh one more time, sorry. >> Yeah, just balancing some of the intangibles, you know, versus this process, you know, you reward the chase. And you know, it's very easy for us on the outside to say, "Okay, it should be that guy >> Oh, yeah, sure. >> when you look at intangibles. >> I think yeah, speaking of evaluations of players, it's a we take everything into account, everything. Uh and I think you have to. I think to to paint a full picture of a of a player, you have to paint a full picture of the person and and the impact that they have on a day-to-day basis, the impact they have in the locker room. So, uh you know, those intangible things that that you need at positions to thrive in this league are very hard to describe, but you know it when guys have it. And we're very fortunate to have a bunch of guys that uh like I I mentioned, focus on the work. Uh this is training camp, it's going to be hard. You know, they're not in pads yet. They know that's coming, they know the heat's going to get turned up, and we're just going to focus on what's in front of us. >> Drake and Penix have both talked really highly about Zach Kancey. Saw him make a couple great catches and the crowd already roaring today. How have you seen him progress and what have you liked about >> Zachary's wired the right way, and that's something we knew going into the draft and certainly have figured out about him spending so much time with him through the off-season program in the training camp. He's somebody that really puts in the effort on a day-to-day basis, and and that's a again, was no surprise cuz that's what That's what Kirby told me. That's what all his coaches have told us in the past, and it's true. You watch him at practice and and and he goes and and he goes and he goes, and he's got the right makeup for for what we want him to be. >> Do you think that's the fans being here at all? Like fans today, first day, like does that >> I love it. Yeah, I mean, our I love it, our guys love it. I can promise you the second you have the crowd out there, it brings a level of intensity, brings a level of excitement to what we do. I think they bring the juice for us, so I love that they're here. I love that they're on the hill. I told the guys last night, and you talked about going over there sign autographs for our guys. I was that kid. You know, I know what that feels like, and it's so It's a can be a special moment for them, so we want to do our part and and and thank them for supporting us. The least we can do is go over there and and say hello, take a picture, sign an autograph. >> When do you guys expect Juwan Taylor back? >> In the next few days, weeks is the hope. Continues to work very hard. Uh he's uh in every meeting. He's pushing, and I think he's getting closer. >> So, Kendall was out today as well. Is that just kind of a planned rest day? >> Sure. There will be a scheduled rest days for a bunch of guys as we go through this program. Guys that are rehabbing from injuries, those type of things. >> You had mentioned that he had like this like calf thing that's been around for a long time. How much of a problem is that? I mean, is it not a thing you guys are really too like >> I feel that we have a We have a good plan for that his injury. He's addressed it and and will continue to be smart about it. >> You mentioned pads coming coming on soon. Is that Monday? Is that the plan? >> Yep. There's a I don't want to I'll let you know. There's it's I know it's not tomorrow. We're in shells one more day tomorrow with an off day and then pads come on either Monday or Tuesday. Lots of rules that I need to pay attention to. >> Anything else? Whose autograph? You were good. >> Uh whose autograph is the one that stands out? >> Well, you know, there there was those early '90s Eagles teams. So, uh you know, it was getting close to Jerome Brown and Reggie White and uh shoot, Eric Allen. I mean, there those were just being around those players as a young kid was was incredible. Okay, thanks, guys. >> Thanks, coach. Appreciate it. >> Thank you. >> Do we have any other questions?

title: Bradley Chubb Addresses The Media | Buffalo Bills
text: Now, it's been 3 days to actually put it on the field. How do you think it suits the personality you guys have? >> I think it suits us very well, man. Um I feel like once we fully fully get it, you know, the guys being under um in the system, they'll play so fast and just be the best version of ourselves. And um you you start to see glimpse of it and you know what I'm saying? In 3 days in, well, 3 days and a couple months in, like you said, and uh it's still a work in progress, but guys are getting it. Guys are um locking into it fast and and buying in, for sure. >> So, you go up to CJ as he was walking off the field. What did you say? What did Did he say to you and what have you heard uh >> Yeah, I haven't heard anything. He didn't say anything. I just said, man, keep your head up. Whatever it is, God got you. And um you know, we dapped it up and um got to the back to the rest of practice. So, I'm I'm pretty sure we'll hear something about that pretty soon, but you know, just praying for the best for him. >> What did you see CJ say from your time together in Florida? >> Um just the confidence. Um he he already had the skillset, you know, it wasn't nothing I knew I taught him about playing football. It's just about the the mindset of of what's expected from him. And you see him take that every day to the field, which um you know, is a big step. As a rookie, you know, uh high draft pick, you got a lot expected of you. So, just be yourself. And that's all I told him, just be yourself, but do what got you here, you know, cuz they picked you that high for a reason. And you can see him doing the things that he need to do out here. >> What does that mean, "How you do it?" You just tell him to believe in himself? Do you see a translator or is there more to it? >> I mean, it's just spending time with guys. I feel like when young guys see see vets believing in them, it just brings the best out of them. Cuz that's that's what happened to me. I had great vets when I first came into the league and uh you know, just showed me the way, just believed in me, showed that belief in me from the jump, and it just gave me the supreme confidence to do what I what I do. >> Brad, I mean, what are your first impressions of Jim? And just um the way he gets his message across. Uh what's what's most other DCs? >> Uh it's been dope, man. Jim is a great guy, very cerebral when it comes to the game of football, just knows so much about schemes, about um why he's calling things. And I feel like um the difference I've seen in him versus other DCs I've been with is when we're installing, like he's installing with with the reason why we're installing, you know? Um, it's it's never just putting a play in just to put a play in. It's um, each play has a has a purpose, has a reason, and and he tells us exactly what he wants out of us in that play. And um, when you got a guy like that, it's it's easy to play for cuz you know where you stand. You know if I'm doing the job if I'm not doing the job. And so, uh, it's easy to, you know, go out there and and play fast. >> Do you think of his demeanor? He's got a bit of a quieter demeanor. >> Off guard, off guard. Yeah, he's quiet. >> He he I mean, what what do you make the What do you make the fact but but yet he's got this attacking style of your offense. And and for for a quiet guy, it's like it seems I mean, how does it reflect on you? >> Yeah, the silent assassin, man. I mean, that's that's how you got to see it. He he schemes it all up, but he's not going to say much to you, but you know, like I said, what's expected out of you. And like he he don't have to say much, you know, at that point. But when you talk to him, you have conversations with him, he's he's a lot more talkative, but um, you know, that's just his demeanor. And I like it cuz at the end of the day you want that stealth, that that guy who's not, you know, trying to be in the media and trying to do all this. He's just about the business. >> Jamal and Joe both talked about your leadership. How would you describe yourself as a player? >> I'd describe myself just being me, honestly. Um, what's what's got me here, you know, I've been doing the same style of leadership since I was in college, and I feel like it's it's carried over. Just being the the true version of myself each and every day. Feel like people respect that, especially when they see me go out there and do the things I do on the field. Um, trying to just be the best version of me, and that that brings everybody else along with you. And it's not oh, I I got to do this to make guys like me. It's just just me being myself. >> How How much of a benefit is it for you throughout the entire summer to go up against Deion? >> Yeah, it's going to be a great benefit, man. We were just talking about that actually on the field, like um, I do a rush, he's like, "Hey, man, good good stuff on that one." I do a rush that's not too good, and he he locks it up and I'm telling him the same thing and it's it's learning from each other, you know? Um I've had great tackles that I played against throughout the summer in the past, but Dion's consensus the top 10 tackles in the league each year and year out. So, um being able to have that those battles each and every day is going to be uh good for both of us and I'm excited about it. >> Over your career, have you had like conversations with tackles who will tell that you'll maybe they'll tell you, "Hey, I see you doing this. You know, this is where I can take advantage of you." You can say the same thing to them. I know you're not on game day. >> Yeah. No. >> But but is does that happen throughout the league? >> Uh throughout the league, I would not I wouldn't say so. Like unless you're like real cool with the guy, which I'm not cool with tackles until you know, we're teammates. But um throughout practice like when I was with Garett Bolles in in Denver, we talked a lot. Um Terron Armstead out out in Miami, we talked a lot and then Papale was coming up. So, he was still young um trying to see different things, but um you know, having those battles with him were were great, too. So, you know, like I said, Dion's been le- year in year out top 10. So, it it's been fun to to go in. Into this battle. >> Sorry, I didn't >> You good. >> Has this fresh start re-energized you a little bit? >> Oh, for sure, man. Uh I I feel like I didn't never lost no energy, to be honest with you, but you know, when you kind of uh you know, go season in season out not having the results you want like, you know, in the win column. You know, I had probably one 11-win season, one playoff appearance for me myself, too, technically, but I didn't play in one. Um you know, it it's uh it is re-energizing to get to a a city and a team and an organization who has expectations of not just the first round, not just the second round, you know, being in in the in the long haul in the playoff run playing far into January. So, you know, just trying to bring my what I bring to the table into this atmosphere and um bring the best out of everybody. >> You've played in the Ralph for you several times. Uh what's it like going into a new stadium with all your anticipation next week? >> Man, I'm really excited about it. You know, I got a chance to see it before it was all said and done like we were still kind of under construction and stuff. So, I'm excited to see the fi- the finished product. But, um I was telling somebody the other day like I I miss I'm going to miss the old Highmark Stadium, you know, that that old grungy feeling of just old-school football. That's going to be, you know, always something that um that you remember coming into the up to Buffalo and playing in, but you know, change is good. New is good. I had a lot of changes off-season, so being in the new stadium with the with this team, I know it's going to be different for a lot of those guys, but it's going to be good for us. >> What was it about the old stadium that really that that kind of endeared you to it? >> I guess it's that old-school feel. Everybody share the same tunnel. The locker room's not super updated, you know, it's the showers cold, you know, even when it's cold outside, you know, just stuff like that. Not talking trash about it, but you know, just stuff like that that you you like, "Okay, we're here to play a football game, you know?"

title: Pete Carmichael Speaks To The Media | Buffalo Bills
text: Hey, you've worked some great running backs throughout your career. What are your early impressions of Buffalo's running back room? And how do you envision getting them more involved maybe in the passing game as you've done in New Orleans? >> Yeah, I think that obviously excited about that room. There's been a lot of production in the run game over the past, but again, new year, new season. When you talk about getting them some throws in the past game, a lot of that sometimes is just giving them those opportunities. But again, there's a lot of competition in that room. Really excited about where that room's at. >> Peet, where do you see the connection growing between Josh Allen and DJ Moore? >> Yeah, I think that you know, it's nice to see them connect a couple explosives early on in these first couple practices, but again, I think that's something that's going to continue to evolve, continue to grow as they get more reps with each other. They had a lot of work in the off season. I think that'll just continue to evolve as they, you know, learn each other. But I guess um, you know, I've been pleased with how that progress is going. >> Hey Peet, as you look through the Bills' film the last couple years in your career, do you see a need for any sort of possibility of increasing the running back screen game at all for this team? >> Well, I think as you go into the off season, you look at when I first got here, hey, some things that we might be able to do differently. I think that uh, you know, a lot of that might be specific to a team that you're playing. How do the screens look? How do the screens to the halfback look? Sorry, are they more are we better off getting them on the perimeter? So, I think there's just uh, that's always a part of the game that you like to be able to be productive in. And I think some of that might be specific to who you're playing. >> Peet, there's a lot of talk about Kion this off season. You've been around this league a while. What what are the keys to a young wide receiver in his growth to kind of get to a spot where he really understands everything about playing the position, chemistry? Like what what what is the key there for those guys in the first few years? >> Uh I would say this. I I love his focus. I love his um his mindset when he's coming to the building. Uh he is working extremely hard. He's playing fast. I think a lot of that just develops over time, but I think that all the intentions are are great. He is um uh you know, able to play multiple positions. And so, those opportunities are going to come with uh with time. >> Have you over your years have you seen guys other wide receivers? Like, is there something that happens that you they figure out a little bit as they go along? >> Yeah, I think they just start, you know, with the more experience they start playing a little bit more confidently, more um experienced. Maybe they have a better um uh you know, just talking about other guys in the past that we you know, that I've been a part of there's been times where guys have all of a sudden it's clicked. >> The uh fullback was a big part of this offense last year. You have two guys competing to to replace the one that that was here. How do you balance evaluating that competition with installing plays and getting a sense of how much you may use that position this season? >> I would agree. It's been a big part of uh the success that this offense has had in the past. I think that evaluating that position will will increase as when the pads get on. And so, again, that's what part of training camp's about. And you always want to be able to put your best personnel on the field. Uh maybe in and that personnel may change based on the situation. But again, as the pads get on, we get some reps and and be able to see. Um be excited about that. >> You've got you've got experience with a head coach that's responsible for calling the plays in your time with Shawn, but in your role now, how do you feel? What's on your short list in terms of taking the load off of the head coach knowing he's got the play-calling responsibilities in your own? >> Well, I think that it's uh again, what is his message? And he's not going to be able to be at all the call it the offensive meetings. And so, making sure that whatever message he's giving is the same message that the players are hearing from us as coaches. Uh obviously, Joe does a great job in front of the team. He's, you know, passionate about it, and they can feel that. But again, it's just he's got other responsibilities. He's There's times on the field where he wants to go over and watch the defense or be with the defense or the special teams. And it's just being able to make sure that what he wants is what's being communicated. >> that, are there like gaps you're trying to seek out to say, "Okay, Joe's not going to have time for this. This is where I step in." >> Yeah, I think that uh over the, you know, over the time that I've been here, start seeing, "Oh, you know what? I can I can help with this or I can Let me put this on my plate." But I think that uh again, he's very involved. But it's just really, yeah, what if he doesn't have time to do something, making sure that it's getting done. >> You zoom in here, study the film on this offense, now seeing them on the field together, what do you believe is the potential of this team? >> Well, I I think this. It's a new year, new season, so nothing's nothing's promised to us. And you can go back over the years and say, "Oh, this has been a a team that's been a top rushing team. It's been a team that's been a top passing team. It's been a team a couple years ago that was really good with protection." But all those things just just because they've been good in the past don't just just aren't handed to you. So, I think again, that's what's happening now and through the work. But uh you know, there's a lot of guys in this building that have been a part of it. But again, it's just not something that's just like, "Ah, you know, it's just going to happen." Has to happen through work, preparation. >> Drew's going to Drew's going to Hall of Fame on Saturday. When you started working with him, when did you know right away that he was pretty special? >> Uh yeah, so I I was fortunate to be with him in San Diego as well for four of his five years. And I you always knew that he had had what it took. He had he had that that uh the stuff that you can't coach outside the building. Um all that. He had it and just the way he worked, uh prepared, the way he was able to communicate with players, his relationships, all that stuff was special. And then again, it you know, went on to the field, but he's always had those special traits. >> What will it mean to you to to be there to to see him inducted? >> Yeah, it's pretty special. Uh I it's it's a special moment and be going to be a lot of guys just great to see again that are all there celebrating his what he deserves. And he's uh he's meant so much not only to his teammates, but the city. Uh what him and Sean were able to do in New Orleans and bring everybody It was it was special to be a part of. >> With Alec and Austin at left guard, what are you looking for to determine who winds up being the winner of that battle? >> Yeah, I think that's going to come when the you know, as the pads get on. A lot right now they're getting reps and uh develop as we go through here, but excited about both guys and um with what we you know, they've been able to do so far without the pads on, we're excited about. >> Is it different for each guy? I mean, is it the same parameters for both or does each guy have their own things that they need to work on that you want to see happen for them to be the guy? >> Yeah, I think each guy is you know, each guy is his own guy and and you might not specific to them, but just in general when you're talking about maybe two guys that are playing in one position, you know, one the same position, you know, one guy might need more work in the run game, one guy might need more work in the pass game, but again, I think a lot of those questions start to get answered when the pads come on. >> You've been a part of a lot of training camps, right? Anything that stood out about how Joe has tried to pass along his message to start camp or maybe how he's kind of set up this training camp to you? >> Yeah, I think this I would say he had when he got named head coach, he had a he presented a vision and uh he knew exactly what what kind of team he wanted, what kind of players he wants to surround himself with, and I think he's conveyed that message in team meetings, to the people in the building. I think it's been pretty uh pretty fun to see. >> You talked earlier about the connection between Josh and DJ, but how has your connection grown with Josh since you stepped into this? Maybe what's the thing that you've learned the most about him since you've been here? >> Yeah, I think that uh obviously get to be around him every day, and that's pretty special in itself, but I think you just you love the competitiveness, he's extremely smart. I think there's just there's so much yeah, what you see on the field, but also off the field, where you see him interacting with guys and his ability to communicate, he's special. >> What level of intentionality is there to you two spending time together and sort of growing that rapport, understanding how important the relationship is between an offensive coordinator and a >> Yeah, obviously, and I think that uh on top of that is just the relationship that he has with Joe, and Joe as the play caller, and um you know, in a sense, you know, Joe's this is Joe's offense, it's Josh's off it's it's our off offense that we're building, but I think that there's a relationship um not only with with us, but in that whole uh quarterback room, and then with the team, and again, Joe's a big part of that as well. >> How do you view the quarterback room outside of Josh as Kyle and Shane are, you know, getting their reps? >> Yeah, excited to walk into that room every day, uh feel real confident with the group of guys that we have in there. Obviously, Josh is special, but real confident in Kyle and uh Shane as well. >> If we mention what Drew Brees meant to the city, can you maybe put your mind back to the time before the Saints punched through and win that Super Bowl, and everything that's built up around having a great quarterback and a city that hadn't won it yet and anything that you can maybe see from that time to where you are now. >> Well, I I think this. I think we got there, you know, I'm going to say it was right after the season of Katrina. And so there was just a lot of uh destruction. You know, it was it was obviously um tough time and I think that the excitement of the team uh winning, it just kind of brought everybody together, but I think that they purposely uh brought the city with them and the the the passion of the fans and and then all of a sudden to have success early, that first game in the Superdome uh was week three against Atlanta and just the noise in the game that day and just you could just tell that something special was being built. >> You're not from there, but as an ambassador, I suppose, to having won a Super Bowl with New Orleans, can you put into words what he means to New Orleans? >> Uh I think that he's he's always going to have a place there. He's special. I think that uh I don't know if there's a group of wasn't there's a lot of guys from that team that did a lot of great things and them getting out into the community, them uh letting the people be a part of it was pretty special. >> I think there's a lot of unknowns going into the season with with Joe and and and it's natural for people to wonder if if Joe what kind of a coach head coach Joe can be as a first-time head coach. What gives you the confidence that to see that he's capable of of of taking this job and taking this team to the next level? >> Well, the way he communicates and the way he talks to the team, uh the messages he portrays, he has a vision, he has a belief, he's sticking to it. And again, there's been a lot of head coaches that have been successful uh calling an offense and I I he has he has those characteristics.

title: Top takeaways from Week 1 of training camp | Altitude Advantage
text: Welcome into a training camp edition of Altitude Advantage. I'm your host Eric DeLalla here with the Hall of Famer Steve Atwater. >> Let's go, AB. >> Let's go. Sounds like Steve, come on, say something. >> All right. >> Say something. Get us going. And then we got >> And then we got uh Suzanna Wera, digital content coordinator. >> I don't have quite that much energy, but >> Well, then get Come on, let's go. >> let's go. >> Let's go. All right, we are we're fired up because the first few days of training camp, they're done. They're complete. They're in the books. The Broncos are heading into their first uh kind of day off here. We had the 3-day or 2-day acclimation period on Wednesday and Thursday. 2 days of camp complete. Um and we're here to kind of break it down over the next few minutes. What we've seen. Still a lot of camp to go, Steve, but uh but we've we've seen some good stuff so far and I think it starts with this offense and the big plays that we've seen out there. >> Yeah, we've seen a ton of explosive plays and I think most teams when they start off training camp, they, you know, they they have that, but it looks a little different this year. It looks like we we're going to have some deep play deep ball threats. Uh balls put on the money. Uh we know we got a great offensive line coming back. Uh there's a lot of good things to look forward to and uh good reasons to think that this will be able to carry over into the season. >> Steve, you say that like every team has this to some degree and I and I agree, but I feel like often you get to camp and the defense has the the early edge and like the first few days, especially as like install is going on that a lot of times the defense is just frankly dominant in a lot of places and it's not like the defense hasn't made its plays too, but this offense has looked really good in my opinion early in camp and does that speak to the the continuity, the kind of bringing back the same guys, having guys that kind of know what they're doing and and a quarterback that is quite frankly to me looks like he's kind of at that next level. >> I I think it's a combination of all those things. Uh guys having the familiarity with the offense. Um you know, the addition of Jaylen Waddle, Uh everybody feeling healthy, coming back fresh, and I think everybody has that confidence in this in the in this offense and in Davis Webb in his first year. I think everybody's trying to prove like look man, we're going to be good with Davis Webb. You know, we're going to we're going to make Davis Webb uh be office coordinator of the year, whatever, you know, but they they're supporting him and it shows out there on the field that you know, they are executing at a high level. >> And since you've been doing some some observations for denverbroncos.com, nice job. You're doing a good job. Um we've seen a bunch of guys make plays offensively. Evan Engram's gotten open a lot. Marvin Mims uh today another long catch. Uh who's kind of stood out to you in terms of uh what you've heard from Sean Payton and just kind of quite frankly what we've seen on the field in terms of these big catches. >> Yeah, I think Marvin Mims is the first guy that comes to mind. Sean Payton talked yesterday about how those 40-50 yard receptions and finding the ball over his shoulder is his strength and I think just in a couple of days here we've already seen that and he looks to be just as what he was when we when we left off last year. So, um he's definitely stood out and then I mean I'm sure we'll talk about Bow, but just his mobility and the way that he's looked and his confidence the last couple days has has really uh you know, stood out very early. >> Yeah, he had a play earlier Saturday as we're recording this that he was kind of flushed from the pocket, a guy in his face, and he just he just flicked it down the field and the receiver was able to adjust, makes a 50-yard touchdown pass. It just looked easy and it was like and not that he hasn't done that before, but but Sean Payton asked him about it today and he said that's Bow's superpower or one of his superpowers that he can extend the play, doesn't take sacks, and he often is able to make that second act and I don't want to compare guys too much, but it's like that's what Mahomes does so well that makes him so hard to stop. That's what Josh Allen does so well that makes him so hard to stop. Lamar Jackson, I mean, you could go on and on. These guys that can make plays after the initial thing kind of breaks down. And Steve, as a defense, I'm sure that's >> Oh, super frustrating. >> Super frustrating for defenses and a heck of a talent for your offense to uh have that ability to almost be in the grass and everybody feeling like it's a sack and then, oh no, it's not a sack and then oh, it's a touchdown. You know, it's just the opposite. You know, you think you're getting a sack on defense and then it's a touchdown. It's uh it's completely demoralizing for the offense. But uh for the team who scored the touchdown, um man, it's a wonderful feeling. And it's beautiful it's a beautiful thing for us to watch it happen. >> Yeah, and and Bo had a couple throws, I mean, he had a throw down the sideline to RJ Harvey that he just put right exactly where it needed to be. And not that Bo hasn't made great throws over the the years, but I I think that like it's kind of what we talked about the end of last year, that step that he got to, um it seems like he's picking up right where he was and um he said that he feels as good as he thought he needed to feel, feels great, um no limitations. He was asked is he going to change the way he plays in terms of running around? He said, absolutely not. Um he he knows that this is one of his strengths. Um and I think you whether it's Sean Payton, Bo Nix, anybody you talk to, like this guy, like you said, Steve, Bo's ready to go, it seems like and that's we've got a lot of camp left, preseason, all that, but like that's that's really encouraging early in training camp. >> Yeah, but it also uh you know, I want to also point out the fact that he feels that way, like, all right, I feel like I'm at my best when I do have the ability to scramble and my coach isn't restricting me. Because some coaches, they'll say, look, man, we don't want you to do this, we don't want you to do that. The coaches have his back on that. And that's that's a huge part of him having the confidence level that he has, too, because he knows, "Hey, I can make this statement and my coaches is right. He's He's with me. He He wants me to feel comfortable to be able to extend plays, to be able to make plays with my legs when I have to, cuz I'm going to have to do it sometimes." Sometimes he's going to have to make plays with his legs because guys will be covered or for whatever reason. So, it's great that he's able to practice that and, you know, everybody's on the same page. >> And Sean Payton's been asked about that since Bo Nix arrived of how much do you try to say, "Hey, let's stay within structure, stay within the pocket" or coach that out of him. And Sean Payton has said many times, "You don't want to coach that out of him too much or even coach him on it too much cuz he's got this great natural timing instinct of how long do I hold the ball, how long do I hang in the pocket before I say I'm going to I'm going to take off." And some guys, they take off and they start running immediately. Bo has a great ability to keep his eyes >> Look down the field. Yeah. >> which makes it even more challenging and I think goes back to the Mahomes, the Allens in terms of what makes it difficult for guys to stop. Um I'm sure we'll see plenty more of Bo as as camp goes on, obviously, and I would expect many more great plays. And one of the guys we've seen him connect with and and really different quarterbacks connect with it is Evan Engram, who we heard Sean talk about it's a priority and they're looking for different ways to get him involved. >> Yeah, absolutely. And he talked about his relationship with Davis Webb and how he thinks that Davis Webb is going to prioritize finding different ways to get him involved. And you know, we obviously saw that yesterday. He had a long reception and just he's been very involved, I would say, the last couple of days. We've really seen him multiple times, you know, with each of the quarterbacks. And so, it's been good to see and good to hear that he's going to be a huge part of the offensive plan this season. >> Yeah, I I can't Sorry, sorry. Steve, go ahead. >> No, I was just I was just going to say that it's so vital that you get that tight end involved in the pass game cuz that's going to help open up everything else. Just like the run game helps open up the pass game. Having a tight end that you can throw the ball to in these clutch situations when hey, the receiver's not open or we're not running the ball well. Oh, but our tight end, you know. That be able to have that three three-headed monster boy, that that can really be a huge advantage. And we thought we were going to see more of that last year. We didn't get get to see as much of it. We got got to see it here and there, but just not really enough of But I hope that that's going to be a bigger part of this offense this year, just utilizing the tight end along with all the other weapons. >> Yeah, and I I think Evan Engram is a guy that obviously talented, he can run, he's fast, all those things. He's a He's a matchup problem. And if you can find those matchups, it will be big for for Sean Payton and Davis Webb. Um but there's guys everywhere like Pat Bryant. I mentioned the touchdown pass earlier like he's making a play, Marvin Mims making a play, Courtland Sutton. Um Well, Jordan Humphrey made a a diving catch yesterday that was really Exactly. And and then I can't help but thinking that some of or a lot of this goes back to Jaylen Waddle and just not only the plays he's made cuz there's a lot of times where he gets open and and Sean Payton said a lot of the times the reason it looks like he's wide open is because it's not that just that he's fast but that he stops so much faster than everybody. But in addition to what he's shown with his catches, I've got to think he's already like he's taking away your number one corner or whoever it is, one of your top corners. Uh that will just open everything up because man, if you have a cornerback that can cover him one-on-one, you got to you you there's not that many teams that have those type of players. I think we have one. We got a PS2. But he's one that he's rare. Yeah, 100% and uh you love to see those battles uh how they're going to play out, but uh you know in the end we got two great players on both sides of the ball there um and um for this offense especially it's it's going to be so refreshing for Broncos country to see that uh extra layer of explosiveness and uh also you just utilizing all the weapons on the offensive side of the ball. Um I think I think uh Broncos country is man, they're they're they're ready for it. >> Yeah. So he's uh we've talked a lot about the pass catchers. Another guy who's he's excited, he's optimistic and he's he's got like this infectious energy. We heard from Jaleel Johnson uh yesterday and and he's one of the I think storylines of camp so far. He To me he looks like he's got burst and he's got juice. There was one today he just hits the hole fast and Sean Payton was talking about how like he was a big reason why this team won 14 games a year ago and that things changed when he went out, but but clearly a motivated JK that's heading into this season. >> Yeah, and I I like that Sean Payton mentioned that cuz I think when you have somebody that misses the end of the season that can kind of get lost in translation and he made a point to say, "Listen, we ended up where we were because he was with us for those 10 games and what he did during those 10 games." But I motivated is I feel like an understatement. He was eager yesterday, he was excited. Um just awesome to see a lot of energy from him and like you mentioned, I feel like from the little we've seen so far, he's looked very explosive, bursts of energy. Um so energy both on and off the field from him. >> Yeah, that's right. >> But he he's so amazing, man. I and I love to see this how um you know, Sean Payton could have overlooked that you know, the fact that JK Dobbins had a significant contribution, but he he mentioned it. He brought it up and you know, it that makes the player that makes JK Dobbins feels like hey man, I'm I'm appreciated and you know, some coaches don't do that and to have a head coach that does that is huge because the great players. I think need to hear that sometimes they need a little bit of confirmation from your coach that hey, you're appreciated and we need you. We we we want you to play well and all those good things. So but yeah, I I agree with what you said there JK you know, have having him back and you know, he talked a lot about you know, his health and we're we're hoping that he's healthy. We know nobody can control how it turns out but obviously we're all hoping that he's going to be healthy. No, not not all the way down and you know, guys who can do that I'm very impressed. Dobbins said he's back to that he I think he said he'll be like Elasti-Girl if he gets tackled a certain way. So yeah, I mean he's he's confident. I think you've probably got to have a certain level of belief when you've suffered some tough injuries of like this isn't you almost have to have like a mindset of this isn't going to happen to me and it is done and you've got to play that way cuz if you if you play scared or you're worried about the injuries, you can't play fast. You can't be the guy you were and Alex Singleton I thought it was interesting. He said everyone talks about the injuries JK suffered. I'm more impressed that like he comes back better each time and and he had almost 800 yards in 10 games last year. I think you have to go back to 2005 to find a Broncos running back that had that many yards in 10 games. So it's been like essentially the best start to a season in two decades for a Broncos running back. He He was an emotional leader. Um he did a lot of things >> And it wasn't on like 25 carries a game, either. >> No. No. I mean, he averaged 5 yards a a carry, and he's had that for his career. Like, it's going to be uh I don't know how how many guys end up making it, but it's going to be a good room. title: QB Bo Nix: ‘We’re heading in the right direction as a team’
text: So, how how does it feel to be back the first year, just to be back out there full time? >> It feels great. It feels normal. It feels like we're headed in the right direction as a team. We're all sort of you know, continuing to get our feet wet first couple days, learning some new things and also getting back to our our favorites. And so, I think it's been good to see everybody move around. It's been a competitive first couple days offense and defense which is what you want to see. A lot of you know, both sides of the ball are making a lot of plays. It's just a fun time right now. >> How do you feel your leadership has grown from year one to year three? >> I've drastically. Year one I'm trying to just you know, not mess up for the team. And I feel like year three I'm trying to make plays for the team. So, it's just um quite the different feeling. Um you know, it's just a confidence level thing I think. Playing as many games as I have already it's just um there's hardly going to be a situation I haven't been in. So, you know, it's good to lead our team. It's good to you know, be on a team with other solid leaders, um other veteran guys that do a great job leader of leadership. It's not just me out there. It's there's a lot of voices and um I just I think we have a um a really good feel right now with the leadership and and the guys that are responding to our leadership and we got a really good team. >> Russell, I know that you were kind of champion at the bit to come back. You said in the spring you were ready. They were being concerned with the human. Sean Payton says now he's on the active list here right where the team wants you to be. How good is it you know, to hear that from him? How's the feeling off? >> I feel great. Um feel normal. Feel um you know, nothing's holding me back. I'm out there playing like I normally do and um you know, feel really good in my my spot. So, I'm continuing to push it and progress and also going to continue to uh you know, physically get ready for through long season. Um but right now I'm exactly where I want to be as a as a team. you know, for our plan and um, actually was a little bit ahead from uh, where I was last year going into the season, going into the summer. So, um, you know, feel really good. Feel like I'm in a good spot and um, I think it's you know, it's showing on the field. >> Coach Shaw was saying that one of your superpowers is to extend plays, kind of make that second act play. Is that something you think you've gotten better at over your career? And then what's it feel like? It seems like you're pretty fired up. What what's it feel like? >> I think uh, it is a strength and um, I think it's like any strength it can be overused, utilized and it can be um, you know, overused and so I think for me it's just about the balance. It's making the plays when they're there, but at the same time using that creativity and skillset when it's not. So, um, today, you know, get always, I feel like every practice I've ever been in there's going to be a time or two during practice that you have to move and um, escape and practice that dynamic play. And so, our guys are in tune with it and those guys are moving around with me and um, you know, it's just all about there's uh, you know, the play's never over and um, you know, also being smart and just making plays. >> You've said you've had a lot of completions to Jaylen Waddle already in camp. What's it been like working with him and what type of receiver is he on the field? >> He's an explosive playmaker. Um, guy's really good at what he does. He gets open, he makes plays, he's fast, he's really explosive. Um, he's great ball in hand, he's great going to get the ball deep, he's great, you know, in screen game. He can do just a lot of things. He's very versatile. So, um, he adds an extra element to our offense um, and it's exciting. Man, we got a lot of different weapons that we're using and um, I think top to bottom this is uh, just a really strong team, really good. Um, we just got to find what works for us and find um, ways to utilize all our um, all our tools. >> Do you feel like Do you feel like that confidence and everything that he adds as well along with Davis might lead to more opportunities in the middle of the field? >> Uh middle of the field, outside, vertically, behind the line of scrimmage, you know, anywhere. We're going to utilize him and you know, I think it's just whatever the defense is giving us, we're going to take. >> Well, with the Yeah, the standard question for quarterbacks coming off of injuries. You know, you've talked about balance, but is there talk or thought in your mind of maybe not taking off quite as much? >> Absolutely not. I'm going to I'm going to roll and I'm going to be as athletic as I can be and um like earlier question, it's a strength of ours and so we got to use our strengths and um for me that's when I feel um at my best and that's when I feel um free when I'm playing like that, when I'm moving around. Um it's a good thing, but at the same time, I also know what it's like to you know, not have that asset and have to stay in the pocket. So, I feel strong no matter what the play is going to be, no matter what happens defensively, no matter what my reaction is. Um I feel, you know, capable of doing anything. >> How about sliding? How about sliding? >> Well, it's always, you know, the situation. You know, if I'm out to get a first down, I'll go down, won't take necessary hits. At the same time, a key third or fourth down, you know, you have to go get the first down and that's why you train hard in the off season to withstand those hits and um it's all about being smart, you know, I'm not going to be dumb. I know I'm not going to run over everybody on the field, so >> [snorts] >> I just got to be smart and um put us put me in a good situation so that we can move on, go to the next play. >> With Davis, with Davis, you got a little bit of reps and works with him during mini camp, where you were limited, but how's that process been getting the on-field reps and hearing that communication from >> It's been really good. Um honestly, felt like we picked up right where um they left off in spring and feel like I picked up right where, you know, left off with coach. And so, it's the voice in my ear, but um, you know, both were very, you know, coach and Davis both very calm, decisive, give me the play. Um, I feel like Davis is doing a really good job of um, communicating with me and not over communicating, but just give me a few uh, things here and there, reminders, little things about a play. Like, "Hey, you know, don't forget this. Hey, remember you got this." Um, and so I think that's going to be, you know, great as we go with that communication in my ear and um, you know, he's been waiting for this moment for a long time. He's been preparing for this and um, he's really put us in a good spot. >> So, was there was there a specific play in any of those off-season shot came to you? Was that different? Making it up? Making this change? Making Davis the play call? What was that conversation in any way? >> Well, honestly, I don't specifically remember it, but I know um, that was a long process getting him here in the first place. You know, coach Colin um, calling it for me the first couple years, getting the foundation in. Um, and I think it was just uh, coach's decision and um, you know, I think it was a um, you know, a good decision for all and you know, coach is not going to go away. He's still going to be there. He's still going to be, you know, alongside Davis on the sideline with the with the call sheet. Um, same system and we're just going to attack it how we see fit and now we got a good um, just good calms, good communication, um, a good process. Going to have a lot of people seeing a lot of different things, which is good. Always what a quarterback wants and so um, not much is going to change, just a different voice in my ear and um, maybe just a different diagram on the play sheet. >> So, are there any examples specifically of differences to so far? >> With uh, Davis and coach? Hard to say without playing a game yet. Um, but I don't I don't expect there to be any differences. Um, you know, other than just coach was a little bit more he gave me the play and let me go. I think Davis may, you know, be able to give me a few more reminders, add a few more things in in the sentence, but um, it'll be pretty much the same. >> Last last two Parker and Mike, obviously you have a remark, please. You haven't seen You haven't played obviously your three years, but going into your three, where do you where do you feel the experience in the games you've played is it Is it looking at defenses? Is it your own playbook? Like what where does that show up? >> I think it's both. I think it's understanding my playbook and understanding what we're doing so that we can attack defenses. I think when you have a second nature thought process and you know the play and you're not thinking about operation or motion or a route concept or a handoff point, you can attack the defense in a little bit more of a strategic way. And so my eyes are up a little bit more. I just feel comfortable. It's like, you know, riding a bike for the third year as opposed to the first. You know, you get up on it and it's you know, it's by memory at this point. And so I feel good. I feel I feel like there's a lot of growth to be had. Like just in practice, there's things that I know and we've gone over in in meetings and I see a look and I got to get to something faster and but at least I'm recognizing it quicker and you know, that's just one step to getting there. And so I'm excited about the growth and know that there's plenty left, but also I feel stronger where I'm at. >> Last one, Gus. You've come a long way since you you described yourself as a rookie just trying not to mess up. >> Mhm. >> So part of the progression now is this is essentially a contract year for you. How do you not think about that? How do you approach that or what's your switching mindset there? >> Well, the way I think competitively the way we are as players is you better treat every year as a year that you have to prove and you have to go out there and show the team that you're, you know, worth what they're putting in for you and what are they building around you and you can't ever let up and think that, you know, what I've I've made it. I've gotten to where I need to be and because quite honestly, I'll would feel that way. There's always the next season. There's always the next championship to go after and so I think every year is, you know, for every player it's going to feel like a contract year. It should because you got to go out there and continue to earn it day by day cuz there's, you know, only 32 people in my position that and a lot of many others that are trying to get, you know, in that same position. So no days can you take off and no days can you come out here and give half effort or not be prepared, not be ready to go. And I think at the end of the day that's just the internal motivation I have to not let my teammates down and not let the organization down and, you know, I owe them my 100%. And no matter if I was being paid for it or not being paid for it. They're my teammates and we all work hard together and it's my job to go out there and put them in the best situation possible.

title: QB Past and Future! Bernie talks with Shedeur!! | Training Camp Interviews

How do you galvanize that leadership to put it put your put your game together, but also put your team together out on the field? >> I would say overall you just be yourself. [snorts] You don't you don't you don't do anything odd or weird. I think you just be yourself. And people at this point in life, people like love genuine and people love authentic and people love realness. That's why we don't have the petty quarterback battles internally of that. That's not up to us. It's up to, you know, whoever the coach is thinking, whoever put their best foot forward. Well, that's an awesomely mature attitude to this. So, >> yeah. So, that that that's where I say I say we've grown the most uh this year. >> I'll say for sure in the quarterback room. So then we use each other in the best situation. >> For the fans out here listening to this today, you should massively be excited because this got a mature young man here for a secondear quarterback. I'm excited for it. >> God bless you, man. >> Appreciate it. >> Enjoy the day. Looking forward to it. >> Yes, sir. >> You matter. >> Definitely, too. >> You matter, brother.

Emmanuel Moseley Ward, the young safety out of Toledo, today there was one that Deshaun completed actually to Jack Stoll. And what he did so well in college was punch that football out. Punch it out and ends up being an interception right after that. So, >> Yeah, us quarterbacks don't count that as an interception, but that's from a team perspective, that's phenomenal to see a young guy with that savviness. >> Yeah, he did well. Now, as you hear everybody around us right now, all the kids, everybody's clamoring for Shedeur Sanders.
