Now, those people, they're just excited to get a little bit of time with Shedeur Sanders. But earlier today, Bernie, >> We had plenty of fun time. >> of time and a lot of fun as you sat down. The meeting of the quarterbacks, Bernie Kosar, Shedeur Sanders, take a watch. >> Bernie Kosar out here for day two for me at Browns training camp. Super honored today to be talking to the awesome Shedeur Sanders. >> What's going on? >> Welcome out here today. >> you're awesome, man. >> Uh thank you for swelling my cranium, but I was I was joking with some people about my my real respect for you. And I'm not saying this just to be a suck-up here early in the interview and stuff. What you do with the younger kids with the the grade school, the high school, the college kids is absolutely commendable. So, you know, we have those opportunities, we're talking to them and if you get this look or you get certain things, say let's be a little bit more aggressive. This is the time to see if you can make those throws, if the receivers can get their depth, have that those timing routes. But, this is the perfect time to be able to make all the mistakes you possibly can because, you know, it doesn't it doesn't really count. And you won't you don't want to get into a game and you haven't ran that or tried it out and and try it in a game and it goes you goes wrong. So, yeah, there's a fine line between, but you just got to know and understand what we're working on. >> Deshaun, I know it'll be fine with the passing game, but so far in training camp, what is the offense giving from the looks of the defense giving you guys out there on the daily? >> Uh it's multiple. I mean, they're doing all types of different stuff, showing us different things. So, it's really good, especially for the quarterbacks, running backs, and the O-line, just protection-wise. They're showing us different things each and every every time. And then each group is getting different looks. So, just because the first group is going up and you think the second group is going to get the same look, they switch it up on us. So, it's been awesome for us to be in the be in the meeting rooms and see the different things and try to work on it now. >> So, Deshaun, given that you know that you know this is the time to kind of make a few mistakes and air it out a little bit. How concerned are you with the fact that you know we've seen those back-to-back interceptions on day one and then another one to Quincy yesterday. Are these just things that are going to happen early on in practice and you're just trying to figure out how far you can take things? >> Of course. I mean, again, it goes back with timing. Certain things that, you know, the little things with depth and and and the type of when the ball is coming out and and chasing the coming back down to the to the catch point. But then again, you know, we have a really really good defense. So, they're going to make plays, too. So, again, like I said, you know, sometimes you want to be aggressive and they're going to make plays. We're going to make plays. So, I think it would be really bad if we're, you know, completing all the balls and touchdowns and and they weren't making plays. But we have a really good defense. And uh we have a really good offense. We love to compete and you know, again, we learn from those and you know, I put that in the memory bank. So, I know that, you know, versus this look and this play that I got to be a little bit more cautious on trying to be aggressive. >> Just one last thing on the Quincy one yesterday. What did you see on that on that play or >> I just tried to try to squeeze it in on the IB route towards the middle. That was something that Quincy and when I talked to him, it was a wing wing set and he saw the chip so he came back backside and every our progression's on the right side. So, being able to just see the backside coverage on a lot of things. That happened on the first day, also. So, that's something that again, you know, I go up to him, he come to me, he tells me different things and then, you know, when we get them on the opposite side, you know, he comes to me and asks me what I'm looking at. So, it's been really good to learn from from each other and compete. >> Deshaun, how much the GoPro cameras, how are those used in meetings? What are you getting out of the GoPro cameras? >> The biggest thing with the GoPros is just being able to see where our eyes are. First off, you know, in the huddle, being able to call the plays, you know, see who we're looking at and then once we get up there seeing our eye progression. Whenever the ball snaps and where our eyes going, looking at the defense and uh it's a good point of view, a different point of view for us to be able to, you know, learn and study. >> Deshaun, how much of getting back to form and playing at the level you want to is you know, kind of getting up back to the speed of the game? Is that something that you think you're still kind of kind of getting acclimated to? >> Uh man, that's going to grow. I think you I think I can't remember who mentioned it, but that's when the pass come on and things kind of really get, you know, bullets are really flying. Um, but the biggest thing for me is just let my instincts take over. So, uh not doing that uh not doing anything extra and not doing anything less, just kind of just staying balanced and letting it come. So, day to day it's getting better um and you know, honestly I I think the biggest thing is just playing football. So, whenever the preseason games come up and we're out there playing, I think that's where we can learn and just each game is just an opportunity to get better at it. >> Is Deshaun Deshaun, just kind of off of that, how important is the how how much are you kind of looking forward to getting to play some preseason snaps, whether it's, you know, all three games, two, what what whatever that that, you know, coach Monken decides to do? >> Uh I'm I'm looking forward to it. Uh I haven't played football in a long time. So, for me uh it doesn't matter how long I play, how many games I play, I just want to play football. Uh you know, a lot of people wrote me off and said that I wouldn't be playing football again after two ACL uh two Achilles injuries. So, uh you know, I'm proving everyone and proving myself, right? So, uh it's a great opportunity for me to get out there and showcase what I can do. >> Coach Monken has talked about now that you're healthy, your athletic ability, your mobility and all that and he's going to utilize that a lot not a lot, more designed runs. What do you feel about that part of the the offense that you're stepping into? >> Uh I'm comfortable with it. Um you know, we had short talks about that, but um and again, I think he he knows he came from a a guy in the Mar who won two MVPs and uses legs as much as he's throwing and he know I think he knows how to call the right right plays at the right time for the quarterback to be able to use his feet. So, I'm going to trust him and the coaching staff and whenever those plays called just try to execute. >> Do you have a time in mind when you're hoping that coach makes a decision on the starter? >> I have no idea. I think every day just taking it one day at a time and I think you know the organization and coach is going to make the best decision for you know for the team and we just got to go from there. >> Deshaun, what what would it be like for you if you do come out and play like you did in 2020 to go six years without to come back and play like that. How incredible would that be? >> I mean it'd be awesome. That's that's what I'm playing that's what I'm training for and and working for so that's what's been on my mind the whole time is just playing really really good productive football so we can win a lot of games here and that's the ultimate job. You got to win in this in this business and if you're not winning then they're going to find somebody else but you know that's the ultimate job is to come out play well produce and and win. >> A couple more? >> Yeah, I think Casey and Boston has been doing a heck of a job picking up the offense being able to learn from the other veteran receivers in the room but just making plays and I think just being able to see them come out here and just you know go up for balls make it contested catches has been really good. I think they're going to be very productive and helpful for this offense. >> How does your accuracy feel and the last time you played live football in 2020 you said your arm wasn't completely 100%. >> Right. >> So, how does it feel now? How's the ball coming out? Is it going exactly where you want it to go and how do you feel about that? >> Yeah, I think way it's two years removed from my my shoulder injury, really 3 years, 23. Um, so, you know, coming back in '24, you know, I was only like 7 7 8 months from that injury. Um, wasn't where I was comfortable with it, but, you know, when when, you know, they're investing, you got to play, so you got to perform. Uh, but you can't make that as an excuse. But right now, sitting here talking to you guys, I feel very comfortable, very strong, uh, fluent. You know, now it's just building that trust within the receivers, cuz everyone runs different routes. We have different type of guys, so just been able to talk all that trust and let it rip. I think that's the biggest thing and don't be afraid of it, so. >> We talked to Jimmy yesterday and uh, he was asked about, you know, the potential of you actually coming back next year, and he kind of left the door open saying that anything can happen. Do you kind of view it in that same light that, you know, there is potentially a future here still in Cleveland? >> Oh, for sure. I mean, I think I think, you know, when I first got here, it was just it was a lot of stuff going on, as as the world know. But, uh, I don't have no bad feeling towards Cleveland. I love Cleveland. Me and my wife, we got our house on the East side, so we're here all the time. We were here this summer. Uh, if you ask around, I'm at pretty much all the restaurants. I'm hanging out, so I haven't had a bad experience outside of, you know, just different times in the stadium. But, again, I don't know why that narrative is out there that people thinking that I don't like Cleveland and my family. We've been enjoying it. Uh, we've been enjoying our time here, and yeah, that that if the opportunity shows up, it will we'll see where it goes, but uh, you got >> The last year when you weren't playing, you were still in meeting and and helping Gabriel and Sanders and Mayock here. What does Shurmur look like now? A year after >> Yeah, he's definitely improved. He's he's grown a lot. Uh, you can see within his fundamentals, his reads, uh, being able to execute, call the play, so you can tell he's a lot more comfortable, uh, and that he's been putting in the work to be able to be where he is right now. >> Thank you, guys. >> Thank you. >> Thanks.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference | August 1st, 2026
text: No. All right. Doing fine. I don't think you're really going to know until you get through all the installs because we're not game planning against our defense. Each day has been a different part of the pass game. So, it's hard to really and one day you go with the ones, the other day you go with the twos. Certainly, that match-up's going to be different in terms of who you're going against. So, I think the most important thing is from a process standpoint, how are we operating at the line of scrimmage? Where are their eyes? Have they taken command of won the huddle and then teams and then uh you know, understanding the concepts. So, I think they're all doing good. I mean, they're all fine. I mean, all of our players are working through mistakes and uh fighting like hell to get better. Oh, no. We got eight. Today's day four. We'll go through next Thursday for our main installs. We'll go through eight installs. So, we got Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. Gap scheme's going Monday uh for a reason. That's first day of pads. So, the other days, the first three days when you're in shells and and helmets, you really want to stay in wide zone and tight zone uh rather than getting in the gap schemes. So, next week we'll get much more in the gap schemes. Well, it all depends on how you look at six practices in a row. I think after you get through the six practices, you'll look at well, was day three, you know, the same time? Were they in full pads? You know, obviously, next Friday is not going to be we're going to be in helmets, right? So, it's 6 days in a row, but the players get 1 day off a week. So, you can either spot it or you can just say we're just going to make it every Sunday. Right? They want to go to church, they want to spend it with their family. Uh they get Sunday, it's consistent. We did the same thing for family days, you know, here in the organization. Every Monday's family day. You just try to make it consistent. What is that What does that do? It makes one long week. But, let's say we'd had the day off on Thursday or Friday next week. Well, then when do you give them the next day off? Right? It's like you it's just a planning part of it. So, we don't intend on going six straight days of contact, hitting. First, you can't, okay? Or the the length. first of all, all four highly intelligent and want to be perfect. >> [snorts] >> And they want to get us in the right player protection. And at times, but at times, they can try to be too perfect. And it's just Okay. You're creating anxiety at the line of scrimmage. We got to get up, get down, run the play, right? Learn from our mistakes, and then we can take it from there. But, all of them are trying to to do it right, get us in in the right play, and I've been I've been really impressed. Yesterday was our best day in terms of that. Certain things not as good, but yesterday there was a number of quarterback controlled situations that they were exceptional at. >> How many orders do you see these guys out here? >> Tomorrow has to be Monday has to be 90 minutes mandated by the league. So it'll be padded day and 90 minutes. These early practices are mandated in terms of when you get through the first six are mandated in terms of the amount of time. It ramps up from 90 to 105 to 120 and then works back down as you work your way back up. And then after that hell, if you want to go 2 and 1/2 hours you can. We're not going to do that. There'll be some days we will, but it is allowed. >> Ty, yesterday I know you talked about Deshaun's picks in the earlier practice, but what did you see on that throw that Quincy picked off? >> Well, similar in the fact that we were in a slot formation without an open one and we had talked earlier about that specific individual route and how you have to be careful of all the traffic that could be in there. And what was really cool about it is that we had talked about it earlier in the day. And I'll be damned if he didn't go in there and there was traffic in there and he threw it. We got an interception. So to me that was really cool. Not at the moment it wasn't really cool, but uh looking at it now it's really cool that it was able to back up what we had talked about that he has to be careful >> [clears throat] >> in terms of that route and the spacing that's not created when we're going to go to that. >> Ty >> I'm interested in this topic of cadences that we talked about last week. You said you wanted 10 eventually in a game. Are they numbers or quarterbacks says cadence five in the huddle or or how how are they identified? >> Oh, it's in the huddle. We'll tell him. I mean, we rarely do we just say call whatever the hell you want. I'm not saying that's what you're asking. I'm just saying and they'll understand when and where we're thinking of certain cadences. So it's all part of and we're going to have wristbands. It's on the wristband. Tell them what to be. You You but only the quarterback sees that then he communicates that in the huddle. But there's so much more to it. You get to line of scrimmage, there's communication, there's talk, there's blocking assignments. It's easy to just kind of not stay dialed into what the cadences are. It's why you got to continue to fight to work it every day. >> Was it better yesterday? >> It was better yesterday. Not on defense. I think we had uh I think we had 14 penalties yesterday, which is not ideal. 12 total that were pre-snap. Offense had four, defense had eight. >> I'm waiting >> So, not not ideal, but again, um some of that's the cost of doing business. If you want to be in a textile front, you want to crowd the line of scrimmage, you're going to have a few of those. But now's the time to work it, right, and get better at it. >> I want to ask you about the different person about Deion and Shedeur in the meetings. We see them with such different personalities. So, how are they like in meetings? >> Well, they they do have different personalities, as Dylan does. They're every every human being's unique, right? Everybody else's taken. So, they they definitely have different personalities. Um but both are very sharp. Obviously, Deion, based on his experience, right, in the NFL, is going to have a little bit better grasp, right, of what's being asked of him. Just from an operational standpoint, from a cadence standpoint, from a offensive system standpoint. Cuz there's still going to be some similarities from system to system, right? Changing plays, right? Cadence, right? There's It's called one thing here and another. Well, Shedeur is just at the early stages of that. Dylan's been in three different programs. And then now been in his fifth offense, so he's probably got a little bit more experience at at that. Uh so, again, every player works at a different speed or pace. It's our job to, by the time they play, to really get them up to up to speed where they can play at a high level. Um where they can play fast. And that's that's the part of the system. >> Kind of kind of kind of a two-part question. Have you given any thought to letting, you know, each quarterback get consecutive days running the ones to see if they get in a little bit of a rhythm? And then, are the twos like when when you put up the second and the third team unit, is the defense running kind of more of a vanilla defense? Are they running the exact same stuff as the starting team? >> Well, they're installing. Every The scripts are the same. So, from field to field, allows us to communicate that. So, you're getting the exact same I mean, look, other than the personnel may be different on both sides of the ball. It's going to have that. Um we have not really gone back-to-back with the ones. Doesn't mean you can't. Whether you went 2 days with Deshaun and and then he went 2 days the other way, you could say, they get in a rhythm, but then you put them with the twos for 2 days, and that could break the rhythm. I mean, we we've just made the decision to go every other day just to try as best we can, uh to give each quarterback an opportunity with the ones. Is it going to be ideal? No. Right? Cuz you're installing. So, and you're going to get some ones and twos. But, ultimately, whichever way you decide to divide the reps, even if it was in practice within the practice, isn't always ideal. >> So, Gabriel and Taylor are getting many more reps than they did in the spring season. Is that cuz you have more practice time, or did you guys amp it up? >> Well, we have we have more practice time. We have more reps. And it's not even, uh maybe, you know, we didn't get other than mini camps, we didn't get a walk. So, they actually get We two-spot our walk. You guys aren't here. So, they get We get 35 reps in our walk, so they each get full reps. And we're going two-spot, so they'll get more reps there. When we two-spot on the field, which we were able to do cuz we have more bodies. We had some guys not here. We had more guys banged up. It allowed us to go two-spot. That's the point of trying to go two-spot to get many reps as you can, uh not equally, but as many reps as we can. >> Cover more? >> And we got And what other What else? I just thought of it. What happened yesterday was when the other field, say with Dylan, the other field was a little bit behind, that gave us a chance to get, okay, let's let's go out place Dylan, go back up there, go back up with your group. Let's get as many as we can get, right? Uh especially for the quarterbacks. It's not always ideal, that's the hard part, is to get all those reps with the quarterbacks is hard because it taxes everybody else. Quarterbacks are never taxed, besides maybe their shoulder. Outside of that, they're not They're not staggering up the line of scrimmage after 20 straight plays. So, that's the hard part. How do you balance your players' reps and and trying to get your quarterbacks' reps? >> I kind of do Deshaun kind of talked about in practice it's sometimes the best time to take some chances and try to Do you mention squeezing the ball in certain areas and test it out, if you will? And there are certain sessions that are maybe better for that than others. Just how do you communicate things to them, like when those opportunities present themselves, and then how do you kind of evaluate them as you go through this whole process, knowing like sometimes they were just trying something, sometimes it's not You don't want interceptions ever, but how do you kind of balance that? >> Right, it's it's a combination of all that. It's great question, by the way, cuz it's it's Now is the time to push the envelope in a lot of ways to see where they're at. Certainly don't want the interceptions. And too many of them are beyond a teaching tool, right? Like at some point you're like, okay, I'm beyond I'm beyond being taught here. Okay, stop throwing the ball to the other freaking side. All right, but it is part of uh the process of just working through it. And interceptions are part of the game, unfortunately, but again, did you learn from that? That we'll find out as we keep moving on, right? Uh that we're not Are we making the same mistakes? Are we learning from that and moving on cuz we're never too old to learn. I get a kick when people say, "Well, you're this far along." Hell, I'm 60. I'm I'm not done learning. I don't That never ends of learning and getting better. >> Chris got one here. Todd, coming kind of off of that, you know, how much do you kind of percentage-wise is it the what you, you know, you see on the film you know, the mental side of the processing everything when you're comparing the two? Are you looking judging what you see on the film, you know, kind of what they're doing process-wise compared to the physical side of that? >> Oh, yeah, that's part of it. Like there's a mental aspect of the operation and uh Does it look like you want it to look like? Just start before the snap. >> Mhm. >> Right? Does it look like That's why we do perfect operation. How's it look before the snap? And then there's the physical um part of it. Now, at this point when you're installing, when I'm scripting, I really I'm not scripting based on who's a quarterback. They each have a different skill set. So, as of right now, I'm not evaluating any of them. I I'm not making a decision on any of them till we get through all the installs and we get to where okay, the practices are the same, we're scripting it based on who's taking the reps. That's part of it. And we're playing the preseason games and we're um or we're going against the Bills. I'll take I'll take that back. We are evaluating, but not to that extreme. Nothing's going to be decided over these install practices. We're just getting it in, letting the guys compete, see see where we're at. That's all positions. And then once we get further along in pads, the full installs are in, we get to compete against other people, that's really when I'm going to be able to see it cuz I have I haven't coached any of the four quarterbacks till now. I have not been around them. I don't have any preconceived notions of who they've been or where they're going. I just take it day-to-day. We install and as we get further along, we'll have a better idea. >> Good. >> Thank you. See you. >> Have a good day off. >> I don't know where my mic is.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'Tucker just wants to go put in the work'
text: You got anybody coming back today from the [snorts] >> We do. Kamal Haden, >> you were uh really complimentary of him toward the end of last year about how he had grown. Um just what have you seen from his development since he joined during Final Cuts in 24? I think >> where he is now. >> Yeah. So, that's always a really cool thing to see and I think it's really impacted his ability to go out and play. >> They have some question after that injury. It was pretty gruesome, but you know, he could even come back from that or do you think did they feel like there was good chance there? >> Um, yeah, I know it was a gruesome deal. uh any anybody that's coming off a pretty significant injury, I think there's always a little bit of a you know unknown too, but if you attack it the right way, which he has, uh I think we feel confident that he'll be able to return to form. >> Matt, what does that mean? He was challenged. >> He was challenged. We challenge everybody, but like specifically I mean um you know I I hit him directly with a few challenges and and he answered them and so he's he's been great. >> So like he's a pretty fun-loving effervescent personality guy. Was it more about just making sure he was focused and and knew what his opportunity was or >> I think all Yeah, all of that. With Ganon's new defense, is there value for the offense this time of the year seeing new looks or am I >> Oh, absolutely. There's there's been some some uh exotic looks in practice. Um and it's I mean we're going to see some of that early on in the season. >> Speaking of that, Matt, the very first play team, I think Jordan's booting out the way to the right and he's got a corner right in his face. They they he had a good play versus the play the offense had for sure. >> Some of the guys on your offensive staff now you've worked with longer than any time in your career. Talk about Adam Stenovich as your offensive coordinator. What does he do that complements what you need? >> Well, I I think first of all, I think he's he's a really intelligent football coach. Um, I mean, he's the designer behind our run game, but where you've where I've seen the most growth from him is just in the passing game, like he's I mean, he's making corrections out there on the field like that. I'm I'm like, you notice it every day that you don't always see from guys that have a background that he's had in terms of the offensive line room. So, he's worked extremely hard at it and he I think he's got total command of everything we're trying to do from the run game to the pass game to obviously pass protection. Um, and then even in the quarterback room, I mean, just the growth that I've seen, he spends a lot of time in our QB room and um, just the detail and fundamental of that position. >> Monday, >> you got your wish. So you guys can just mark it either whether it's good or not. >> How did Tucker handle that first day of practice feedback? >> I think he did a great job. I mean, not it wasn't shocking to me. Um but yeah, I think he handled everything great. >> Tucker said that he set a personal goal of being back for the joint practice with the Cardinals. Is that realistic from the team's point of view? >> Yeah, I I would say so, but I mean, he's he's got to hit all the benchmarks along the way. And if that's the case, then absolutely. >> What does it say about, you know, Jir Gibbs is not practicing in Detroit until he gets his new deal? What does it tell you about Tucker that he's out there even though he doesn't have what he probably wants? Uh has a family, two kids, and um he just he's a smart guy, and so he's he's picked it up pretty fast. Matt, are you going to have to manage Banks's reps all the way through camp or will there be a point where with his knee he can just go full go? >> I think early on certainly there's going to be a management and then we'll just see how it responds along the way. >> What do you like about deny Dennis Sutton on the interior and what does the process look like for figuring out do we want him inside outside or you know is it something that that versatility kind of shines through? Yeah, I think um you know he's another guy that's definitely flashed throughout the course of the offseason and into the early po portions of camp. I'm just most excited for all those guys to get the pads on to see you know how that's that's real football. So um we put a lot of limits on our rushers in terms of what is allowed. We we don't want any bull rushing in, you know, this portion of camp when you have when you don't have pads on. And so, um, but his versatility has definitely shown up and I think in those known passing situations, you're always trying to get your best rushers out out on the field, whether that's inside, outside and, um, but he he's responded to all that well. >> Matt, is Tyrod Taylor maybe more vocal in meetings than your typical backup? And how much has he seen in this league that Jordan hasn't seen yet? >> No, I think Tyrod picks his spots. I he's a he's a pretty mellow guy, but when he does talk, I mean, it it definitely has a lot of value and he's seen a lot. Uh he's he's you know, knows a lot of ball and different ways to do things. So, it you know, when opportunities present themselves, certainly, you know, you would be dumb not to pick a guy like that, like his brain. >> Where's um where's Valentine at? You know, he he played so well for you as a rookie when you needed him to. you challenged him to bulk up. He did. I'm guessing you probably challenged him on the tackling front this off seasonason. Where is he kind of at right now for you? >> Yeah, I think he's he's done everything that we've asked him to do. And I think he goes out there and he competes at a high level. Uh he's making plays out there. Um and you know, it's just he's got to continue to do that throughout the course when we when we get the pads on, we get into the preseason games and then into the regular season. Coach, you talked about a couple days ago that this is probably the most excited you've been for a team and just every team is different every year. For you, where does that energy come from? Is it the new players? Is it stuff that you want to bring from last year into the new year or writing a new chapter? Where does that energy come from? >> Yeah, I think it's just the overall vibe we have in in the building. And it's not just exclusive to our players. It's our coaching staff, our support staff. I think everybody's on the same page and pulling in the same direction. And um that makes it a hell of a lot more fun to come to work every day. >> Is Bo Melton officially a wide receiver again? >> Yes. >> Any chance that you know in a pinch you would >> Well, I think the the fact that he's got time on task back there like I mean we'd hate to put him in that position but if crap hit the fan and you needed somebody at least he could go function. And do you just feel like he's more comfortable now that he's back at wide receiver? >> Yeah, I do. Yeah, absolutely. >> Yeah. >> Now, what do you think he's capable of if he's playing there on a semi-regular B? I mean, he's had some really good moments for you. What do you think he's capable of if he gets >> Well, he he's got an elite trait. I mean, he can he can take the top off the coverage and then I think he adds so much value and he you know, you're gonna get his best effort on every play. Like he does a lot of dirty work going digging out I mean there was there was a clip of him last year where he was blocking Dre Green Law, you know, downfield and um so digging out a linebacker, safeties, whoever. Um he just there's no challenge too big for him and then the value he brings on teams is pretty significant. >> Two more please. >> Did [clears throat] you not get to go to Smackdown with the other guys the other night? Did you get >> No, I did not. I didn't go to Smackdown. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Nick Niemann 1-on-1: 'Trying to be the best that I can, show what I can do and help the team'
text: Nick, I was wondering, you know, uh the special teams piece. Uh new coordinator. Has it been a big change? Or I mean, how are you looking at that? >> Yeah, I mean, I think anytime you get a new coach, there's going to be some new wrinkles, you know. Cam is he came from, you know, the Bill Belichick tree, which is arguably like kind of the Mecca of special teams. So, really excited to have him around and, you know, he brings a lot of energy. He's out there in cleats running around excited to be out there. Um you know, special teams is simple, but there's also some nuances and new schemes that come in. So, we'll definitely have some of that, but uh just super excited to get to work with, you know, a new guy and try to get this thing going. So. >> Uh Nick, one thing I've noticed is you guys have done a boatload of drills. Talking about special teams periods. A boatload of drills. Uh but not a lot of group things. Is that a little different? >> Yeah, I mean, I wasn't here last year, so I can't speak on that, but I think probably a little bit just comes with, you know, the start of training camp. You don't just want to jump into things without having your technique right and that type of thing. So, definitely, you know, want to start out on the right foot that way, but also, um special teams is a huge just fundamental component, you know, it's it's just about leverage and straining and knowing how to set up your blocks the right way and coverage and that type of thing. So, you got to start with square one and work your way up. So, I think that's where we are right now, but you know, we'll get it going soon. So. >> Now, to me, it's really hard. Uh they're it's like any other offensive play. You run down there and everybody's assigned a guy and stuff. And yet, you have shown the uncanny knack for making tackles. And and so, how how does I mean, what's that knack? Can you describe that knack, how you do that? Cuz that's hard. >> Yeah. >> And it's craziness, but it's hard. >> I mean, I think it's partially, you know, being put in the right positions. Um you know, special teams is a very big matchup situation where you want to be put in good matchups. So, I think between that and just having good good instincts, I guess, and having a good feel for things, just like you can be instinctual by linebacker or other positions. So, I don't know if I have a direct answer for you, but I just go out and and make tackles. So. >> Nick, one other thing for you. Like last year, you were leading the team in special teams tackles by a bunch. And then, okay, you're hurt for an extended time, as I recall. And and I look down and you're still leading the team in special teams tackles. I mean, how do how did you look at that? Did you ever notice that that "Oh, by golly, I still got 12 and the closest guy to me has got eight." Were you >> Yeah, I mean, kind of cool, I guess, but it it just was tough to not be out there. Um I guess the competitor in me, I I want to get the most tackles on the unit. Um I feel like I that's something I can provide to the unit and the team and kind of has been how I found a little bit of a role in this league. So, um just trying to be the best that I can and you know, show what I can do and help the team the best that I can and just tackle. So. >> Nick, uh like this year, uh uh hopes, dreams, aspirations, maybe you just uh mention them all, but your hopes, dreams, aspirations for this year for you. >> Yeah, I think just provide this team the best role that I can, offense or not offense, I've been special teams, just be the best player that I player that I can be in both of those spots and um you know, try to be a leader for the special teams unit. Um try to take us, you know, the right direction, take another step forward in that standpoint of things and um just be the best player that I can be on defense and provide whatever they need me to do and take off running. >> Speaking of the defensive piece, new coordinator there, how's that going for you? Do you think, "Hey, no, this is a good fit." How do you feel about him? >> I really like the defense. I think, you know, everyone's really excited about that and you know, JG brings a special aspect just having been a head coach. I mean, that's huge and you know, the scheme that he runs, he's wicked smart. Um you could sit with him in a meeting for 5 minutes and realize that. Um I think it just excites everybody. He wants to put everyone in the right positions to, you know, be at their best and I think it'll be really exciting to see how this group, you know, takes off running this season.

title: Tucker Kraft: ‘This is one of the greatest training camp atmospheres’
text: Most importantly, like I don't want anyone to get their expectations too high. I'm not going to be doing anything too crazy here for a while, but um you know, as long as um you know, our GM and our training staff and the coaches, everyone's on the same page, I'll just get phased in um period by period until until you guys see me out there taking team reps. So, that's the goal. Um we're on that ramp-up phase right now to to get ready for week one. >> Talk concerning hesitation to go full bore >> Absolutely not. >> without a contract though. >> Um >> You know what I mean? Like cuz there's risk involved in that. Um from the business standpoint, is there any >> Yeah, absolutely. Um I understand other people's worries in that facet. However, I myself um I'm just worried about getting back to who I was pre-injury. Um I had a great meeting this morning with the guys from the Badger Lab, Dr. Hendershot, and he told me, you know, my my knee looks spectacular. Um almost like he had never seen a rehabilitation like mine. So, the fact that we're um getting those results, um the data will speak for itself, and my my comeback is ever ascending day by day. >> Did you only find out this morning that today would be the day to get back out there? >> Well, I mean, we we've been I've been, you know, me, myself, I've been pushing it for since before our first practice, trying to start off not on the pump, but um ultimately, we just had to check a few more boxes and make sure, you know, we got the green light. >> Under 9 months, right? >> Uh I never I never had, you know, 9 months is is just the the data-backed cookie-cutter rehabilitation timeline. if you would ask me if if I was ready a month ago, I would have said yes. But it's just um you know, it's just a testament to how we do business here in this building. Um They want to make sure that their their players, potential investments, everyone is is accountable to their recovery. We got great training staff here and they had my back the last 8 and 1/2 months and even before then with any knick-knack I would have went to the training room with, so we're doing great. >> So, when were you at that place where you tell all of the guys like, "Hey, I'm ready to start getting back on the field and working out?" Like, when did you kind of feel you were at that place you were ready to start to get out there? >> I'd say, yeah, maybe maybe a month ago. I've been here now for the last I mean, since since March um working out and and it came to a point in my recovery where I just had these guardrails up in my rehab and and the trainers were kind of just overseeing me apply more speed, more aggression towards every movement I was doing and um that's led us here. >> Tucker, how how much does your presence and your voice matter to this offense? Not just what you do with the ball in your hands and on the field, but your voice in the huddle in big moments, in money moments, in the fourth quarter. What does it mean to have you >> Yeah, I mean, I I just want to bring the the confidence along to let everyone know that um we're going to be all right as as long as we can control what we can control and we can hold hold ourselves accountable to the standard of, you know, that alone, you know, our attitude and our effort um one play at a time. That's that's always been, you know, you can go back to media sessions I've had since my rookie year. I've always just talked about going one and 0. Being being the best I can be at my position involves me winning my one-on-one match up as consistently as possible. >> Your teammates are really excited to see you out there. What is the support looked like and are there any teammates in particular that have really helped you along the way? >> Um I I'd say teammate in particular was um for sure Christian, you know, us having the same surgeon um him getting injured uh about a month and a half later in the season um but but seeing him bounce back and and you know, kind of laying the path for me essentially in a training room. You know, we just went from from you know, one guy to the next. You know, we we only played one game together. So, one and a half. it was just a testament to his hard work to, you know, I have the confidence to see him coming off his injury and him competing now at a high level making great plays in practice. And uh now now it's my opportunity. >> Hunter, do you want to be the number one paid tight end in the NFL? >> My goal is to be the number one tight end for this team. >> Just we know you have the chemistry with Jordan, but you know, as as you said, the best opportunity for you guys to win a Super Bowl is with you on the field. And is it good to do that now? Obviously, you know, having the the last several months away from the team, but just starting now in training camp to get to that point. Is that just big in terms of progressing us along? >> Yeah. Um getting getting any rep is is valuable. Um whether it's you know, 10, 50, or or 100 from now until we play week one in Minnesota. It's it's all about um banking them and and stacking them and and growing together because you know, ultimately as several people have made aware, we've we really established our our roster and and who we believe the core um core of it is. So, with with that moving forward, it's it's our job to you know, bring all of it fruition. >> How many hours a day is your even if you're not in the locker >> I'm going to I'm going to simulate everything um and and get in it as much of a routine as I can to prepare myself for practices moving forward. I'm going to I'm going to be in the same dress as everyone else all the time cuz I'm back now. Uh uh I mean, I'm going to be I'm going to be a part of practice phase by phase as much as I can moving forward. So, wherever the team is at I am now a part of practice in every facet now. >> How many hours a day is your workout been the last 7 or 8 months? >> Oh, it comes and goes in phases. Early on, it's really just, you know, range of motion um till you can and get that motion back, push the swelling out. Then after that, it's it's stability and and balance. Um I would say it really kicks off when you get around 4 or 5 months. You're you're in here for about 4 to 6 hours. Um and it stays that way until until you get to be about you know, the last month and a half where I'm at now, where I've I'm really transitioned out of the training room. Um and like I'm not someone who I don't need hands on me all the time. I I went to a school with no athletic trainer. Then I went to a a smaller college with, you know, they had two athletic trainers on staff. Um I spent a lot of time with them, but they were also short on time. So, I learned how to do a lot of stuff on my own. So, I have I have a pretty decent training room setup in my own house. I I almost always have. So, um I'm I'm proactive. You guys jumped. >> [laughter] >> I'm proactive individually. Um so, I I get a lot of time I get a lot of time here, but I spend a lot of time at home also cooling myself down, warming myself up. >> So, after 5 or 6 hours, how much pain do you have that afternoon or the next morning that you have to monitor? >> Um I'm I'm fortunate. I I've done thing r- done things right this entire time. I I haven't had to fight through pain or swelling at all during my ACL rehab. >> What have you learned about yourself through this whole process? >> Really just the endurance through resilience. Um I've learned uh uh Rich Bisaccia used to say, you know, every decision you make has an impact on your team. So, when I'm I'm sitting there feeling sorry for myself, drenched in sweat, maybe maybe a little doubtful of my ability at the moment, I I can really just lean into the pain knowing that uh what I have ahead of me is is these 53 guys um really relying on my ability when I return to play. >> Tucker, is this period of time difficult now, you know, being back out there but not being fully back out there? And how badly do you just want to be out there? >> No, I've I've accepted it's all part of the all part of the plan. Goody and I have have talked about how, you know, he's essentially protecting me from myself because I'm all gas like a like a tricycle. I don't come with brakes. um it's it's really just um helping me establish that mindset of of consistency through a slow ramp up and that's it. >> I mean, Tucker, it was a long journey to get to this point. When you put on the jersey and and hyped up the fans, were there emotions running through your mind? >> Oh, of course. Yeah. I and I've I've established so many times that I'm grateful to be in this organization, um especially because of I mean, I've only known this training camp. Um so, I have a bias when I say that I think it's it's one of the greatest training camp atmospheres, especially when we get into family night and so on. So, emotions were there riding the bike down with my jersey on for real, not not just as a a pub spectator, but yeah. >> Tucker, it's obviously full steam ahead to get you ready for week one. Have you told your agent, "Don't even tell me about my contract" or do you want to be involved? >> No, I I'm I'm in I'm as involved as I can possibly be in it. Um every every number, data point, argument, um I'm I'm going to be my own advocate as much as I can because I know what what my abilities are and and what I bring to the table. >> Is that Is that you you talking with Jack or you talking to to me directly? >> I I I'm an omnipotent third party in a sense where >> what that means. >> where I don't neither neither talk to me. They talk to each other and my agent reports back to me. >> Does that make it emotional this process by wanting to be a part of it, wanting to be your own advocate? >> Um no, I I don't take anything personal. I play football and front office plays numbers. That's That's the way I see it and and I've been reassured of that so many times that I I feel like I can't take anything personal, so. >> Have you been bad or you not happy with this? >> I've said I've alluded to something like that in the past, too. Um people talk about things like that, but they're not me. I've I've had a great experience so far and I'm going to continue to push and and be the best I can be. >> Todd, was there any intention to get a preseason deal or preseason games or just week one? >> I do not see that happening. maybe potentially you know, what I would like to do it's not even cleared um or anything like that. So, it also might not even happen, but being part of a joint practice um because that would be the closest thing I would get to stepping on the football field before the football field, so. That's might not happen, still in the works, but >> Would that just be a comfort thing? >> Yeah, yeah, it's just it's just it's just learning how to play competitive again cuz there's you know, I would say like I'm 98% back. It's that that 2% again is me getting ripped on my face from a D end or taking on contact playing a little bit more full back and you know, getting getting back to the the catch transition again and and everything like that. You can't you can't simulate that stuff when you know, you're constantly playing against your own teammates. So.
