Um, but yeah, I think he handled everything great. >> Said that he set a personal goal of being back for the joint practice with the Cardinals. Is that realistic from the team's point of view? Yeah, I I would say so, but I mean, he's he's got to hit all the benchmarks along the way, and if that's the case, then absolutely. >> What does it say about, you know, Jir Gibbs is not practicing in Detroit until he gets his new deal? [clears throat] What does it tell you about Tucker that he's out there even though he doesn't have what he probably wants? Yeah, I mean it's just I think a lot of these things are are out of the players control and I think Tuck just wants to go put in the work and that's the guy that we we drafted and um but yeah, I think that's big time of him. >> St. Juice obviously didn't practice during the offseason, had a big play the other day. What have you three days into it, but what are your early impressions of what might be able to provide for you guys? Yeah, I think he's a he's a an intriguing guy for sure. I mean, we've gone against him in the past uh when he was in Washington, but you just don't see many corners that look like him. And he's just I've been super impressed with the person the day he came in here. You can tell he's a really mature guy. Uh has a family, two kids, and um he just he's a smart guy, and so he's he's picked it up pretty fast. Matt, are you going to have to manage Banks's reps all the way through camp or will there be a point where with his knee he can just go full go? >> I think early on certainly there's going to be a management and then we'll just see how it responds along the way. >> What do you like about tonight Dennis Sutton on the interior and what does the process look like for figuring out do we want him inside outside or you know is it something that that versatility kind of shines through? Yeah, I think um you know he's another guy that's definitely flashed throughout the course of the off season and into the early po portions of camp. I'm just most excited for all those guys to get the pads on to see you know how that's that's real football. So um we put a lot of limits on our rushers in terms of what is allowed. We we don't want any bull rushing in, you know, this portion of camp when you have when you don't have pads on. And so, um, but his versatility has definitely shown up. And I think in those known passing situations, you're always trying to get your best rushers out out on the field, whether that's inside, outside, and, um, but he he's responded to all that. Well, >> is Tyrod Taylor maybe more vocal in meetings than your typical backup? And how much has he seen in this league that Jordan hasn't seen yet? >> No, I think Tyrod picks his spots. He's a he's a pretty mellow guy, but when he does talk, I mean, it it definitely has a lot of value and he's seen a lot. Uh he's he's you know, knows a lot of ball and different ways to do things. So, it you know, when opportunities present themselves, certainly, you know, you would be dumb not to pick a guy like that like his brain. >> Where's um where's Valentine at? You know, he he played so well for you as a rookie when you needed him to. you challenged him to bulk up. He did. I'm guessing you probably challenged him on the tackling front this off season. Where is he kind of at right now? >> Yeah, I think he's he's done everything that we've asked him to do. And I think he goes out there and he competes at a high level. Uh he's making plays out there. Um and you know, it's just he's got to continue to do that throughout the course when we when we get the pads on, we get into the preseason games and then into the regular season. Coach, you talked about a couple days ago that this is probably the most excited you've been for a team and just every team is different every year. For you, where does that energy come from? Is it the new players? Is it stuff that you want to bring from last year into the new year or writing a new chapter? Where does that energy come from? >> Yeah, I think it's just the overall vibe we have in in the building. And it's not just exclusive to our players, it's our coaching staff, our support staff. I think everybody's on the same page and pulling in the same direction. And um that makes it a hell of a lot more fun to come to work every day. >> Is Bo Melton officially a wide receiver again? >> Yes. >> Any chance that you know again? >> Well, I think the the fact that he's got time on task back there like I mean we'd hate to put him in that position but if crap hit the fan and he needed somebody at least he could go function. And do you just feel like he's more comfortable now that he's back at wide receiver? >> Yeah, I do. Yeah, absolutely. >> Yeah. >> Now, what do you think he's capable of if he's playing there on a semi-regular B? I mean, he's had some really good moments for you. What do you think he's capable of if he >> Well, he he's got an elite trait. I mean, he can he can take the top off the coverage and then I think he adds so much value and he you know you're gonna get his best effort on every play like he does a lot of dirty work going digging out I mean there was there was a clip of him last year where he was blocking Dre Green Law you know downfield and um so digging out a linebacker safeties whoever um he just there's no challenge too big for him and then the value he brings on teams is pretty significant. >> Please, >> did you not get to go to Smackdown with the other guys the other night? Did you get >> No, I did not. I didn't go to Smackdown. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: Hey, hey, hey. Hey, hey, hey. Hey. Hey. Hey. hey, hey. Hey, hey, I don't Heat. Heat. hey, hey. Hey, N Hey. Good morning. >> Your son was trying to be one of us in the locker room yesterday. Are you raising him to be one of us? >> What What was he doing in the locker room? >> Ask some questions and taking video. >> Um, yeah. I did not know that. [laughter] I'm glad I do know that so I can address that. >> He did a good job. >> Did he? What did he ask? Um, he he did ask >> Well, that's that's not a high bar, though. >> I know. >> He did ask for your batting rating as a coach. >> Okay. >> We got 99. >> All right. >> He was asking guys if you guys should run the ball more. >> Yeah. Do you want us to run the ball more? >> No, sir. >> You let Jordan love cook this? >> Yeah, we're going to let him cook. >> Matt, he did say he wanted to be one of us. He probably want to talk him out of there, right? >> Hey, whatever he wants to do, he can do. He better he better go at it hard, Um, Keshan was saying yesterday that he likes how you have them practicing because you're not being as brutal as in years past and you're taking care of them. Is that a concerted effort or is that just an observation? >> I didn't know we were taking care of them. I mean, it's been pretty much the same rep count we've had. Um, I will say this, I think our guys are doing a much better job of just our our procedure. So, we're getting the same amount of work done in a much smaller amount of time. So, I think there's I mean, you always want to be efficient, but I think that's more credit to our players. We're trying to get the calls in a little bit quicker. Um, but they're transitioning and ultimately it's on them. So, we have had to scale back a little bit of the the rep count just because of the number of guys that we've had out early in camp, but hopefully we can build upon that as as these guys progress back into practice. >> Mentioning the plays getting in quicker. Is that or was that in any way part of your kind of breaking down of the offense then kind of trying to build back up something along the lines of getting a better tempo as far as the operation goes? Yeah, I think that was a definitely a point of emphasis this off season just trying to get in and out of the huddle a little bit quicker. Um, you know, I think anytime an offense approaches the line of scrimmage, the faster they approach the line of scrimmage, the more pressure it puts on a defense. So, um, yeah, that that was a big point of emphasis. >> Will we finally see some live field goals today? >> No. >> When might that happen? most likely on uh what is it? Sunday. >> Is Adren Cooper okay? >> Yeah, it's just it's standard training camp nicks and bruises and um you know, we'll we'll warm him up, see how he feels. If he's feeling good, he'll be out there. If not, we'll we're going to be we'll be cautious with a guy like him. Matt, on Baldwin's interception, which looked like a great kind of break on the ball, great play on defense, but was there a miscommunication between the quarterback and the receiver? It looked like the receiver was looking for it. >> Yeah, he's I I would say that he's got to get his eyes back and and a worst case scenario, break that ball up. Um they were our defense was playing a single high. We were running a double move. Uh we'd like to get a little bit more width on that, but um there was certainly a an opening in there. It's just we we got to go attack that football. But that was a hell of a play by Jonno. >> Now, when you look at a play like that or Marlon Brown's pick the day before, those are guys that are obviously trying to make an impression and make a threeman roster. What is that? You got a lot more work to do obviously, but what does play like that do for those type of guys? >> Well, I think it gives them a lot of confidence and ultimately, you know, if if you're more confident when you're out there, you're probably going to play a lot better. So, I'm excited about all those guys, especially the guys that haven't had a ton of exposure as just as we progress throughout camp and then into those preseason games just to get a great evaluation on them. >> I know the pads aren't on, but what have you seen from Belton throughout the offseason as he's gotten more snaps at guard? Yeah, I I think there's been a lot of great moments and then there's certainly some things like most players that you got to clean up and he's a young guy so I would expect him to just the more reps he gets the better he he will be. >> Matt, your takeaways the last three years defensively have gone 18 then 31 then 14. And when you break that down, is is there a rhyme or reason maybe for that fluctuation? Yeah, I mean I think that's this one of the secret sauces that everybody's trying to figure out h how do you get the ball back? Certainly it's been a point of emphasis and I feel like last year we emphasized it as much if not more than any other year and it just they didn't come. So um you know I think some of it is just in order to get the ball back at times you might have to be a little bit more aggressive defensively. I think when you look at some of the teams that are able to take the ball away, uh, you see that. So, um, but, you know, there's there's a lot of variables that go into being able to get the ball away. >> Just saw Tucker Craft biking with his helmet. Is he off the PUP list today? >> I have. Has that been confirmed? Okay. Sorry, I was in meeting so I was waiting on that one. Um, but yes, thank you, Jason. Good assist. Where's Haden at with his recovery from injury? >> I think he's close. I would say he's close. He he certainly looked really fast on Marlin's interception as he was streaking down the sideline. So, I we made a joke of that in the team meeting as as I showed that one. I was like, "Hey, Kamal, you look look pretty good." He said he's ready to go, but um ultimately it's that's a medical decision. Uh Matt, going back to uh Eagle Eye Andy, noticing that in the photo, what is your plan then now that he's going to be out there? What approach are you going to take with Tucker? >> Uh it'll it'll just be it'll be no team. So, we're just going to kind of, you know, get him back ingrained into the process and and into individual. What's great is when they do come off pup then he now he can partake in some of the walkthrough periods um especially that we do in the evenings. So just to get them back hearing the call lining up and then just going through that. >> Is there a long-term concern on Jerber? >> No long-term concern. >> Have you got any further information on Luke in terms of long-term concerns? No, I think that's I think that will work itself out, but it's going to be it's not going to be in the short term. >> Is there a plan for getting Wyatt and Tom, some of those long-term entry guys into team stuff? >> Yeah, but again, I think that's going to be down the road a little bit. So, whether it's it's next week or after family night, I I think remains to be seen. >> What's your plan for tomorrow without practice? What what do you do? What's your day like? Well, tomorrow's a a good opportunity for us as a staff just to kind of get ahead. So, we'll we'll make sure we have a plan for for the next three practices before we have another off day. Um, and then there's always some projects that we're doing trying to look ahead for things that are upcoming in the future. >> Sunday, Sunday full pads or is that go kind of go in between the go full pads on Monday? >> Trying to think what day is today? Friday. No, Monday will be the first full padded practice. So it's the fifth >> Do they allow shells on or is that just >> It's Yeah. So the You mean those spider pads that we wear? Yeah. So they'll be out there in those today. So the guys will look a little bit bigger. >> All right, guys. Thanks.

title: Grant Udinski & Jakobi Meyers on Year 2 Offense, WR Depth | Press Conference | Jacksonville Jaguars
text: There we go. >> Travis had the deep reception. Just kind of what have you seen out of him for these first four days and kind of how is he looking back on the field? >> The deep reception was awesome to see. It's great getting him back out there with the guys. He has such an infectious energy that it affects not just the receivers, probably the offensive line coaches and everybody out there. He's continued to progress from a route, technique, fundamental standpoint, but also a knowledge of the offense and just the system in general. So, it's exciting to see and that development will hopefully continue. What does he add when he's right and out there to what you want to get? >> There's so much that he adds. And I think it starts with, like I said, the energy and his play style and what he brings to the huddle, which you don't always see on the field. It's probably a little bit more apparent that when he has the ball in his hands, he can create something special. He can make guys miss. He has a great awareness of defenders and space out there on the field, but he also has great ball skills. So, those things kind of pop off the tape. But the other elements of it with the details that he, you know, tries to execute is run assignments, alignments, splits, those stuff don't always show up on tape, but those are impactful really for the entire offense. >> The offense has kind of been established after a year together. Does it make it easier to kind of picture where you see him fitting into things on offense? >> Certainly. I think not just for him. I think for everybody, we have a little bit clearer picture of who they are and who we want to be and how we as coaches can help bring the best out of them. As you get a bigger and bigger sample size, that becomes easier. That's one of the challenges of year one where you don't necessarily know where guys fit within our system. And really on us as coaches, it's more about adapting our system to them. So the more reps we get together and the more communication we have about how they see things, how they see defense is, how they like to approach this route or how they like to maybe approach a certain look allows us to build things around them and hopefully the quarterbacks, wide receivers, offensive line all feel more comfortable, which accelerates their growth and play. um when you have continuity a quarterback play caller coordinator. Does that allow you to experiment more knowing you have your greatest hits in your pocket or do you want to make those greatest hits even greater? >> That's a great question. It's always a tough challenge especially going into the off season when you're re-evaluating what were we good at and what could we be good at. And I think ultimately you try to strike that balance of not throwing out the good just to bring in some new experimentation, but we're always going to try to continue to evolve. So in some areas it might be something small like technique. We may change one technique of the offensive line or a footwork. But in some areas it might be a totally different scheme or totally different way of running a scheme we ran previously. So we have our fair share excuse me our fair share of experimentation that we'll work through throughout training camp. It might not all be at once but through the offseason we have a plan that we work through all these different ideas and things that we want to work towards. But we're ultimately want to balance that back and have that foundation to still rely on regardless of where we go or where that evolution ends up. >> Williams on Wednesday that trying to put Nate, put Tanner in uncomfortable situations, give them a lot of reps early. What have you seen from them early returns through four practices? >> The exciting thing is seeing how those guys embrace those challenges cuz they both really attack it head on. And it's not easy to go out there and be a rookie and operate whether you're in an circumstance that's set up for success or a circumstance that's set up for a challenging block or a challenging route or challenging look. But regardless of what those guys have been throw have had thrown at them, they've attacked it with full effort, full intensity. And whether it's success or failure, they've come back and grown from it and had the right attitude, continue to try to learn from things and get better every single day. So that that's what's exciting about seeing those guys in those challenging situations is just the way they handle it and they love their teammates out there when they do it. They're not blaming others. They're taking accountability. So to see those things from young guys is really exciting. >> I know the hunt depicted it. I know we asked you about Nate, but in terms of Tanner, kind of his origin story, where you maybe first saw him, where he is now compared to where you thought he would be on August 2nd. >> That's a great question. I try to stay out of the predictions and saying a guy's going to be at this certain spot at this certain time because it's a little bit outside of our control and ultimately it's not going to do anything but get us in trouble. But I think where we saw what we saw on tape from him was the ball skills and some of the toughness and the growth. Another guy that got better year over year over year. And even for our short time with him here in the spring, you see a guy from when he showed up and at his first individual drills in rookie mini camp to where he is now. There's improvements really in every facet of his game. Now, it might not be obviously apparent, but there are little things with how his stance is, how he's approaching blocks, his understanding of what we're trying to attack in the different run schemes. So, his growth from a tight end who might have been using certain ways when he was at Ball State or even, you know, in high school that his experience is totally unique. He's really grown to try to understand the full offense and be able to fit that role as a complete tight end, which is encouraging. to bring that one. >> Is it eye opening how what Parker has done since you guys have arrived? Is it Do you end up back in the office every day like, "Hey, you just did it again. Another play. Another I it seems like he makes a play. >> It's like every 10 minutes. >> It I think that's just about right. It's every 10 minutes." I I don't want to say it's not eye opening, but that's who Parker is. So, it's almost as if us the coaches and players who have been around him know that that's what Parker's made of. So, it's maybe not a surprise to us. I certainly don't want to take it for granted that we have a player of that capacity, but when he goes out there and the ball's in the air, I have the utmost confidence that he's going to come down with it. So, it's never a surprise when he's going up there making those acrobatic catches, unbelievable body control, unbelievable ability to track the ball, strong hand, strong at the point of attack. So, all those things are so consistently showing up that, like I said, you're smiling, you appreciate it, but and you don't take it for granted, but it's not a surprise. >> To bring back one of our favorite questions from last year, we've seen Anton on the left side of the offensive line. And I know Cole was rehabbing and all of the things, but just kind of what have you seen out of him? >> Yeah, you said it. One of our favorite questions last year. Unfortunately, I'm going to give you the same answer as last year. We We're going to continue to mix and match guys and try to find the best five. We know that it's very rare for the same five offensive line to start at the same exact position for every single play for an entire season. For whatever reason that may be, we're really fortunate to have guys like Anton who are flexible, who can play left and right. We've had other guys that practice play left right. We've had guys play tackle and guard. That is one of those things that we talk about not taking Park for granted. I certainly don't take that for granted. The depth that we have at the O line position, not just Anton, but across the board. Their flexibility and their willingness to go in there and change positions cuz that's not an easy thing to do. You learn all those body patterns and those movement patterns at left tackle or right tackle and you learn the calls and you learn the looks on what that looks like and then one day later you're going out there and you're changing everything that you got to do and oh by the way, you're doing it against Trayvon Walker and Josh Ein. That's no easy task. So, it's a it's an absolute blessing for us as coaches to have guys like that. >> And with the offensive line going tomorrow, so what are you going to be evaluating as you guys go into kind of that next phase? >> That's an interesting question because you certainly ramp up the intensity and physicality a little bit when you put the pads on, but it doesn't necessarily change what we're evaluating because we're still evaluating physicality and we're still evaluating hand placement and striking and footwork and all of those details whether we have pads on or don't have pads on. Everything we do, whether it's in a live rep on a team setting or it's a walkthrough, we're building habits on the football field. So, we're evaluating the all the same criteria. The way it looks is just a little bit different. >> Jacobe needed a lot of last year. Uh, but do you see him benefiting from knowing the scheme more? >> I think so. It was really impressive to see him come in last year and pick up the system and his role as quickly as he did. And I think a lot of people noticed the chemistry that him and Trevor had pretty instantaneously. So, it's nice now to be able to work on some of those finer details and get into some of the depth of the offense now that he doesn't have to just try to figure out where to line up because he's showing up and having to play a game four days later and then learn a brand new game plan and play a game six days later. So, I think that benefits him, that benefits the quarterbacks, that benefits everybody when they already know what they're doing and now they can spend more time focusing on how to do it. What makes you a good option on third guy last year this year as well and maybe a twoinut? >> You probably start with the toughness and physicality. I think that pops out on tape. His willingness to handle the protection system mentally and you combine that with his ability to block linebackers. He would try to block a defensive end one-on-one all day if you let him. And that's the type of guy is. So, we love that having him out there. And then you add the route ability. You probably saw a little bit more of that in college where we didn't maybe get the most out of it last year, but certainly something we're going to continue to evolve and develop with him. So, you have that combination of a back who can be playing at a high level in protection and playing at a high level as a pass catcher. That's a great option on third down. >> Oh, great. Great. That's an understatement. >> He brings an element. I think Liam's made the point of staying on schedule and keeping our kind of setting that that tempo of our offense with the run game specifically. I think the balance that he has in the run game and the vision and the ability to have strong runs and take two yard runs and make them into five yard runs. Those may not seem like a big deal, but it's such a big difference being able to play on schedule and stay on schedule. You look at the success of our offense on schedule versus off schedule and really it's the same across the league. It is drastically different. So those abilities to find those creases, understand how defenses are going to play out, flow over the top, flow underneath, different backers, different fronts, and even just really that run style with great balance and strength at the point of attack and at the point of contact. It it adds a lot for the offensive line, but it adds a lot for the play call for Liam as well. >> Was that question about Rodriguez? >> It was about Rodriguez. Sorry. >> I'm good. CJ Williams and Josh Cameron. Those are young guys that have flashed a lot. What have you seen out of them through the early days of camp? >> Really, that they're very similar to the guys we saw on TA. They're tough, smart, competitive guys that work really hard. >> They're in here early, they're in here late. They're great to be around. The guys love being around. They play tough. They play hard. All the cliches, I I hate to say it, but all the cliches that you want as a coach and a player, they've brought that and more every single day. So, you love to see that and then you love to see the consistency on top of it. So, when you see them make plays, just like I talk about Parker, it's not a surprise. I don't want to take it for granted, but it's not a surprise because you see the amount of work they put in. >> Thank you. >> Appreciate you guys. >> You came in last year and you looked like you already knew the offense, but how much further ahead are you now with an offse? >> No, I definitely didn't. I'm not going to lie. I was I told somebody the other day, I was just copy and pasting. Like, they gave me the answers, I put them down, >> and that's what it was. But now I understand why they call certain plays, what they looking for with certain plays. And that that helped me with my routes a lot because I can get to the right spot at the right time. And I think that's ultimately what Trevor need out of us. >> Not as much thinking. >> Not as much thinking and playing football and thinking is tough. You know what I mean? So >> when you got here last year, Travis, you know, just got hurt. What's it been like kind of getting to know him and what are your impressions just seeing him out here first couple days? >> I just like watching him play. I've been watching him for a long I feel like everybody been watching him. He like the country son, you know what I mean? So we all just kind of watching him grow up as a man. And I just think he a really good dude honestly. Like he he fun to be around. He always enjoy your energy. Always laughing, always smiling. So it's hard to be upset when he in the room and it's hard to be upset when he on the field. You know what I mean? Like so we win when he good. >> Where will he help the rest of the receivers when he's out? >> Wherever he wants him. He that type of talent. So I think whatever the coaches ask him to do, whatever they design for him, ultimately we'll be okay because he's that caliber player. He can play inside, he can play outside, he can give you a break, he can go to defense, you know what I mean? He probably could throw it to you if we need him to. So, who who knows for real? But I'm sure whatever he put his mind to, he'll find a way to get it done and help us a lot. >> You're a professional football player. You've seen a ton, but does he even do stuff that you go whoa a little bit every once in a while? >> It's just the spring like like the jumps. Even his drops look good. I'm like, I don't know how you how you manage to make your drops look good, but I kind of want to take that from him even though, you know what I mean? Like it'll be something. But no, he just dynamic, man. man. He's just fun to watch and I feel like the game going to be in good hands if we keep getting players like that coming into the league and we take care of them. You know what I'm saying? Like not put too much pressure on them and just help grow them the right way. I think the NFL will be in good hands. >> Heard you've already talked about BTJ, but he was just mentioning you guys personality are a lot alike. He takes a lot from you. How much have you seen grow from him since your arrival and specifically this off season? >> I mean, honestly, man, he's having a I think he's having a great camp so far and it just built off the spring. I mean, he had one of the better springs that I've seen of a younger guy since I've been in the league. But like, he if he just doing half of what he doing now, I think he would be in a good spot. Like, he's having a great camp. I'm really just proud of them. And all the young guys, they come in, they real professional. They all come in and they're doing a great job. So, >> how hard is it to throw the deep ball to him because he's so fast? I mean, is that challenging for even the quarterback side of it? >> I would assume so. Somebody like even when he don't look like he trying, he's still moving. So, I'm assuming it got to be tough or you got to have a cannon on you. You know what I mean? Like something that can really get it down the field at all times because he could roll effortless. Effortless. I couldn't say that, but y'all know what I mean. We got it out somewhere. >> Aside from the uh aside from like the more complete knowledge of the offense, where are you better >> as a player right now? >> Like I was saying earlier, the understanding like like I said, as long as I understand why you call on the play, I know the timing where I need to get there. And I think that's huge for me playing quarterback. I always want to be in the right spot at the right time because it don't matter how good the route is. If I can't get there at the right time, I'm not getting the ball and I'm not helping the quarterback. So, >> huge serve, you know, and you signed your contract last year. Some stability coming in with a offense that function. It feels very stable. >> I see it's a good situation for you. >> I mean, yeah, it is. But that's all outside. Honestly, I'm a little bit more secure on the inside. So, I'm just happy like the world is finally matching that. But >> it's another day. I just got to show up and do my job regardless. At the end of the day, >> this looks like a very balanced receiving court where you could have four or five guys hitting 800, 900 yards. >> Do you guys see it that way? And do you embrace that? >> Uh the yards, I really don't know honestly cuz the balance. >> Oh, the balance. I would say yeah, that's the best way to describe us honestly. I think we got a very well balanced room and that's top down like rookies, undrafted guys like I think all the way through we got guys who are smart first and foremost who understand what they're doing and then second can make a bunch of plays. So I think we in a good spot. >> Guys come on tomorrow. What does that look like uh mentally switching that flip? Like is there okay now we can be a little bit more intense or how does that look? I mean, I would I'm going just tell the guys, be aggressive first and then if you got to pull it back, it's easier to go backwards than to try to go out there, fill it out, get hit in your mouth, and now you think you about to go hit somebody. It's not going to work like that. So, be aggressive first and let them pull you back. >> How how uh what's the maturity level you felt about this group coming off last year? >> And I think Williams mentioned, hey, I want to get practicing like you were by the end of last year. How close are you guys to that at the early stages of camp, do you think? I mean, I kind of spoke on it a little bit, but the guys really have been taking their jobs very ser like very serious. Like, they're real professional. I'm talking about BTJ Parker always going to be who he is. Like, all the guys, man, they they know exactly what they doing. title: Coen & Hunter Speak to the Media | July 31, 2026
text: Start with Trevor Etienne. Just what's kind of progression have you seen through these first two days? >> Yeah, I thought um you know, day one was not you know, his best or our best as a receiver and group you know, as a crew. I thought yesterday was very sharp. Um that he did some I mean, some of the throws he made yesterday were legitimate like big time big time throws that you know, you're really excited about seeing. I thought there was some things in the red zone today that he did really well and I think there's a couple clips that we can learn from in terms of just how fast things happen down there and for like a bigger dude, something we're just working on is like some of the routes that a concept maybe that you run in the red zone that you also run up the field that the footwork up the field maybe like three steps in the in the gun or hitch, it has to be a different footwork in the red zone. So like those were some things that came up a little bit of how fast it happens down in the red area and with such limited inventory of red zone concepts in a lot of what we were running was things that we were also running up the field. So a couple of those things came up, but I I in terms of running the show, the operation, and also accuracy and putting the ball on the guys and spreading it out. I mean, I think he's seeing it really well right now. >> What kind of magic is McCaffrey on at this point and how is he taking advantage of it? >> Yeah, he is. I mean, you know, Patrick we're we're trying to be smart. It's a long year. It's a long camp. He's a pro's pro. I know exactly he's not going to you know, miss a beat in terms of knowing what he has to do, the scheme, the concepts, all that. I mean, love to get him more, but it's it's smart. I think it's the right thing to do and I'm not worried about him, but it's a great opportunity for for Y and for you know, some of those other guys to get more reps with the first group, right? Like that's just different when you get reps and Trevor's talking to you and you're protecting for Trevor and you're working with the first group. It's definitely a little bit more of a heightened sense of urgency and I'm pleased with the way Whites responded so far. >> How much pressure does it take off of you and your job in the big picture to have the special teams, the three main guys operating at such a peak level of efficiency? You know, going into you go into the season with those guys, you kind of you know exactly where you're going to get. >> Totally. I mean, being in LA in the early years like 18 and you had the the three specialists that we had and you know, with the special teams coach returning and you don't have as much turnover there. I mean, that's huge to have that continuity, chemistry. Like I don't it's not like I'm coaching any of those guys on how to kick, you know, or what to do from that standpoint. So, they're very diligent and detailed in the way that they go about their business and approach and I think Heath and and Luke and those guys do a phenomenal job. The players trust them that not just schematically, but they trust that they have their best interest in mind and and they love to play for those guys and I think that the leadership of obviously Logan and Ross and Cam continuing to come into his own. I think the players, the other players on the special teams units just have so much confidence because those three set the tone. >> Certainly proven what a great all-around player he is for you guys, but what what are some areas that you're looking to to see out of him in terms of his the evolution of his game? >> Yeah, I think just removing him from the core a little bit more and getting him out in space a little bit more. So, all right, whether it's at the slot position, whether it's at number one in a three by one to the to the trip side or put him one-on-one on the backside. Like I've got to move him around a little bit more so that he's get, you know, gets put in positions to run routes maybe he's not always going to be running, right? That middle of the field in which he's done such a great job of working. Something that I'd like to be intentional of over the next few days is just putting him into some more receiver positions and and just moving him around a little bit to get his skill set to continue to expand. >> You were doing some individual uh coaching with Travis during Indy drills this year. How important are those moments being that he has to split time? >> That's they're they're so crucial to have the the time and you have to be extremely intentional with that time when we have them because it is limited. I mean, just per side of ball, especially right now offensively, he's just over here a little bit less when you're doing some of the individual work and you know, it's shown a little bit with some of the timing that we need to continue to work on and that's why those guys get some more extra work after practice, but you know, I'm pleased with the way he's at least attacked everything that we're trying to do. Would I like to see those guys, you know, come down with that 50/50 ball down here, but you know, I'm never really concerned with Travis's ability to try to stay locked in and to be present wherever he is in the moment. >> has Jarrian popped the first couple times? >> Yeah, yeah, I thought today he had a really nice day. You know, got his hands on a lot of balls today. I mean, he he's physical when he plays with anticipation and just plays free and he's not overthinking it and we're not maybe putting him in positions to overthink. He's able to just go play and he's a physical dude at the line of scrimmage. He he likes to be up front and challenge people in their faces. He likes to do those things and so we got to continue to put him in positions that he's, you know, he can be successful, but I've been really pleased with Jarrian. >> Josh Cameron is a guy to be around. >> Yeah, I got it. >> How much better is Brian catching the ball? Just the physicality. >> Yeah, I mean, I think you got, you know, you guys were all here and you know, see it today and to be able to, you know, obviously we got to get the pads on, we got to hit and all that, but I've been pleased with with how strong his hands have been at some of the point, you know, contact and you know, those contested catches that obviously the quarterbacks going to continue to trust him in those positions. We all trust him to make those plays. You know, I think we're just continuing to see, right? Like from the spring to now, just taking those steps that we all wanted to see and and that we're all excited to see because if he can add that element of not just being on the outside and going vertical, but also like when you're fast as he is, those runaways and crossers, man, those can be a tough cover with a big dude like that. So, I I was very pleased. I mean, all those guys made some plays today, which was nice to see and especially yesterday. I mean, some of the routes PT ran yesterday, I mean, they were high high level. Like when he can get open and run and open up his stride and now it's like is he running by you? Is he going to run the deep out? Is he running the deep curl? Is he going to run the deep dagger? I mean, that puts a corner in a bind especially when you can open up your stride like he can. >> Justin Jefferson has made some big catches, drawn some some PI. What have you seen out of that? >> That's huge thing about the PI. Like I remember you look at some of these outside receivers specifically the physical ones. I mean, when you can draw PIs, I mean, that's an explosive pass. That's what that is. So, I mean, guys get paid off of those things. Like if they have like eight DPIs, I mean, that just adds to it, right? And that and we look at it the same way. So, his he's so strong. I mean, 223 lb or whatever he is, 225 lb, um wants to do some of the dirty work and and and wants to block. He takes pride in that. Um I think the quarterbacks have trusted him so far to be able to kind of put the ball up whether it's hey, you let him go try to get it a little bit or man, let's try to go put it up back shoulder or make him let him go be physical and use his skill set, but you know, those those young rookie wide outs have I've been pleased with just their ability to step in early and and just play. Not running around, misaligned, trying to figure it out. I've been very pleased with those guys. >> Uh shells on Sunday, pads on Monday. >> Yeah. >> Um do you anticipate having any heavier run game after 6 11 on 11? >> Definitely. And really all three practices so far in team run, which is always the first period of the day, that's been in a rack of four plays for you know, 4-1, 4-2, 4-1, 4-2. That's been 3-1 run to pass, you know, so we'll continue to do that as the pads come on and then especially when we get to >> [snorts] >> later on, which is true team, which is usually 50-50 like two runs, two passes, we may mix in more 3-1 in some of those periods as well. I've been pleased with it obviously it's very difficult to evaluate and sometimes you can get into some bad habits when you're not, you know, hitting and blocking with pads on and but I've been pleased with the guys so far. >> What do you like about what you've seen from B.J. Green? What do you think about him? >> There was a stretch of practice today where three or four of those guys >> make play after play. >> Oh, yeah. B.J.'s done a great job. I think something that we have been stressing with him is the run game. Like his get-off in the in the pass rush, we all appreciate. We got to work on the top of rush with him a little bit more, but his ability so far, especially last two days of setting vertical edges in the run game, that's been something I mean you look at him and you're like, man, I mean he but he's explosive, he can get underneath your pads. He's kind of a problem for tight ends, especially at the point of attack when he can get underneath them. I've been very pleased with him. He asked me today, I mean he's like, "What does it take to get thrown out of practice?" And I'm like, "What do you mean?" He goes, "No, not in a bad way." He's like, "In a way that I'm disrupting to the point where you have to take, you know, that's right." So, you know, he's he's on his mind in terms of wanting to take the next step, right? And we were laughing, it was a cool moment, but you could tell B.J. wants to make an impact on this team. He's worked his tail off to get to this point and we're seeing it every day. >> A couple more on B.J. Green. >> I just spoke to him and he said, "I'm not even close to arriving yet." What's Is that rare to see a second year guy come out and say I haven't even tapped my potential? >> Yeah, I mean, but he's he's so spot-on. I I really we all believe that there is something in there that is going to continue to show itself and reveal itself and um he's playing with a lot of confidence right now. He knows what he's doing more than he ever did and I I've just been so impressed with him specifically in the run game. I mean, that's when we start throwing it more and we get into more of those situations and especially preseason games when we can see him like we did against Miami last year show up in a good way. But it's been setting edges in the run game and using his hands like he he's a guy that uses the technique I'm not saying to a T, but he does like he'll do exactly what you say. You say go run through that wall, he's going to go which one? You know, but he uses the proper technique and fundamentals and he's violent and that's all really what you can ask for as a coach. >> When practice is down, Connor, what's going to be the major focus or point of emphasis going into this next block of practices? >> It's [clears throat] continuing to take care of one another and stay you know, staying off the ground. I thought we did a better job today of staying off the ground and protecting each other while you know, I'm showing them in the team meetings like guys, we we've got to protect each other like we this is such a time where the acclimation period man, we're trying to get good work, but we're not evaluating how tough you are today. We're not evaluating how physical you are today. Like we'll evaluate that as the pads come on and so the shift kind of goes to like all right, we're now we're evaluating physicality and toughness and finishing all that. Can we still stay off the ground and protect each other and practice the right way because bad teams they're they're on the ground a lot in practice. Good teams typically aren't. >> Thank you, coach. Thank you. >> Yeah, thanks, guys. >> Appreciate it. >> All right. How's it been so far? >> What do you mean, practice? >> It's been great to be back. Yeah. >> Uh you missed 9 months, obviously weren't on the practice field, just kind of what was that process like working your way back and having to watch the whole off-season? >> Uh it was a learning process, you know, I was able to get in the playbook for the second year on both sides of the ball, Learning and understanding that that's not my job, but everyone else's job so I can get comfortable just go out there and play fast when I touch the grass. >> We heard a lot about the virtual meeting room and how you were a guy that really took advantage of that. Could you kind of talk us through what that process was like in being in there and being able to see like a full lineup? >> Uh it's perfect for me, you know, I got first priority for that room cuz I'm playing both sides of the ball. So, just going in there every day learning learning new plays like I said, just learning the process and knowing everybody's job just not mine's is really really helped me get on the field and just play fast. I know y'all one play in practice just now I've had to come out, but hey they was running hurry up. So, I just had to jump back in and just learn the play on the fly and continue to do what I was doing. So, it was it had me more comfortable. I didn't panic. I was able to guard who I had to guard and stuff. >> Tony said you commented the other day that you put on 10 lb of muscle but feel lighter on your feet. Can you explain that? >> Uh yeah, I put on 10 lb, you know, I was a small guy coming in everybody like gain weight gain weight. Coach is like, hey play at whatever weight you happy at. So, me just coming in and putting on them pounds and being like, ah I was I was scared at first. You know, I'm like, ah dang I ain't never play at this weight. I'm going to feel heavy. I'm not going to be able to do what I do. But, training and being able to put those months in not just on the grass but in the weight room too just putting in that the work it made me feel lighter on my feet when I finally touch the grass. So, I'm just happy to be at this weight and continue to play at this weight. >> You also feel faster? >> Yeah, a lot faster. >> The 22.6 I mean, what was the goal >> to be? I didn't have no standard, you know, just going out there and running see how fast I get. I'm like, dang 21.5 oh yeah, I definitely got 22. And then and then didn't hit 22. It just didn't went 22.6. So, me hitting 22.6 was definitely had me like on the rise and I'm ready to I'm trying to hit 23 now. >> I'm going to say is that the next goal? >> Yeah, that's the next goal. >> It's like not many I think there's only two guys that ran faster than 22.6 in games. It's Tyreek Hill and Raheem Mostert. So, like now you got guys that you're chasing down. >> Yeah, yeah, yeah, I got it. I'm a defensive back and a receiver, so I got to be able to put them up and put them down. >> Liam showed us the practice schedule and showed how you have highlighted sections. How much I know you're in the playbook, I know you're watching film. How much do you have to study schedule to just be out here? >> I really don't even study the schedule. I just go out there and do my job, you know. Coaches put the schedule together, they they tell you you're going to be here two plays, you're going to be there this play. I just go over there and do what they tell me to do, but I just study the whole playbook. I don't try to just get the plays that they're giving me. If I'm not in on a couple plays, I'm listening, I'm trying to learn what what I got to do. >> Sorry, I I should have said with the white jersey and having to switch and doing all that. Like, how do you know exactly where to to go to on one play or on off play? >> The coaches communicate with me, you know, they they show me before practice, but you know, in the heat of things, you're just going out there and playing, so they're coming and let me know tryouts you out or you got three plays off or you got two plays off or you you in right now, so the coaches communicate with me very well. >> There was a post of you and the and the old sheriff and some firefighters a couple days ago. What was that about? How did that come about? >> Uh I don't want to comment on that, but I was just out there just having fun with Sheriff TK. >> Liam has made mention about the fact that it doesn't look like you're coming off an injury, that you're just kind of free out there. How mentally are you approaching? Do you feel free out there? >> Oh, yeah, I definitely do feel free, you know, they let me go out there and just do my thing, let me be me, you know, they give me the coaching points and let me know my technique falling off or if I need to up my technique, so I definitely feel free. >> Do you feel like you're coming off an injury or >> No, no, no, I'm feeling 9 months in, so I don't feel like I I'm coming off an injury. >> What is your most personal thing that you're trying to get better at? Like, I know everybody wants to be better every day, but do you have like a set thing that you're trying to focus on? >> Uh just get the rust off right now. Just I've been gone for 9 months and been able not to be out here with my teammates for 9 months, so finally being able to hit the grass, knock the rust off, and just continue to click with the quarterbacks and click with the defense. >> It took a while last year before you flipped sides in a single practice, and it's been immediate here, obviously. Is this more kind of what you thought it would be like when you were drafted, just get thrown in on both sides right away, and just kind of go like that? >> Uh no, I knew it was going to be different, you know, coaches haven't seen me play on both sides of the ball other than just in games, so practice is a little different. So, they had to just get adjusted to me and get adjusted to how I work. >> And the schedule this year for meetings and practices, is that I mean, meetings and stuff like that, is that pretty much the same as last year? It's been the same all year. >> yeah, it's definitely been the same. It's been the same since last year. They knew how to work that work the schedule with that, so. >> Rams, if you're trying to get better each year, how do you measure that? >> How do I measure it? >> Is it internals, or numbers, what do you look at? >> Uh it's definitely not numbers. It's just going to have been internal, you know, when I come out and be consistent, you know, I don't got to listen to coach say, "Oh, you need to do this." Or I don't got to hear the same thing over and over, and I know I'm being consistent, and I'm on teach tape, then I know I'm getting better. >> Rust off, better. >> Couple more if you got it. >> Buster uh said yesterday how he'll tease you about, "Oh, you got to come up out of that teal jersey and get a white one." >> That's all the DBs. >> The relationship with the guys, even though you're splitting time, just how is that coming along? And I I imagine as you're recovering, they were right there in your corner. >> Uh yeah, yeah, the relationship with all the guys, we just went bowling before camp started. Uh first day back in OTAs, all the guy all the defensive guys came over to my house, so it's you know, we just grow our connection, you know, not just in here in the building, but we also try to be able to connect with each other outside of the building. >> And then the same for the offensive guys, I'd imagine. >> Uh yeah, me and BT is really my BT is really like my uh main guy that I try to stay on because I want him to do better, I want him to be better. And, you know, Park and Cobb, they going to always do their thing, they going to always be there, You know, they're the first people in the building. You know, me and BT chasing that. We want to be the first person in the building. Might not be able to beat Park cuz he he here and he turned on the alarm and turned off the alarm. So, >> [laughter] >> Park is here all day, but you know, we we just try to you know, make each other better in that room. We just continue to stay on top of each other. You know, I've been out for 9 months. So, all those guys are staying on me like, "Chub, this is what you got to do. This how you get that. This how you do this." So, they definitely, you know, helped me a lot. >> Any of those guys good fisherman or not? >> Any of those guys good fisherman? Uh Tim. Tim is a good fisherman. You know, he take all the guys out of saltwater, but I got to get him on that freshwater. >> All right. Take care of yourself.

text: [music] >> Welcome back. It's Jags [music] AM. It's the most wonderful time of the year, not Christmas, but football is back with us as we get excited. Training camp in full swing. How much do you How much weight do you put on that? So, you know, it's just a mental of it, how it happened in football. But, you know, you just got to work through that eventually and then now I feel great. So, it all worked out. No, I mean, I can never say I feel pleased. Like I said, I probably said this again and repetitive. If I once I feel pleased, like I said, I won't be here anymore. Like there won't be a Christian Mahogany in the building. I won't be here once I'm pleased. So, I'm never pleased. I I definitely didn't play up to who I want to be and the player I want to be and who Hank and, you know, uh Brad and Dan want me to be. So, I just got to be better in all facets of the game. >> Where do you think you made your biggest gains heading into the year? >> Probably pass pro. Definitely, that was the biggest concern cuz, you know, playing no excuse, but playing left guard for full full full season. I haven't done that. I didn't do that in a long time. Yeah, around the same. No, nothing different. No. >> What does that polishing process look like? Is that looking at the back of tape >> Yeah, definitely. That was the biggest thing. I watched I watched like I would say maybe two of my best games and then what got me and then like my worst games as well and then just seeing what I did wrong, how how I got beat. I'm never a guy that's going to be like, "Okay, I got beat. These guys These guys are NFL all pros. These guys are good." I'm never going to put my head down and be like, "Oh, damn, I lost." You know, you're going to lose, but it's how you lose. You know, so the biggest thing for me was just watching how I lost, fixing that, and then just make sure it doesn't happen again. >> Does having someone like Skipper, someone you played with now coaching you, help that? >> It's definitely easier cuz you have a player-to-player relationship, even though like I don't really see like it's hard to say he's my coach yet, but it's it's Dan, it's Skipper. He's He's a great dude. He's a great He's going to be a great coach. And it's so much easier in the process to talk to him as well, for sure.

title: Why the Lions Can't Just Sign a Corner
text: with with the depth elsewhere. >> Yeah, can can I add this too? Like I I I you know I'm part of the crowd where and you guys know me, you know, we've been doing this a while where I'm like, "Problem? Let's go spend money and fix it." That's how most fans think. Let's go make a trade. Let's go make a signing. That's how That's the easy way to discuss it, but the problem is is finding a good cornerback is like trying to find a good tackle. It's like trying to find these premium positions that when teams when you have a good corner, you don't trade them. Unless you can't pay them, of course, which is a another conversation. So, for the crowd out there that is like, "Hey, just go sign another good corner or go trade for another good corner." The point I always bring up is you tell me a team that's just selling a good corner. Like they just They just It's the same thing with offensive line depth in the league. Like no team has offensive line depth because everyone has all the good offensive line They want to keep all the good offensive linemen. So, um it's it's obviously a it's a problem for the Lions. I'd be, you know, I would be lying if I said it wasn't that their secondary is the way it looks right now with the question marks with Brian and Kirby, but I just want the fans to keep that in mind that, you know, as much as we can just say go sign a corner, like go do me a favor. Go look at the free agent corners and tell me if any of those guys interest you, okay? And then we can get back to you. That's a homework assignment. And in the comment in the chat, you tell me what you think of that of that uh list cuz it ain't pretty. Um so, it's unfortunate it's like that, but that's where we are. I mean, you can't predict You can semi predict maybe with the TA situation, but to to ultimately have it the way it happened, it's it's unfortunate. It's how it works. >> Well, there's some huge names on that list, but like names that are flawed, that are past their prime, that have had uh in in battled issues with their teams. You're talking about Trevon Diggs, Marshon Lattimore, Tre'Davious White. Like those are former stars in this league, you know, guys that racked up the interceptions, but like there's a reason they're not on a roster right now, right? Like there There's very clear reasons these guys are not on rosters. And look, if if you got to bring one in to kick the tires, like several years ago, I I'll I'll never forget Rashean Mathis kind of changing my perception of the ability to go find a guy on the street that's got a track record and, you know, a little bit more of a polished technician than than all flash and he really bailed out the Lions at that that time when they needed a guy. So, you know, maybe there is a quote-unquote Rashean Mathis floating around out there that that I'm not seeing, but um you know, I you talk about trading for a quarterback and I I have no idea who's available. This is the time of year where teams are selling, right? Everybody's kind of optimistic, but you look at that Sauce Gardner trade last year. Two first-rounders and AD Mitchell, and I understand Mitchell wasn't lighting up with the Colts, but that was their second-round pick the year before. So, two first-rounders and a second-rounder effectively to to go out and get a top corner. Like we already know. That's that's not the Lions' way of doing business. I think if they found somebody out there, you know, they'll throw a third-rounder at a guy. Like that's that's a Brad Holmes special. Like does it feel like the team was naive here, or were they cautiously optimistic? Like with the Arnold situation, it just felt like they didn't take it as seriously as they needed to. >> Yeah, I think there was definitely some of that. I mean, this has been a story since February. I think a lot of people actually didn't really realize the severity of it until he was released. Um at least in the NFL world, not saying the Lions, but like the NFL world, I was surprised to see so many tweets about being like, "Oh, has this been brewing like this the whole time?" I'm like, "Yeah, where you guys been?" Um but the Lions certainly were privy to this information all off-season. And so, the fact that they didn't make a move maybe could suggest that they felt like this would get resolved and, you know, he'd be a member of the team 2026, but um or maybe they it's as simple as if it happens, it happens, we like our guys. but it really did seem like, you know, even dating back to Dan's comments at owner's meetings that like they were believing what he said. And uh if that's the case, then that's the approach you want to go with, fine, but you know, I think you had to kind of handle that with a little bit more sensitivity based on you know, the alleged crimes that are potentially being committed here.
