I mean, I see you and Patrick sometimes talking to each other, too. >> I think it just makes camp more fun. Like, there's no hiding that these are the hardest days of the season, and uh they should be. You're building the foundation, and this is where all your your mental confidence and everything you can fall back on when things get hard in the season is built. And so when you can lighten the mood and and laugh a little bit and you know jaw back and forth a little bit, it makes it easier, makes it more fun and and brings the energy to, you know, otherwise long hard days. >> How's Travis? >> What's that? >> How's Travis look? >> Looks young, man. Looks spruce. Looks like a guy who just got married. He's looking good. He's looking good. But he's uh him and Patrick seem to have, you know, have that connection they've always had connecting on some critical third downs throughout practice over the past few days. Um and he's in there blocking. I mean, he's in line and blocking. So, they're still asking him to do everything. >> Drew, whenever the pass come on, how different is it out there? >> I mean, that's when real football starts. We can put the jerseys on and run around all here, but it's not a seven on seven league and uh that's when the real football starts. So, it's nice to get out here, you know, get your legs underneath you, get moving, do some football related movements. But next week's gonna get real. It's going to get real. Thanks, guys. What about Chiefs appeal to you when you sign? >> Uh, just championship football. Um, as usually it you can tell they got a great culture here and stuff like that. And I knew some of the guys that were already on the team before, so having talked with them, I just I like everything I was hearing. >> I knew Josh uh Chris. Chris used to play here. Um and I met Chris Jones before matched up with Cyrus Allen a little bit out here. What stands out just about >> Uh he's a good player, quick. So >> how challenging was your year out of football? What what was maybe the most challenging part about Uh, I think the most challenging was like the earlier parts when I uh couldn't walk and do the normal stuff I'm used to doing. Uh, but I felt like that year sitting down, I kind of learned a lot about myself and it kind of made me grow like a little more love for football and cherish it a little more because it can get taken away anytime. >> Where you at now? Do you feel 100%? >> Oh yeah, most definitely. Yes, sir. Um maybe going into OTAAS I was a little but that them six weeks we took off was big and now I'm like I think a year removed and so I'm good now. Yes sir. >> You're with a lot of new guys in the secondary including yourselves. How have you guys tried to mesh together and then are you adjusting to this new play? >> Uh we knew that going in. So during OTAAS and stuff we were doing we were having dinners and stuff like that. Um, and you know, we during lunch, even at training camp, we try to sit together and talk and stuff like that. But with the playbook, uh, it's it was challenging in OTAAS, but I feel like for the most part, we're getting the hang of it now. >> Dave, you ever come here with a reputation as being a slot owner? >> Do you I'm sure you probably feel it's your best position, but do you feel like there's other things you can bring to the secondary as well? >> Yeah, most definitely. Uh, whatever they need me, I feel I can play. Uh, it's just I leave that up to Spags, though. Wherever he se wherever he sees me fit. But yeah, I feel I can play multiple positions. Anything you want to demonstrate, Jer, when it comes to the pads, knowing you haven't been in pads in so long. >> You should say that again. >> Anything you want to demonstrate when the pads come on, especially given you haven't been in pads in a while. >> Uh, nah, not really. It's like riding a bike. I think it just comes natural. >> Dave Merritt has reputation being one of the best defensive backs coaches in the NFL. What early on, like what are some of the takeaways from him and and playing under him? >> Uh, he's going to challenge the hell out of you. Um, and you could tell he knows a lot about football and he's he's he's very attentive to details and he demands that from his players too. That's the most thing I've seen. >> Ask you about the slot early. What is your appreciation for the difficulty of playing inside? >> Uh, my appreciation for it. >> Yeah. Just what what goes into to being good at that as opposed to >> I think it's like a willingness. You have to want to be physical, want to tackle, and um that's really it. Once you have that want to, I think it comes pretty easy cuz it's just like playing corner. We just covering stuff like >> You're competing for a spot in the DB room, but you've competed all your life, especially as an undrafted free agent. Is this any different? >> Nah, I think we're all competing. Uh going into training camp every year, they bring guys in and guys leave. So, if you lose that competitive edge, I think that's the quickest way to get your way out the NFL. >> Along the lines, the the Chiefs are trying to replace Trent McDuffy, who was also, you know, great slot. What do you feel about the competition? There's a lot of a lot of you guys that are in there kind of competing for that spot. What have you kind of learned from them and what's the competition been like for you? >> Uh, I think that would be a better question for the coaches honestly. >> Good. >> Mhm. >> Thanks. >> Appreciate. How's Patrick look so far to you based on how he's looked in past years? >> Yeah. Well, I only been with Pat two years, so I can't tell you for everything, but he he looks pretty good. Obviously, Pat's one of our hardest workers on the team. Uh he's worked so hard to get back from that knee and obviously he's a leader on the team and he wants to show guys that he's all in. So, we're all in with him. >> You guys had that deep ball connection yesterday. Is that something that you worked on in the offseason? >> Uh yeah, whenever we got the opportunity, you know, he was limited in LTA. So, we tried our hardest to work at it and we're going to continue working on it throughout this camp. What's your question about? >> Oh yeah, sorry. This this isn't even surprising. I told y'all guys in the offseason that Cyrus is doing this and he's going to he's going to continue showing out in camp. >> What was your excitement to be able to ditch the yellow jersey and be out here just pulling up? >> Oh yeah. I mean the yellow jersey that was that was just something precautionary. Um coming into camp obviously I knew I was going to get into more contact building the shoulder up and I feel fine. And I feel I feel good. >> How do you feel compared to even like after you started playing last year? Were you ever fully 100%? How much better do you feel now compared to last year? >> Uh last year I I was never 100%. I I was never going to be 100% until I got the surgery. So I got the surgery, been working on it, building muscle mass, obviously working at it in the offseason, getting stronger and obviously building that shoulder back. >> Outside of trying to get yourself physically ready for camp and everything, what did you try to do when you look at yourself that what you do from a route running standpoint and everything? I mean, last year was kind of hard to look at cuz my routes kind of got changed and I couldn't run a lot of the things that I would normally run and couldn't run it in the way that I would want to. So, I was kind of just looking at it as in what would I do in this situation when I was watching the film and it was a lot of things that I could have done and could have done better and obviously I worked at it offseason. I I know we're still pretty early in the camp Xavier, but when you actually look at the installs and the plays you guys are putting together, how different or unique is it compared to what you saw from the offense the first two years? >> Yeah, I mean the offense is pretty much the same. We're just fine-tuning and obviously dialing in on the fundamentals and obviously our plays that made us what we were and we kind of cut a lot of things out. Obviously coach re talked about it and we're we're just attacking the fundamental plays and making those plays on the field. Xavier, do you kind of see yourself taking a bigger leadership role this year? >> Um, yeah, definitely that's something I want to do. I don't want to be a guy that's obviously all loud. I'm a kind of lead by example. If guys need help, um, need obviously wisdom in certain certain routes. I kind of been here. I know a little bit now. Obviously, I'm a third year, but just [laughter] still young, but get it get the guys obviously lined up telling them all you can run this on this play. Um just being that leader obviously letting the guys know that they can run certain routes certain ways. >> How nice is it going to be? Would you get number four back out there with you being able to play? >> Yeah, that's it's obviously huge to get Rashid back. He's a dynamic player. Um can't wait to have him back fully in offense. >> How has your relationship with Andy changed in camp, you know, in your career now? >> Yeah, obviously Coach Reed has a little more trust in me. Um, obviously coming back, um, building that leadership role is something that we talked about. Um, obviously being more vocal, something I need to work on, obviously. And then obviously coming out and just showing by example. That's something I want to work on too as well. >> Thank you guys.

title: Chiefs Training Camp LIVE w/Mitch Holthus and Matt McMullen | JULY 31, 2026
text: [music] >> Well, we got a sold-out crowd here at St. Joe today. Clouds covering the sun. It's a beautiful day today. Hey, how are you? Nice to see you. The days get long out here at St. Joe. They can get hot. Coach Reid says it every day. He's like, "You just got to show up and push through." >> I got the left, too. >> Thanks for coming out today, ladies and gentlemen. Until next time, go Chiefs. >> It is the 67th training camp in franchise history. It is the 16th at St. Joseph in St. Joseph, Missouri at Missouri Western State University. >> [music] >> It is the 14th under future Pro Football Hall of Fame head coach Andy Reid, and we are here and back at it again and are live as our streams from camp brought to you everyone by the great people at Mosaic Life Care. Remember, Mosaic Life Care is the proud presenting print presenting sponsor of Kansas City Chiefs training camp. Hi everyone, I'm Mitch Holthus, voice of the Chiefs, along with the new director of editorial content and the old uh senior team reporter uh Matt McMullen. Are you still got that title? Is it still new? >> Yeah, it's pretty verbose. You can just call me the team reporter, that's enough. >> I like the whole being a director, you're an officer now. Uh >> [laughter] >> so here we are. Um 33rd camp for me, you're at This is number 10 for me. 10, it's a milestone. But what we've seen so far, now keep in mind, Matt and I came in last Friday with the rookies, quarterbacks, and guys rehabbing off injuries and other eligible guys, and then the veterans joined the party uh earlier this week. This is the third practice with everybody here, but your overall impressions since even last Friday. >> Well, first of all, it's 75° right now. So over the weekend, it was heat indexes in the triple digits. There was one day it was like 115 heat index. It's 75° right now. This is crazy. What do you think? >> And perfect cloudy skies and and some rain in the Chiefs Kingdom and badly needed rains, but yeah, excited about this crew. It's the first time under Andy Reid, let's be honest, that we're starting camp or having camp coming off a losing season. And people have talked and prognosticated over the last several months about what do the Chiefs have at 6 and 11? And the most asked question in the northern hemisphere is, how's Patrick Mahomes? Will he be ready week one in Monday night football against the Broncos? We'll have that answer for you later in our live show, but so far so good. >> The hunger is apparent, I think, from the entire team. So, one thing that happens every training camp, the very first day, no one gets to watch it from the media. It's only internal. It's a conditioning test. It's like a run test. It's like you're back in high school running the back and forth on the field to make sure everyone's ready for what training camp is going to be. And Coach Reid said, this was the best conditioning test he's ever seen in his time here. And think about the teams that we've had. We've had Super Bowl championship winning teams, and he said this conditioning test was the very best. So, this team is hungry right now. they look at last year and say, that's not who we are. They're eager to prove who they are this season, and to show it in a conditioning test is exciting. And so far they're showing it in these practices. We're only on day three right now. This is part of a ramp up. No padded practices yet. That'll be next week. Uh but so far the hunger has stood out to me. >> Yeah, it's an excellent point. I also think there's a physical refresh. And we've talked about this on Defending the Kingdom or throughout the off season is the fact that a team that goes to three straight Super Bowls, and you've mentioned it, three straight years of the shortest off season of any team in NFL history. But you can also sense now there was a chance to exhale, to basically take the go in and get the oil changed. Uh Rick Burkholder told us there were guys that had postponed surgeries. They got things cleaned up. And I can see that so far. There's just a tempo and a uh uh real energy to this camp so far. >> Yeah, I think everyone had a chance to kind of take a breath. Now, we don't want to have that extended off season. Uh we want to be playing in February. But if your reality is that you have to have that extended off season, how are you going to use it? And I think a lot of our players used it the right way. I think our our used it the right way. And that's one thing that's standing out to me right now as well is the new life in our coaching staff. Uh De'Marco Murray with the running backs has been fun to watch and Chadd Ochocinco with the wide receivers has been fun to watch as well. >> And we continue to pray for Eric Bieniemy and me and uh that situation. You could you know about it. Uh but EB's not here right now but um we are remembering him and the family in prayer. Um one thing though in the NFL in the off season, Matt, you and I chuckle about it. People love the NFL, they want to follow it. They If they had a game every day of the week, they'd love it. >> We're heading that direction, I think. >> We're getting there. So, [laughter] we are headed that way. But, the fact that there's also narratives that come out because there's nothing to talk about. So, let's create something to talk about nationally. And one of those narratives is defensive back. The Chiefs did lose Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson to the Rams. We lost Joshua Williams, Bryan Cook to the Bengals. And the class of '22 that was so good getting to three Super Bowls and winning two of them basically's gone. Only George Karlaftis is back. But, I'm going to go to the defensive backs here cuz that's what we're going to be our first focus on our live show here is the DBs. But, the narrative was, "Oh my gosh, the Chiefs are going to give up a touchdown every time the other team passes the ball." What I'm seeing right now and what I've said publicly and privately, there's a chance that this secondary could be better and I think measurably better. >> I couldn't disagree more with that misconception nationally that our secondary is in bad shape. In a way, I think it might be deeper than it was last year. Now, there's a lot of potential there when you guys to go out there and reach their potential but I'm really excited about it overall. I mean, overall we could talk about uh corner and safety but one area I'm really excited about is the depth we have at slot corner going into this year. Now, in the past, we really haven't had that. We've kind of put guys in different roles, "Hey, can you handle this?" And they've done a good job but uh we have numerous players I think who kind of fit a slot style corner. So, Chris Roland Wallace has been around for a while. He's a great example of why camp is important because he entered this camp 2 years ago with no promises at all and made this team and has been a contributor for this team. He could be that slot guy. Kei'Trel Clark is a name to know. Really good player for the Dolphins a couple of years ago. Missed all of last season due to a knee injury, but ton of experience and success playing in the slot before missing all of last season. He was number six in the NFL in yards allowed per coverage snap in 2024. That gets your attention. And also Jayden Kennedy, our fourth-round pick out of Oregon. A really interesting player. He flashed during rookie camp. I think he was maybe my number one takeaway from rookie mini camp rookie training camp is that guy belongs because he made plays every single day. We'll see if he can carry it now over into this veteran portion, but he could also be a slot guy. That's one area looking at our DB room. We'll talk about everybody, but the slot is an area I'm very excited about. >> And the slot is very key to Steve Spagnuolo's defense. We play more snaps in nickel, which would include a slot, and that slot can rotate between a corner or a safety or a hybrid. Christian Ronald Wallace comes to mind. And so that is a very key spot that maybe people don't talk about enough. You mentioned Kennedy and we're going to talk to him in a second. You had a chance earlier to run him down in camp. But when you look at what he did in college, two really good years at Ole Miss, then he was at Oregon and was a very productive player. When you talk about getting value in the draft class, I think I think Brett Veach hit it again. There's a real value throughout this rookie class. >> Here's a fun note on Kennedy. So he allowed just 104 passing yards on 344 coverage snaps last season at Oregon. That was the fewest among all qualified draft eligible corners. And there's one more. He also allowed just five first down catches all year last season, fewest in the power four. You know who was number two on that list? It's Mansour Delane. So we got both of those guys. >> Well, and the other stat that and that reflects on this is he did not give up a pass over 11 yards at Oregon. >> No. >> And think about who they played in this in the Big Ten. And in high-level competition and many times in faster games as far as teams in like a sped up offense. So, we're uh kind of excited. There are 19 defensive backs in this camp. If you break it down, uh there are 11 corners. Uh there are seven safeties, but again, it gets a little murky with some of these guys like Christian Roland-Wallace. And then there's uh in the middle, I'm going to put L'Jarius Sneed. Yeah, he's back uh rehabbing from an injury, but remember L'Jarius, his signature play was stripping Zay Flowers of the football in the AFC Championship game on the march to the Super Bowl 58 championship. But um he again, he's rehabbing from injury, but this is going to be really, really competitive with these 19 guys. And I think maybe you keep 10, five corners, five safeties. >> [cheering] >> There's Nic Jones with a big play behind him. Ben loves the crowd, by the way. Uh but the out of these 19, it's going to be very competitive and go down to the final cut. Maybe more competitive than any position on this team. >> So, we kept nine defensive backs for week one last year. That was interesting because we kept exactly 10 in each of the six seasons prior. So, you figure we'll keep between nine and 10 of this 19. And to your point, I think there's a lot of competition at the back end of this group. I mean, think of outside corner for starters here. I think we're kind of four deep there right now. Noel Williams is a player we'll talk about. I'm very excited about him. He was a standout for me during OTAs. He's carried that here into this camp. Had an interception yesterday. So, Noel Williams, I think has a real shot to be a starter on this team. >> We know about Mont Dell >> number six overall pick in the draft this year. Christian Fulton is healthy. We were excited about Christian Fulton last year. >> He looks way different. >> Yeah, he does. He looks like the guy we thought we were getting last year from the Chargers. A guy that was really good for them. So, he's in this situation. And also L'Jarius Sneed. We know what Sneed can do when he's healthy. So, those four names alone, you feel good about any of those guys, I think, playing outside corner for this team. >> And a safety group that is also very competitive. And we're going to talk about some of the guys that maybe you don't think about that have kind of flashed here. And one of those is a safety that's on my list. But you had a chance to catch up with Jayden Kennedy. We talked about him in competing for the slot role. And keep in mind special teams enters the discussion big time when you talk about the DBs. You've got they become a core piece of making a top special teams unit. So here's Matt's chat with Chiefs rookie Jayden Kennedy. >> Kennedy. Jayden, it's hot out here. I'm sure you heard a lot about the St. Joe heat before camp, but how you getting through? >> Uh pretty good. Um the whole summer I was back home it was about hotter than this in Florida. So I'm I was kind of used to it, you know. Um but definitely it's still pretty hot. >> You're making plays out here. It's day two right now of rookie mini camp. Uh you've made a interception yesterday, another PBU today. How's it feel to go out there and make plays? >> Great, man. You know, just seeing my training from the summer, you know, finally work out here. So definitely pretty cool. >> Looking back to rookie mini camp in the spring, what have you learned about yourself in that time do you think? >> Uh I don't think I learned mostly like now like how to be a pro. Like now we have like like no school now, you know, so I'm just like using those extra hours the right way. >> Anybody in the DB room you've especially kind of leaned on over the summer to make sure you're ready for all of this? >> I talked to Connor, somebody Connor. Talked to Curl as well. And um talked to Snead as well. >> Well, speaking of those guys, they all have experience playing the slot. It's an area you really excel. What do you love about playing the slot? >> Uh just how I'm, you know, so like I'm like most time I'm around the ball, you know, if it's run play, you know, I'm attacking on the run. If it's pass play, you know, normally the slot guys, you know, getting the ball. If not, you know, the outside guys. But just like how I'm in tune to the game plan, like on blitzes, on the run, on on the pass. So like all phases of the game, I'm basically like in there, in tune. >> Yeah, hope you like blitzing cuz Spags loves blitzing his slot corners. Has he talked to you about that at all so far? >> Definitely, yes, sir. And even like watching the film from last year to seeing like how much like Trent blitzes and and uh um Sneed blitzes as well. Just seeing like how the past they used and like how they won in inside with the with the with the alignment. So, yeah, it's pretty cool to see. >> One more day of this rookie camp. Uh what are you hoping to show the vets when they get here next week? >> That um they can trust me, you know, on on certain calls, you know, I'll talk to them. I'll make plays and stuff, doing doing my job. >> All right, good stuff there from Jayden. You know, we talk about this ever since the 2022 draft class, we've talked about finding a class like that. And it's not just their talent, but it's also kind of their mental makeup. I don't want to get ahead of myself, but we have a shot, I think, of having that with guys like Jayden Kennedy, I think. >> Much harder to do in this day and age with NIL. We've talked about that, and I'll talk about it even further uh throughout the fall with so many guys shifting schools every year, and so it's hard to vet guys to try to find that mental and emotional toughness. But Brett Veach is on to something here. Something that the DB DB room has since Brett Veach has been general manager and Andy Reid's been coach here are the undrafted free agents that seem to show up in this position area. I think of Kevin Knowles. >> Yeah. >> Right? Who's changed his number, if you're coming to camp, he was 38, but L'Jarius Sneed got his old number back. He's wearing 35, but he was so good last year in special teams. Really, really good. And uh and a safety that I'm going to talk about later, but I know he's caught your eye. >> Yeah, Xavier Wompa uh from Iowa. If you're an Iowa fan, you know all about him. He was the number one recruit in the state of Iowa back in 2022. Now, he's one of our undrafted free agent uh signees, and he's flashed out here. DeShawn Singleton is another one uh you Cornhuskers fans know all about him. Uh he picked off a pass on Sunday during the rookie camp. So, you think about the NFL, most players are undrafted free agents. That's how most guys enter the league, and the Chiefs have had so much success over the years finding undrafted free agents that not only help us, but are major contributors and help us win Super Bowls. So, uh it's difficult to find those guys, but that's why our scouting staff is the very best in the NFL. They find guys like this and so far so good for guys like Wampa and Singleton. >> Your point is really well taken. It's overlooked, but the National Football League you have to have impact undrafted free agents. Either right away that help you or going to the crock pot like I say that mold into a player in a year or two. Now let's get to the most asked question in the northern hemisphere. And a reminder that our live shows from here at camp are brought to you by Mosaic Life Care, the proud presenting sponsor of Chiefs training camp and their staff's over here to our left uh having a day here at camp. But the biggest question you got asked every day, so did I. How's Mahomes look? How's he going to be? Is he going to be ready for Monday Night Football on September the 14th? I thought he was way ahead of schedule in OTAs and seeing him this spring and early summer. I'm going to tell you he's way, way ahead of schedule. What have you seen here from Patrick Mahomes? >> Yeah, he looks pretty good. He looks pretty good. Uh he ran a speed option in team drill yesterday, so just take that for what you will. We put it on social media. Uh it's unbelievable what he's doing. Uh this guy tore his ACL 7 months ago and he began camp uh fully cleared to participate in practice. He's done every 11-on-11 rep asked of him. Uh it's just remarkable. And it's not a surprise. I mean, it is a surprise from the state of human anatomy, uh but in terms of who we're talking about here, he's Patrick Mahomes. And he will do whatever it takes to help this team win. And one way I describe it is he is a tacking his rehab with the same ferocity of like a fourth-quarter drive in the Super Bowl. You know, when he has the ball in the fourth quarter of the Super Bowl, you know he's going to get the job done, right? Similar idea here where uh he was presented with a challenge like this for the first time in his career. Hey, you have a torn ACL. Well, how are you going to respond to it? Are you going to mope about it or are you going to attack it? He's attacked it every single day. We're seeing the fruits of that labor right now. It's pretty exciting. He looks great. >> Yeah, and he's surrounded by like the best medical crew I think on the planet. >> Julie Frymyer's been great on our athletic training staff here, but also he's got his own folks that help him. But, he's been relentless. I'd see him from time to time in the spring just kind of and he was just I'm like, "Oh my god, this guy works so very hard every day to get here." And I mean 7 to 8 hours a day basically in the off season, but he does look rejuvenated as well. He looks stronger in his upper body. When he showed up here at camp, we hadn't seen him since mandatory mini camp, he looked even different from then. Like he's just I just think overall and he's doing I don't see anything he's not doing. And one thing we wanted to watch was because in the spring and early summer he did not participate in 11 on 11. Now, you're not in pads in OTAs or mini camps. There's really strict rules and even to ramp up here in training camp the NFLPA and the NFL works together to have a ramp up period. But, he's been in 11 on 11. He's been in the shotgun. He's been under center. He's been in the red zone. He's done it all and I don't see anything that makes me think he's any less than the Patrick Mahomes we know and love. >> And I talked about that speed option play that he ran and that you saw on social. That's one thing. But, the play that really stood out to me yesterday, you might remember this one, is he had to maneuver his way through the pocket on that throw to Jaylen Royals kind of early in the 11 on 11 period. And it was classic Patrick Mahomes where he's moving around. He's moving with his agility back and forth as the defensive ends are flying around him. That's Patrick Mahomes, right? You can extend plays by maneuvering in the pocket and finding the open man down field and he did that. So, I think he's only going to get better. The next step is padded practices. Can he go out there in pads and and do 11 on 11? But, so far he's given me no reason to doubt that he's going to be out there. We'll have to see and we still don't technically know about week one, but so far so good. >> So far so good. The other play that was huge yesterday was blitz period. And Spags put on an intricate blitz. They picked up the blitz, but in a split second Pat read it and found Xavier Worthy with a 50-yard touchdown against cover zero. >> Uh-huh. >> Pat loves cover zero. He can throw half the field open, but it was like he was flawless in it. And you reminded me, you got to keep reminding me, he's 7 months away from ACL surgery. Um the dude's an alien, but so far I mean, not even so far so good. So far so spectacular Pat's back. >> And we did She Said Rewind after that Chargers game, which was just a a devastating day, right? We missed the playoffs. Patrick Mahomes is lost for uh we don't know how long, walking out with uh his arms around the trainers. A brutal day, a day that we're not used to here in Chiefs Kingdom. And to think of everything that's happened in the time since, the 7 months since then, and to get to a day like this where we see him running around and making plays and being Patrick Mahomes, just puts a smile on your face. So, we always say this, don't take this guy for granted. He's special. >> One caution here though, and I've I've said this, he's a horse in a paddock. You know, he wants to run. It's like we have to protect Pat from himself. >> We were even saying that during the speed option. Like, I don't know. >> No speed option. No speed [laughter] option. Well, he made a pass play the day before the speed option that he missed. It was a it was a not a great throw necessarily for Pat. And he's jumping up and down. And he's jumping up and down on the bad knee. Remember Bill Gramatica uh who tore his ACL after getting a game-winning walk-off field goal. I'm like, no Bill Gramatica. No Bill Gramatica. And I'm like, it's just his instinct. >> And so, you almost have to protect Pat from his own himself. >> It's tricky because you want him to be himself, right? But there is a matter of making sure he doesn't take unnecessary risks. But uh again, so far so good. You want to see him out there having fun, doing the stuff that Patrick Mahomes does. And uh it's been a joy to watch him so far. >> There are four players in the quarterback room. Justin Fields, former first-round pick of the Chicago Bears. He's played a lot in this league. He right now is getting the number two reps. When you look at Justin Fields, what he's been able to do in his career, he's won games. He's won a lot of games. He's been a spectacular runner. If you look at his stats as a runner, it's now just being consistent in his accuracy on throws, especially in this offense. This is a different offense he's in now than the ones he's run previously at the other teams in his career. >> How about some trivia for everybody at home? So, Justin Fields is part of a pretty elite club. Only three quarterbacks in NFL history have rushed for 1,000 yards in a season. You know them, right? >> Yep. >> All right, let's give everyone at home a few seconds here. All right, who are they? >> So, it's Michael Vick. >> Uh and it's Lamar Jackson. And >> And Justin Fields. >> Fields. Like think of who Think of that line of guys. Uh >> It shows the athlete that he is. And he's going [music] to be more than that here in Kansas City if called upon. But it shows the kind of guy we have in our quarterback room. And we'll talk about Fields as a passer, but I think there's ways to use him even when Patrick Mahomes is out there and healthy. [music] There's ways that you can use his skill set. So, we haven't seen much of that yet. We'll see if that transpires over the course of the season, but having an an an athlete like that is a weapon. >> And the We've said this often, but the Wikipedia page definition the definition of a backup quarterback in the National Football League, whether he's on the Chiefs or on any of the other 31 teams, he must be able to win a game by himself. That is That's the check box you have to check. Now, if you're Chad Henne, who should never buy another meal ever again when he comes back to Kansas City, if you can win a playoff game, remember the divisional playoff hero [music] that he became uh filling in when Pat Mahomes got hurt in the playoffs. Twice he did it, including his had a 98-yard drive against the Jaguars. But that's your definition. So, whomever the backup is of winning this job behind Patrick Mahomes, they have to check that box, Matt. >> You ever think how crazy it is that Chad Henne not only played in that game against the Browns in 2020, he threw the ball on fourth down on our side of the field late in the fourth quarter. >> It was awesome. We went trips. We put Tyreek Hill on the inside. That was the start of Tyreek Hill's [music] uh being inside on trips and it turned into, you know, big thing for Tyreek. >> It was awesome, but it shows that Coach Reid is going to trust whoever's in there. Whoever is in there, he expects to run the offense and he's not going to hold back based on who's in there. And uh Fields has shown us some things. Yesterday, I think was his best day as a Chief so far. Uh I wrote these down. He did [music] a great throw outside the numbers to Andrew Armstrong, a player we'll talk about later, uh early in the practice. Awesome throw, perfect throw. He also threw Mason Pline, a tight end here, uh threw him open a bit later during 11-on-11. Awesome kind of uh over-the-shoulder throw to Mason Pline. So, Justin Fields was a first-round draft pick for a reason. He has a lot of talent. I think one thing he hasn't had is stability in his career. Think of some of the places that he's been. In Chicago, not a lot of stability there for him. In New York, not a lot of stability. The one place he had stability was Pittsburgh. And he actually opened that season for the Steelers a couple years ago because Russell Wilson was injured. They went four and one in his starts, I believe. So, Justin Fields can play in this league, particularly when he has stability around him. He's not going to find a place more stable than this. >> Yeah, he's had so many coordinators, so many changes. And you're thinking, is that that big a deal? Yeah, if it were they're changing you and your your software program every month and it's driving you crazy cuz all you're doing is trying to train and learn a new system. That's kind of what Justin Fields has been through. Now, both of us though are excited about another member of the 2026 draft class down the line. But Garrett Nussmeier at LSU two years ago, if you look what he did, highly productive in the 2024 season for the LSU Tigers. Over 4,200 yards passing. 29 touchdown passes. He was spectacular. And 25 was a little bit like the Peter Woods version uh on defense, which we'll talk about Peter in later live streams. But we're seeing enough here and have seen enough from Garrett Nussmeier to go, "Ooh, maybe there's something there." And he comes from great stock, right? His dad's been in the league, offensive coordinator in the league right now. But, there's something to him more than just being a coach's kid. >> So, I mentioned Noah Williams earlier. He was my standout of OTAs from the defensive perspective. If I have to pick one guy offensively outside of Patrick Mahomes that impressed me during OTAs, it was Garrett Nussmeier. He was really, really impressive. Just flashed consistently throughout OTAs. He's continued that here into this camp. He made a great throw a few days ago rolling to his left before firing a great pass to Jake Branstool who made kind of a toe-tap grab inside the boundary. Keep in mind, Garrett Nussmeier was a number three quarterback on Dane Brugler's board for The Athletic. I think Dane Brugler is the best like public draft analyst out there, does all this work and research. He had Nussmeier as the number three quarterback in this class behind only Fernando Mendoza and Ty Simpson, two guys that each went in the first round. >> Injuries are the reason I think Nussmeier fell to the seventh round. A lot of injuries last year. He is healthy now and he looks like a guy that should have gone a lot higher in the draft. >> At least twice I've seen him throw no-look passes for completions. >> Yes. >> He'll throw He'll give you a little Mahomes on the no-look, but he's had the ability to turn on a dime. Um so, he not only can read the defense, he's a better athlete than I think people give him credit. But, we've seen him spin and turn and create a play moving to both sides. It's not just like cuz your instinct takes over as a quarterback, you're always moving right or or and you don't even know you're doing it. He can go both ways. We've seen him make completions like pivoting, moving, um in quick-twitch plays both ways. There's just I'm I'm excited to watch him in the preseason. >> Sometimes the draft gets analyzed a little bit too much. We have so much information at our disposal. Just rewind the clock a year and this is a player who was LSU's starting quarterback coming off an awesome season and a Heisman Trophy contender, right? And has a season with injuries and and whatever that he'd like to forget. He's still that guy from 2 years ago and we're seeing that so far. I'm with you. I can't wait to see what he does in the preseason. I think he's going to surprise a lot of people. >> The fourth guy in that quarterback room now is well known to the Chiefs Kingdom. We knew him before when he was you know, he's been around a while, but Chris Oladokun the fact that he had to play three games last year. He started two games and honestly, Matt, he could have won both of those games. What people don't realize in trying to respect Chris Oladokun in his 35 attempts in the real games, he has thrown no interceptions. None, zero. And so there was a chance to win both games that he started. It was right there. And so Chris Oladokun does a lot to help this team and was on the cusp of doing it, but those two starts, even though losses, were immeasurable for him and to have that in his background and the fact that he played in the real stuff. >> Chris is a really talented player. I think we know that, but the thing that stands out to me about Chris the most is his heart. >> Chris wants to be here and Chris wants to help this team win any way he can and I really respect that as people that love this team. I love when I see a player who also loves this team and is unselfish. Wants to do whatever it takes. For years Chris was still eligible to go to rookie mini camp. For four years in a row I think because he didn't have any NFL service time. And I think some players after a couple years would be like, nah, I don't want to do that. Like I'm not a rookie. I don't want to go to rookie mini camp. He would go for four straight years just to help and be an extension of Patrick Mahomes. To be an extension of the veterans on this team and this coaching staff. Says everything about him and finally had a chance to play a little bit last year, showed us some things and he's back here once again. I just admire his heart and how much he loves this team and I have no doubt he'll do whatever it takes to help this team win whether it be starting games in the regular season or being a scout team quarterback. He'll do whatever it takes and I appreciate that. >> And Matt, you know who respects him, trusts him, and asks him, "What do you see? What do you think? What should I do?" You know who that person is? >> 15. >> Patrick Mahomes. He relies on Chris Olodokun a lot and has had for several seasons. So, finally, Matt and I are going to give you some early people you're not thinking about necessarily that could really impact the 2026 season. I'll let you start first. You've already alluded to him. A couple of these guys we've kind of already mentioned, but I want to talk about them more. And so, I'll let you go. Who's at the top of your list of like, "Hey, you need to know about this guy cuz he could break through." >> Right now, it's Cyrus Allen for me. So, right before we came on, Cyrus Allen made the second of two great plays today. He made a toe-tap grab down the sideline here during 7-on-7. Earlier today, when practice first began during 11-on-11, he made a one-handed catch in double coverage. So, Cyrus Allen's a player we knew a lot about coming in. We knew he was a great route runner, a lot of production last year, but was a sixth-round draft pick. He doesn't look like that right now. Long way to go. Got to keep stacking days, but Cyrus Allen has stood out to me just about every day we've been up here. >> We talked about him earlier, but mine's going to be Xavier Wompa. Right now, he has rotated in He has scorched his way up the chart. Here's what you need to know though about Xavier Wompa, the undrafted free agent at the University of Iowa. And he's an Iowa player, a University of Iowa player that didn't come from Florida or Texas or California. He came from Southeast Polk High School in Des Moines, on the east side of Des Moines. This is an Iowa kid that has a chance to really help this team. Here's your big stat. At Iowa, Matty had 400 466 career special teams snaps. We have got to find guys on this team who become dogs on special teams. We've seen players like a >> you know, when you look at Slater, the Larry Izzo types of the world who became [music] players for years in the National Football League because they could play special teams. Now, Womp has got he can play on scrimmage downs, but Xavier Womp to me is not somebody I thought we'd be talking about on July the 31st in this camp. >> I love his blend of size, speed, and length. Uh he's 6'2, 208 lb, ran a 44840 at the combine. [music and singing] When he did media the other day, I'm like, this guy's tall and lengthy. Didn't really expect that from him. So, I'm with you on that. Can I give you another one? >> Uh so, Noah Whamsley, mentioned him earlier. Uh Noah is a player that coming into this year, I was really looking forward to watching because one thing we talked about a lot on a field pass and Chiefs rewind at the end of last season when we were already out of it is hey, we can begin the process of getting back to the playoffs right now. We can start player evaluation right now and and see what some of these young guys can do. And Noah is a player that I think really took advantage of that. Uh you look at last season at the end of last year, he was playing almost 100% of the snaps in like each of the final five games of the season, I think, and he played well. Uh really impressed me. And uh for me, I was thinking, can he come into OTAs and kind of continue that progression? He did. Like I said earlier, he was one of my standouts of OTAs. And so far, he's doing that in camp. I mentioned earlier that interception he had uh yesterday in the red zone. Just a really exciting player that I think is ready for this moment and could be a starting corner for us this season. >> He looks to punch the ball out. He looks to make an impact play. As you mentioned, that he looks to do that every snap. Something that was void last year for the Chiefs. Too many third and longs given up. Noah's going to not going to win every battle, but he's going to win more than his share. Chiefs [music] only had 12 takeaways last year. It's hard to win games if you don't take the ball away in the NFL or get teams off the field. Noah Williams will be able to do both. Can I have another one here as we close things out? >> And this is one that's not super sexy, but Kingsley Suamataia is turning into a player. We remember the struggles his rookie year trying to play left tackle. >> At left guard, he has found a home. And with Kingsley Suamataia, and then we always blend it in with Creed Humphrey to his right shoulder, and then over there >> is uh Trey Smith. They're both Pro Bowlers. But, Kingsley Suamataia so far even in the spring and summer, and so far in this camp, has the potential to be a Pro Bowl left guard, I kid you not. >> So, speaking of misconceptions, we said earlier there was a misconception about our secondary. We'll talk about it on later live streams, but there's a a national misconception, I think, about our offensive line, where people don't really know much about our offensive line. When healthy, I think this has the potential to be one of the best offensive lines in football. And it's beyond just what we know we have in guys like Creed and Trey. It's also players like Kingsley having an opportunity to play left guard last year, seizing it, and growing into, I think, one of the better [music] left guards in the NFL. He's still like 22 years old, as well. He's really young. He's like a ball of clay. Uh he's going to keep emerging, I think. But, I'm with you. Kingsley's an exciting player that >> uh is making the most of his opportunity. Can I give you one more? >> Sure. >> Andrew Armstrong at wide receiver is a name that everybody should know. I think there's going to be an opportunity for one of these guys you don't know much about to make this team at wide receiver at the back end, especially if we keep seven of them. And Armstrong is making the most of his chances out here. He's flashed almost every day he's been out there with the veterans. Uh just a really impressive [music] kind of long, lanky player uh that hasn't done a lot in the NFL uh so far, but has a chance in this camp, I think. >> Ashton Gelati left practice earlier today. He was one I was going to put on here because he's got [music] a chance to be a real key to this team, just because of his versatility. We've seen it in the summer and the spring. Uh we saw it a bit last year. Remember when he dropped in coverage and got an interception. So, we'll uh Coach Reid will talk about that and keep you updated. So, hopefully nothing serious with Ashton Gelati, but he was the third on my list of the six that you and I were going to talk about. There's more, and we'll talk about that in future live streams. We always want to make you feel like you're here. A lot of you watch from around the Earth, basically, because the Chiefs Kingdom is far-reaching. We want you to feel like you're here. That is our job. And thanks to our whole 65 TPT crew, David Kelsey, and others for putting this together. But, all throughout camp, we're going to keep doing these.
