title: Colts Owner & CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon on finding a way, season ahead
text: So, I just wanted to start by, um, sharing something that I spoke to the team about on Tuesday. And that was as we reflected on last season, this one phrase just kept coming to my mind. And that was find a way. And so, that was the mantra that we settled on kind of for this season. And we came to find a way because we thought about what are the qualities that successful people have. And those qualities are consistency. Those qualities are resilience in the face of adversity. And those qualities, most importantly, are a mental toughness and a find a way mindset. And I know and believe that on our roster and in our organization, we have everything we need this year to get where we need to go. Second, I wanted to make sure I took a minute to thank Westfield and Grand Park for being such wonderful hosts for us for eight seasons. And finally, most importantly, I wanted to thank our fans. It's always such a pleasure and so fun to be able to get up close with our fans during training camp. And I just want to thank our fans for believing in us. >> All right, go ahead. Any any questions? >> Laura, you mentioned reasons to leave here and take things back to the complex. And what will be there for the fans >> So, it was a Kevin, it was a tough decision to come to. Um, because as I said, Grand Park's been a great host. But ultimately, I think we have to look at our team. And as training camps evolved over the years, it was it was it wasn't a financial decision. It was really more of an about be operational efficiency and making sure our team can prepare to perform on game day. And that was just the best decision. But I also want to add that our fans and having them be able to experience what they're experiencing here will remain a priority. And we just have to figure that out, but it's definitely a priority for us. >> Charlie, when you say find a way, is that kind of global? It's not just during a game, it's the week before the game, it's the month before it it's trying to get What is finding a way specifically? >> So, I think finding a way really comes down to that you know, you look at we showed a video that had guys that even when they were on our team to show them that it is in you, that believe Ultimately, that belief in yourself. I think about, you know, someone like Al catching the ball, you know, like with his head this way that I think it's that's ultimately these guys are so talented and I feel like our roster is in amazing shape, but it really comes down to people are going to make mistakes and you have to have that mindset, that inner belief, that inner faith that you you're going to make mistakes, but what are you going to do with those mistakes? How are you going to handle it? Because, I mean, I don't know if there's anyone in here standing here that hasn't made a mistake. I would love to talk to you because I feel like that's just that's just how life goes. So, it's kind of more what are you going to do when that adversity comes? Are you going to stay disciplined? Are you going to stay consistent? Or are you going to go in the fetal position? And I think that kind of comes down to that find a way mindset, which is to have that inner belief. And that's what I feel like my job, the coaches' job, our staff is to help these guys realize and maximize their potential. >> Charlie, we all know that Al Golden Terry's going to the Pro Football Hall of Fame next week. You're going to present him. What did that mean to you when you got the news from him that he was going >> You're going to make me cry again. >> [laughter] >> No, I mean, it's just I mean, speaking of finding a way, I mean, when I think about Adam and I know, Mike, we talked about it. It's I mean, South Dakota State, undrafted free agent, played 24 seasons. I mean, I was laughing thinking about like talk about like that's almost a quarter of a century. I mean, just I mean the 2,673 points, what? I mean, it's just like it's just amazing. I'm so proud of him and it was such an honor because, you know, my dad loved him, our family loved him and he was kind of that one piece, you know, when you think about putting together a team and my dad's journey, you know, to getting to those you know, winning the one Super Bowl but getting to two Super Bowls and he was kind of that last piece, you know, I feel like he came in, he was like magic dust, you know, we went right to the Super Bowl that year. So, it means so much to me. I'm so excited for him. >> As you evaluated last season and you came up with that model for this season, what would you say like your team and the organization fell or struggled in the game of the final four game? >> Well, we certainly can't use injuries as an excuse because that's something every team goes through, but I think ultimately, you know, sometimes I've talked to coaches and players about what, you know, if you haven't, you know, quite had success yet, right? You have to think about Sometimes it's important to think about where you came from, you know, where you are now and what you want to become and I think that's, you know, I think it's hard, you know, when we've had years of not quite getting over that hump, but I think just that's why we're kind of hammering on that is that if we have all the talent, we have everyone we need to get where we need to go, we just have to continue to make sure we're building a culture that is promoting like that inner belief and inner faith that we can do it. >> What makes you think that this year, I guess, will be different, right? I mean, you talk about inner belief, wanting to finish the season, what what is it that gives you that feeling that much? >> So, James, one of the first things that comes to mind to me is, you know, that first quality in success, consistency. You know, I think when you don't have, you know, quarterback position as an example, you You that's the leader of our team. I think it's going into the second year. Nathaniel, you know, seeing what we saw that first half. I mean, that's such a key thing. I mean, it's key for coaches, the way we build our scheme. It's key for Chris, the way we build our roster and fill in the pieces. I mean, so that's that's kind of one example, but I think, you know, it's we have everything we need to get where we need to go. >> Chris was asked about the pressure [cheering] he feels going into this season. Do you view this as a possible pressure season for Tim and Sean Payton? Sure. What needs to happen to ensure that pressure is there? >> I think even if you're Seattle, you know, I think the pressure is always there, but certainly, I mean, as I've told Chris and Sean, you know, the sense of urgency has never been higher and we have to find a way. >> I I probably you mentioned that higher sense of urgency back in January. Do you feel like you felt that this off season? You know, you [cheering] guys didn't do a ton in free agency. Did did you felt like you had the higher sense of urgency leading into obviously >> [cheering] >> Uh I mean, I think yeah, I think the sense of urgency was higher, Kevin. I think it's it's also, you know, as Chris said and as, you know, he knows we have to win and things, you know, I was talking about my dad's, you know, I think about building that team that eventually went to the Super Bowl and getting to you know, it goes decades back almost, you know, getting Tony, getting Peyton, eventually getting Adam, getting those pieces, but I think this year just we've got all the right guys that we need to be healthy. We've got, you know, a great quarterback room. Um we've got I think we just have to keep, you know, like I said, keep believing that we've got everything we need to get where we need to go. >> Karly, can you and you've been to many training camps, obviously. Can you get a feel for an individual team in camp, like the pulse or whatever? Is there Is there a feel that you have a feel for what this team >> So, it's only the third day and I think until the pads come on, you know, I think that everything changes as you guys know in the pads come on, but I think you know, when I think about even during OTAs, you know, they're not there's only like a small chunk that's mandatory, but I think seeing starting then, I think seeing the guys that showed up, seeing the way guys that were hurt, that rehabbed. I mean, I think everyone is very dialed in. So, I I feel I feel really good about where we are right now. >> Jonathan Taylor said that he wants to be a Colt for life a couple of days ago. Um I know it's a funny word "contract". How important is it for you, uh the owner, who's calling the shots here, to try to figure out a way to get something done for him? How important is >> Yeah. Um well, I love Jonathan. I mean, he's he's I'm really proud of the leader that he's become on our team. I mean, he's one of our pillars. He has pictures on the stadium for a reason. Um and I would love it if he would be a Colt for life. >> You talked about the the the the roster where it sort of needs to be, but if Chris comes to you and says, "You know, we need a receiver, and it's going to cost X million." Are you fine with that? Do you kind of leave that up to him? Or do you sort of have a veto? >> So, I mean, Chris it's up to Chris, but he keeps me in the loop, and obviously when, you know, it's a decision like that, you know, he would I would be involved, and he does a great job of that. Um but I think we just we're just going to have to see how that plays out cuz I think he's kind of in charge of the depth there. >> Okay. >> Is there anything Let's take a couple more. >> Is there anything in year one with the main business of this franchise that you've learned that you're carrying forward into year two? I mean, that probably everybody around here has seen you everything about it, but is there anything that's kind of surprised you that you're taking into this season? >> Uh so, Dominic, I would say what one thing is I think a lot of what I'm doing it's really it's not a lot different than what I was doing before. So, it was interesting to me how, you know, the when your title changes, which I'm not really a big title person, personally, but it's like how, it's a little bit of a vibe change with some people, but I think most most people that, you know, I think I I'm very proud of the way that our family runs our organization and it's very, you know, we're family-owned and we care about our people, so I think it's kind of love it's leveled out now, but at first it definitely was a little bit, you know, me coming in the room meant being a little bit, you know, just a different vibe than it was before, but um cuz everyone's been so supportive through, you know, cuz it's, you know, losing our dad, losing my boss, you know, but it's just been I'm just really proud of the culture we have at our organization. >> And the flexibility at quarterback, I know you had that with Daniel coming into year two, but he also had an injury history, so how do you just balance both of those? >> I mean, I feel like every player, you know, has injuries and I just think Daniel has, like I said, he has a he has a find-a-way mindset. I mean, the level of preparation that he did even it was a week after his Achilles and he was out he was out in walk-through on his little wheelie thing. I mean, to me, like yesterday morning I'm working out and he's six it's like 6:00 a.m. and he's coming out of the quarterback room. So, he did that and he did that all through even his injury, you know, there's guys that could there are guys that could choose to stay in the training room and not be involved, but instead he kind of just found he found a way to help, you the quarterback room with when Philip was there and Riley and Anthony and he's just been he's just such a great leader and I just believe that I believe he's going to find a way to figure it out and stay healthy and get us where we need to go. >> Last question here. >> So, it's day three in training camp and like I said, I believe we have everyone here to get us where we need to go. Um Chris wouldn't be here if I didn't believe that and we're just going to have to see how things play out. Yeah, I mean that's something that Chris Chris is looking into and he keeps me informed on it, but yeah, if it's you know, if it makes sense then we would certainly do that. >> All right. All right, thanks. Thanks everyone.

title: Colts' Riley Leonard shines at training camp, throws deep ball to WR Nick Westbrook Ikhine
text: Thunderstorms brought the Colts inside for day four of training camp practice, but we still got to see a lot of action out on the field today at Grand Park. I'm Nathan Brown, your Colts Insider here with Joel A. Erickson to break down the Colts fourth day on the field before an incoming off day tomorrow on Sunday. Um got a chance to see some red zone work, some uh two-minute drills by um all three quarterbacks, lots of different guys in the offense making plays. Um what in particular stood out to you, Joel? Um we got to see the offense get some uh team reps in. >> I think it's Riley Leonard. Uh for two reasons. I think the number one thing so far in camp we've seen them trade off snaps evenly with Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard. That was not the case today. There was an early period where uh the number one offense was on one field, the number two offense was on the other field. Those were Riley Leonard snaps over there. And then they ended with a two-minute drill. Same thing. Riley Leonard got a two-minute drill. Anthony Richardson did not. What he did with it is the other interesting thing. He's been kind of up and down in in what we've seen so far until that two-minute drill. Second play of the two-minute drill, he hits Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, who's having a great camp, on the first real deep ball of camp. They score. He looks good in that. It just you get the feeling with Riley Leonard sometimes that he's just a gamer. He's the kind of guy I know it's not a game. I know we're indoors and it's a practice. But he's the kind of guy that when it's the ball's moving and you're placing it, he just kind of finds a way to make plays. >> You mentioned Nick Westbrook-Ikhine. I think he had my play of the day there as you mentioned that deep ball from Riley Leonard in that two-minute drill. He had another great play yesterday um in first-team reps with D'Angelo Jones coming back for uh kind of a jump ball there on the sidelines. Made great plays on both of those. I would say um the somewhat wide-open race that we felt like there was going into training camp with that number three wide receiver spot, it seems like he's taken a uh solid step through four days of practice to stand out. >> Yeah, it's always big for a guy who's the new guy who doesn't have the time in the offense to do that. That kind of adds a little extra to what he's done so far. My player of the day, I'm going to go with Seth McGowan, Uh uh the running back, the seventh-round running back. I think that's another competition where it feels like it's early, but he's kind of got a edge leg up on D.J. Giddens. Had a run today. You can never tell with these padless practices how the runs go, except if Quenton Nelson runs over to tell you good job, you probably had an actual touchdown. So, Seth McGowan's run was off to the right side, cutting back the other way for a touchdown. I think that was a big play today. >> As we mentioned, we have an off day tomorrow. The Colts will be will be back on the field on Monday. We'll be back in pads on Monday for the first time in training camp for um a couple days in a row. We'll get to see I know we just talked to some linemen um on both offense and defense. These guys are very excited to get the pads on and feel and feel like this camp really starts in earnest. Um we'll start to see a little bit more physical play. We'll get a chance to see from running backs like Seth McGowan and D.J. Giddens who are fighting for that number two running back spot. Um who maybe stands out um and maybe see some physical play between the secondary and the wide receivers as well. That'll do it for us today breaking down day four of Colts training camp. I'm Nathan Brown. He's Joel A. Erickson with the Indy Star. We'll have several stories coming over the next couple days on indystar.com. Be sure to check those out. Check out our video clips on our YouTube page and we will see you back here on Monday. >> What are you looking for in What what what are you looking for in the red zone in terms of like, you know, the things you look for to show that you had a red zone touchdown? >> Um just when we get down there executing positive plays, no negatives. And when teams come out there and play us too hard, being able to run the ball down their throats. And um they play us man, just winning our winning our one-on-ones. >> Four practices in, what have you seen from Daniel? >> Um he looks like he never got hurt. I mean, you see he's throwing dimes left and right on the field. Um getting out of the pocket, scrambling, and different things like that. And I think his confidence is building more and more every day. And when we put the pads on, I think it'll just take it to another level. >> Well, from a chemistry standpoint, how how has that evolved from your year one to year two again? >> Um um it's light and day from last year because, you know, last year him and AR were splitting the ones reps. So, this year coming in, he knows it's his team. Um we just went down to Florida a couple weeks ago. The whole offense went down there and threw. He got us all together down there at IMG. So, we built some chemistry down there. So, coming into camp, um it's like we never lost a step. >> Well, he's taken off running for four or five times now at this point this week. Does Does that give you guys a sigh of relief now? >> Uh definitely gives us a sigh of relief, and um I think it gives himself a sigh of relief that he knows he has the ability and the confidence to go out there and do, you know, some guys coming off that injury might not try to escape the pocket and do different things like that. But, especially being in a practice setting, you don't have to go out there and do that. So, him just doing that just shows us all that he's ready. >> Well, what's How would you uh describe this tight end room? >> Um I would say it's very versatile. Uh Tyler Tyler can pretty much do everything. Will Will's like the speedster of the group. You you know, Will come in, he's going he's going to find a way to get the ball. He doesn't like get a lot of game game reps cuz the three of us are dual lot, but whenever Will's on the field, he finds a way to make a play. And um me and Trey I always call us like the bulldogs of the room. And if we get a chance to get the ball, we're going to try to run run through somebody's face. >> What do you notice from uh Krystin Poutsch's development in uh being a senior football? >> Uh man, I tell him I'm like, "Man, you remind me so much of myself when I first got here. Um the things you're messing up, the things you're thinking about." I'm like, "Bro, I was doing the same exact stuff." So, when I see him do it, I try to um coach him through it and just give him little pointers here and there cuz I know it's a lot cuz it's like going to school all over again with the terminology and things like that. So, I know his mind's spinning every day. But, I just try to help him as much as possible. And then having Tom in the room, Tom helps us a lot, and he spends a lot of extra time with him and things like that. So, honestly he's gotten better and better every day. So, just hopefully see him take that next step starting on Monday. >> What are the areas where you've seen him take the biggest leap say from OTAs to now and where does he do you still feel like he's got some work to do? >> Um I would say just, you know, in the run game that first step is so important with the technique and things like that. So, now he's getting out of his quicker first step more aggressive. So, now it's just that aspect of shooting your hands cuz you're so they coach you so much on footwork and technique you forget about the upper body part and being aggressive. So, that's like the next step in his development, matching his feet with his hands and striking somebody. >> Quinton, for you decade in, how did you make it to last this long in the league? >> Um I would just say doing everything the coaches asked me to do. Um whether it be well I'm in year 10, I'm still playing special teams and things like that. So, guys get up to this age and they don't want to play special teams. But as someone who's not a starter anymore, they ask you to play special teams, you go out there and do it. And then I would also just being available. I would say that's the biggest thing. Um being available and when my number's called going out there and doing what I'm asked to do. >> You never envisioned this long or not or did you? >> Uh no, somebody just asked me the other day, "Did you envision playing this long?" I was like, "Honestly, I was just taking it year by year and whatever happened happened." And it's been a great experience so far. So, hopefully try to keep it going. >> Quinton, just what are your impressions of Daniel just his growth, his bounce back, and the way he looks so far? >> Yeah, I mean he's been incredible. He's back like he's never left. Um and he just worked so so hard to get here and uh it's uh been an awesome to see. >> How much more different or I guess better on the field just going to year two knowing you already know who he is personality-wise, work-wise compared to last year? >> It feels great. >> Quinton, it's been noted and it's evident the work that he had to put in the last 8 months to get to this point. What's something you maybe learned about him and the way he attacked the process maybe you didn't know when you were working with him? >> Yeah, I mean he he's always been a hard worker. Um first one in, last one out. But I think he really enjoys the work that he does to be the best quarterback he can be. Um this was a totally new challenge for him where you know, it's work that you don't want to do. He he's waking up super early, rehabbing and then late at night rehabbing. Um and it's it's tedious work that you got to do every day that he did. Um and we just appreciate him a ton. >> How much have you guys benefited from another year of continuity with that offensive line? Obviously you have one change, but I mean you you've been here before where you had that continuity and glue together. what what does that do for you guys right now? >> Yeah, um it's been awesome. Uh feel like we've had a good 4 days and stuff to improve on. but Bort adding a year, um Ganz adding a year, you know, obviously Bernie's been doing it for a long time, but even he's finding ways to get better. And then adding Jaylen Travis into the mix. Um it's been really fun to see these young players growing uh and working so hard to get better. >> And the coaching staff, too. I think nine of the the 11 starters on the offense when you have that continuity, what does that do for a team that kind of helps you guys hit the ground running in the offensive starting lineup? >> Yeah, it it helps us a bunch. >> What what have you seen from Jaylen since early on in camp? He's getting a lot more time. >> Who's Jaylen? >> For Travis. >> Trav- Travis? Got to be honest, I'm pretty focused on myself uh and like the left side and Bort next to me like working with him and working with him that I don't really pay that much attention to Ganz and uh Jaylen, but I mean I I all I needed to see like last year um and this off season and in camp with the way they work and how much it matters to them and how much they care. And then also obviously how talented they he is as well. So you add hard work to town that's that's awesome. Yeah. He's been great since they won and it's not easy. The center has a tremendous responsibility in our offense with having to make all the calls, read the defenses, see the safety rotation, everything and I mean he's just taking the ball by the horns and he's gotten better every year when it comes to that. To the point where he's able to check protections and having a center like that who's that smart and then also again that talented and able to run the way he can and also get movement is awesome. Yeah, it's definitely important to work as efficient as you can and like work smarter while also working hard. but that's just something you grow at as a player and you learn from older guys from a young age. So I was lucky enough to play with some great players that were able to teach me how to do that. So I haven't had any discussions. That's not up to me and um yeah, I'm just really thankful to be here. Excited for this year and uh love this team, love my teammates. >> Last year when how different will Monday be just putting the pads on and when you compare that to week one versus now getting into the work out and practices? >> Compare it to week one this week this that we just had? Um yeah, it'll be more physical. Um when you put the pads on, you'll be hear a lot more banging out there. And it's just even more like football. Um being able to grab on to those shoulder blades alignment never grab. Uh we just put our hands on and um yeah. but uh we we love it when the pads come on. Um you callous your body, you get sore from all the hits you take and all the hits you give. And uh it it's fun. Uh it's having those shoulder pads on, these helmets on, I feel like it's what makes the game fun cuz you can just play with reckless abandon and come off the ball hard and uh yeah. How you guys doing? >> Oh, different much different camp for you this year obviously. >> Yeah. >> Year two. How how different how can you how can you can't contrast last year versus this year in terms of like your preparedness? >> Yeah, I feel like last year um the training camp it was just you know I was a rookie trying find my foot in and and routine and also just uh learn the playbook and and putting on you know kind of just I wanted to stress on myself. But I feel like this year man I I been around a group of guys that have showed me how to do it and uh man just getting right with my faith. I think the Lord has blessed all of us with these amazing talents and I think it's it's for us to just go out there and be us the the person he made us to be and you know uh just taking what all the advice that I got from all my vets even outside of my room. Uh just knowing what they did to keep their body healthy and what to expect especially in year two and and I feel like I've applied that and and it's been helping me a lot. >> Tell us about some of the the physical and athletic the you made in the off season. How are you seeing that translate to the field now or are you >> Oh yeah, definitely. I just feel a lot lighter on my feet. Just feel more explosive. Um man, just feeling great shape. I feel like I I got a lot of fat off of me, which was very needed. But I feel amazing, man. >> What do you think of the opportunity ahead of you because of the opportunity you have opposite of Al Woods and Moore? >> Yeah, man. I'm excited. Excited just to just to elevate from last year. I feel like I showed some some splashes and some you know, some little clips of of what I'm capable of doing last year, but I just want to build off of that and you know, just take it day by day and just get every get better every day, you know, learn from the mistakes I made yesterday and the mistakes I make today and just continue to just critique every part of my game. >> Is it one of those positions on the roster where there's maybe just about as much competition as anywhere? How have you experienced that and what is that competition and and the opportunity and that you have there in like the first four days of training camp? >> I was man, it's been amazing. I think you know, going in uh knowing me, I I love competing. I love competing against, you know, great players who are around me, great players at, you know, offense side. So, I feel like that's always something that I loved and and you know, I feel right at home. >> Al Woods has acknowledged that there's a lot of pressure on him to kind of take over and be the guy at least in the locker room this year. Have you noticed any changes in him this year compared to last? Like kind of taking ownership of things and everything? >> Yeah, I mean I mean, me and Al Woods have spent like almost every day together. So, you know, we're always just sharing stuff that's on our mind. I think with him he's he's done a great job. He's a stepping into like a leadership role, you know, behind the scenes and just just helping out, you know, me and all the young guys cuz I'm still young guys, I'm on my second year. And he's just been feeding into everybody, you know, giving everybody wisdom and what helped him, especially him being young being in his third year. So, it also helps us cuz you know, it's it's he's it's like bugging us wisdom, but it's like man, he just he just got done with his second year. He just got done with his first year. So, he's able to to give us information on what what helped him and and you know, we we can apply it in and do it to our everyday life. >> You talked about this last year in an interview. Can you explain a little bit mentally how did you deal with okay, I'm a second round pick, expectations might have been this, but I'm not playing as much as I wanted to. How do you squirrel that away and just mentally prepare yourself for the front of the season? >> Yeah, I mean, I'll be lying if I say it wasn't tough mentally, but for me, I really know my faith heavy. I know that my Lord and Savior Christ is is in him and he's he's everything that he's brought me out the slums. He's brought me in from the the darkest rooms, darkest places and and once I lean on him, I understand that man, I'm I'm performing for him. You know, I'm not performing for the outside noise. It's it's a it's a one man alliance and I'm just trying to be, you know, who he called me to be every single day and that kind of helped me just to just to ease off, just to not put unwanted stress cuz I feel like stress is for everybody. Stress and the things that make you overthink that that takes away your joy is not from him. You know, the peace and the love, that's what he wants to feel. You know, feeling the the love that that the Lord put around us and that he instilled in the word. So, you know, I leaned on that heavily heavily and and it's helped me a lot. >> Off day tomorrow, pads on Monday. >> Oh, man. >> At your position, how much do you embrace and anticipate >> Oh. >> getting finally getting the >> That's where it starts and that's where it starts. I feel like this is like a warm up, you know, warm up with no pads and you know, just t-shirts and everything, shorts, but once you put the pads on, that's where everything matters and that's where you have to really, you know, one of the pillars we we want to uh build off of is is being physical. So, it starts it starts Monday and carry Monday all the way till, you know, Super Bowl. So, that's that's the goal. >> In the short time you've been teammates with Arden Key and better in person off the field than large, what have you learned from him in the last few months? >> Man, Arden, he's just he's just allowed me to really look at the game from a different lens. He he's helped me slow down the game, slow down everything and just it's just how to not look at the big picture, but have blinders on and just just make your process a lot more quicker so you can play free. And that's one thing I love. He's always helping us even when we're not paying attention or we're just so focused in taking notes. He'll He'll call us to the side and and give us more you know, little tips and tools of of what else we can we can do that will help better our game. >> How are you all doing? >> Had a nice bomb today. What's what's that like when you're kind of in the thick of this competition here looking to establish yourself? You make a play like that. >> Yeah, it always feels good. I mean, whenever the ball gets thrown your way, especially a deep one, you just you see it in the air, try to run under it, come down with it. It was a great throw by Riley, obviously in great protection to be able to get it off. So, I was happy with it. >> And then yesterday on a contested catch on the comeback for it, go up for it. What do you remember about that play too? That one stood out. Oh, yeah, yeah, I remember the one Daniel threw. Yeah, kind of similar thing. We're just running my route. I knew I wasn't the primary look, but just ran the route to win it. Necessarily didn't like killing him on the on the release or anything, but saw that D.J. gave me a chance. So, I just tried to estab- establish that trust and come down with the play. >> You've been in different situations in your career where you had sometimes a lot of opportunities, other times not many at all. But how's that prepared you for maybe this position you're in here, which is kind of just be ready and see where you fit in? >> Yeah, I I think you could say that. You know, looking at it like that, you know, there's a bunch of different things that I've gone through that have led to me being here right now and try to learn from all of it. And like you said, I've had, you know, years where it felt like everything was going right and years where it felt like everything was going wrong. And so, I just try to learn from that and just understand that it is a game going against, you know, professional players every day. You just try to win all the reps that you can and just see what comes of it. >> When you look at last year, coming into this time with the Colts, was there any specific thing you thought, this is where I really want to get better at to get back to where I was in Tennessee in terms of playing and doing production and stuff like that? >> Uh I mean, that wasn't really the motivation. It was just I saw it was a good team. Um, you know, I I played against them, you know, week one and got got kind of walloped when I was in Miami. Uh, so I saw that and then watched, you know, that those first eight weeks and was watching throughout the season. Um, and just understanding, you know, the the organization I always had respect for. Uh, so that was kind of more of the motivation. >> Did you Did you learn anything about what they did from you just in the spring and with OTAs and everything? >> Oh, a little bit. I mean, that's understanding I'm a bigger body receiver, you know, just go go out, play big, you know, establish yourself in the run game, do the dirty work. That's kind of what I've always hung my hat on and how I've carved out a career so far in the NFL. Uh, so, you know, my thought is, you know, if that's what's got me to this position, just continue to try to do that well. >> When you look at the wide receivers room as a whole, I see there's some opportunity there. How do you all push each other, but also maintain like that camaraderie? >> Yeah, it's been a great group so far. I love I love being in that room. I feel like everybody um, is competing, but, you know, everybody's quick to help and offer advice or, you know, whatever it might be. Um, lend an extra hand, extra time, you know, studying, whatever it might be, uh, to to push each other to get better. So, it's been a great great room so far. >> You've been in the league a while now, but how does going to a coach like Reggie Wayne How How has he kind of helped take your game up a different level so far? >> Yeah, I mean, I just appreciate how, you know, he shoots it straight. Um, and obviously I have all the respect for him. I understand and watching him, you know, when I was growing up and the type of player that he is, you know, take everything that he everything that he has to say coaching wise, um, to heart cuz I know that, you know, it works. Um, so it's huge just having that having that, um, you know, veteran presence and a guy that's done it before. >> You mentioned >> Who are the couple more that you're around talent-wise, skill set-wise in your wide receiver room? Who have you benefited or you Where have you benefited the most benefited the most from the guys that you're around? >> Yeah, honestly, Alex been a huge huge guy for me so far. You know, obviously he's not out there, but you usually, you know, on the sideline watching practice, he's in my ear whether it's with, you know, a coaching point or encouragement. Um he's been a guy that, you know, with what he can do right now, he's making the most of it. >> You mentioned that blocking earlier, just being versatile and doing it. I mean, how did you get that mentality pretty early on and how has that served you well? That particular blocking in a place like this with JT. >> Yeah, I mean, early on, you know, my first few years, we had Derrick, so you hand him the ball 30, 40 times and something good's going to happen and it's the same thing here with JT, so that's something you definitely got to take pride in. I've kind of always have as a receiver try to take pride in blocking. >> Knowing there's some competition in this group for that number three spot right now and with Alec not yet on the field, I know that Mike has some more reps for you at the moment. Is there like an added sense of urgency to take advantage of the the reps and the times that you're getting to see the ball in this first week or week and a half of camp before he comes back? >> I don't I'm not really putting that on myself. Um you know, I can't really focus on that. It's not anything I can control. And so right now, I'm just trying to take advantage of the reps that I am getting. Um been blessed that Reggie's been giving me some some good reps and reps with the ones, and so I'm just trying to be out there, be in the right spot when those opportunities do come. Um but I feel like if I try to put that urgency on myself, uh you know, I feel like I'm squeezing too tight and trying to hold on to something. Just let it let it come and if it happens, great. You know, if not, you know, oh well, but I'm just going to give it my all and try to get it. >> Yep.

title: Colts' CJ Allen released from PUP list, Irsay-Gordon shares message to team
text: We've wrapped up day three of Colts training camp here at Graham Park. Just got a chance to speak with Colts principal team owner Carly Ers Gordon and some other thoughts that we have um on day three of camp coming here on uh ramble ramble. We've just wrapped up day three of Colts training camp here at Grand Park. to break it all down. I'm here with Joel A. Ericson. I'm Nathan Brown, your Colts insiders for the Indianapolis Star. Couple thoughts here um from training camp on Friday. Uh first up, we got a chance to speak with Karly Ers Gordon, the Colts principal team owner going into her second season at top the franchise. Um she said that she already came up with the team's motto, thinking through what we saw at the end of last season. The Colts lost, of course, seven straight games. after starting eight and two, they miss the playoffs after trending toward the top seed in the AFC East. Her motto this year for this team, find a way. >> Yeah, I I think what what kind of has been the the emphasis for the first two days and what's behind this behind that for me is injuries can't be an excuse this year. that I think that's really what they're getting at is we can't have um and I would contend that the injuries they had last year, especially to the starting quarterback and the backup quarterback that those are very significant injuries, but it feels like that the messaging we're getting is no matter what happens, we have to get to where we want to get to. >> She said that she believes in the group that they have here. Uh we of course went into the off season uh with Carly saying that there was a high sense of urgency. The urgency had never been higher. some combination of that phrase, I think close to a dozen times in her season ending press conference in early January. The Colts weren't super active in free agency. They of course resigned their starting quarterback Daniel Jones and uh top wide receiver Alec Pierce to big deals, but brought in a handful of uh maybe role type players or reserves to in in particular bulk up um the depth on the defense. We didn't see any big star signings outside of that. Carly said that she still believes in the group that they have here. Um, she also believes in longtime general general manager Chris Ballard who enters 2026 in a contract year. Carly said that she wouldn't have Chris here if she didn't believe in him. Um, and they will see where the season goes and and figure out that future for the the two sides [music] later on. >> That's another one where I think sort of the reality of the situation kind of tells you what she's saying. He's in the last year of his contract. He doesn't have an extension. Ballard said it the other day. That means they need to win. That's kind of all you need to know. However you want to word it, a sense of urgency has never been higher. The fact that he doesn't have an extension tells you where this franchise is. >> There's some other missing extensions too, of course, that we've talked and written about previously. Jonathan Taylor, uh, Deorest Buckner, Josh DS, Grover Stewart, among those entering 2026 in contract years. Uh Carly said that she would be willing to uh pursue extensions. Um wasn't completely closed off to it, but those would largely rely on Chris Ballard. And Ballard has told us multiple times over the last couple months that he's going to do what is right for this organization's future, even if he's not guaranteed to be a part of it. >> You guys know this time of year, a lot of times these contract situations happen between now and the start of the regular season. There was a practice today. My one play of the day is really five plays of the day. Five bobbled snaps from Anthony Richardson. None of them were really awful. None of them were like snapped over his head. There was one that was a little bit low. This is a concern. This I think this is a a significant concern for Richardson given what he said about bobbling the snap when he came back from the eye injury in December. >> Yeah, he told us in that first interview um since his injury in late December, uh he of course returned to the practice field um had his 21day uh return window open, but ultimately was not activated. did not see uh see a game since uh October when he suffered his fractured orbital orbital bone that also led to some vision limitations. He told us at the time in December that um he he could see things really well far away, but it was uh those things like a snapped ball, especially out of the shotgun that he was struggling with um just kind of in the a one- foot bubble essentially around him. I think all of those snaps of course were um out of the shotgun and he was uh you know some of them I think there was at least one that he dropped alto together today. Um just was not a sharp day from Richardson as he battles Riley Leonard for that backup quarterback spot. That was certainly uh to me as well the the thing that really stood out um some plays both ways on both sides of the ball today. We got to see some kicking um to start that camp battle as well. Uh Blake Groupy six for six today. Spencer Schrader five for six mix missing uh what was it? Uh his 50 yarder if memory serves me right. Um so early days in that battle as well. It's probably one of the most interesting battles in camp I think and we'll have to see how that continues to trend. >> They have their first afternoon practice tomorrow. We'll see if the rain holds off. They're supposed to go at 4:00. We will be here. Some of you will be here. For the Indie Star, I'm Joel A. Ericson. This is Nathan Brown from Colts training camp. Yeah, >> I guess sense of relief being cleared two days in. >> Yeah, no doubt, man. It felt good, ran around, man. It just felt great to get back doing football. >> How how long were you down or whatever from training? >> Uh, just a couple days. It wasn't nothing too serious though, you know. We just wanted to take the the proper, you know, proper steps of being feeling like I can move and stuff like that. >> Do you feel good? >> Yeah, I feel good. Yeah, for sure. No doubt. I'm sure it's a lot of information coming at you like the mic is a pretty responsible position. So, what's that balance and like just trying to get your footing in the NFL while taking on all this information, >> man? I see it as like a just a great opportunity and a blessing. You know, everything that I kind of pray prayed for, you know, uh like I said, it's everything I dreamed of. So, man, just exciting. That's how I look at it. >> What can you tell us about CJ Allen day back in your hometown? Oh, it was just very fun though seeing the community come together, you know, we have on all blue, you know, and all blue represents, you know, Mark County and the coach because both of the teams are are blue. So, man, it was fun. >> The opportunity you have this year on this defense, your first year, like how exciting is that for you and how much, you know, responsibility you take for for what you can do with this defense? >> Like I said, man, it's definitely uh it's definitely exciting. That's how I kind of see it as a great opportunity. You know, I know nothing is given. I got to go out there and earn each and every day and that's what I'm willing to do. >> CJ, when did you strain the C? >> I think like Thursday. >> Yeah, real recent. Like I say, it wasn't nothing like crazy. It was like just a small little tweak, what not, but uh you know, I had to just be honest with them, tell them I had a little tweak and stuff like that. So, yeah. >> CJ from college to here, you got a lot of reps, but what are the things you're seeing now? >> I think, man, really just the little things like are you in your right gap? Are you one step off from your gap? you know, these lineers in the lead, you know, they're fast. So, you know, one step can get you out your whole play. >> The excitement of just putting your helmet on. Like, how did that feel this morning knowing, okay, this is it's finally here. Finally here. Not all the way here, but it's here. >> No, it it definitely felt good walking out my cleats on, you know, and uh being able to walk up the uh the blue carpet with my teammates, my linebackers, and stuff like that. So, man, it it was great. >> L said you were you said you were basically there every day this summer. What did you focus on during that time playing? >> Man, really just my body just getting my body back right, you know, u and coming in, you know, and diving deeper in the playbook and stuff like that. So, I just wanted to be here and where I'm going to be in camp. >> TJ, what what is the responsibility like of being in that huddle with with veteran guys? You're wearing the mic, I think, right? title: Indianapolis Colts team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon holds training camp press conference
text: So, I just wanted to start by um sharing something that I spoke to the team with about on Tuesday. And that was as we reflected on last season, this one phrase just kept coming to my mind, and that was find a way. And so, that was the mantra that we settled on kind of for this season. And we came to find a way because we thought about what are the qualities that successful people have. And those qualities are consistency. Those qualities are resilience in the face of adversity. And those qualities, most importantly, are a mental toughness and a find a way mindset. And I know and believe that on our roster and in our organization, we have everything we need this year to get where we need to go. Second, I wanted to make sure I took a minute to thank Westfield and Grand Park for being such wonderful hosts for us for eight seasons. And finally, most importantly, I wanted to thank our fans. It's always such a pleasure and so fun to be able to get up close with our fans during training camp. And I just want to thank our fans for believing in us. All right, go ahead. So, any any questions? >> All right, what were the reasons to leave here and and to take things back to the complex and what will be there for the fans from a attendance standpoint? >> So, it was a Kevin, it was a tough decision to come to um cuz as I said, Grand Park's been a great host, but ultimately, I think we have to look at our team and as training camps evolved over the years, it was it was it wasn't a financial decision. It was really more of an about the operational efficiency and making sure our team can prepare to perform on game day, and that was just the best decision. But, I also want to add that our fans and having them be able to experience what they're experiencing here will remain a priority, and we just have to figure that out, but it's definitely a priority for us. >> Carla, when you say find a way, is that kind of global? It's not just during a game, it's the week before the game, it's the month before it it's training camp. What is finding a way specifically? >> So, I think finding a way really comes down to that. You know, you look at we showed a video that had guys that even when they weren't on our team to show them that it is in you, that believe ultimately that believe in yourself. I think about you know, someone like Al catching the ball, you know, like with his head this way that I think it's that's ultimately these guys are so talented and I feel like our roster is in amazing shape, but it really comes down to people are going to make mistakes and you have to have that mindset, that inner belief, that inner faith that you you're going to make mistakes, but what are you going to do with those mistakes? How are you going to handle them? Because I mean, I don't know if there's anyone in here standing here that hasn't made a mistake, I would love to talk to you because I feel like that's just that's just how life goes. So, it's kind of more what are you going to do when that adversity comes? Are you going to stay disciplined? Are you going to stay consistent? Or are you going to go in the fetal position? And I think that kind of comes down to that find a way mindset, which is to have that inner belief. And that's what I feel like my job, the coaches job, our staff is to help these guys realize and maximize their potential. >> Carla, what way do you feel >> that um Vinny Testaverde is going to the Pro Football Hall of Fame next week. You want to present him. What did that mean to you when you got the news from him that he was >> You're going to make me cry again. >> [laughter] >> No, I mean, it's just I mean, speaking of finding a way, I mean, when I think about Adam and I know Mike, we talked about it. It's I mean, sounds like he got to stay undrafted free agent, played 24 seasons. I mean, I was laughing thinking about like talk about that's almost a quarter of a century. I mean, just I mean, at 2,673 points, what? I mean, it's just like it's just amazing. I'm so proud of him and it was such an honor because, you know, my dad loved him, our family loved him, and he was kind of that one piece, you know, when you think about putting together a team and my dad's journey, you know, to getting to those, you know, winning the one Super Bowl, but getting to two Super Bowls, and he was kind of that last piece, you know, I feel like he came in, he was like magic dust, you know, we went right to the Super Bowl that year. So, it means so much to me. I'm so excited for him. >> As you evaluated last season and you came with that motto for this year, in what way do you feel like the the team and the organization fell a little bit short or struggled in being able to find a way over the closing stretch last year? >> Well, we certainly can't use injuries as an excuse because that's something every team goes through, but I think ultimately, you know, sometimes I've talked to coaches and players about what, you know, if you haven't, you know, quite had success yet, right? You have to think about Sometimes it's important to think about where you came from, you know, where you are now, and what you want to become, and I think that's, you know, I think it's hard, you know, when we've had years of not quite getting over that hump, but I think just that's why we're kind of hammering on that is that if we have all the talent, we have everyone we need to get where we need to go, we just have to continue to make sure we're building a culture that is promoting like that inner belief and inner faith that we can do it. >> What makes you think that this year, I guess, will be different, Carly? I mean, you talked about inner belief, wanting to finish the season. What makes this year give you that feeling or that notion? >> So, James, one of the first things that comes to mind to me is, you know, that first quality in success, consistency. You know, I think when you don't have, you know, quarterback position as an example, you know, So, the leader of our team. I think it's going into the second year, Danielle, you know, seeing what we saw that first half. I mean, that's such a key thing. I mean, it's key for coaches, the way we build our scheme. It's key for Chris, the way we build our roster and filling the pieces. I mean, so that's that's kind of one example, but I think, you know, it's we have everything we need to get >> Chris was asked about the pressure he feels going into this season. Do you view this as a consequential season for Jim Irsay's future and what needs to happen to ensure that future here? >> I think even if you're Seattle, you know, I think the pressure is always there, but certainly, I mean, as I've told Chris and Shane, you know, the sense of urgency has never been higher and we have to find a way. >> I probably you mentioned a higher sense of urgency back in January. Do you feel like you felt that this off season? You know, you guys didn't do a ton in free agency. Did did did you feel like you had the higher sense of urgency leading into, obviously, now getting into the preseason? >> Uh I mean, I think, yeah, I think the sense of urgency was higher, Kevin. I think it's it's also, you know, as Chris said and as, you know, he knows we have to win. And things, you know, I was talking about my dad's, you know, I think about building that team that eventually went to the Super Bowl and getting to you know, it's goes decades back almost, you know, getting Tony, getting Peyton, eventually getting Adam, getting those pieces. But I think this year just we've got all the right guys that we need to be healthy. We've got, you know, a great quarterback room. Um we've got I think we just have to keep, you know, like I said, keep believing that we've got everything we need to get where we need to go. >> I mean, can you you've been to many training camps, obviously. Can you get a feel for an individual team in camp, like the pulse or what have you? Is there is there a feel that you have a feel yet for what you're seeing? >> So, it's only the third day and I think until the pads come on, you know, I think that everything changes, as you guys know when the pads come on, but I think you know, when I think about even during OTAs, you know, they're not there's only like a small chunk that's mandatory, but I think seeing starting then, I think seeing the guys that showed up, seeing the way guys that were hurt, that rehabbed. I mean, I think everyone is very dialed in. So, I I feel I feel really good about where we are right now. >> Your special teams coordinator said that he wants to be a coach for life. He signed like a couple days ago. Um I know it's a funny first contract. How important is it for you as the owner who's calling the shots here to try to figure out a way to get something done for him? >> Yeah. Um well, I love Jonathan. I mean, he's he's I'm really proud of the leader that he's become on our team. I mean, he's one of our pillars. He has pictures on the stadium for a reason. Um and I would love it if he would be a coach for life. >> You talked about the the the roster where it sort of needs to be, but if Chris comes to you and says, "You know, we need a receiver, and it's going to cost X million." Are you fine with that? Do you kind of leave that up to him? Or or do you sort of have a veto? >> So, I mean, Chris it's up to Chris, but he keeps me in the loop. And obviously, when, you know, it's a decision like that, you know, he would I would [crying] be involved, and he does a great job of that. Um but I think we just we're just going to see how that plays out cuz I think he's kind of in charge of the depth there. >> Is there anything Let's take a couple more. >> Is there anything in year one of being the main face of this franchise that you learned that you are carrying forward this year? Anything that surprised I know you were around it and obviously knew everything about it, but is there anything that kind of surprised you that you're taking into this season? >> Uh so, Donny, I would say what one thing is I think a lot of what I'm doing, it's really it's not a lot different than what I was doing before. So, it was interesting to me how, you know, the when your title changes, which I'm not really a big title person personally, but it's like how, you know, it's a little bit of a vibe change with some people, but I think most most people that, you know, I think I I'm very proud of the way that our family runs our organization and it's very, you know, we're family-owned and we care about our people, so I think it's kind of it's leveled out now, but at first it definitely was a little bit, me coming in the room meant being a little bit, you know, just a different vibe than it was before, but um just everyone's been so supportive through, you know, cuz it's, you know, losing our dad, losing my boss, you know, but it's just been I'm just really proud of the culture we have at our organization. >> You mentioned stability at quarterback. I know you have that with Daniel coming into year two, but he also has an injury history, so how do you, I guess, balance both of those things? >> Well, I mean, I feel like every player, has injuries and I just think Daniel has, like I said, he has a he has a find-a-way mindset. I mean, the level of preparation that he did even it was a week after his Achilles and he was out he was out in walk-through on his little wheelie thing. I mean, to me, like yesterday morning I'm working out and he's six it's like 6:00 a.m. and he's coming out of the quarterback room, so he did and he did that all through even his injury, you know, guys could There are guys that could choose to stay in the training room and not be involved, but instead he kind of just found he found a way to help, you know, the quarterback room when when Philip was there and Riley and Anthony and he's just been he's just such a great leader and I just believe that I believe he's going to find a way to figure it out and stay healthy and get us where we need to go. >> He told us his last question here that he wouldn't have signed an extension cuz he feels like they need to win. How where have you guys left off discussions about Daniel's future with you? >> So, it's day three in training camp and like I said, I believe we have everyone here to get us where we need to go. Um Chris wouldn't be here if I didn't believe that and we're just going to have to see how things play out. >> And I'm Jonathan um in player extensions during the season at large, do you feel like um you'd be open to or the franchise would be open to signing extensions knowing how much is riding on this season and then how much could change um going forward next year depending on how the season goes? >> Yeah, I mean that's something that Chris Chris is looking into and he keeps you informed on it, but yeah, if it's you know, if it makes sense and we would certainly do that.
