title: Sean McVay, Tyler Higbee & Kobie Turner Address the Media After First Practice With Pads
text: All right, guys. You guys go ahead. >> Uh scheduled rest days for Miles and Devante today? >> Yes, absolutely. Yeah, my hand You know what's funny? I don't even know what I did. It was It looks worse than what it is. What do you think, Jerry? >> I don't know what happened there. >> I [laughter] I don't even know. I I think I got excited hitting somebody's shoulder pads or whatever and too thin-skinned, I guess, huh? So, I'm good. >> What I know he wasn't out there today, but what have been your impressions of Miles Garrett, his impact on you guys? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, I think first and foremost as a person, you know, just how receptive he is to Joe Woods coach, Chris Shula, what a great teammate he's been in terms of imparting wisdom. It's really cool even just going in the outside linebacker room, feeling the vibe in there. And then, you know, in the team meetings, he he's been great and then his on-the-field play, his presence, you feel him. You know, you guys have heard me talk about that. Certain defensive guys, you just feel them. They elicit a certain amount of attention where he can really change the math for you. It's what he's done throughout his career and it's obviously a limited inventory where it's been a couple practices without pads on, but his ability to be able to understand sets, have real reactionary rushes where you're not predetermined, um very, very impressed and and incredibly impressed with the human as well. Really excited that he's on our on our team. >> Coach, I asked Puka about this the other day, but he's become so proficient at getting open. How have you seen him grow at reading defenses throughout his career? >> Well, I think repetition is the mother of learning and he's got a quarterback that he's got an incredible rapport with. He's one of those guys that when you watch him, even going back to his career at BYU, the game just makes sense to him. Certain guys have a great spatial awareness and he's so tough, he doesn't flinch on inside routes. He showed a real capacity to be able to win on the perimeter last year. Um and the way that he works at he's only getting better, but very conscientious. You know, I think the cool thing is is you look at he's had a chance to learn from two of the best and two of the most cerebral receivers and Cooper Kupp and Devante Adams now and he's been a sponge from them. He's got great coaches. Um it's been really cool watching Rob Calbrese and Eric Yarber, um you know, continue to lean on you know, him lean on them and then also Robert Woods, you know, it's awesome having him on the coaching staff and Nate did a great job with those guys last year. So, he's got a lot of people and he's got great humility and curiosity to continue to learn and um he's been outstanding. >> Talk about what Robert Woods has brought to the staff so far. >> Well, swag. He's up the athleticism of the coaching staff. Um but just you know, what's really cool is is he was one of the guys that really set the foundation of what the culture is. Mentally and physically tough players that are smart. They love to compete. Um they've got a competitive stamina. He represents all those things and then you know, what's really cool is is he's got a passion for trying to be able to help people grow and you can see he's pouring into all of the players in that room from top to bottom and and you can see how much respect they have. He's loving it and uh I'm really grateful that he decided to come coach with us. >> Sean, you talked to start camp the opportunity that exists for the two young quarterbacks to kind of step up. Today was another step along that way. How would you say that they have responded to that challenge in this kind of a unique way that you've gone about it and give them a lot of opportunities? >> It's been good, you know, because I think it serves, you know, I think it benefits two things where it gives them reps that they wouldn't get otherwise, Vinnie. Um I thought both Stetson and Ty did a nice job. We'll go back and we'll look at the tape and it's always hard to feel because we're not tackling those guys. Are you really reading with your feet? Are you speeding it up if the rush ends up getting there? Um but the way that we want to be able to think about what's the best thing for Matthew and then how do we figure out what does it look like to be able to bring those guys along and Dave Ragone does a great job with that room, but I've been pleased with those guys. I think uh you know, I think they've done really well. I I mentioned it, you know, Stetson is really taking incredible strides, done a lot of good things and I think Ty has improved tremendously from the spring until now as well. >> Obviously, there's a lot of time between now and the season opener, but not a whole lot of time. What exactly do you need to see from one of those two to give you that that that confidence that you can go into a season with either of those guys. >> You know, it's hard to I can't put up my finger on anything. I think it's really what we ask of our team. It's It's let's stack days. Let's be present. We're not to Australia yet. You know, we're just starting the second block. This was our first day in pads. And so, felt like both of those guys had a lot of good things that they can learn on learn from and thought they did a nice job taking what the defense gave them. And you know, we'll look at the film, but I've been really pleased with both of them. You can see it's important to them. They're intentional. Their teammates like them. They've got good command of the huddle. And so, a lot of positives you know, from both those guys. >> Where have you noticed improvement from Ty from when he first got here to to where he's at now? >> Yeah, I think really even just you know, from the things we talked about in the spring Nate just even being able to call the plays in the huddle where we get in and out. When the games are real, it's a 40-second play clock and they don't stop it where we get the ability to be able to stop it in 25 seconds out of a quarter or clock stoppage. And so, he's done really well. And then I think you know, some of the even things mechanically about being able to speed up his release. Um, you know, some of the timing and rhythm in terms of with his lower half being married up with the routes. And you know, Dave does a great job. And those are some of the things I've seen from him. >> Couple more guys. >> Can you uh tell what Higbee's role is at this point in his career? >> Yeah, Tyler is I mean you look at it. He's the greatest tight end in Rams history. Um, he's got an incredible He's been an incredible leader. And you know, what I think is is we've got four tight ends that have played a lot of meaningful football for us that are going to continue to play meaningful football. Um, what that looks like is game plan dependent, but he's going to be a big factor in what we do. Uh, the the beauty is is that he's got the ability to be a real contributor in the pass game, in the run game. He can play in line. He can be a move player for us. And he's also shown proficiency as a protector. And so, And really I could say the same about Colby, about Davis, and about Terrance Ferguson as well. And so, those young guys have a lot to learn from from those guys. But uh, Higs is uh, you know, he's one of the all-time glue guys. You know, we say great leaders unite everyone. And he's one of those guys that has just such a great vibe and a great way about himself. And um, you know, I'm sure when you guys talk to him there's just a good energy and vibe and it's the same influence and impact he has on his teammates and on his coaches. >> Of course it's still early you guys just put on pads but what have you seen from a young lineman like Keegan Trosin and what have you seen from >> It it doesn't seem too big for him you know he seems real steady secure to be able to take coaching you see the agility and the flexibility to be able to play on the right and left sides of the line you know Wendy does a great job of really kind of throwing those guys into the mix those young linemen and you know you're either sinking or swimming and he's doing a good job keeping his head above water and he's got a lot of great guys to learn from in that room. >> So Sean McDermott watching practice with you how did that come about what's he like then? >> Well he worked with Ryan Wendell you know Ryan Wendell was with him before and and Sean and I have known each other just from coaching against one another and you know we were on the competition committee together and you know he's a good guy and and I think he's just coming around and being able to pick up you know I think all of us as coaches are constantly curious and trying to just be able to kind of share with one another and it was great to have him out here today. >> And then Jerry last one. >> Jordan Whittington steady consistent you know a guy that can really do a lot of different things for us Maria he's obviously been a really good contributor on offense and in you know the special teams phases for us and he's one of those guys that you know I think the game honors toughness and he's one of those guys that the game honors because of the way that he plays and incredibly selfless you know he makes the plays when he gets his opportunities but he also gets just as excited springing a block for one of our running backs and he's a great teammate love everything Jordan Whittington is about. >> Uh any update on Aaron and or is that something that realistically you don't expect until you guys are done with camp? >> Well it'll be here's what I would tell you there won't be any news on that front until we get back to Woodland Hills you know we have some different things which you know I know I totally understand what I don't want to do is put any there's some conversations that we've had we've loosely had some different timelines that are kind of temporary. I want to keep those between us just, you know, if something unforeseen happens out of respect for for him and the situation, but I know this, you know, that things are going in the right direction and if there's an arrow, it's trending upwards. >> As coach Ford asked you about his future >> You know what that is? >> [laughter] >> That is it is ooh, what do you think? I don't know. But no, you know, well, that'll be something that I think once we get back to Woodland Hills, we'll have a better idea of what that timeline looks like. There won't be any decision in anything in terms of Aaron's situation while we're here. That's kind of already been, you know, set out, you know, when we've talked, you know, since the last, you know, for the last couple weeks. Okay? >> Thanks. >> Thanks, guys. Was he at the facility? >> What's up, y'all? How we doing? >> How are you? >> Good. Good. Good so far. First day of pads, you know. Early feels feels good to be back out here running around with the boys and playing football, real football. >> When you look at some of the other tight ends that are in your room, can you see how they've elevated over an off season? >> Oh, yeah, definitely. I mean, we've No, I said this, you know, last year we had one of the deepest tight ends, you know, we've added added to that this year and you know, it's a very deep tight end room, probably the deepest that I've ever been a part of. Um and so it's it's fun being able to, you know, with the with the depth we've been able to do some different things and you know, about continuing to build on that and you know, did some good things last year and about seeing how we can refine and perfect it and get even better this year. >> Coach just brought up your leadership on this team. How have you viewed your role as a leader being with the organization for so long? >> Yeah, I mean, it's it's you know, been a blessing. Grateful. I understand it's kind of rare to be in the same position for that long and so you know, I just try to take advantage of it, you know, I'm being myself and I love this game. I love competing. You know, I try to try to just, you know, translate and help however however I can. >> Tyler, building off of being a leader and and pouring in some of the younger guys especially in the tight end room and and Ty Sambrailo. How do you pour into those younger guys like Jake Ferguson and Vance Ferguson and Ty Sambrailo? >> Yeah, you know, just being myself, you know. The better those guys are, the better this team's going to be. So, I just try to do what I can to help and help those guys be the best version of themselves and then you know, at the end at the end of the day it's going to make us a better football team. So. >> There's a really strong camaraderie amongst the tight end room. What's it like just having that again and and carrying over and having everybody return from >> Yeah, it's it's it's special. And again, in this league how how there can be so much turnover to have the same unit come back this year and you know, after the the fun and and some of the things we've had, you know, last year with getting all the guys on the field and some of the 13 personnel stuff, you know, the more we can do is you know, the more guys we can get out there. And it's fun. We had a great great great group, great year last year and you know, working to build on that and it's it's special to have the same guys back and get after it again. >> You've been around long enough to see this organization make some pretty ruthless decisions if they think you'll make the team better on the field. How does it feel knowing [clears throat] that they still believe that you can contribute and and have a have a key impact with this team on the >> Yeah, it's cool. I mean, you know, I'm again, I understand how rare it is to be in the same position or on the same team for as long as I have been. I don't take that with don't take that lightly. You know, so I give everything I got. You know, I try to try to be be the best I can, best teammate, best player. You know, I come in here and I work every day. You know, I expect to earn it. I don't feel like it's like I'm just going to be here because I've been here that long. You know what I mean? It's like I got to come out here and earn this thing every day. So, you know, I I I try to do that and take pride in that and and come to work every day and just be the best I can. >> Regarding the world's fastest wide receiver >> Mhm. >> What did you bring to the table as a player? >> No doubt. You know, he was a special player. Um, to play alongside him for years and uh, we're actually just talking about today. I think it was five seasons together. Um, he's a special player. Um, and so it's great been great to have him. You know, I've seen him first hand do what he does on the field. You know, for him to bring that, um, to that receiver room and and add to that, it's uh, it's a special. You know, not only can he coach it, but he can actually, you know, show these guys how to do it cuz he's done it. Um, so, you know, it's it's great to have him. >> You been through a lot health wise the past couple seasons. Just where you feeling at and how good was it to have a full regular camp? >> Yeah, feel great. Yeah, you know, um, I was talking to somebody today about couple years ago I was in there rehabbing, you know, 6 hours a day, you know, knee and shoulder and uh, having a full off season, feel healthy, feel good, and ready to go, and uh, they got a good plan with me, you know, I think during this camp, and uh, yeah, feel great. >> What have been your impressions of Myles Garrett so far? >> He's special, man. He's special. Um, you know, seeing a guy like that move the way that he does at that size, uh, it's impressive. It's impressive. So, I'm I'm happy I'm getting to go against him in camp and not in the regular season. So, he's out there embarrassing me on, you know, national TV, but uh, yeah, it's uh, it's special. It's going to be good work for us. It's good work for our for our edges, and uh, we're lucky to have him on our team. >> One week into camp, what stands out to you overall about this offense? >> I'm sorry? >> Yeah, you know, we're just getting it. I mean, we have a lot of guys returning this year. Um, you know, did some good things, and uh, you know, I think just the mindset, we expect to be great. Um, so, coming in working, and and nobody's complacent, you know, even after having some success last year. Um, we want to be better, and uh, expect to be better, and everybody just comes ready to work. So. >> Obviously Stansly has been around for a bit with you guys. Ty has been with you guys for a bit. What have you seen from both of them that have really really grown so far? >> Yeah, I mean, seeing Stansly Stansly's progression over the, you know, last couple years, it's it's uh, you know, it's impressive. Um, and then seeing Ty just from, you know, OTAs to now, um, seeing his progression, and you know, and that's what camp's for. We come out here to work, you know. I said it before, but it's easy to football, and it's like we're kind of here to work and get better and you know, keep making strides in the right direction. You know, to peak at the right time when the season starts. Yeah. Heck of a player, you know. Hall of Fame player. One of the best to ever best ever do it at his position. Um So, you know, we'll we'll see, you know. I hope he hope he does, you know, but we'll see. We'll see. >> Hey Tyler, what do you like about today's scrimmage? What do you think you did well and what do you think you need to really get stronger on? >> Uh to obviously today, you're not getting the pads on for the first time playing some real football. You know, we were I was talking to you know, Colby pre-practice and he's like this is the first time we've put on pads since you know, the season ended. You know, OTAs you're not in pads and the first first first block we're out here in no pads. So, it's nice to play some real football. Much you're always shaking some rust off, you know. Personally, want to get a little tighter hands in run game. You know, but but again, it was it's nice to get the pads on and play some real football cuz that's what we do on Sundays, so. >> One more thing now. >> Last one guys. >> Tyler, the word on the street is if you guys don't get to the Super Bowl and win it, it was a bad season. Do you guys talk about that? >> No, I mean that's that's a long way away, you know. We got We got to go handle business week one first, you know. And prior to that, we got to come out here and handle business tomorrow. Work and get better. That's all you You got to be where your feet are. Can't really think too far ahead, too far in the past. And yeah, just come out here and work tomorrow. That's that's kind of where our mindset's at. >> Thanks everyone. >> All right. Thank you guys. Yeah, thank you guys. Have a good night. >> Oh, this is cool. I'm team I'm great. I'm great. Sun's shining, another day of ball. Be out here with the guys. It doesn't get better than that. Yeah, it feels good. This is real ball now. You know, all the other stuff is cool. You get to work your craft, but uh nothing like, you know, setting the pads, getting some real ball in. So, it's cool to to start inching a little bit closer and closer to the season. >> What have been your impressions of Myles Garrett? >> Yeah, he's a freak athlete, for sure. Um, you know, he won Defensive Player of the Year for a reason. Um, he's a really good talent, and he he pays a lot of attention to I see him taking notes all the time. So, um now the biggest thing is going to be how do we incorporate him into our rush? How do we rush for as one? How do we bring him in, you know, a part of our group? Excuse me. And uh continue to build that camaraderie that uh you know, to have the connection to be able to communicate non-verbally, verbally, um to just understand kind of what he's doing and for him to understand what we're doing as well. So, uh but that's what camp is for, to continue to to bring things together. And yeah, it's definitely exciting to have him out there with us. >> Is it hard not to dream a little bit when you know he captivates so much attention from opposing teams that it's like, "Hey, this opens up opportunities for all of us as well." >> Yeah, I mean, we definitely understand the opportunities that should get opened up. Um, and if, you know, those opportunities don't open up and and they leave him soloed up, then he's going to take advantage. So, it's cool to to definitely be able to have a front uh where you know any one of us can win, and to know, all right, if there's going to be more attention here, then it's time for us to eat. So, um it it's it's a really good challenge as well to make sure that our toolbox is nice and sharpened up so that when it comes season time, uh we're ready to win at a high clip. >> Kobe, Coach McVay mentioned that Byron Young was learning so much from Myles Garrett looking at you. What are some of the things that you've learned from him so far? >> Yeah, honestly, um I'm just continuing to, I guess, understand what it is that he does. There's some things, you know, I I heard it all rookie year uh with AD where it's like, all right, there's some things that he can do that, you know, nobody else can really do. There's some things that Myles can do that nobody else can really do. Uh but, you know, I've been able to appreciate some of the simplicity of a lot of his rushes, right? Like, he's just beating you off the snap. Uh he's getting to his rip and then he's able to work at the top of the rush and he works at the top of the rush really well. He's able to bend corners and so I feel like I can be similar in the way of I feel like my top of the rush is what makes me a really good player as well. So figuring out ways to just sometimes just dumb it down, just get to my rip or get to my arm over or whatever it is, get to that hip, get a good get off and get to the top of the rush and allow, you know, my top of the rush mechanics, whether it be the rip, coming back out and countering with the hump, a spin, whatever it be to take over. >> Spending time around Byron Young these past few years, what is it about him that's led him to kind of find a new gear each year? >> Yeah, I mean, dude is just a worker. You see it in the locker room, you see it just around the building, but you also see it on the tape, right? Whenever there's a play, I think of Colts game, Daniel Jones, really the play that I feel set the tone for that game. Daniel Jones was known for, you know, having a little bit of speed to be able to get around the edge, extend plays. Byron runs him down and he's not the same for the rest of that game. And so I think the effort he's able to play with and just he continues to build confidence the more and more that he feels comfortable in this defense the more and more that he feels that he has clarity about what his assignment is. From there he just takes off and I mean, you guys saw it last year. I'm looking forward to see what this year brings for him. >> It was an eventful off season for you on a personal level. Can you talk tell us how that influence impacts you kind of coming into camp? >> Yeah. Yeah, no, it's been honestly, like, it's been the greatest off season of my life. I got married last off season and that's a close second. But for me and Alyssa to be able to bring Rowan into this world and to be able to spend four really good months of every day being with her and and spending, you know, so much of that quality time has been great. So it gives you a little bit more purpose. It gives you a little bit more reason and it also gives you a lot more focus, too. Like, when I'm in the building and I I I've I've always carried myself in this way and when I've been in the building it's been all about business. Uh but especially now because I'm trying to get home to baby girl and spend some time with her before she has to go to sleep. Um but yeah, I mean it gives you a new purpose and yeah, I'm excited to to be able to represent her as a part of the name that's on the back of my jersey as well this upcoming year. >> Kobe, we see the musical notes on your thigh pads and obviously when you're not playing football, you're you're singing and playing the piano. How do you think playing music and making music music has made you a better football player? >> Yeah, I feel like the attention to detail, the time spent on my craft. Like there's so much time uh in the off-season or even during the season where I just sit at the keyboard or like right before the walk-through today I was playing guitar and just vibing kind of sitting there and just having fun and I feel like that same thing applies to me football-wise. Like whether it's time during the off-season, I go back through. Now I've only had three seasons, so it's not that much film, but I've gone back through every game of my three seasons basically and looked at, all right, what's worked, what hasn't worked, what can I continue to build off of. So I think a lot of that attention to detail and then I also think the camaraderie aspect of it, right? Like spending so much of my life being in a choir or having to, you know, conduct a group or to arrange music for a group, whatever that's been, it's been about bringing together different voices, bringing together different personalities, different people towards one common goal. And I think that's played a lot into my leadership as well uh to be able to bring together, you know, all of these different personalities that are in my room, all of the different personalities on this team um into one, you know, succinct group. And obviously I don't take all the credit for that or, you know, whatever that I I don't take a ton of credit for that, but I do think that that plays a really big role. I'm used to working with people and that's to me is the best thing about both of these things that I get to do with music, it's being able to connect with other people through my music. And with football, it's being able to connect with those guys in that locker room to be able to play 11 as one, to rush for as one um and to be able to celebrate each and every person's success. >> Does your baby girl have a favorite song yet? >> Hmm, I sing to her a ton of How Deep Is Your Love by the Bee Gees. That's my go-to and she like she chills out from that one. But between that, my mom sings her You Are My Sunshine sunshine, so I'll steal that a little bit. Um and then there's a Spanish song coming on the porch with no mas throw me a contract that the grandparents sing to her and so we all kind of sing that and we bring in all of the cousins and stuff like that. It's a really fun song, so all of those. >> How did you How did you get the custom pads put together for you? >> I forget. This is I think it's Tredecal. I seen I saw another guy get some custom pads and I was like, I know exactly what I want. Like throw some throw a treble clef and throw a bass clef on them. I don't have them. My treble clef is back in Woodland Hills, but but yeah, I saw that and I was like, this is absolutely what I'm going to go for. And so I've been rocking them since then. >> Well, we can do >> Last one, what have you seen overall from what this defense has been able to do this season? >> Yeah, I think we have a lot of really great flashes of our potential. It's about continuing to stack days. Um and you know, it's camp. It's going to have a lot of ups and downs. But when we're playing all together and all as one, we're a scary front. We're a scary defense. Front end, back end, at the second level. Like we we have a complete package of a defense. So it's about putting it together, coming together, being on the same page and we're going to go and ball out this year. Thank you. Appreciate you. >> Thank you.

title: Calen Bullock on Confidence, Communication and Taking the Ball Away | Full Q&A
text: How you doing? >> It's okay. Hey, what is the something that you have been able to see with having a read relationship with you? >> Uh Reed came in uh smart guy uh just picked up he was just rolling. So, just hitting the field with him, him going out there showing and communicating with me, we're on the same page, it makes our both our jobs easier. >> So, you're talking about you know kind of the fact that he's won a Super Bowl, he's been with the AP. What have you Have you noticed anything that's different with a guy that has won a Super Bowl and that he's brought to you? >> it is his knowledge, his work ethic. Uh like you said, he been he been to the Super Bowl. He knows what it takes. He's seen how a Super Bowl team looks like from offense, defense, special teams. He knows how it looks. So, just picking his brain in the meeting rooms and seeing what he see out there in the field, it helps me a lot also on the field with him. >> Every year is different, but with you guys returning nine starters defensively, just how easy is it for a transition to get the new guys that are joining the squad to kind of just catch up to speed and you guys have everything kind of under control? >> Uh you said how easy is it for the new guys to catch up to speed? Uh for me uh I was saying it's it's gotten easier year by year. Uh which it helps me a lot just go out there, you know, being in the defense for 3 years, I'm comfortable in positions. I know the defense in and out. So, just for me I'm out I'm out there comfortable. I'm out there playing with confidence cuz when you know the playbook, I always tell the young guys, when you know the playbook and you know what you're out there doing, you're not thinking too much, it helps you go out there and make plays and play with some confidence. >> What have you seen from Kamar as far as you want him taking that next step? >> Uh KD comes in every single day, he's the same person. Very consistent. Uh year in year out, he shows why he's one of the best corners. And he he shows you by his game and you know, Kamar, he's a guy a lot of people probably don't know, he's a smart football player. He's you going to see him in the building he's walking around watching film all day and just him elevating his game on that level just knowing what to expect knowing the down and distance what what to expect out the receivers it just shows his level of game how it improved each year year in year in year out. Every day yeah, I get to see everything it's the same way so I would say me and him we always watching film together and we always if we not with each other we sending videos to each other how you see this how you want to play this if we on the same side how you want me to communicate this or drive this how do you see it so that just helps us when we going out there it brings us closer and this off season work we put in together brings us closer to on the field. Is there anything that you specifically want to work on in your game this off season? I would say just you know me being down more not just in the post all the time I think teams know I'm the post safety so just me trying to improve my game in other places. When you do bring in a new safety to your defense like Reed what's the most important thing he has to do so that he does fit in and doesn't disrupt what you guys have? It's not it's not even just him trying to fit in or disrupt what we got. He's he's a part of the team too he's part of defense too so we're playing around him also so if he sees something he communicate it we going to play if he tell me something I'm going to play what he see and that's just how we all build with each other we got each other's back it's not it's not the case of him fitting in with us we we welcome him with open arms and it's not even like he's slowing us down he came in he was rolling he knew the defense as soon as he came. I think it's the plays seeing the plays last year that we messed up on I think last year it was a lot of plays that we wish we could have got back. Uh it was games we could have had a lot of shutouts, but it was our mistakes. So, I would say our mindset is just being consistent each day, every single day, no matter what. Just being the same people every single day. Like you said, we set the the bar high last year, so we know that this year we got to go out there and show it again. >> Two players last year that were fully healthy, Jake Plummer, Jaylen Smith, and safety Jaylen Reed. Um you know, they're coming back now fully healthy. They didn't play last year. When you're on that sideline and you're watching them in the game, what have you noticed about them? >> Uh their confidence level. Uh them guys, they just been itching just to get back on the field, especially especially Jaylen. Him missing the whole season last year, you know, seeing him go out there in week three, uh week one through week three, uh him on special teams, he was making a lot of plays, being very impact player, but seeing him in this camp, and he's becoming a smarter football player, and his confidence level is really high, and he's a very key piece to us. Even Jaylen Reed, he got to go in in the back end of the season, and he played for us in the playoffs. So, now this year is him just having that confidence in his head, and still having the mindset that he's a key piece of this defense. And when his number get called, he show up every single day, both of them. >> Talk to us much about CJ now in his second year in this offense and the way that it's going. >> Say it again. >> Talk to us much about CJ and the offense now that they're second year with you. >> I would say CJ, uh just in this offense he's more comfortable out there, uh making better reads, making better decisions with the ball. And you know, he's our leader, so we talk to him what we see on the defense. If we see something, we talk about it in the locker room, and he tell us too. So, just that level of confidence we got a level of confidence in him, and he got confidence in himself, and that's all we really need from him. And we know when he has that confidence, he's one of the best in the league. >> You got 10 interceptions in the two seasons. How do you handle the balance between making a play on the ball versus making sure you make a play on >> Uh I'm trying to make a play on the ball every single time. It's It's a gamble. title: Minnesota Vikings Team Press Conferences | Training Camp, August 1
text: Man, it's good, man. It's been a long time. But, uh I've been waiting, man. And uh football right around the corner for me, so I've just been waiting to go out there and hit somebody. >> How do you describe that anticipation and and wanting to be out there? >> Uh I mean, we go out there for 18 games, 17 games, whatever it is. And then, we get off break. And then, I get my little break like 2 weeks, and then I'm ready to go back to hit somebody, so I don't even know. It's just a defensive mindset, man. I just love playing backer. I love going hitting people, building everything. >> Fans are out here today. What what kind of energy does that give practice? >> Uh it's it's it's going to be a good practice. Uh you know, it's like it's like playing in US Bank. Uh you get people watching you, a lot of people watching you, and everybody just want to do that, and do this, do that, you know? So, they just want to go out there and have fun. Just We're going to keep the energy up today. >> What's your first impression of Jamal Adams? >> Uh Jamal Adams, I mean, I watched him uh watched him growing up. Um he's a great player, man. Played safety, played uh and then he transferred over to backer. I saw him last year a little bit. Uh He he's a good guy. Um good vet uh to look up to. Um He he he actually comes to me a little bit for help. Uh and that's cool. Uh so, I just try to do what I can to help him and then learn from him, too. >> Fans being at practice, does that add anything to you? >> Oh, it always adds it it adds all the, you know, motivation in the world. It adds all the the fun. You know, they bring all the energy every time they come. I just love it. >> How do you describe kind of how you're you're approaching this training camp? >> My approach is the same as it always has been. Just day by day, getting better, seeing what happened the day before, improving from that. And it's been that way my whole life. Just keep climbing, keep taking steps, and just seeing what it is I can improve on. And then, I'm going to Guys are the limit. This guy's not even the limit. It's beyond that, you know? >> I guess yeah, going off of last year, what was something that you like uh saw and wanted to build on? >> Going off last year, I definitely wanted to build on my run game, my pass protecting. Um There was some good, some bad, but there's always things you want to improve on. and then special teams, uh same thing, just trying to improve on the you know the the technique, the fundamentals, and just making sure the play style is to the best it can be, being violent, being being who you know I'm made to be. >> How do you approach kind of the competition in camp, the the individuals, and how do you parse that out with you know it's your still on the same team, but this is the time to compete? >> Yeah, I mean that helps everybody get better at the end of the day. That's what competition is, and I welcome it in all aspects of my life if I'm being honest. And it's really end of the day it's me versus me. I mean everybody I see understands that, they hear that, but the truth of the matter is I got to be better than I was yesterday. I got to be better than I was last year, last month, you know, a few months ago, and that's the goal every single day. And I just keep doing that, and then you know, let the chips fall where they may, but I know it's out of my hands. Uh I'm just going to be the best I can be every day and keep improving. >> It was great, yeah. Uh it's just good to get out here with all the guys, kind of get in the system, and be uh getting live reps out here. >> Yeah, you were taking first team reps, like what was that like? How did that feel? >> Yeah, it definitely just a blessing to be out there with all these talented guys that I kind of grew up watching on TV, too. So, uh it's just a real feeling to be out there, but I can't take that lightly. I got to go out there and show out what I can do, what they brought me here to do. >> Ready to strap the pads on? >> Yeah, I'm definitely ready for that. Today was a little bit of a taste with the little tiny pads on today, so I'm ready to get those pads on and actually start hitting a little bit. >> What do you feel like the big the biggest learning curve has been so far? >> Um I would just say Flo's tricky defense. I would just say that, uh and then learning different spots, so remembering what different packages we were in, and what spot I'm in, and know knowing what my responsibility is within the defense. >> What is the process of starting as stack backer, now being on the edge today? Like what what is the process that's allowed that to happen so quickly, I guess? >> Yeah, I would just say uh they told me first thing when I got here that they wanted me to be versatile and be able to play a lot of things. That's how that going to get on the field. So, I didn't take that lightly. I took that opportunity to study pretty much every single backer position. So, when the time come, I played will all spring. Then when we came here, I came out here in fall camp, they were saying, "I want you to play some Sam." I was ready for the job because I'd been studying over the break and throughout spring the whole time. I want to know every position so that I can stay out there as much as possible. >> How's that process of studying all those parts look like for you? Is it like a lot of just reading through it? Is it practicing kind of physically? What is it? >> Yeah, I would say for me, I definitely like to just look at the X's and O's on some paper, draw it out myself, and then I like to see it on the screen, see the guys from last year running through the defenses in the in the live game situation, see how it kind of plays out. And then I also like to get out here and go through the motions myself even if I have nobody out here with me. I'll kind of just like for conditioning too, I'll get to my drop and then make sure that I'm yelling out my responsibility before the next play so that I get that conditioning and so that I can also get that recall for every single play. >> Were you versatile in college? Like have you always prided yourself on your versatility throughout your football life? >> I would say so, yeah. Ever since I played defensive end basically my first 2 years of college, but I got recruited to college as an athlete. They didn't really know where to put me. They were like, "We need you at DN, so you're going to play DN." So, I learned how to play DN. I thought that I was a pretty good DN and then they said, "Hey, we need you to move back to Mike backer. We need you at backer." So, then I played backer that my last year at Central Arkansas. And then when I got to Cincinnati, I played all three spots. So, yeah, I just pride myself on being versatile and just working hard and trying to get to the ball every play. >> I know you talked about the studying, but what do you what do you think is your biggest strength throughout your life that's allowed you to be so adaptable? >> I would just say my the chip on my shoulder and just the hard work that I put in there every single day. I'm not the the best, I'm not the fastest, I'm not the most talented, but I'm going to work harder than anybody on the field. >> Seems like you're getting a lot of reps and opportunities. So, how would you kind of assess yourself through these first few days? >> Uh, >> mean, I really think about it as a snowball effect. You know, how how much better can I get? You know, what I do right now or the rep that just passed is not enough. So, execution, it has to be at a all-time high. The mental, it has to be at a all-time high. And not even that, just fellowship when I'm on the sideline, making sure I'm being a great teammate, not just a great player. And so, trying to do that and being real intentional about that, that has helped not only me as a person, but my style of play when I'm on the field, just to go out there and execute at an elite level. >> What was your preparation like from getting a taste of this in mini camp and OTAs to like getting to the summer, like kind of getting an idea of what you need to know for Brian Flores' defense? >> Yeah, treat every treat every moment like it's a game day, like I'm prepared for a game. Like me coming out here right now, I treated it like it was a Super Bowl, because I don't want getting to a Super Bowl or getting to preseason versus the Giants or week one versus the Packers for it to be that. When I'm out here, okay, we're playing the Giants this rep. Okay, we're playing the Packers this rep. Okay, now we're in the Super Bowl this rep. How am I going to combat? How am I going to gauge this bad rep and turn it into a great play this next rep. And so, and that's the thing about Brian Flores, he only has one standard and it doesn't he doesn't shy away from it. Everyone he holds everyone to the same standard and so, that not only pushes the team, but pushes us individually to hold each other up to that same standard, man. >> You had a couple of big breakups there in one of those 11 >> [laughter] >> 11 periods. Just tell us about kind of getting in there and getting breakup on Justin Jefferson. >> Yeah, I mean, it's never about the guy across from me. It's all about me. You know, knowing myself is better than knowing my opponent. You know, how I can't let him speed up my tempo. I can't Oh, that's Justin Jefferson out there. No, that's a receiver out there. It's all about me at the end of the day. So, and being a cornerback, that's what you That's how you got to think out there, man, because it's one of the hardest positions in in the game. And so, you can't let who you're going against affect how you play because then that's me not trusting my technique. That's me not executing at the level I know I can. So, first things first, having confidence in myself. And I mean, that's what helped me go out there and just perform the way I do. It's never about them, always about me. >> How does that help you adjust though to the NFL when you get to face the best wide receiver in the entire league in practice? >> Yeah, like I said, nameless, faceless opponent, man. That's how I think about it, man. If there's no name to him and they don't got a face. It's not about status. It's not about the receiver. And at the end of the day, I played on the defense we play in, it's team defense. It's no hero ball out there as Brian Flores always say, man. So, going out there, how can I how can I make sure that I'm doing my one 11th one 11th on the field a part of this championship wheel to keep it rolling. And so, I mean, that's what helps me be in the NFL. That's what helps me stay grounded in my cleats, man, and go out there and execute. >> Was that nameless face more talented than other nameless faces? [laughter] >> No, he did he definitely is more talented. >> It is, but if there's a movie out there I I can't remember I think it's Thunderstruck and that was the first time I heard the saying where hard work beats talent when talent fails to work hard. So, I mean, I I tie that to that statement when I say nameless, faceless opponents. And that goes back to what I previously said. It's never about who's across from me, but about me and what can I do and how am I being how am I playing a part in this championship wheel. >> If you think back to when you were drafted a few months ago, what's the biggest thing you've learned? >> It's not about it's just not about football. If you think you if this is my best, my best is not enough. And so, thinking thinking back to that draft and being where I am now, you have to get better. You know, every day is an opportunity to come out here and not only just pull my best, but make somebody else better. Because going if whether I'm going against Justin Jefferson or Juwan Jennings, he's expecting me to go 100% so he can get the best work possible. So he can get the best rep and get the best improvement out of this possible. So it's not just me out there, you know, he's counting on me to play my best too. And so that's one thing I learned being in the NFL right now today. >> So >> Yeah, rookie is is exactly how they explain it, but you know, it's fun. I can't wait to go through the process of being a rookie, so I'm just taking it day by day and you know, just living my dream out right now. >> What was like the biggest learning curve for you this week? >> Um I don't know. I can't single anything out. I'll just say that um You know, sir. Coach Flo is is a very, you know, demanding coach. He has a standard and the standard is continuously going to give get raised. But you know, every day I got to come in and meet the new standard, so that's the hard part, understanding Coach Flo. >> So you know, pads on one way or another, how much are you looking forward to that? that's that's you know, that's part of that's the real football, but um I'm excited. It's just ready to get out here and you know, be able to be physical, but also take care of our guys, make sure we have everybody we need, so >> First time of a void that so you can run on it. Do you look at it as an opportunity to maybe come in here and play a lot right away? >> I'm just going day by day, boss. Um I'm just worrying about tomorrow or the rest of today right now. I'm not worried about tomorrow when I get to tomorrow, but however that pans out is however it's going to pan out and I'm going to just be ready for whatever my opportunity does arise. >> Who are some of the guys that you've had conversations with just trying to break things down for you? >> Uh Josh. Telly's Telly's like um I he's like my big brother. Um And you know, we have a really good relationship, but I can't really single him out because you know, you know, Murph helped me out a lot, you know, Zay helps me out a lot, Theo helps me out a lot. All the guys in that room that have been here for years are are constantly helping me out trying to get me up to speed and, you know, get me to understand why they do it this way, but Telly's Telly's my guy, man. I love him. >> How comfortable are you feeling fitting into this defense right now? >> Uh I feel comfortable. Um but you know, things can change day-to-day, so you know, I just got to be quick on my toes and whatever Flo needs me to do, that's just how I'm going to be. If I'm uncomfortable doing it, as long as I get the job done, I get the job done.

And so we see the a similar pattern to where the split of first team reps is not perfectly 50/50. It leans ever so slightly toward Kyler Murray. What does that mean for you to have that energy, excitement? >> It's really just one of those things. So I feel like with the great energy we start off right leads up to a good practice >> getting ready to get the pass mentally physically what does that do just to know that it's time >> uh you know really it's just a bunch of things that going in that protecting the ball protecting our quarterback just things like that you know uh without pads it's more of you know slower motion type of thing but with pads I feel like more quicker more faster and you know we can actually get into it >> kind of wide open how do you set yourself apart >> uh I mean really we all just it's a crazy question honestly but we all just work together honestly so I don't really think you know I don't really look at it as going in as okay running back two running back two this you know just whatever for the team I'm here for >> I think like probably a quarter of this team is in one of their first two years of the league what's it like in the building in the locker room having that big of a group of you know foundational part of this team >> I feel like it's huge just because we get to build a bond as young guys but we also have younger guys stepping up being leaders you know shoes. Some first year guys have to step up step and be leaders. Some second year guys have to step and be leaders. And I feel like the older guys that we have on this team, you know, they're leading us the right way and teaching us the right things on how to become leaders. >> We're going to talk to Jacob Rodriguez in a bit and obviously he's just a rookie, but it seems like he has a knack for getting the ball. What have you noticed on that front? >> Uh he has a like he has a magnet for the ball honestly. Uh it's actually great to watch. He was like that in college, too. But uh I love seeing T get to the ball punching. I think he got one for me honestly and you know that's what they being taught. you know, get at the ball and I feel like on Sundays we'll have a bunch of possessions that come back to us just because of things like that. >> Is it fair to pull off the peanut punch in practice? >> I feel like it is. We going to get in the game, we might as well work it at practice. So, we hold on to the ball, they punch at it. It's just what it is. >> It feels like talking to a lot of what you guys do at practice is very intentional to simulate a game environment. Have you felt that from the staff or has that message been passed out? >> Oh, definitely. You know, we talk about it every day. Just like I mean, it's been said for years. You practice how you play. So, if it's intentional here, high purpose, it's going to be like that on Sundays, which will make it easier for doing here at practice. >> Man, some big humans when you get behind them, you know? I feel like they'll move mountains for you. But I feel like it's great. Honestly, couldn't be better, you know. >> What's the one area you've been focused on this season? Uh, I would just say probably getting my pads down, my pad level lower. Honestly, last year I ran kind of high, which was not a normal thing, but I feel like this offseason I've been trying to work on that and get better at that. >> He mentioned that he wants to see you guys every >> Yeah. Yes, sir. Just, you know, um, paying attention in meetings, reading stuff different, watching film differently, honestly. You know, not just from the offensive side, but also from the defensive side. And I feel like when we're in team meetings, Coach Hley does a great job doing that. you know, he uh sits there, he explains the offensive side to us and he explains the defensive side to us. So, we get we both get an understanding of what's going on.

title: S Dante Trader Jr. meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: In your two years, it feels like you're already an established vet. How do you How much youth is on this roster? How do you take advantage of that? >> Just using what I was what I learned last year, especially from my you know Evan Flo's in my season, and allowing you know my teammates to gain knowledge from that experience. If it's anybody in my room or the young vets that are I mean young rookies that are in there, I've been through the similar things, the goods, the bads, the ugly, everything. I have a story to help them you know mitigate their downfalls and their stresses, just alleviate anything I could. So, just using that and then on top of the vets I was with last year and this year, using everything I can to help coach up you know the guys next to me and everywhere in my position group. >> Different position but still in the secondary. Have you reached out to Chris Johnson at all in that way or has he sought you out to to discuss things with >> All the time. From football, just schedule, body things and maintenance and sleep schedules and how do you study, everything like that. So, I've helped CJ and I've helped Tavai, I've helped all the the the guys in my room with everything they need and they ask for cuz they're really open. You know, they don't have no no ego, no pride. They they openly ask anything and you know we love it so we we can help them. >> What's the biggest piece of advice that you're giving them? >> You use the talent that you you got and that you you know got here with. You know, I was going with Tavai, I'm like bro you got a lot of instincts. You got you're a lot of smart. Let it go. Let it go. Don't over process, don't over analyze as smart safeties can do. Just go make plays and y'all see him now. I'm like that's you. That's the Mook from Texas. Like go play Mook. You'll be that. We all going to need that type of player all year round. >> Dots, I think it was like seven takeaways for that defense in the first two days of camp. What is it that you guys have been doing off field that makes you such ball hawks now when you get out to practice? >> Just being competitive. When you competitive and near and all in the right windows, you going to get takeaways. Whatever you emphasize, you're going to get out there. And it's we have a standard out in the in the meeting room. If we going to run it and we don't get takeaways, we we going to emphasize every day We take away drills. Like I said, what you emphasize shows up and it's been showing up and from the start of OTAs where we're X's on the field, hey, we need you to be 10 by 12 top of the numbers. We need you to be 12 by 12 by 14 plus one on the hash. When you're there, the ball the ball has to lift. Tips and overthrows, that's what you're seeing. You're seeing competitive over routes, dig routes. So, the instincts and the guys is play making abilities are showing through the roof. >> How is Hack's defense better suited to put you guys in a like sports? >> I would say eyes on quarterback. There's a lot of eyes on quarterback and who gets paid the most, who's the most uh, you know, key guy on the field? It's the quarterback. Who's the guy you don't want and you're when you're on your own team to touch? Quarterback. So, we having our eyes on the guy that's going to give us the ball. So, just this system alone allows you to play top down, everybody on a string. As you see, we all 11 to the to the ball. We're going to close up the run game with, you know, our big guys up front and then our edge pressure on the edge. So, just being able to close those lanes and then keep and limit explosive with cover three shells and post and things like that. >> You know, Hack's background is coaching the secondary. He has his ways of coaching that unit. Is there anything technique wise for you that's different in in in his defense that that you're learning in there? >> I would say DB's DB, you know, everybody has their own spin, but I'll say it's just a more attention to detail for every coverage and one thing about him, he's going to have one way on a paper, he's going to look at it, change the call. Let's see it on this way. Uh, let's tweak it. He's trying to he's changing changing it all the time to help it suit everybody on the field and then whatever is going to make us, you know, stop the offense on that on that given day. So, it's every like it's um, changing every day. So, what that's really the the good part and tough part at the same time. >> Do you feel like you grew in terms of how you watched tape in your rookie year to now? Like when you go back after practice and watch, is it easier for you to assess and kind of absorb what you did and didn't do well? >> Yeah, is I say now you're not learning, you know, playbook and how to play in the NFL. Now it's learning, okay, now I can look at formations and quarterbacks and how I'm getting attacked versus did I line up right? Did I Did I execute this job right? Now, it's just again, like you can see, okay, this being a step wide or step late or when I get two by two extra reduced, I know I'm going to get this type of action with this back field alignment with a second and eight. You know what I'm saying? So, now you can see all those pictures in the game. You go out there on the field and next time you look at the sticks, look at the formation, you can process and be easier than versus let me just line up and be correct. You know what I'm saying? That was last year. Now, I can just process everything that I'm seeing. >> I know you did a good job last year with just kind of picking the brain of a lot of guys. Are you still doing that? I know you your leadership role has kind of changed, but are you still finding ways to still improve yourself in the midst of everything? >> Yeah. So, this This offseason, I was with Jordan Brooks. Wherever Jordan Brooks was, I was. I was over his house every day. We doing two-a-days. We training. Um we had a plan for everything in our game, you know, our techniques, our run fits, our striking, our shutting poles. And when we make plays, we laugh now. It's like we've been working on that. Like we've been doing that. So, we we've been with each other. So, he's been giving me the keys to the league. He all pro. He's had advice over the years. He's giving me things to help me speed up my process. He like, "Hey, look, Trey, like I wish I knew this year, too. I wish I knew this and did this." So, and then you see it on on the field when me and him are not in the right spot. We demanding in each other from each other and then the same vice versa and you seen that today on one of those plays. >> This is the first time we got to see Malik run in practice. What kind of threat can that be when he's capable of doing? >> So, when you got the threat of a quarterback, you you extend plays. Covering for 3 seconds is hard as it is. So, imagine covering for 6 seconds with Malik being able to run and and gun it. So, now you're seeing him, we got to plaster. We got to work on plaster drills. And even now when you got the Q pulls and the pull reads and read schemes, like you're going to need the post safety. You're down one. So, that creates a lot of problems, you know, for the back end. What are you going to call? So, if you call certain calls they run the ball. You're going to you got to stack the box and account for certain guys and then that leaves opportunity for explosive. So, you got to you got to know where he is and you got to know the scheme of the call if you got to, you know, the quarterback technique or anything like that. >> Coach, it seems like the last three days you guys do a lot of specific work down and distance, second and eight, third and three as opposed to just going out there. What does that do for you as a player, situational awareness and that kind of thing? >> Like I said back in OTAs, Coach Athly does a great job job going part to whole, right? So, in a situation he goes second and eight. In second and eight in the league that's get back on track. So, they didn't get a positive, you know, run or pass. So, they they got heavy tendencies of we got to get to third and manageable or third and this. So, you get certain type of calls. So, when I give the down and distance and the personnel, "Hey, it's second and eight." We got to be a little ready for a hunkering down on on a run. So, he's teaching that. So, we go on to the field, if guys get a pass call from the sideline you still got to have a run mindset. You see what I'm saying? So, he's teaching us the game through the game, especially when I said part to whole. >> Your your your confidence was pretty good last season. Can your confidence get higher now that you got a year under your belt? >> Yeah, for sure. I think confidence comes from reps and then knowing who you are and what you're capable of and also knowing your weaknesses and doing everything to mitigate that. Ultimately, you got an opportunity, you just got to go get it. Like nobody going to hand you nothing. I've never been handed anything. So, I got to go take it. There's competition all around this program and we're just going to ready to take off from that. So, my confidence, you know, is is here.

I made it the final play of the competition. Now you got me again. See, you can't just throw that out there. I mean, I you know how much I I don't even remember all the stuff that happened yesterday and you're asking me about one play on No, I actually remember the play now. So, we put the ball down third down and we made a call defensively where we knew where the man side was going to be and I told Zach once he figured that out to call a certain game and he did and it was a very veteran move on a game and Proc's just got to see it and come off faster and that is a big your question. It's actually a really good question now that I'm kind of thinking about it. He uh it's a good learning lesson that in those situations you just got to recognize the game and come off it quicker. But it was a very well executed game by Zack. I mean it was a beautiful thing. >> How is um how is Jacob Rodriguez doing in terms of getting his hands on the ball, forcing turnovers um since his arrival? >> What have you seen? >> Yeah, I've seen that. >> Yeah, he's violent, right? He's got a he's got a really good knack for getting the ball out. A lot of guys throw punches and miss and hit ribs and hit the back and hit shoulder pads and they're trying to get the ball out. He's he's got a really good feel and he's got really good timing and very instinctual. I mean Han, there was one I think a couple practices ago where Han was actually had two hands on the ball and Jacob came in and I mean it was a violent punch and the ball came out. I think Han even kind of smacked him on the back and was like that was a heck of a punch. Now Han's got to hold on the ball. But I don't know who would have been able to hold on the ball in that. But you can see even running sideline to sideline he's constantly taking swings at it and they're um they're very deliberate and then I just think he's got really good width and range and in zone coverage he's got the ability to get up and get his hands on the football. So that's what you're probably seeing. But he's done a nice job so far. >> Sticking with what have you seen in the first half? >> Um been impressed. I mean, I think he's still got work to do and within the scheme, but um we've moved him around. He's he's made some contested catches, which I think is very impressive with guys right there. And I think that's probably the number one thing that I wanted to see from him when there was people around him and when the catches were hard, could he make them? um you know cuz he does have good size and he has a good catch radius and I just it's a compliment to him in the first three that he's been able to make some of those plays. Um he's got he's got a ways to go for what we expect of him but I'm pleased with the way how he's approached stuff right now. >> Jeff, you guys have fans here for the first time today. How much you looking forward to coaching in front of them sort of for the first time? And just as a followup, when you were when it was announced you were the news broke that [clears throat] you were hired and you were watching the game inside Hard Rock Stadium, did you allow yourself to think about being center stage? >> Um, no. I didn't really think about myself being center stage to be honest with you. It just, you know, I'm not going to use any cliches, but I it's really never been about me. I'm not the one playing. Those guys should be center stage, not me. Um, as far as practicing with front of the fans today, I think it's great for our players. I think it's good to get them in an environment where people are watching and it it changes the scenery a little bit. It brings some excitement and some juice and maybe some of them will get a little bit anxious and you know I think that's good for the young players and I think it's good for the city to get people out and open as many practices as we can to let people see us play and the energy and how hard these guys are working and everything that it takes and all the effort and the time that they put in to getting ready to go into Hard Rock and play a game. Um I always get really excited when you see a lot of young kids out there. I think it's that's a really cool de deal to see these kids who probably think it's the coolest thing in the world to get close to these players. That's like the most exciting thing for me and you know maybe help change a kid and and get them working harder and doing things maybe that they can be here one day doing these type of things. So those are those are the cool things to me but I'm excited for the fans. Um once whether I put a headset on or once I start coaching I that kind of all disappears you know it's just kind of have a job to do out there and focus on getting the team better today. >> You alter anything about practice with fans there? Like do you have the rookies hype up the fans at the beginning like that's been done in the past or do you do it keep it the same? >> Hopefully we hype them up by the way the guys make the plays. I mean I'm just if guys want to hype up the rookies in their own their way they can. and I'm focused on how to get better in practice today and hopefully score some touchdowns and get them excited and hopefully make some big plays on defense and get him excited, but no, I haven't really thought about that. Um, but if certain players want to go out and get them all all hyped up, then that's great. >> What is it about Bigger skill set that allows him to play inside and outside and how much is it situation specific? Um, he's got really good size and he's athletic for his size and he has the ability to line up inside because of that, but then he's got the athleticism and the strength that we like um especially on rundowns to set the edge. And it will be um it will be specific based on down distance personnel, what packages we want to use, whether we want to get in the different looks, odd, even. But I like where he's at and it's three days so we'll see if you know we'll see how much we need to do that. >> Going back to Isaiah's question, is that common place where you're willing to give guys autonomy in practice to make calls and change things on their own within the play that they see? >> Um, not too much, especially right now. know, but that was a that was an example of I know Zach and I know how Zach's mind works and I made the call in and I tagged something and then I yelled out to Zach that if he gets a feel for something, he can switch the game and he kind of smirked at me and he switched it and I knew he would and I had a pretty good feeling it would work. So, I think that's a coach trusting a player who's done it for a long time and in the competitor competitive nature of practice in that point. I wanted to make sure that the defense won that down and they did. But I can't do that all the time because I want the offense to win downs, too. That's been a big deal for me. When the defense gets an interception, you'll see me not celebrate. I go up to the quarterback and tap him on the back and just call the next play while all the defensive coaches are running down the sideline. I stay out of that now. Now we score a touchdown, I go high five the wide receivers instead of go talk to the DB. So, I'm getting better at that. It's taken me three days to get used to that. >> What excites you about pads uh coming on at tomorrow's practice and and something close to real football being played? >> Yeah, I think the game changes when pads come on. I I think it's easier to run the ball when the pads come on. I think offensive linemen can get their hands underneath shoulder pads. I think they can kind of hold in certain places that aren't going to get called. I think they can move people better. I think DBs can reroute wide receivers better because there's more surface air to get your hands on wide receivers. And I think certain positions it be it becomes way more real. Like let's be honest, it becomes more real. It allows us to practice in different tempos. we can go thud where you guys will see a lot of the NFL thud somebody up, wrap them up, and then kind of let them go. Um, I do think you need to have that physicality and you need to callish your body, whether it's your shoulders or whether it's your hands or whether it's, you know, a lot of your body getting used to that physical contact, which is really hard. And then it's going to allow us to go live and play real football and see who can tackle, who can break tackles. that, you know, when people talk too about playing the game, I think there's a lot of safety that we still need to get better at in this game throughout the league, right? So, we start teaching the proper way to tackle and keeping our head out of the tackle and protecting yourself. Well, how do you do that if you really don't practice it and get it on tape and correct it? So, I think playing real football is huge and being aggressive and physical and live and actually having periods where we go to the ground is huge, but I think it also allows us to teach how to do things properly for the safety of the game. Um, and those are all things that are very important to me. >> We talked on Thursday about guys learning in different ways, [clears throat] whether that's seeing, hearing, the physical act of doing it. with a new team, how have you and the staff kind of gone about figuring out how guys learn best as individuals? And then how much are you able to kind of tailor that learning experience for an individual versus trusting your overall install to kind of get them where they're going to learn it best? >> You you have to find out how each player learns. I mean, that's it's not me in front of the whole entire room. I'm going to I'm going to teach how I believe is the best way to get my points across. But say you were coaching the running backs and there's only five running backs in the room. That's your job as a running back coach to be the head coach of the running backs and get to know how each one of those guys learn because that's your job as a teacher just like it would be as a school teacher to figure out how maybe a kid who's here versus here to teach everybody, right? And if that's extra time, if it's me and you need to go out and do an extra walkth through cuz you learn better walking through and then maybe I take him in the classroom extra in my office and we watch video because he learns best watching the video. And then there's rep guys who just need more reps on the field. But you better figure that out as a position coach and that's 100% on them to figure out how each one of their players learns individuals. I think the best coaches are the best teachers and I think that's why I have a ton of respect for all the teachers um all the school teachers because they need to figure out how each kid learns and each kid learns differently. >> Count the defense has forced like nine 10 takeaways.
