title: Spencer Rattler talks offensive weapons | Saints Training Camp 2026
text: How do you think your camp's gone so far? >> It's been good, man. You know, it's always fun those first few days getting going. Um guys are flying around. It's been fun. Couple things to clean up as usual that first week or so in camp, but um you know, I think all all the guys [snorts] look great right now. It's been fun. >> Could you take us through the throw to Lance at the back of the end there? Like that one fired you up? >> Yeah, it was a you know, good play call. Um I was excited for for Bryce because, you know, want to get his confidence going. I think he's a good good young player. Um he made two good back-to-back catches right there and um you know [snorts] corner bit a little bit just got to throw it firm to Bryce. He made a great catch and it's always fun to celebrate in the end zone. >> Is it I mean like that like you need really good timing with somebody like how do you build that with a rookie who's just coming in, you know, >> yeah I mean specifically on that play it's you know happens very quickly and that's kind of like just an alert for us. So, uh, for him to be able to weave through all that coverage, um, it might look like nothing's there at first, but for him to just feel that zone in the in the back end zone was big time. And just got to hit him and hit him in stride and he made a good play. >> Mindset, your preparation, none of that changes [clears throat] from this year. Like, you do things the same way. You do you, right? >> That's right. You know, you got to uh continue to just improve. Um, you know, no matter what the situation is, continue to improve. um you know, do whatever you can to to help this team and uh stay ready at all times and and just try to whatever group you're with, just try to move the ball and get the energy going and and uh be clean. >> Especially with all the weapons they brought in on offense, like is it really noticeable to you as a quarterback? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, um I think you guys could all tell out there. I mean, it looks good. Like I mean, I feel like on first team, second team, even even some of the third team guys, like we it it's a deep roster, you know, on the offensive side of the ball. I think you got a lot of obviously skill at the wide opposition. Now the tight end room is deep. Um running back room is is is really good and the O line looks great. So, [snorts] um the horses are in the stable for sure, you know, and I think once we all learn our assignment, keep building, keep building, keep growing. Um it's going to look even better and better. >> Can you tell that the the receivers should grow to that it's a faster group? Does it does it like feel faster from your end? >> Um you definitely know what guys are a little twitchier. you know, you got to we call it KYP, kind of know your personnel. Um, you know, judge, judging off a guy speed, but all these guys can run. I think that's something that stands out. All these guys are quick, are fast out of their breaks, um, have good feel on the field, and um, our job is just to facilitate and get it to them in stride. >> How different are their speeds? I mean, talking about Bright, he's like 63, Jordan 6, Bar 10 or so. How different do their speeds impact the way that you read the defense and get involved? Um, you know, they're all a part of a certain play based off, you know, their strengths, I guess you can say, right? Um, obviously Barry's super, you know, quick, smaller guy, more of a slot guy. So, he's a little twitched up. You got to, you know, kind of put it on him. Um, obviously Jordan and and Bryce and all these guys. Bryce is, you know, good top end speed. Kind of um, you know, just a young guy that can just his top end speed on deep routes is is really nice. And, um, but yeah, you just got to know your personnel. um just kind of judge it off that and try to give him a good ball. >> What does Zach added to the room? How do you like that? >> Yeah, we like Zack, man. I like Zack. Respect him. Um obviously he's been through it before, so that's I think that's kind of cool to add him to the room and kind of hear his insight on what it was like going through his situations and multiple stops, seeing what that was like. Obviously, he's played with um you know, some big time guys before, too. So, just hearing stories about that and um I think it just adds more experience in the room. Um and he's a he's a good guy, too. you know, we all like to compete, have fun, and uh it's a great addition. >> A lot of um teammates have noted Tyler's leadership. Have you noticed any just like being your quarterback, any like um notable differences in how like in Tyler's game? >> Um yeah, you know, I think uh obviously, you know, as you play, you get a little more comfortable in the pocket. Obviously, you know, the system more. I think him coming in last year as a first year player, um, learning the system, getting it down, you know, I feel like both of us, um, you know, have it down to a T. Now being two years into it, uh, feels a lot smoother for us coming into this camp rather than last camp. Um, you know, last camp I feel like we were just working on snap count and we're false starts and pre- snap procedure issues. So, it's a lot cleaner in in um, you know, this year around. Um, so I would say just growing in the offense and then obviously, you know, confidence-wise, I think as you play, you get a little more confidence. >> Has your role changed last year? Y'all were always very supportive of each other. Why was that important specifically for you? And how have you seen your relationship evolve over this last year? >> Yeah, I mean, we're in the QB room, it's always going to be, you know, you got to be there for each other. think, you know, that's big when whoever's playing, you got to you got to help them to the, you know, as much as you can because when you're out there, it's it's different than watching from the side. Um, but I think we all do a good job of building together, competing versus each other. You know, he throws a good ball, I want to match it. I throw a good ball, he wants to match it. Maybe, you know, we'll talk a little smack back and forth in Indie. You got to get the juices going. And, um, I think we all have fun doing that, you know, with Scotty and Nus and those guys. And, [snorts] um, you know, it's fun just competing with them. got a couple of guys, Kell, Chris, going back to last year as well, kind of elevate when talk about you elevating you up in terms of like, hey, this is a starting quarterback in the NFL. Just what does that mean to you to have that trust and relationship still around the team? >> Yeah, I mean, it's awesome. You know, you want uh we went to battle with those guys. I went to battle with those guys and, you know, we always got each other's backs. You know, I think it'd be the same thing uh vice versa. So, um obviously respect Chris a ton for for saying that. um you know [snorts] cuz he's one of the best players in the league and has seen how it's supposed to look and obviously big shout out to Chris as well you know congrats to him um really deserving um worked his butt off and he obviously went through a lot to get to this point so happy for him but to answer your question yeah it means a lot and um just want to keep building keep uh getting closer with the guys and keep growing. >> Do you think there was maybe going to be an opportunity to like land one of those 32 jobs elsewhere or anything? Is that something that you wanted at all or? >> Um, you know, hey, look, I'm just focused on my job right now here. Obviously, you know, this is a great situation here. We got a great young team, a great young quarterback room. Um, we're all still growing, all still in the same area of our career. Um, you know, whatever I can do to help this team elevate, that's my job right now. >> You said really good hat guy. >> These were specially delivered to us quarterbacks um only. So we we were excited when we got these in our locker the other day. >> Yeah. Appreciate it. >> Drew going to the Hall of Fame as a quarterback. >> Obviously one of the greatest of all time, you know, ton of respect for Drew. Every time, you know, we we cross paths. It's great to just catch up with him and [snorts] um you know, just dap him up, say what's up, you know, hear what he's got to talk about. But I mean, we all knew that was coming. He's one of the goats and um super cool that you know he gets to go into the first ballot hall of fame. >> Similar to Taesm had his statement, you know, thanking the city of New Orleans and everything. Um just what is it that he meant to y'all um you know throughout your time with him? >> Yeah, Taesm was awesome. I mean, uh true vet, a guy that has literally done it all at every position. So for him, you know, last year, I think he really was in the quarterback room more maybe than the tight end and running back room. So getting to spend a little more time with him, seeing how he is and his process, I thought that was really cool. And uh but for him to be able to balance all those things and you know, he did so much in New Orleans. Um obviously wish Taesm the best and you know, one of the New Orleans goats for sure. >> Thank you. >> Thank you guys. Yep.

Let's start with this. >> What uh sort of differences do you notice in the run game now that Travis is here, and you guys brought in David, and just generally, how do you feel about that aspect of your guys' offense? >> Uh I like it a lot. Um I think David is an excellent communicator. you know, I've got so much stuff running through my mind just about the schematics of every play that he can kind of pay attention to the actual D-linemen, their tendencies, their um movement patterns, see things that I'm not necessarily seeing until we get to a game plan week. Um so, that's been really helpful. It's like, you know, some zone like our zone calls and when he sees the D-line movement stuff. Um all of that as I've said before, Travis is um super versatile. Uh I think he's a guy that is super elusive, but also stick his stick his head in there and, you know, get the grimy yards. >> What about the overall approach and plan from the coaching staff? Do you feel like they kind of honed in from what worked and didn't work last season? so far, absolutely. Um uh I think our first two installs, first three installs that we've done so far, um was kind of the things that have kind of that transitioned to the things that we were good at last year. Um and that I think that's going to be our bread and butter and then I think our further installs would be like our supplementary run game. has it been weird getting to work with coach Clapp? >> No, not at all. I mean, even even when he was a player, like he's a guy that, you know, coaches he was a guy that coached people up. Um and then from a uh seeing the game standpoint, even as a player, he was years ahead of all of us. So, I think that's been really beneficial for me just to kind of have him as a a brain to pick with. >> Yeah. Oh, yeah, I mean, you get two I I think two of your former teammates on staff. Josh was the other one. Uh I I mean, just like from a player standpoint, you know, you had J'Mar last year, Will this year, Josh is on staff. Having somebody you know kind of kind of been there, done that. Like does that help when you're when you're hearing stuff from them? >> Yeah. I mean, obviously you trust everybody on the staff, but then people that you have that personal connection with, um I think it's just a little bit easier to take, you know, critiques and criticisms and um things that you can get better at. >> Are there ever moments that because they're your former teammates and then it's like they're going into coach mode that you're like, "Oh." Or like >> No. Uh you know, I feel like like even though Kliff is a coach like you still have the charisma from when you're you're you're the relationship from when you were a player. But like no, I wouldn't say so. Not really. >> How happy are you that Kliff got a contract extension? >> Uh that's what I wanted to start with and I forgot. Uh huge congrats. I can't think of a person more worthy. Um a guy that, you know, really battled injuries and was resilient and, you know, fought through to the other side and now he's set. he deserves it. >> Speaking of resilience, what is there anything in particular that gives you confidence from anything you've done differently or any, you know, medical responses you've gotten that that you can that the last few something you've moved past? >> Um it's a good question. I don't think my confidence ever wavered. Um like I I trust my process. I trust my plan. Um and I mean I think we've implemented a few extra things in the weight room to kind of supplement, but my confidence never wavered in who I am as a player, who I am as a person, and what I can do on the football field. Um so. >> When you say supplement, like is that not pushing as hard as you used to or like what what's kind of the goal of supplement? >> Uh more correctional work. So like things that I've had, you know, surgeries on in the past or injuries in the past. Just doing like even more supplemental work to strengthen, mobilize, um activate those types of things. >> What is Have you Have you had any injuries that were either a recurrence or related to a previous injury or they all been somewhat separate? >> Every single one has been separate. Yeah, everyone's been >> And so there like none of those are things that shouldn't limit you. >> No. No, no, no. No. Not at all. And I I've got no fear. So. >> When you watched Shaq last year play in training camp and obviously developing behind the scenes and then starting, looking at him now, what's the area where you see the most growth in him? >> Uh leadership, communication. Um I think he was light-years ahead of any rookie that I would have thought of last year. But I think that's only grown. Um just, you know, the command of the huddle, um our communication back and forth on protections. Um yeah, and I think he's just he's picking up and seeing a lot of things right now. >> A lot of guys have talked about the value of a second year in a season of both sides of football. But for for you on the the offensive line and particularly in your position, what does a second year allow you? >> From him? >> No. >> Or my second year? >> year. You you in this system in Carolina. >> Oh, got you, got you, got you, got you, got you, got you. No, no. Um Sorry, can you repeat that one more time, the beginning part? >> the um you going into a second year in Carolina Moore's system. Guys have talked about like the value of >> Yes, absolutely. Absolutely. familiarity. I mean, this last year that was my third offense in 3 years. Um so it was just a lot of change, a lot of different um calls to be made, a lot of different ways of saying things. So I think just having a consistent back-to-back year of all right, this is our offense. These are installs. This is what is going to be our our bread and butter. This is how we're going to communicate. Like I think that's super valuable for me, for the whole offensive line. Um I think it'll allow us to be even more cohesive. >> You're one of the few guys on this offense that had the chance to play with Drew Brees, who'll be going into the Hall of Fame next week. maybe your thoughts on that, but then also like what's maybe a story that sticks out the most to you that encapsulates like who he was as a player and a leader? >> My thoughts on that? No one more deserving. The I mean, I was only with him for 2 years, but the most prepared intelligent He's incredible. Like, as a football player, I can't think of anybody that's better. Like, he was special. What was the second part of the question? >> Just maybe a story that could be like a first time meeting him or something along the journey of those 2 years that like just really captures who he was as a player or even as a leader. >> Mhm. I think people have talked about it before, but I think his in here on his own on Saturdays after everybody has left, just walking through the game on the field, like, the first 15, whatever, going through a whole drive and just, like, sitting back and watching that from a distance, like, the the attention to detail was crazy. And I think that's Yeah, that's why he's my goat. >> Have you got a chance to like reflect on that and just like when he's talking next week, will you think about like, hey, I was snapping the ball to this guy? >> Uh yeah, and I'm I'm a I'm a lucky ass dude. Like Like, I I don't know what to say because I can't speak highly enough about him. He was the best. >> Do you feel like that forced your game to like almost get get like to learn faster because he knows so much of the offense and he's like he's Drew Brees that it felt like it felt like it you helped your progression get up to speed faster, sort of thing? >> Yes and no. I think um Yes, because I wanted to on my own, but also he did everything. Like, run game, pass game, like, my job when he was the quarterback was to get up and put my hand on the ball and snap it. And that was it. That was it. Um I'm I'm I'm being so serious. I got to the line as fast as I could and I put my hand on the ball. Um but just out of my own want to. >> Yes, as well. >> It might be a weird question, but like we always talk about how important it is to spend time away from the field, hang out off the field. Tyler keeps talking about like all the group of guys that had kids in the same year. What's like the 3:00 a.m. text messages of waking up knowing that somebody else is going through it like we were talking about like the social it's good. It's it's a grind. Um I mean I know that me, Tyler, Dave and at least one other person have the kids within like a week or two of each other. Which is crazy. Um but just knowing that we're all kind of in the same season. Like oh, how'd your kid sleep last night? Oh, mine was up at 1:00, 3:00, 5:00, and 7:00. Um like that's just it's it's fun to talk about. Um and I feel like that gives you a way to bond even just outside of ball. >> Back to Chris for a second. Um as a leader, how have you seen him take Jordan under his wing? >> I think right now they're you know like two peas in a little pod. Um and like I I'm I'm proud of him overall just as a leader. Um he's a guy that just puts in the work, does his thing. Um and I'm excited for where this year is going to take him. Now like the contract, you don't have to worry about that anymore. You just get to go play ball. >> Hey, you see this There seems to be a real positive vibe at the start of this training camp. What what are the reasons why you think this team might be poised to make a big jump? >> I think we have a ton of talent. I think that the way our scheme is going right now, it's excellent. And I think when you have a young quarterback who is the guy and you can bring in the extra pieces around them. Like that gives you all the confidence in the world. Um and I think the way that we're preparing the way that we're in the t-shirts out there and the physicality is there. The work ethic is there. The guys getting extra work in after practice in the weight room. Like those are all things that you're seeing and I think it's something like everybody's buying into it. So, I think that's why the confidence is so high. >> How it was like to just out season when you saw all the movies and you were thinking what was going to happen when these pieces ain't going to work together actually? >> I was just waiting for the next one. Um and I I love every single movie that we made. so props to him for a great off season. >> So part of that, what's been your early impressions of Jeremiah coming into the draft? >> Jay Wright? Uh I think Jay Wright is a people mover. Um I think he's a sponge. He's a guy that is is he wants to get better. He wants to learn. I think he's only been playing on the line for two or three years. Like he hasn't been playing that long. Um but he's physical. He wants to learn. He wants to grow. Um and I think that he can turn into a really good player on the offensive line. >> What does his previous experience at defensive line potentially provide him from your perspective? >> I mean I think he knows the technique. Like the like defensive line techniques more than more so than any of us would. you know, how to combat moves, how to counter moves. Um I haven't seen it yet per se, but I think that he has that knowledge and that skill set in him. >> Aaron, I know you and Sage are really close. >> Do you have a good sense of like ship on it the ship that he has in the shoulder going into this season? >> The chip? >> Oh, um I think he just wants the ball. yeah, that's really all I got on that. >> Thank you. Yeah, appreciate y'all. Y'all have a good one.

title: Why Noah Fant is Excited About the Saints Offense & Tight End Room
text: Are you were you a little bit more vocal today than usual on the field or was that just because we were in indoor? >> I think it was just cuz we're in the indoor. Um it's always fun chirping with the defense a little bit. But uh yeah, I think you guys just got a little little extra hearing because we were in the indoor, but it was fun. >> What do you like about that? I mean that that back and forth and especially in in an environment like this where you know teammates >> Yeah. You know, honestly, it just like is it like pushes each other to be better every day. Um, which is which is cool. And, um, I think we got a lot of talent on offense and a lot of talent on defense. So, it's just like pushing each other to be better. Um, attack our deficiencies and, um, try and be a great team. So, >> seems like the tight end group this year, just a lot of a lot of really talented players who can do a lot of different things. Like, how much of a competition is there is there in that room? >> Uh, yeah. I think everybody's always competing every day. Um, I think we have a really good cohesion in our room though. It's like everybody's rooting for each other and trying to get better each and every day. And uh, you know, the chips will fall where they may when we're guys like in and out and playing and things like that of that nature. But we're all rooting for each other. We all want each other to get better and I'm all trying to help each other also in the same time. So, um, it's a great cohesion in the room. Um, Chase has did a great job. Um Josh Hill is like a a dark horse for us in the in the tight end room that might not he might not get a love a bunch of the time but former player here and he helps us a lot also. So it's a it's a great room so far and I'm I'm super happy to be a part of it. >> Tight room similar to this as far as the amount of talent. Uh, I mean, yeah, that's a that's a tough question because I feel like tight ends rooms are always, you know, usually very talented. Um, and u, usually everybody gets along really well. Um, it's a good group of guys most of the time. So, um, but here is definitely like like there's a lot of talent in this room. Um, when I was in Seattle, there was a good amount of talent in that room also. Um, but yeah, so same in C like Cincinnati, like there's a good amount of talent, but I I've really enjoyed being here so far. So, >> Edward spoke about how the way that Tyl was able to beat people with his mind as a second year quarterback has impressed him a lot. What was it about Tyler as a second year most? >> I think it's just his leadership qualities like being in the huddle with him um between each period. uh if he doesn't think that you know relaying from the coaches or him himself if he doesn't feel like a period has gone that well just just encouraging the guys to like pick it up um get going and all those things of that nature he's done a really good job of leading in that in that standpoint and also just like kind of like from a secondyear guy of kind of doing the San Diego stuff and just kind of bringing guys together and getting guys together in that nature has been really cool to see from such a young guy in the NFL. Um he's just kind of taking it by the reigns and really taking and run with it. So I think everybody's kind of building around him um in that in that standpoint. So it's been really cool. >> Justin was talking just like stood out. Yeah, I think that I mean he definitely has a catchable ball, but it's like you there's quarterbacks that don't have as much as they just like it's a rocket every time. He has great great touch. Um he has great feel for putting it in spots and zones where you can uh catch it and get up field. So I' I've been really impressed with all of that and uh I think you know that's why he's in the positions he's in. He has a lot of he has a lot of talent in that in that standpoint and um so it's been good work so far. We got a lot a lot of training camp left to continue to improve on all those things though. So, >> like I'm sure you've been in offenses and just like have >> a lot of skill guys like is there ever challenge or whatever when you got a lot of miles and stuff like that? >> For sure. Yeah. I mean, I think that that's um a big part in the NFL just in general like you're going to have a lot of talent around you at all times. Um if you have a good team and uh you just have to be prepared to like, you know, every play whatever is asked of you and just doing that to the best of your ability. You're not always going to have the ball in your hand. Um you know, I've kind of learned that over the course of my career and like you know, there's guys like Chris Olive, right? It's like he's going to have the ball a lot. He's a really good player and uh as he should, but it's like it's, you know, we're going to surround him with a bunch of talent and a bunch of guys that can do similar things and everybody's going to get their opportunity at some point. So, you just got to be ready for it. >> Is that something that you like really experienced last year? >> Yeah. Yeah, definitely. I think that that was a a little bit of a different experience. I haven't been in a an offense before that like there was as many like targets as that per game. Um, you know, I've been I had been with DK. I've been with Courtland, um, Tyler Lockett. Um, but Jamar Jamar got a lot of targets a game as he should have. He's a great player, like transcending, uh, wide receiver. But I think, uh, Chris, I mean, he I think he's just just as as much up there. You know what I'm saying? Like, he's a great player. So, um, we'll see how it all shakes out. I think all of us are just, to your point, I think we know that we have a lot of talent. We have we know we have a lot of miles to feed, but we're just going to do the do our job every play. And if we're doing that, we're going to be in a good spot at the end of the year. >> In addition to kind of the the pass catching prowess that you bring, you have really strong run blocking experience as well. What do you think this system maybe uh puts you in position to do in that area of the game? >> Yeah, I think it's just like really leaning into the fact of like like really like leaning into my strengths and then attacking any deficiencies I may have in my game. And um and I think this coach coaching staff really prides themselves on putting the each player in the best positions to like where they'll be successful. Um so I'm just really trying to lean into that and each and every day. Obviously the pass game is important here but the as is the run game. Um so I've just been trying to lean into both sides of that and uh try and be the most like all-around player I can be to try and help the offense um and be a good like compliment off of Jawan in the tight end room also. So, um I think it's been I think it's been going well so far and I think that we have a the good thing is like we have a lot of training camp left to like continue to build that and continue to build that camaraderie and that cohesiveness and uh like really build an identity for sure. >> For sure. I think Maliki has done a great job. Um he's a he's a big dude. He's he's a strong guy and and he can catch the ball really well too. I think like I mean when I you go through the whole title room it's like Maliki, you got Trey, Zire, like Oscar, all these guys. It's like they have a bunch of talent and everybody knows it. Um and it's just really cool to be a part of that and see everybody do do certain things really well and and flourish from there. So >> with all that talent in that room, just curious your perspective on over the past few years, we've seen sort of the multi-tight end uh focus become kind of an emphasis or a trend around the league. just kind of put your perspective on the additional opportunity. >> I'm all for it. Yeah. Any any 12 and 13 personnel, I love it. I love it. You don't have to tempt me with that. I love that. So, as many tight ends as we can get on the field, that's I'm all for it. >> what does that allow an offense to, you know, have that reliable? >> Yeah, I think it's I think it's honestly great. I think it's tough for defenses in certain scenarios where it's like you have a lot of bigger guys on the field, so how are you going to match it? And then if you got if those bigger guys can then also run routes and and do really good things in the pass game. Now we're now we're really cooking with grease. So it's like it's one of those things. It's a it's a give and take. But um Kellen does a great job with all that stuff. It's it's my job to kind of like whenever I'm told to go in to go in and and do the best I can. But uh he does a great job with mixing up the personnels and all that stuff. But any 12 and person 12 and 13 personnel, you can put a stamp on it that I love it. >> [laughter] >> What's [snorts] your excitement around Tyler going with the year or two around the building? >> Yeah, I think that's just like everybody kind of like seeing the talent that he had, seeing the last five games that he put together and just like taking that and running with it and building off of it. And I think around the whole the building in general, it's been the whole like we're building around them and and moving forward and trying to build this thing the right way and and be a great team. So, um, he's done a great job taking it, like I said before, taking it by the reins and really just running with it and doing his thing. So, um, we're all following behind him. >> Have you been on a team that relies like heavily on 12 personnel? >> Yeah. Yeah, I think I think most of the teams I've been on, like when when I was in Seattle, we we ran a lot of 12 and 13 personnel. Um, my first few years there. U, but um, last year in Cincinnati, we did a a decent amount of 12 personnel also. So, a lot of the teams I've been on have have been a good amount of 12 and 13. Um, but like you were saying before, it's becoming even more of a trend in the league where it's like 12 and 13 personnel is like a big thing. So, um, I love it. >> Just adding on to that, like you mentioned the multiplicity of each guy in the room tempo historically. Do you think that's a separator just be able to keep them in that look and stay up tempo and still be able to 100%. Yeah. I think that if you can get into tempo in those like 12 and 13 personnel, that's where it gets real dangerous because it's like you're you got guys that that know like the whole playbook conceptually and can do all these things can you can get into different run formations and mix it up and play action, all that stuff. It's like that's where things really start to open up. Um but that's also, you know, not to take a new away from 11 also. I know the the receivers love being on the field. So, um, but yeah, I I definitely think to your point that's that is a huge thing. Catching catching a team in what nickel base personnel, whatever you're hunting up that game and uh being able to do that is huge. >> Installing. >> Yeah. Yeah. >> But like just how approaches. I think the biggest thing is he's just like dialed like every day like he knows what he wants to attack. He knows what he wants to get done. It's very detailed of like there's there's no questions like really when you're going into practice, you know what's expected of you. You know what what what we're trying to get what we're trying to accomplish in that play. And um I think that's been my biggest like like biggest um what's the word I'm looking for? like biggest like I'm most pleased with that to see that is like he's just so detailed and dialed. It's like it makes it easy for us to just go out there and like do what we're what we're asked to do. So >> waste of time >> Oh, for sure. Yeah. I think it's very efficient throughout the day. I don't really have any complaints about any of that stuff. Like I and I'm I'm the new guy anyway, so I'm just kind of following in line and doing my thing and and uh trying to help the any of the tight ends how I can. But I have no complaints when it comes to that stuff. think it's a welloiled machine. I think he's put a lot of thought into how he runs everything and um I've really enjoyed it. So, >> we know you spoke about 12 and 13 personnels, but obviously posted with the offensive line. Just what do you think about them and even guys like David Edwards and how they were performing and doing so far in? >> It's been it's been great so far honestly. Um funny story is that Dave was actually in my combine class. So, we trained for combine together. um we end up on the same team now. But it's like it's pretty cool just like how how great of a player that he's developed into. Um and he I mean and then dealing with like Tally and KB on the outside like a lot of the time with the tackles, working triples and all that stuff like combos that we need to work with them. It's been awesome. The the level of communication um the level of like football IQ, all those things that those guys have has been has been really cool. Um, and obviously got Eric Lee and all those guys from the center position. So, it's been it's been awesome. I think they're gonna put on a great show and um do their thing. So, it's been good.

title: Saints CB Quincy Riley Prepping For Year 2 and Learning From Veterans
text: getting into your rookie season, becoming a starter so early and now kind of holding on to that that have you hit that moment yet of everybody talks about like the game slowing down and and if you have like when did that happen? >> Um I say the game started slowing slowing down. um last season like towards the end of when I got real comfortable just being in this the system um and being under great vets um great coaching everything. So I think last season was like when I really start slowing down for me >> and and where are you now versus that? Like do you feel like it's even more manageable now? >> Um yeah, as days go on though I keep stacking days I feel like it's slowing down even more but now just about just getting better each time and be ready for the when the season come. What was kind of your focus over the off season to get ready for training camp in your second year? >> Um, just don't make the same mistake twice. Like if I made a mistake my rookie year, don't make that same mistake this year and just keep getting better. >> He was talking to us last week. He mentioned two players specifically and talking about their improvements. It was you and Kool-Aid. And how important is that maybe to you knowing just how important your role is to this team this year? Um, that's super important because I mean like everybody got a job on this team and if I'm doing my job that just put us one step closer to our goal. Like so if everybody just do their job then we going to keep getting better and push towards our goal. So as long as I'm doing my job I can be happy and now I got to push somebody else to do their job and I think it work out for us through the interception you had just a couple days ago at the goal line. >> Um it was just a great we coach put us in a great call. Me and Jay Reed um it was a manto man call. My me and J Reed worked it out. Like I first I take the first outside route, he take the first inside route and I guess a receiver got caught up or something and it it was zero pressure so um ball had to come out hot. So I was just patient and um I seen the ball thrown and just just wanted to catch the ball. >> Is there anything you're recognizing um that helps you anticipate that type of throw in terms of like it seemed like offense was changing? >> Um for sure it all comes down to down the distance formation. what's the situational um and then just like execute my job. >> This is also your second year's system. How much more comfortable are you with him and with that scheme and how does it allow you to thrive? >> Uh I'm I'm getting like I said I'm getting more comfortable. But um it's a lot more comfortability out there for me though. But just being my second year, I feel like I have open conversations with him where he understand like my play style. um I understand what kind of defense he want to run and where I can do this and do that at and we just have open conversations like that. >> How much better this season? >> Um I feel like we got a good pieces um a lot of speed in that room. So that um that challenged us in practice. So I feel like when we go against speeder receivers, I think we'll be more comfortable with those. Um but I feel like the receiver room got better. >> Talk about having great veterans to lean on. How much is having Justin back there helping me prepare for a second year? >> Uh I think that's a blessing about God having them guys in the same room as me and I can look at them and knowing they on the back end of me like they helping me throughout the play like okay I can you can be right here Quincy or I'm be right here for you. So it helped me play faster for sure. >> You sorry you've been around Tyler for a few years now. >> What about his jump has sort of struck you the most? Is there something about his development as a quarterback that surprises you or did you see this coming? But from having seen him for a few years to where he is now, what's the biggest thing that stands out for you? >> Um, the biggest thing stand out like what I'm seeing from first day, like even in college, like the first day I ever met him, like I think his leadership role, like I think he he got the ability to come in any type of room and just demand like this what it's going to be and what it's not going to be. So I think that's like the biggest thing I ever seen from him. you notice the slot, you know, how how much of an emphasis has it been on kind of building that communication from, you know, the edges to the interior back? >> Um, for sure it's different. Like he was at that safety position, so now he got to learn new techn um new terminology for um the star position and now me and him actually working hand in hand together um with me playing to the field. So I think just just each day just him just coming coming to talk to me, anything about it like we just getting better. talk about the duel of you and Kool-Aid being outside corners in this defense. >> Talk about it. The duel >> the duo of you and Koolaid being the outside corners in this defense. >> Um I just think we just come to practice every day, get each other better. Um and if one of us go down, the next man up. So I think it's just a group. It's just not just one one and two. I think it's just a whole group all together. Though >> last season like these two have potential to be the best duo. Is that something you guys embrace? Do you think that could be a possibility after this coming season? How do you feel about that? >> Um, we I I embrace everything. But I just really think just just coming in every day, just getting each other better. Even like from Ike to uh MJ, just everybody just coming in just getting better. That's our main focus right now. >> How would you describe your relationship with Kool-Aid though? Just from he's talked about wanting to step into that leadership role and everything. Like what's what's y'all's relationship like? Um, I think we got a more closer relationship that I would say with anybody just because we talk outside of football a lot. Um, kind of like almost similar person people's personalities and everything. So, I think me and him just got a little more closer connection. >> Justin Reed were talking about you is kind of the the uh physicality that this team allows for for the corners. How do you like that? What's kind of just your vantage point on the violence? Um, I enjoy it though because it shows people that um, the corners can be violent. Um, and you know, throughout the league, I feel like corners shy away from being violent nowadays, but in this defense, it lets you show that you can be that and you just got to want to do it. >> How much do you look for? Uh, >> a lot. I mean, that's when real football can be played for real.

title: Saints QB Spencer Rattler on how the Offense Looks in Camp
text: How do you think your camp's gone so far? >> It's been good, man. You know, it's always fun those first few days getting going. Um guys are flying around. It's been fun. Couple things to clean up as usual that first week or so in camp, but um you know, I think all all the guys look great right now. It's been fun. >> Could you take us through the Lance at the back of the one fired you up? >> Yeah, it was a you know, good play call. Um I was excited for for Bryce because you know want to get his confidence going. I think he's a good good young player. Y'all were always very supportive of each other. Why was that important specifically for you? title: David Edwards On His First Offseason With the Saints, How He Fits the Scheme
text: How's it going? Not >> bad. How are you doing? Doing great with everything now you you're in. Training camp's going like four years. >> It's been great. Yeah, it's been great. Um you know, talking with Ted, talking with Sean, just hey, get acclimated a little bit. So, once you're in it, you're like in it. And so it's been a good acclamation. Training like when practice would start doing your runs outside etc. So just trying to get acclimated >> at this point. What is what would you say is like one thing that is different about training camp whether it's you know because of calendar because of New Orleans or because of the Saints like as somebody new to this who's been around like what what is the defining New Orleans thing that is different about camp >> man um in a fun way those like coolers those giant freezers we got those are pretty awesome um you know we but we do the the staff does just a great job of being being cognizant of of the heat and what it what it does to performance and stuff and so allowing us to have a little bit of time in there just to kind of reset your body and your nervous system, cool off a little bit. But, are there clips? Are there runs? Are you hitting blocks? Are you moving the way you want to move and and protecting this the right way? And so a lot of a lot of good things that we've done so far. You're IDing certain plays maybe different than um you know what the defense is. You're running you know a a play out of this formation and then running it that same play out of a different one, right? So, you know, the mix of formations, motions, shifts, presenting to the defense, you know, a scheme or a formation that ends up being different. And then ultimately, you're hitting blocks, you know, differently, right? On a zone scheme, on a gap scheme, on power, whatever it is, you're you're not hitting the defensive lineman, the linebackers consistently the same way. So, it it just keeps them on their toes a little bit. I know you weren't here last year, but it's players have kind of said and coaches too, but it took some time to kind of discover what like the bread and butter was. Do you feel like, you know, coming into it new that you can tell like, all right, these guys have a clear idea of, you know, what what that bread and butter is? >> I still think we're building that and that's what's it's been really fun. Um, you know, the the cool thing is is that we, you know, we have a a variety of things that we can activate at any time. And now it's just, hey, how many reps can we get under our belt with with Trav, with AK, with all the backs, right? Um to find out how how comfortable they are with each scheme, what we're presenting to them in terms of the blocks, how it all fits together. There's great gap stuff. It's all it's all the same stuff that I've kind of been accustomed to, but it's been really cool to have the nuance and the detail and hey guys, this is how we're hitting it. Here's the intent of the play. Tying in the running backs and the tight ends and the receivers. Like I I really believe our coaches have done a great job of incorporating the entire unit, 11 players working as one um to accomplish great a great play. And the best part is we we're still installing. And so once that full package is in and you can activate a gap scheme, a zone scheme, a keeper, a play action um out of all these different formations, I I just feel like that's going to serve you well as an offense >> going up against God as a teammate. >> It's been great. You know, and I love, you know, even Shep, um, you know, Vern, you know, those guys in the interior are are savvy, good players. Um, and they and there's no like there's no guard between you because you're teammates. So, working with DG on different things like we we talk about how I hit you know his own combo or or a you know a post set in pass pro and he tells me what I'm he's thinking and I'm telling him what I'm thinking. So, um it's been great and that's that's cool because you know we're all in this together. I really feel that and believe that and so um it's been nothing but awesome. What's been your impression just even his approach to getting better? >> You know, KB is um motivated to be a great player. He cares so much about um being a good football player. He's so smart and intelligent, cerebral. Um yeah, I told KB like we're gonna get to a point where um you know, we only have to say the number of the guy we're going to. title: Darius Slayton: ‘There’s a lot of really good football players in our room’ | New York Giants
text: How How you feeling physically? >> Feel pretty good. Yeah. So, I feel pretty good right now. >> Can you take us through the When did the sports hernia start impacting you? >> I [snorts] kind of I pretty much started with it last season and just kind of played that way throughout the whole season. Just cuz I wasn't going to just, you know, cut season short with a surgery or anything, but you know, I I got through last year and I tried to kind of rehab it in the off season and just didn't really work. So, I just went and got my surgery done. >> Coach Niumatalolo's offense, what have you liked the most about it so far in the first few days of camp? >> I like the variety. I like the variety of it and the variety of like what people do. Like so far, you know, I feel like everybody has had a multitude of roles. You know, like so far it's not like, you know, certain guys are like, "Oh, you're just going to run deep." Or "You're just going to run short." Or "This guy's only going to run this or out route." Like I feel like it really has just been a mixed bag of everybody getting a shot at almost everything. >> You talked a lot over the about the last four years about how complicated that offense was for receivers, all the different things. How does this I don't know if compare is the right word or like how would you describe this offense and what it demands of receivers? >> Yeah, I mean, it is definitely it's a little simpler, I would say as far as like like conceptually simpler. But, I feel like it also has a lot of variety to it kind of like I just said where you can end up you could end up in a lot of different spots. >> How have you felt with just as far as um >> [clears throat] >> with Navy's with Navy's offense, just what's been the easiest adjustment I guess for you with it? Are you >> The easiest adjustment I'd probably say is that is that like it's a little more I'll say our last offense was like very memory based. So, like you just had to like hard memorize a lot of things. Whereas this one's a little more intuitive. You know, there's there's clues in the play calls so to speak that can be like, "Okay, like I know if I hear this word or that word." I I kind of either I know exactly what I have or I have an idea of what I have. >> How's the pace of practice, man? Like I know some of the guys have talked about this at a different pace with Harbaugh, but for you, the veteran here, what have you seen from how this pace of practice has been different than maybe before? >> Yeah, practice has been a great pace, but I feel like, again, like they do we've done such a good job of mixing and matching guys that it's allowed for people to be able to play fast and play hard and and ultimately, you know, you stack more explosive reps. And you know, you don't try to you don't get into as many of those for like six or seven eight reps in a row where like the reality is like by the time you get seven eight reps in like you're fried, you know, so um I definitely think that's been great. >> What do you think of this receiving core? It's very different than last year's receivers. Here's Odell and Juju and Braxton and Malachi. What do you think of this receiving core? >> There's a lot of really good football players in our room now and, you know, definitely from a competition level standpoint it's awesome. I mean, obviously, you know, I I literally just missed Odell on the front end, you know, he almost felt like a fake, you know, unicorn, mythical creature, you know, that departed before I came and then, you know, here he is, you know, back on the team with me. You know, obviously, Juju was a great player. Braxton's been a a good pro for a long time and obviously, Malachi's an exciting, huge, young rookie, you know, and he's flashed a lot, you know, over just these first few days. He's made some flashes, so um definitely raised the competition level in the room for sure. >> How do you rebound from last year? >> Um first and foremost is getting healthy. You know, I need I need to be able to run. I need to be able to move how how I'm accustomed to being able to move and um honestly, once once that's all done, you know, I believe I'll play it to a level that I need to play at. >> I was late coming over. How do you How do you feel after the surgery? Having sports >> Yeah, surgery, right? >> Yeah, yeah, I did. Yeah, I had yeah, sports hernia surgery on both legs, but uh I feel good. Feel good right now. >> How much did that impact you last season? >> Uh good bit. I mean, it's I'm not a big excuse person, so like at the end of the day like I could have played better regardless, but um you know, obviously, it's it's different when you know, maybe you're used to being able to catch a ball a little easier and you're having to strain a little more and maybe you come up an inch short here or there, but you know, at the end of the day, if you're out there, you got to make it happen. So. >> How do you think you fit in this this new wide receiver room? >> Yeah, well, everybody keeps trying to fit me in the old guy hole, but you know, Odell's older than me, Braxton's older than me, Juju's same age as me, so, you know, I'm trying to shake that narrative, but no, other than that, you know, I feel like um I've always just kind of been a a glue guy, kind of a do-it-all guy. You know, there's not really too much for a receiver position that you could ask of that I that I'm not capable of doing, so, you know, my plan is to fill whatever holes need to be filled and be successful at my role. >> The last time we talked to you was baggy day and you said we need a Tom Coughlin-esque guy. >> Yeah. >> Do you remember that? >> Did you get that? >> I would say so. I mean, I feel like, you know, I feel like he's in that that echelon, that that elk, you know, and he obviously came from prob- arguably one of the most old school divisions in football of the Ravens and Steelers. So, you know, I definitely think he's what we needed. There's definitely been a sense of accountability um off the rip, uh which has been huge for us, so um definitely definitely glad Coach Harbaugh's here. >> How do you feel about that? How do you feel the sense of accountability? How's that imparted to you guys? >> Um See, if I give specific examples, then people will start putting stuff together who I'm talking about. So, overall, like there's just there's just there's no room for anybody to just do whatever they want. Is the best way I could put it to you. Like, everybody's accountable, everybody has to be on time, everybody has to show effort at practice, or you will be held accountable. So, put it like that. >> Did you From what I've been told, Harbaugh has no problem challenging anyone. Like, if he want he wants to challenge you with something, he's going to challenge you and he wants an answer. Do you like that approach, the idea of there is no BS, it's basically tell me what you saw and I'll listen to you. >> Yeah, I mean he he uh dang, I got to be careful boy. I don't know >> [laughter] >> I almost did it Yeah, I know but I almost did it to myself. But uh already in this camp, you know, he's already kind of expressed that, you know, like at the end of the day, you know, in this life like if somebody's not doing something up to the echelon that you would want them to do, if you go to them and you make that clear to them that that's not what we're going to do around here, you know, then they have a chance to respond. And um that's something he's already done in our first three days of camp and gotten a positive response out of the the individuals that, you know, have he's done that with. So, you know, I think he's, you know, that's really big for a football team. >> How long after Dex was traded did you realize you were the solo you are you are Mr. Longevity here and now by yourself? >> Not long. I sent him a text um you know, so I pretty much knew off rip. Yeah. >> What's two more if y'all got it? >> West Virginia Darius, you've been here for close to a week now at this point. What have you thought of it? Is this your first time being in this side of the state and what have you thought about the fan support over the past few days? >> Fan support's been awesome, honestly. I I wasn't really expecting a ton, you know, being being in middle of nowhere West Virginia, but the fans have definitely showed up and they've been deep and and came out [clears throat] and been loud and obviously, you know, you guys can well, I guess nobody else can see but y'all can see like in the background you have these mountains and trees. So, it's a beautiful landscape and kind of nice to have nothing but football going on. >> What have you seen uh watching Malik go through drills and and what's your reaction to seeing him out there? >> Uh well, me and him have been rehabbing side by side for like the past however X amount of time. So, for me it's just I love to see him, you know, kind of start to get over that hump and get back out there and get to feeling like himself and be in the star that we all know that he can be and you know, obviously he's going to he's going to keep working his way back but you know, just seeing him in a helmet at all, you know, is is a blessing to for sure. >> [music] >> Mhm.

title: Mike Vrabel Discusses the First Week of 2026 Patriots Training Camp
text: Here we are from training camp. Coach is second training camp. >> edition. >> Football's back. >> this last year? >> We did this last year. >> I forget. It's a long time ago. >> forget. You remember everything. Yeah, I know. >> All access. This is the first of the of many. >> It's the first of many that we're going to do all the all year. And I remember sitting here a year ago with you. Sort of the element of the unknown, not knowing what type of team you're going to have, the reaction the fans are going to have to you. We know what type of year you have. How much different is it this year as this is your team now? >> I mean it's it's it's everybody's team. You know what I mean? It's it's our fans team. It's obviously um Robert and Jonathan, it's an extension of their family and and I want our own our players to take ownership of our team and uh making sure that everybody uh is trying to hold each other to that standard. >> Heard Marcus Jones speak a week ago and he talked about, you know, a lot of our players have a chip on our shoulder. Not to trip set about something but knowing now that, hey, we got a target on our back. Guys are gunning for us. You've won three. How different is that the next year? >> Well, again, every year in the National Football League is different. You don't know what's going to happen. You don't know what's going to come. The schedule changes. You go to different places. You know, you look at the lineup and sometimes the lineup changes. It's in very coaches go other places. And and I think I hope that we all have a chip on our shoulder to to be able to do this business. It's a competitive business. We're trying to create competition at every spot. Uh we're trying to compete in practice offensively and defensively and um you know, I think that that just comes with the territory. And so hopefully, you know, that's that's a way to keep complacency uh out out of our our program. >> The business side of football sometimes pop pops up obviously. Your second round pick is signed. He's in here. We've talked about Yacus. Gonzo and maybe some other guys have contract desires. You as the head coach in organizing this football team and being in those type of spots, how do you communicate with those guys? >> The same way I do all the time. It's uh you know, when Gabe's ready to go, uh you know, he's in a return to play. I talked about that a little bit this morning. So, you know, he's working hard. He wants to be out there Uh you can see that the way that Gonzo's practicing and he's acting like a pro and that's what you want from pro football players is that the when they come out here they're focused on football we always understand that there's the business and the professional side of it but you know I've seen a competitive player one that's hungry and is challenging and working on his craft and you know everybody wants to be the best at their position and Gonzo has a has a great chance to be able to do that. >> I know the league limits how many days you can be in full pads but I remember I would play with some guys and they were superstars without the pads on having the pads on does that really separate guys cuz >> Well we just look at pad level and you know how you can play a block and get off a block and you stay on your feet and tackle and you know again how can you handle some of the chaos and you know we try to practice just like we play we we running guys in and out and you know we try to move and we be as as efficient as we possibly can and I think our guys understand how how we have to practice. >> There's some guys that get overshadowed and not talked about like for instance on your wide receiver you made made a lot of additions this past year Ke'Shawn Booty you talked about him earlier in one of your press conferences about his work ethic I remember last year how much you mentioned him how ready he got to July and that's a guy that's out here having a pretty good camp so >> Sure he's gotten off to a good start and again talked about being a professional and I said this to him last year you know there's always going to be a lot of noise out there I think that's what you know that's everybody's job is to try to create noise and figure out what's going on and you know Ke'Shawn's handled everything exactly like a pro when he's gotten his opportunities last year he took advantage of them he's doing the same thing early on in camp and you know we appreciate what he's done. >> Coach great stuff. >> Wow. >> Good luck the rest of camp. >> Appreciate it. >> Can't wait to see you in that first preseason game. >> Thank you. >> Playing all the starters right? >> As of now. >> All right there you go here's >> That may change. >> Coach Mike Vrabel >> Oh.
