text: This is the Greg Bedard Patriots podcast with Nick Cattles. >> Everybody, it's the Greg Bedard Patriots podcast here at Gillette Stadium. Patriots wrapped up their sixth practice, second straight uh padded practice. It was a really good day for Drake May uh in the offense. Yesterday was a little sketchy at times for the offense, especially with the run blocking. Wasn't as much running today, but Drake May was extremely sharp. They could use the whole arsenal, a lot of play action, things like that, multiple personnel. Uh and they had it working. Drake May seemed in complete command. I had him 11 on 11 with five touchdowns and two sacks allowed. Not those those were on him. Um Really loved there was one play in the red zone where Drake May started off under center, saw something, backed out in the shotgun, audibled at the line, made a few gestures to the receivers, and then uh even though there was a free blitzer coming against him, he stood in, uh hit Demario Douglas in the left corner to beat Christian Gonzalez. Uh that was my uh favorite like Drake May play of the day, probably the the quote-unquote play of the day. And it was funny because it happened in the sort of opposite left corner end zone opposite the stands here, which were pretty full with fans and they were juiced up for one-on-ones and everything. But during team, uh Drake May hit Hunter Henry for a touchdown in the left corner of the end zone. When Drake released it, I and I saw the ball in the air, I didn't think that there was a much chance that Hunter Henry could get it, but uh the veteran tight end stuck his uh left paw out, tipped it up to himself, caught it, got his feet in bounds for a touchdown. Nobody really reacted among the fans, so I don't think they realized how good that play was. Uh it was outstanding. Uh, we did see, uh, Drake Maye and AJ Brown continue to make progress today. There was a session where they had a lot more of the field to work with. They weren't confined, um, to the red zone during that period. And I don't know if they set up Christian Gonzalez, but there was a double move with AJ Brown, and that got him wide open, uh, beyond Christian Gonzalez, uh, for a touchdown. So, those guys continue to just expand their familiarity and repertoire together. So, that was good to see. Um, I think that, uh, couple other things. So, we got more one-on-ones today. Will Campbell, uh, was three and oh. So was Michael Wenu. Both of them are now five and oh through two, uh, two days of padded practices. He was able to absorb the bull rush really well, and then, uh, the next time out, uh, he was aggressive, went out, really forceful punch, really good to see. Uh, I'm not going to go over the moon about Will Campbell at this point. Just it has nothing to do with him. I do like what I've seen, uh, as far as his improvement. title: Landon Dickerson & More on the Start of Training Camp
text: Everybody got their mic. There's not a lot of microphones, but all right. >> Sure the neighbors said that the new scheme is a little easier on them in some ways, notably because they get some more help or whatever. I'm just curious if you know it's easier in any way for the interior guys. >> Yeah, I think for the O-line as a whole, a big emphasis is eliminating kind of the slow play, um you know, not having a lot of time on the clock. Just getting up there, being able to make a call, stick with it, and run the play. So, I think for us it's just about getting to the ball and playing fast, which can help a lot. I mean, I'm sure you guys see that, you know, Vic and his defense, they like to move around and do all this other stuff. So, if you can get up there quick and just, you know, run your plays and not rely on what they're doing, then makes everybody's life a little easier. >> And then three days into practice, how are you feeling? >> No, I feel good. >> There was some talk this off season that maybe you considered retiring. Was there any any real consideration of that? >> Uh no. I'm not sure where you guys got that. So. >> At this point in your career, are you are you concerned at all though about the the cumulative wear and tear on your body? >> Not really. >> First time I asked you about going out to Columbia, what was that experience like? >> Yeah, I mean, Columbia, beautiful country, beautiful place. Uh you know, trying to look to get treatment, keep my body healthy, and you know, this is my job after all. So, exploring all avenues to try and feel good. >> A lot of you are doing stuff a lot of players have gone through that route. Like I'm just curious how'd you hear about it and how'd you come to find out about it? >> Yeah, I mean, honestly, just talking to a bunch of veteran guys from all across the league and you know, seeing what they do to stay healthy, what they do to feel good, and just it's really about finding what works for you. >> Can you tell if it's helped? >> Uh so far, yeah. >> And in like which ways you can >> Yeah, I mean, just feel good overall. I mean, football's that it doesn't feel soft and fuzzy whenever you play it, so I mean, yeah. Maybe. >> How much better is the off season when you don't have to rehab and you can just focus on on getting ready for the season. >> Yeah, not having a surgery is uh very nice. So. >> Did you lose Did you slow down any weight? >> Um I mean, not more than uh big trip to the bathroom. >> They say and not carrying his weight. >> Oh, yeah. >> You had last year obviously had the surgery during training camp. You had other injuries during the course of the season. >> Yeah. >> How do you feel this year versus last year? >> Yeah, I mean, like I said, not having surgery a week before the first game, good. Uh probably shouldn't have gone out there and played, but uh you live and you learn, you do stupid stuff when you're young, so. Yeah, I learned that mistake and uh yeah, other than that, not having to get cut on is nice. >> How's it going differently? >> Last year? Not came back till I was ready. >> How's it been acclimating to the new blocking scheme? What's the uh the biggest challenge so far? Anything that you're finding most interesting? >> Yeah, I mean, um again, like I said, this offense is is really just about being quick, getting to the ball and running our plays, and I think for us it's it's sometimes you want to overthink things, not in a bad way, but in a In the system we were in before, it was kind of problem-solving once we got to the line of scrimmage. This is just lets us get up there and play ball fast. >> And what's it been like with with the new voice in Chris Foerster? Um after all those years with Stout. >> Yeah, I mean, Cooper's doing a great job, obviously. Uh having a guy that you know, has coached in the league for a few years with some good offensive lines and also played. Um you know, he's got a lot of knowledge. Everybody's a little different in how they teach and coach things, and I think it's always it's a blessing to have somebody come in, you know, Stout I think is a tremendous, probably one of the best O-line coaches to ever coach. But there's also things that are new that Cooper brings in that, you know, I've learned from that could help me, so it's always good just gathering information and figuring out, you know, new things that work for you. >> As you know, you've been praised for your toughness and playing through injuries. As you go forward in your career, are you going to reconsider how you approach injury maintenance? >> Uh I mean, yeah. That's I don't think there's any reason to be tough and work through it if it's just going to wear you down because they don't pay you to be hurt. >> Is that a tough realization? Is that a tough realization to come to? >> I mean, not really, if you want to keep your job. >> How does your job change in this new scheme? >> Uh I mean, it doesn't it doesn't change a whole lot. I'm still playing left guard for the Philadelphia Eagles. So, um yeah, as of right now, that's that's still my job. It's just uh Uh the the scheme is different. It's a different kind of offense, and I think that it's uh it's been a tremendous change for us. >> Guys have talked about it being more sideline to sideline, you know, more of an emphasis on movement skills, I guess. How's that adjustment been for you? >> Yeah, I mean, again, I it's it's a different scheme that we've ran in the past, and I think that just with the the personnel and the guys that we have on this team right now, I think that it's a great fit. >> How much exposure did you have previously to the wide zone blocking scheme? Do you ever Do you Is that ever a predominantly the scheme that you ever blocked in? >> I I really haven't ever been in that scheme just throughout college and then the NFL, obviously, when I got here. Uh never been a part of that scheme, but also uh we've played a lot of teams with that scheme, and, you know, it's when you watch it, it's it's kind of it's a cool thing to watch, and now that we get to run it, I have an appreciation for it. >> Are there things about it that you didn't anticipate based on watching it from afar? >> Uh I mean, yeah, once you start to dive into things, it's I mean, it's nothing crazy at the end of the day, kind of I mean, football at its bare bones doesn't change in a whole lot, but there's a lot of things that kind of this new age of football, um you know, with Manion, these kind of West Coast offenses that we're doing to uh give different looks to defenses and make it harder. >> We hadn't talked to you since, I guess, talking about this this doubt on the left. >> Um how was your stance on all that Allen and Town? >> Uh you know I mean I I appreciate Stout, everything he did, the player that he made me be. Um I know a bunch of guys here appreciate what he did and I don't think that anybody faults him. I mean you know he I don't know if you could tell but he's a little older. I know his personality says he's 18 years old but um yeah I think he just decided it was his time to kind of start enjoying life, enjoying his grandkids and you know you can't fault the man for that. >> Yeah, next one. >> Thanks Ty. Few days Few days into practice, how you feeling in the offense? Feel like you're picking it up good? >> Yeah, I feel great. Uh I've been around Shawn a little bit uh with the Packers so you know it was just a little cleaning up and getting on the details of do new words. Um learning the new words but I'm a little familiar with with the offense, what we got going. >> You obviously had a little bit of a head start in this offense. Shawn was mentioning that he was impressed by the recall from all of your teammates. Did you see that as well and how does that like show up on the field? >> Uh man it's been good. Uh you know everybody been been learning the offense well. you know me getting into this offense, it was hard. It was hard to learn but uh being here uh people learning it fa- faster than expected. Um so that that helped us you know build chemistry quicker and you know be able to see things better. >> What do you have in particular to In what ways was it hard to learn? >> Uh it's just a lot of different details and you know assignment alignments you have to have to learn. Um you know it's not just going out and running routes, you know and uh doing doing certain things like that you used to doing as a as a player. Um you know you got to know details that marry up with you know know QB that help him learn us, you know and help us learn them. >> You have a relationship with Shawn where, you know, you guys sort of talk about Green Bay or or it's interesting for you to watch him in this new role? >> Yeah, man. It's fun It's been fun seeing Shawn, you know, uh grow as a as a OC. Um from coming here to OTAs, uh you know, I used to see Shawn around Green Bay a lot, tell him what's up. But now, you know, we talk a little more. Um you know, being that he have that role, you know, it's good to see that. >> How is the chemistry coming along with you and um >> It's been good, man. We been You know, it's only it's only the start of camp. Um you know, and it's been good so far getting it in with him. Um you know, during the teams periods, uh you know, watching him go through with the other receivers, you know, learning from that. Um you know, we just learn from each other and you know, build chemistry that way. >> Have you learned more from Shawn than you probably ever did before in your life? Is there anything you learned about him that you didn't know? >> Uh it's the most I It's the most I really ever heard Shawn talk. You know, I ain't really hear him talk that much um in Green Bay, but um he more hands-on now. Come up talking to the players. Uh you see that and you notice that as a player. Um you know, and some of the other guys come around asking me about Shawn and they see that too. So, you know, that's a good thing. >> How would you describe his teaching style when he's in front of the room? >> He smooth talker. Um you know, he don't get too loud. He He He He just, you know, say what he say um and his details in it. You know, he say every detail he need to help us learn the right way. Um tell us what he need, you know, we just go out and execute that. >> That uh catch you had two days ago, what worked on that play? The catch you had here two days ago, the leaping catch. Uh what worked on that play? What? >> They just trust. building that chemistry like you said, that chemistry and trust. Uh her Jay just coming out, you know, uh he don't see nobody, he just throw it up, you know, and trusting me to go get that. And I that's what I did. >> How much does that mean to you, this >> Uh you know, I I think it's a big opportunity for everybody in our room. you know, we got a lot of players, uh great players in our room, I think, and you know, everybody marry up with each other, you know, everybody could do different things, so I think that help us out all, you know, individually, um and you know, I think it's going to be a fun fun year with that with our group. >> What what are what are your impressions of how he's playing like what what have you seen from him so far? >> Can you repeat that? >> McKyle McKyle Lemon, what have you >> Oh, McKyle. Man, I just I just think he a dog, you know, uh don't talk too much, don't don't complain a lot, he just go out and work. Um and that's what you that's what you want to get from a, you know, a young a young player. Feel me? Uh I think he just go out and work, and he he a baller. >> How much do you appreciate that trust from Jaylen on the second day of camp to to throw up a ball like that for you? >> I mean, as a receiver, that's what you want from your QB, you know, uh to get those opportunities where you can go show the world what you could do. Um man, you know, that's what he did, so you know, you just got to go up and make them plays to build that trust. Uh and and that that coming camp, you know, it start in practice, you know, so when when it happen in the game, you know, it's already been done um a thousand times in practice, so just building that chemistry and trust, you know, uh that's all that's all it take. >> What's been the biggest adjustment What's been the biggest adjustment to moving to Philly? Uh >> I really just say it's like it's a bigger city. Feel me? Uh Green Bay wasn't a lot to do, you know, a lot to get into. but now it's it's a lot that can, you know, get into uh Green Bay, I used used to stay in the house, go to practice. It's all football there. But here, you know, you get out in the community, um do a lot of different things, and just adjusted to like, you know, the people. Um it's different. You didn't really used to see a lot of people around. Uh only at practices, you feel me? So, uh just being around the city, you see a lot more people. And that that's a big adjustment. >> What teammates have you spent most time with? >> Most time with? Yeah. Say it again? >> Teammates you've spent most time with? >> Teammates? I mean, I spent a lot of time with the receiver room. Around here is I I would say it's similar to Green Bay, you know, uh it's a real brotherhood over here. Um everybody everybody like each other. You don't see no no animosity around the building. Um everybody talk to each other. You got groups in the locker room, you know, having convos, um whatever it's about. You feel me? Uh I think I think everybody over here is you know, is is good teammates. Um even the defense, I talk to the defensive players a lot. You know, and I think that's going to help us build a connection to to eventually win uh when season come. >> How challenging has it been? Yeah, it's pretty heralded secondary group with two Pro Bowl All-Pro guys and Richard Sherman. I mean, what are those challenges like going against those guys every day? >> I look at it as a as a plus for us. Um like I was telling our receivers today, like we going against, you know, a a great a great defense put together like put together is it's a elite defense. So, you know, us having our ins and outs with them, um when we get to season, it's going to be easy. You know, going against other people like we not going to see this every week. You know, having a whole defense that's put together like our then our secondary, you know, they just making us better. You know, us going against them every day, learning, you know, what we need to do different to beat them. Um it's not just really beating them. We thinking about it is, you know, going out and beat other corners or other safeties. Feel me? Uh >> Go ahead. >> Yeah, you got >> Uh as a receiver with some size, uh is it is it a help to have Earnest as the position coach as the guy who played in this league? And as a bigger receiver, does that help you at all? >> Yeah, it helped a lot, you know, cuz he he been through it. You know, he played in the league. So, you know, he could be hands-on and you know, he know a lot more um being that he he's been there before. and he's also been up against some guy. You know, he he can show you more like he can relate. So, you know, it helped. He know a lot um and he can help us, you know, help each other. So, yeah, being around coach Amey, I feel like it helped me a lot, you know, knowing that he know a lot and I could put my trust in him, you know, because I know that he didn't been through these things we going through now. >> Thanks, Tay. >> Tay, when you got traded here, uh you you want >> Yeah, I didn't mean to interrupt. >> Uh Pre snaps up. >> How's your first uh pro training camp going? Any surprises? >> Uh no, I feel good, you know, to really get out here with the whole team. First training camp, so now everything's been going good. I've been excited to hit, you know, hit the field each and every day. >> You've always been known as a confident player out in the field. How do you balance coming into this situation, first time in the NFL, maintain that confidence, but also kind of being deferential to veterans and everyone else around? >> Yeah, I know my ability, know what I could do on the field. So, just bringing my talent, you know, to the team um the best I can. Uh whatever they need me to do, you know, just doing at a high level. Whatever they expect, you know, just making sure, you know, I just do my job at a high level. Um you know, just knowing every time I step on the field, just knowing what I got to do. >> What what are you finding is the biggest adjustment? The biggest adjustment so far? >> Um I think obviously just learning a new playbook, you know, my first time with this playbook, first time with the team. so just making sure I get that down is probably the you know the biggest thing and then you know I feel like yeah, that's it. >> What is going into the building trust with Jalen Hurts? >> Uh just making sure um you know I just do my assignment really. Just getting the extra reps in. Um just making sure we'll be on the same page so you know we'll go out there hit the field you know we ain't thinking too much. >> From a non-football perspective what I'm sorry from a non-football perspective what was the biggest thing you learned about Jalen in spending time with him this off season? >> Um man he a cool guy really. You know he just wants the best out of all of us. Um and then you know me being a rookie new to the team you know him bringing me under his wing you know I appreciate him for that. He don't got to do that at all so um you know him just being a leader you know off the field you know that that was pretty cool to see. >> What's it like going up against Cooper DeJean in the slot? >> Yeah no he's a great player. You know he makes me better each and every day making sure I be on my P's and Q's. Um you know you know he's he's one of the best at his position so you know um I appreciate you know that you know when I'm in practice is going against the best. >> And Mekhi have there been moments where you I mean they're throwing a lot at you. Have there been moments where you kind of like it's it almost feels like you know not too much but like just a lot to handle and have you had those challenges? >> You know I don't feel like it's too much you know. Whatever they take at me you know I appreciate that um knowing that they got the trust you know that to me um to you know throw things at me like that so just backing up their trust um just making sure you know I I do my job. >> What what is in this offense what is new to you that maybe you haven't really played with before in terms of what you've been asked to receive? >> Yeah I feel like just the whole offense how it's ran you know. Just the whole you know huddling up you know play calls all that is new to me so just making sure I pick up on that fast so you know I hit the field you know you know that I can back up their trust so you know I go out there do my job. That's all. >> You apparently you suffered a hamstring injury in the spring. What happened there and and how was the recovery? >> You know recovery is good. You know just going out there just pulled a hammy. Um nothing too crazy about that. Just making sure, you know, I would recovered well. So, when I came out to training camp, you know, I was 100% healthy. >> How do you think the veterans like Davante, Hollywood, um, Dontay Vean kind of help you along? What kind of advice do they give you? Like, what How much do you go to them? >> Yeah. Now, it's great to have them guys, you know, in my room. You know, I'm I'm the youngest, you know, guy there. I'm the only rookie. So, to have a bunch of guys, you know, in my room that had experience, you know, in the league, you know, that's the best position I want to be in. So, I'm going out there, you know, asking them for advice. Um, you know, just how to do certain things, how to run routes, you know, what they see cuz they they done it before multiple times, you know, at a high level. So, me just being, you know, the student of the game, you know, rookie coming in, just trying to get all the information I can. >> What's the biggest What's the biggest thing that they taught you or told you? What's the biggest piece of advice that they've given you? >> Yeah. Um, I'll say maybe just just try to perfect me at at my my play. You know, don't try to be like the next guy, you know, just just try to perfect, you know, what I my play is. I think that's the biggest thing. >> As far as guard, what is your interaction with Davante been like? >> Yeah, it's been good. You know, he's a great guy, you know, great receiver. So, um, you know, just giving me all the game that he can get. Yeah. >> You talked about the one of the biggest things is learning the offense. We've seen you line up in the slot a lot. Are they giving you, um, in terms of the offense, learning a lot in terms of splitting wide? Is that Is that as much going to be a part of what you do here as it is lining up in the slot? >> Yeah, I feel like that's that's the, you know, the good thing about this offense that you can move guys all around, you know, not just, you know, being in the slot, but all around. So, you know, whatever they need me to do, you know, I'm making sure I'm available to do that. >> How do you feel about fielding punts and if that's a responsibility they ask you to do, how prepared do you feel to step into that role? >> Yeah, whatever they need me to do, you know, that that's what I'm going to do. You know, I feel comfortable, you know, doing whatever they need me to do. Like you said, catch a punt, whatever, kickoff return, you know, whatever it is, you know, I'm going to make sure I do that, you know, at a high level. >> The time you spent with Jaylen in the summer, how much did that help out here and and how does that help? >> Yeah, and it helps a lot. You know, so it ain't the first time we out here, you know, throwing certain routes, you know, making sure our chemistry right, you know, in the off season. And uh it only made it better when we step out on the field training camp. >> You spent time with Jalen in the summer? >> Yeah, for sure. Yeah, I went out to Houston with him for a couple days, so that was good, you know. Yeah, in his hometown. >> Okay. Thanks for coming. >> Appreciate y'all. >> Just a couple days into camp, how do you feel in this offense? How comfortable are you? feeling good uh just to be out here meeting everyone, getting it going. It's been a lot of fun. >> You spent some time with Jalen, it seems like this off season getting getting in work. Have you seen the benefits of that so far in the first few days? >> Uh definitely. Uh timing is key, you know, whenever you come into a new offense, you got to get the timing down. And I feel like we we was working hard at it and we we've been putting it together a little bit these uh first few days. >> What do you like about this offense? >> Uh just a lot of moving parts. Uh feel like, you know, we all gelling together really good and we're we're we're going to be an attacking offense. >> Sean McVay was telling us before practice that every receiver has a different role in this offense. What would you say your role is right now? >> Uh I feel like, you know, whatever they ask us to be like in the in the room, whatever we're called to do, like we're taking it and we're doing it to the best of our ability. I feel like for me, just being a dynamic guy uh on the offense and getting in and making plays. >> What has the defense presented the challenges the defense has presented? It's a veteran sort of a veteran. >> Mhm. Great defense. Uh they match up really well. They fly around, play great team defense, so it's been a lot of fun going against those guys. >> What's the transition like when, you know, you have a bunch of new receivers coming in and also a new offensive coordinator? Like, what's the learning process? How long do you think it it takes and everything? Is it a long adjustment? >> Uh I mean, credit to to how we putting together a great room because I feel like we all help each other tremendously. And uh Jalen does a good job when we were in the off season like putting us in those situations that when we come out here, we was doing those same situations in the offseason. So, uh it's a it's a good group. >> You play for a lot of play calls. What's your impression of Shawn and how he's presenting the system? >> Uh very detailed. I've been enjoying his meetings. Uh the way he's uh teaching us and the way we're picking up on it. Uh it's been like I said, a lot of fun. >> Did you see McKai in person at all? >> Uh no. >> [laughter] >> I know you and and Jaylen didn't cross paths at at OU, but but um what did you hear about him coming in and and how has that kind of lived up to uh you know, how it's playing out right now? >> Uh even coming in, you know, before I decided that I was going into the league, uh just, you know, great things about Jaylen. Uh true leader, true pro, and the same same thing here. Uh even getting with him, uh totally, you know, a pro for sure. >> In terms of just a guy in in the building, how does he compare to to Mahomes and Lamar and the other quarterbacks you've known? >> Uh true leader. Like, you know, those guys, you get inside those franchises, you can tell like they're a leader. Jay is a leader. Uh feel like he's been a leader everywhere he's been. So, uh it's not really nothing new to him. >> What ways does he show that? >> Uh just professionalism, how he go about his business, uh how he carries himself, lead by example, uh he's vocal, um just, you know, whatever you want in a quarterback, he does it. >> You mentioned those meetings with Shawn Mannion. The players we've spoken to, they say there's always a reason why he's showing something, that everyone understands why they're running a play. How important is that for a receiver? >> Uh very important, easy to get behind. Uh we know in the run game, we got to fly off the ball a certain way because that might marry a route in the passing game. So, for us, it's uh the details matter, and uh there's going to be details that help us win games. >> What's stood out to you so far about McKai as a rookie? >> Uh McKai works extremely hard. he's very detailed as well, and uh he's tough. He's competing every day. Uh you guys can see he's he's getting hit, bouncing back up, you know, going hard the next play. So, I'm impressed with him. >> How important is versatility among you guys in the receiver room? Like you can line up anywhere, do a lot of things. >> Uh it's very important. Like I said, you know, the run game is like a staple for us. So, for all of us to be interchangeable, line up in different places, and do different things is going to allow us to attack the defenses in different ways. >> Going back to Makai, like you know, as a veteran who's kind of been around and played for a bunch of different quarterbacks, like what do you kind of take him under your wing a little bit? I'm sorry, do you kind of take him under your wing a little bit? What kind of things do you point out to him? >> Uh for sure, I try to share as much as I can with him, especially he coming from my guy coach Riley. You know, I come from that system. Uh so, just uh whatever tips I can give him uh to help him with the transition. But, he's he's like I said, he's coming in doing a good job. >> And you see him kind of guy who like seek seek veterans out and stuff and ask for advice or is that >> Oh yeah, he had he had come and ask his questions. Uh come off to the side, ask, you know, what we seeing. So, he's been doing a good job. >> Well, a couple days into camp, just how are you feeling getting back out here? I know a big injury you're coming back from. How you feeling overall? >> Uh I feel good. Uh I feel like, you know, things been going good. I mean, it it feel great to be back. I'm out there moving how I want to move. Just overall, it just feels good to be back. >> You got a smile on your face. Like is it something that you missed during this time? >> Yeah, definitely. Definitely. Yeah, I mean, I definitely missed being out there with the guys. I mean, it was unfortunate what happened, but you know, just happy to be back, man. That's all. >> How's your two for you with, you know, you're much more comfortable in this system now going at, you know, coming off an injury. Now you're healthy going into this camp with kind of a defined role. How does that make you feel and how how's it going for you? >> Uh just attacking every day. I just going in with the confidence knowing that, you know, I've been in this system for a year now. So, I know what to expect. Uh I feel like I've had enough reps, you know, at the position to, you know, consider myself kind of a veteran a little bit with the amount of snaps I played. So, just excited to be back, you know, just excited to show that I can, you know, I'm able to do that again. So, >> How do your responsibilities change with Reed gone? Are you taking on a little bit more communication? Is that correct? >> Yeah, yeah, I mean, definitely. I mean, with Reed gone, I feel like, you know, it's my time to step up, you know, like you said, communication-wise, just getting guys, you know, in the right spots, right places, you know, just playing ball from there. >> Have you ever had an injury that kept you out as long as like this latest one? >> Yeah, no, this this first first for me. I've had I've had like in college small things, nothing crazy, but this one that kept me out the longest. >> What were some of the challenges of going through that? >> Uh just not being able to play uh for that long, to be honest, and it's probably the only thing, but I feel like, you know, going through that process, going through that whole thing mentally, I feel like, you know, I was in the right head space. Uh kept a positive mindset, and I just attacked, you know, every day just trying to get back to my normal self. >> How much did it become more about learning the mental side of the game during that time than I thought it would be? >> Uh it was pretty big. Uh just to keep myself, you know, involved in, you know, what's going on, and trying to help the other guys, you know, that's, you know, asking questions as well. And really just trying to keep my mind sharp. Uh I feel like, you know, in that situation, you can't do nothing but, you know, try to learn as much as you can, and just keep learning. >> When Reed When Reed left in free agency, there was a bit of a question of of where this safety group would stand. How much are you taking ownership that this is your spot now? >> Uh I mean, you know, every we got to come out and compete at the end of the day every day. Uh I mean, there's really nobody's spot. Uh anybody's spot can be taken at any point if you're not doing what you're supposed to do, so just coming in with the mindset that you know, just competing every day. Uh compete a competitive nature, uh and I mean, you got to you got to have that mindset cuz we got a we got a lot of good guys on the in the room that's doing good. Uh Epps, uh Mike Carter doing good, him uh safety. We got the younger guys doing good as well, Sam. Uh so, I mean, it's a it's a good group of guys that's coming in and working and competing every day, and we'll see where it takes us. >> What's it like having Marcus alongside you for, you know, obviously Cooper, you know, goes in the nickel. What's it like having Marcus that veteran presence alongside you? >> Uh I mean, it feels great. Like you said, veteran presence. Uh you know, he kind of I'm kind of, but he's been doing this longer than me, so he kind of sees things differently so being able to know ask the questions that I want to ask and being able to grow my game just watching him do what he do and cuz he's been in this league for so long and he's stayed in this league for so long so just having him there kind of you know helps me kind of see you know how things would be you know in the future whether when I'm in that situation you know help helping the younger guys and just trying to you know work alongside with the with your other partner. >> How do you how do you grade Cooper DeJean at safety? >> Uh Cooper's coming along pretty well. Uh I mean he's obviously learning uh but you know he's coming along pretty well. He's just natural he's he's a natural defensive uh defensive back. You know he's going to make plays on the ball. Um I mean he's going to do what he do. Cooper can do what he do but he's coming along pretty well though. I like I like where he's going. >> What are some of the biggest challenges you think in your mind for someone to go from nickel to safety and have to go back and forth during the game? What what what what challenges do you think that brings? >> Uh I mean just just the position. I feel like you know at at nickel you're close to the ball so you you think differently uh you play differently with with the runs cuz you're close to the ball. Obviously with safety you're further away from the ball so just you know finding the right angles and you're just trying to play in space. I feel like it's a it's a little different than playing close to the ball obviously so I mean that's for anybody that's converting from nickel to safety just trying to figure out you know the depth and you know how to play position. >> Are there certain areas that you identified going into this year that you want to improve on or are you working on them? >> Uh I mean all areas all areas to be honest uh I mean just trying to get better in whatever way I can whether that's mentally or whether that's physically with my ankle or you know catching the ball or just just all over the place so trying to trying to better my game. >> How much how much further do you feel like you were than you know coming in as a rookie last year? >> Say that one more time a bit. >> How much further do you feel you know being in this camp compared to last year you know coming in as a rookie? >> Uh I feel a lot further. Uh I mean obviously like I said earlier I've been in this system for a year now so I've seen a lot and you know I've learned a lot you know with my time and with the snaps that I've played and you know just coming in you know I feel like it's my time you know to take it to the next level as far as my learning and doing doing a little bit more uh and and it's it's it's that time for me. >> How different is it for Joe Kasper to be the secondary coach instead of just a safety coach? >> Uh it's no different. It's no different. I mean, Joe Kasper going to be Joe Kasper. Uh I mean, truthfully, I don't I don't really see a difference. He was still coaching the secondary with what's-his-name was here. They were both doing it, so I mean, it kind of I guess you could say it makes it better cuz that's my position coach, so I can know what he thinking as a as a whole deep knowledge of the safety position, so that's probably the another benefit for me. >> All right, Joe. >> Thanks, Joe. >> Appreciate it.

title: Sean Mannion on the Offense's Focus During Training Camp
text: How are you? >> Doing well, how are you? >> Sorry, but prepared. >> On offense. >> Uh what's your plan for Um what do you stand on Jalen Hurts as a runner in the design? >> Yeah. Yeah, it's a great question. Um you know, he he's very uniquely talented in terms of that athletic ability. It's something he's been um effective with throughout his career. Um so, you know, that that's part of what makes him such a such a special talent. Um but he does a lot of things well. Um you know, I think you know, he he's really operated through all facets of the offense comfortably, but um the the piece of him um as an athlete in the running game is is something unique that um you know, the the those are elements we can lean into, you know, a little bit as well. >> So, he does kind of fall into that category. Um obviously being under center a lot, do you restrict having those at least plus one type of zone read and RPO? Does that restrict him from doing that as much or we see before I guess when we were just being under center? And all of that, is there room for him to have that that that facet of the offense? >> Yeah, I I think it there's definitely room for both. There's room for both and I think a lot of it is just depending on, you know, week by week or or situationally. Um you know, there's a lot of different things that come up throughout the game. Um you know, from one week to the next, things you're seeing from the defense. So, I think to have all those different elements in your back pocket, I think there's I think there's room for many different things. Um the two that you mentioned certainly, you know, can both uh you know, live together in in in some form or fashion. >> What do you look for in these early days? You're throwing so much new stuff at everybody. What do you look for to kind of get a sense of where they are and how they're progressing? >> Yeah, I think the biggest thing we want is is great effort every day and then compete. You know, that was a big thing coming in coming into this this camp for us is is every day is is high-level competition. You're competing against yourself, competing, you know, for a role on the roster, and then and then getting to compete against the defense every day is going to make us better and better. And then, you know, I think you know, for us offensively it's, "Hey, can we have a really sound pre-snap operation?" Um you know, those are some of the things early in camp, you know, day one we we struggled with a little bit. I thought there was improvement day two. Um and then just assignment, alignment, execution. You know, are we getting lined up properly? Um are we are we not having mental errors? Um and so through, you know, through the first two days of practice, it's still early, but um I'm happy with the you know, the progress we've made and we just got to keep improving from there. >> You evaluate the receiver position. Are you just looking for the players who play the best or are you keeping an eye on like complimentary skill sets in that group? >> Yeah, I think we have a very um a very exciting group there and I think just like you said, it's because there are so many complimentary skill sets. Um you know, what we look for, you know, a ton of flexibility in terms of everybody can line up anywhere and and and uh we can move people around and it opens up a lot of exciting possibilities. That's part of what makes this group um really fun to work with. You know, you have a lot of guys who can play off of one another in different ways and um like I said, it opens up a lot of possibilities for our offense just cuz, you know, that whole that whole group um everyone's bringing something to the table. >> I know when it comes to install, when it comes to install, Sean, I guess going back to your playing days or your time in Green Bay, does anything change when it's new versus having the same process there for a couple years? >> You know, I think there's a comfortability that comes maybe, but but honestly, I think every camp I went into, um you know, you might have heard the play before and and uh but you you pick up a new coaching point each time through. I think that's part of the that's part of the joy of coaching, you know, for me is, you know, you know, I'm I'm installing this play now for the second time. These guys were, you know, they did a great job day one. I was really impressed with the retention after the summer break, um which is a testament to our guys. They're pros. You know, they were clearly studying over the off season over the off season program over the break, but getting back to your question, you know, I think that's part of the the fun of coaching, the fun of playing is yeah, I've heard this play before, but how am I going to take it to the next level? And for me, can I give them a coaching point that will help them execute it even better, even though they know it? Can I help them know it even better? And so, each time through, I found um you know, you can you can learn something new about the play that helps you execute it. >> What's your view of the defense? What's your What's your view of the defense? Third year under Fangio, a lot of Pro Bowlers on that side. How How What's your takeaway on them? >> Yeah, I mean, it's a it's a tremendous group. I mean, Coach Fangio, um you know, he's he's a he's as good as it gets in this league and has been for a long time. Um it's going to make us, you know, it's a it's a it's a great competition for us every day going against a an elite unit there. Um you know, I know, you know, playing against Philly the last couple years when I was in Green Bay, they're tough. They're tough. They play hard. They play fundamentally sound. Um you know, there's a lot of great players over there, and um you know, it's it's an awesome challenge for us every day to go against them, and um you know, it'll it'll only make us better. >> So, I'm curious how all the guys on offense have been here for several years in in Nick's system and everything like that. How have you found the transition for these guys to what you're trying to teach? Like, how is that? Like, do you find they're still kind of set in their ways? Are they willing to learn? How has that been working out? >> No, it's been great. They they've been super willing to learn. Um it like like I said, you know, it's a great group of guys to work with. I think the biggest thing is so many of these you know, all these guys are so hungry for um to learn. They're so hungry for, you know, the individual periods where we're teaching them the technique. Um and so, that's been you know, that's all you want as a coach is guys that are that are willing to learn and and want to work at it. And you know, across our entire roster, you know, that those are the type of guys um that Howie's brought in. Those are the type of guys we get to work with every day. And um you know, like I said, you know, again, from the summer from the offseason program, you know, you have a summer break and coming back, I mean, I thought day one and two and we had some pre-snap stuff to to fix, but um their retention was out retention from the spring was outstanding and allows for us to pick up right where we left off and and and kind of keep building from >> Going back to Going back to Vic, how much with how much he's emulated across the league, how instructive is it specifically with with the pre-snap stuff? Um like the motions and some of the formation tells, how helpful is it for you to see how he responds to some of that stuff? >> Yeah, it's it's it's a little bit of a chess chess match every every day, you know, um you're scripting things in practice and then you're studying, you know, how is our defense responding to them, you know, the things we're doing. Um and there might be some commonalities across the league and in other weeks there might not. It's a little bit um you know, depending on the other team's play caller and um you know, their offense their defensive system and and what we're doing to try to um to try to attack it, but certainly, [snorts] you know, each day we're you know, we're studying and trying to see, okay, is there something we can build off of you know, that formation or that motion or that route distribution. and you're trying to gauge how are we able to affect the defense and what else could there be off of that. Some of that might carry over from one opponent to the next. Um like you said, Vic's Vic's been you know, emulated around the league, but there's differences, too. So, it's a little bit of a weekly thing, but you're always studying to see what what's happening out there. >> As far as you want to you want a true fullback or do you when you look about the duties that might be there, what are the What are the thoughts where it could come out of someone out of the backfield or a tight end? >> Yeah, I I think, you know, without getting too too far into the the details of it, I think as as multiple as we can be formationally, I think that's always something we want to try to do and especially um train these guys to do multiple things throughout camp. Um but a lot of it will be, you know, there's a ton of practice left. So, we have to, you know, try to push these guys to to learn as much as they can. How flexible can everybody be in terms of their alignments and assignments? Um while at the same time understanding we're putting them all in the best position to be the best players they can be. >> If as the backs catching the ball out of the backfield, how prominent is that in the offense? How does say Quon and Tank fit into that? >> Yeah, it's again, don't want to get too far into specifics, but I think they're all very very capable of that and you know, the the backs have you know, protection responsibilities. Sometimes you know, sometimes they they might be a free release back. So a lot of it kind of depends on the play. It depends on maybe what the defense is bringing and what we need for from a protection standpoint, but they're all capable pass catchers and and route runners. I I think a lot of it sometimes comes down to the protection element and and do we need you know, a six man of protection, seven man of protection so on and so forth and then some of it is you know, defensively is there a match up we want to attack, but they'd certainly bring that skill set to the table and and you know, it's something that every day like I said, we're we're trying to push these guys and and have everyone have the most as much flexibility with what they can do so that when we get in the season, we know how to put these guys in the best position possible. >> You've during the season the scheme is offensive line friendly. I would like to hear why you think that is and then obviously you're going to be taking from somewhere. You're going to help the offensive line. Where is the contraction coming from? >> Um you know, I I think I understood the first part of your question, but I I guess in terms of being O line friendly, I think one of the things we you know, you know, I preach, uh Coop preaches with the offensive line group every day is assignment commitment, right? We want these guys to go up there, know exactly where to go and play fast. So if you know, throughout all of our teaching, we want to make as many things black and white for them as possible so that we're all on the same page and we're off and running. And if the defense changes the look, you know, at least we all know exactly where we're going and we're going with total assignment commitment to attack our aiming points, attack our targets and then you know, that will ultimately allow us to play fast, play physical, have the play style that we want, but we want to make everything as cut and dry, you know, black and white for the offensive line so that they really can fire off and and have like I said, you know, the term we use is assignment commitment to what they're doing. >> Sean, in the second part in the second part second part >> Oh, yeah. >> Yeah, but if you are going you're talking about help that they get they get help that maybe they do previously they didn't get. And is that you know, I mean they talk about inside help, but obviously at some point >> Yeah, I think I understand I think I understand your question now. Um you know, I think one of the things that's unique about the offensive line is you is they are all working in conjunction with one another with the tight ends. Um so, I think a lot of it is is the time they spend with one another. It's a tight-knit group. Um you know, the unit there's there's a lot of times where, you know, they may work it be working drills with one another. You know, maybe different than a receiver who's running an individual route versus air. There's so much offensive lineman playing in conjunction with another offensive lineman or with a tight end or how the backs, you know, track fits into certain things. Um so, yeah, I think all those things lend itself to um your original question where it's, you know, it does feel I think to them that hey, it's a friendly system where I have help because I'm working with my, you know, with my with my running mate here whether it be the tight end, running back, or offensive lineman. >> Sean, how do you spend your time on on the practice field and in meeting rooms? Obviously, your your background is a quarterback, so do you have to be intentional about moving around with the other position groups or do you lean on your expertise and and find yourself with the quarterbacks? >> Yeah, no, I I definitely have to be intentional. I'd say it's it's a blend of all those things. Um you know, some of it has to do with the special teams time, you know, the quarterbacks aren't in the special teams meetings, so I can always kind of steal some time in the QB room there. Um the offensive line, you know, unless we're using field goal field goal block they typically um you know, you get a little bit extra meeting time to spend them with them there, but um yeah, that's that's been one of the adjustments for me um you know, in this role is is um one, you're addressing the unit every day and and that's been great having all of our unit meetings where the whole unit's in there together. I think that's so critical. But then, you know, also um, you know, spending time with every group. That That's been a lot of fun, honestly. It's been uh It's been great to get to lean into the fundamentals of all the different positions. >> With Jalen, have you had learnings through that of like, "Oh, I hadn't thought of that in that way from that position group's perspective?" >> No, I I think I think the biggest thing is um you know, just you get questions from a different perspective. Um And so, again, you know, I I think that that part's fun to get to talk about um the defense the details blocks up front um with the guys. And And obviously, you know, Coop and and and Ryan, you know, they're in the meeting rooms all the time as a position coach answering those questions. But, you know, when I'm in and out of all the different kind of units, um that part's been a lot of fun. >> When you were with >> Jalen the other day, he said as much as he's trying to learn from you, he's also trying to be of of service to you given his experience. How have you leaned on him throughout the this whole process and how do you feel this off-season? >> Oh, yeah. It It's been a It's been a constant um you know, back-and-forth. And you know, Jalen's had a ton of success in this league and um you know, has has played in a lot of games. So, I you know, I always want to know the things that he feels comfortable with. Um if there's something that maybe we need to detail up further for him. Um you know, cuz there's so many things that um you know, you'd love to dive into really the nitty-gritty of a play and and and help him um you know, help him just to with total mastery and um I think a lot of it is for me as a play-caller getting a feel for, you know, what are his comfort calls. the things that um you know, on a second and long um that he feels, you know, super confident in. So, it's been a great partnership, you know, with Jalen since we got here. you know, the back-and-forth has been outstanding. He asks really thought-provoking questions. And um you know, it it it's been a lot of fun to work with him. >> Have you spent much time studying other teams that transition to this type of offense? And what did you find in terms of how to get a system up and running as quickly as possible? >> Yeah, you know, we we we study, you know, tons of teams around the league. Um, you know, that's that's the that's the fun of the off-season, you know, before these players are in here. Um, obviously we're implement implementing our offensive system, building our offense. Um, but you're always looking around the league, you're always looking in college and and finding new ideas from everywhere. title: Tory Horton: "It's A Blessing To Be Back On The Field" | Seattle Seahawks
text: What's most meaningful to you about being back on the field again? >> Uh yeah, I feel like just making most of my opportunities, you know. Uh it's a blessing to be back on the field and just trying to take in every moment uh cuz you know, just like last year, you never know when you know, it'll be cut short. So, just trying to make the most of every opportunity and just be there for my guys. >> A few weeks ago, Mike McDonald said you guys got really good news and that you're going to be back. Uh talk us through what that was like when you got that good news. >> Uh yeah, you know, it's just a just a whole bit of a excitement, you know. Of course, you always want to hear that, you know, you you've been cleared and you know, uh we're going to start progressing to the field work and you know, that's something that I just been looking forward to. So, having the opportunity to hear that from, you know, the head coach himself, um you know, that's that's great to me and you know, I'm excited about it and I'm just trying to keep moving forward. >> What happened? >> Uh yeah, so it was kind of weird, you know, uh about like week three, I kind of started feeling my shin and you know, uh worked through it through a couple games, got to week nine and you know, got it checked up and found out there was a crack. So, you know, I uh ended up getting surgery on it um and that was that was that. Um just just something that you know, you just got uh you work through till you can't. So, you know, it's just uh not something that I wish happened, but it did and you know, we got the issue solved and you know, the leg ain't going anywhere now, so feel pretty good. >> So, you played a few games with it? >> Uh yeah, uh Uh yeah, it ain't it ain't really like no feel not as bad as it got um until, you know, after the game uh the Washington game, but you know, of course, those couple weeks before just building up, uh there were always a little something there that I felt and you know, over the weeks it just kind of got worse and worse and you know, I finally took the time to get it checked out and that's when we found out that >> Was that news you're playing so well, you had the two touchdowns in Washington game and then then to find out you're going to >> Yeah, you know, um of course that's not the news I wanted to hear especially after the Commanders game. Um I just felt like I I let the team down a little bit just not being able to go back out there as much as I wanted. Um it was even times where I still tried to go out there and you know run some routes and the trainers had to tell me you know to to take it easy. Um but you know dealing with a bone thing is you just got to let that heal. There's no like you know playing through that once you get to a certain uh point. So you know um I I did the most I could and made it to however far I got and you know when the time came and I couldn't go no more I didn't want to put you know my the team at a disadvantage of me going out there knowing that something is bothering me and you know I feel like we just kind of made the smart move of you know just holding out seeing if it heals on its own and you know just kind of the time kind of got away from us. So >> So you didn't have to have surgery? >> I did have surgery. Yeah, I got a metal rod in there. So the leg ain't going anywhere. >> It is your tibia you said? >> Uh yeah, it was a tibia. So it was the the shin bone. Yeah. >> Was there ever a thought after the Washington game that you would be able to come back and play anymore? >> Oh yeah, of course. You know shoot I've been playing with it since week three. So you know I always thought I was going to come back and you know the initial plan was to come back for playoffs and you know we was rehabbing so much and you know being extremely smart about it and you know trying to push through some things to come back for the playoffs. Of course that didn't you know go according to plan but you know I'm excited for my guys and you know now we looking forward to you know another another year just you know just trying to move forward from the injury. >> When was When did you have the surgery? >> Huh? >> When was the surgery? >> February. After the Super Bowl. So I I got to enjoy the Super Bowl. Yeah. >> In what ways are you a different player now than when you signed your last contract? >> Uh yeah, I just feel like it's a lot more mental focus on you know how I approach things. I feel like you know just going out there playing every single snap like it's my last, you know, cuz just having something cut so short, so quick, you know, you kind of look at that and take it for granted of like, you know, I wish I could have done more. I wish I could have did this. And you know, of course everyone want to make the most out of their opportunities and you know, I feel like it just takes me to the next level of just how dialed in you got to be, you know, on yourself and on your body to, you know, make sure you're in the right, you know, condition and shape and just trying to make sure you just, you know, as stable and, you know, just as, you know, I don't know, just as in sync as you could be. Just go out there and compete every day. >> You didn't get a chance to play with Rece Davis and Reed last year. Now you guys are on the same field. What what do you think's possible with you guys out there together? >> Yeah, you know, that's a lot of speed on the field. Me and him talk every day. You know, both from Cali, so we got a lot to relate on and, you know, we just, you know, we just talk about, you know, how how crazy it is to, you know, finally, you know, get some of those practice reps together and just, you know, just see two speedsters side by side just going at it. So, you know, it's fun out there and, you know, of course we still got, you know, the the OG general Coop out there coaching us on everything and you got the technician and, you know, just all around with Jayson, you know, just it's a lot of things out there that, you know, we're just kind of trying to combine and, you know, see our roles and see how, you know, how much weapons and power we got on the field and I feel like there's a lot of things that, you know, we got in the bag that we could, you know, switch it up from and I feel like it's a exciting year to have that. >> You've only now got five practices out here that you've gotten to participate in. >> I'm sorry, sir. >> You've gotten five practices now that you've gotten to participate out here. What's it been like so far adjusting to this new offense? How does it compare to what you played in with Clint Kubiak last year? Any significant differences that you've noticed? >> Oh, yeah, no, yeah, I feel like it's pretty much the same. Just a little a little tweaks here and there, but I love this game. I I like Brian has a, you know, a idea in mind on how he wants to attack the season and this with this offense and I feel like they got a lot of things that they want to try out and it's the perfect time to try those out right now and you know, um, now I got I got a lot of faith in praising, you know, Brian. I feel like, um, you know, we got we got a pretty good season ahead of us. >> Tory, I think it was six touchdowns in eight games last year but before you before you stopped playing, what did you think of the start you were off to? >> Uh, yeah, um, no, I just I just wanted to make the most of my opportunities, you know, like I said, uh, just something that we practice on every day and I feel like, you know, uh, ball finds energy and I feel like I just had, you know, I guess I just had the right energy out there to, you know, find the end zone and, you know, uh, just build a little bit of confidence, uh, get a little bit of Sam's trust, you know, to trust me out there to at least give me a shot and, you know, of course that would just keep building over the over the time we, you know, have together and now I just try to make the most out of everything I got. >> Tory, thank you.

title: Jadarian Price: "I Really Like The Way We Do Things Here On Offense" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Well, we haven't talked to you since camp has started. So, what are your first impressions? >> First impressions are, you know, I'm glad to be back out here and play football with a very special group of guys, special coaching staff, and a special organization. I'm just proud to be and blessed to be out here. >> When you put pads on, what does that allow you to focus on and make you measure yourself against differently? >> Once the pads come on, it allows the, you know, the offensive line to really get their blocks and the double teams to really happen. Do you feel like it's come back really quickly out here? >> That's one thing I've worked on since high school. I've continuously gotten better at it throughout college, and then that's one thing that people question going into the pros. So, I worked on it and just continue to work on it and understand the space and and catching ability, so. >> How do you assess where you are in that catching and pass blocking? >> Like I said, I'm improving, and I've I've shown countless times in practice that I can catch the ball. Still need to show my pass protection a little more, but we're going day by day, and we're day six in camp, so. >> You said you hadn't had a ton of experience running behind fullbacks and doing stuff under center. How's that transition been so far in this offense where you have fullbacks in you and in front of you exclusively? How does it feel to get used to that process out here? >> I love it cuz you got guys like Robbie Goulds who just he's so big but agile. He can get downhill and he he pops. When you see that happen in front of you, it really you know, it makes you want to lower your your shoulder pads and go pop somebody else. So, I really like the way we do things here on offense. >> When it comes to the pass protection, is it more like the the the mental part of it or the physical part of it that's kind of a difference at this level? Or >> Well, there's steps to it. First, you got to recognize who you got cuz NFL defense, especially ours, can do a lot of tricky things. Guys popping in and out, so recognize who you got and and meet him at the line of scrimmage. That's the biggest thing. >> Outside of the guys in your own meeting room, who's been the most helpful in helping navigate whether it's older on the offensive line or you guys have >> Yeah, George Fant has been a huge help ever since I came into the room and um since day one, you know, in OTAs and now being able to watch him and learn in in how he holds the standard for the running back room. That's really inspiring. >> Are there any defensive guys that have given you some advice or kind of taken you aside a little bit? >> Um I wouldn't say any advice, just just guys that let me know that they're defensive players and I'm offensive players and that's how it is, so. >> So, there will be Where is the big another rookie talent show? Have you been thinking about what your performance might be? >> Nope. I'm just worried about day seven of fall camp, so. >> What was and what will be like the first significant thing you spend your like your your like the first thing you buy with your first paycheck? I've already done it this past summer when I went home. Um just got a new house for my family. That was my biggest goal of mine once I made it to the NFL and I did that, so check that off the list. >> And where is that? >> Back home in in Texas. >> Okay. In your hometown? What was the reaction? >> Bunch of smiles and and, you know, blessings, you know, just everything I wanted to do and and put on the board that I was going to do when I was little, so I'm glad that I finally did it. >> Going back to this defense and the defensive players letting you know they're there, what can you say about the Seahawks defense and what are you finding out about it? >> They fly around on every down. you're 30 yards down the field and you got a defensive lineman like Leonard Williams chasing you down. So, that just goes to show the way the guys practice is the reason they were so successful last year and the fact that they can still do it this year um makes me a better player and and the whole team. >> It looked like you and things were ramping up. You know, a few skirmishes out there. Now, you guys just got pads on. How do you feel like kind of increasing in practice? >> Yeah, day two of pads today and practice has gotten a little longer. Um and we're in that second stretch of training camp. So, just understand how to take care of your body, but also improve on the details while still also being physical in the day-to-day basis. Um it's just football and and you know, I'm glad to get better at it. >> What are you taking away from working with Ryan Flurry as the OC? What's it been like working with him and getting up to speed with his offense? >> Yeah, I'm I'm really starting to finally understand the offense and um the the things that we do like I did I would I didn't do too much in college. So, now that I'm opening my game up a little bit, I'm I'm really excited for the season. >> What do you You mentioned George being really really helping you a lot. People view you as you guys just kind of competing for the running back job, but obviously you guys kind of just helping out each other a little bit a lot too. You view it more as that instead of like competing specifically for the job? >> Yeah, I think we both view it as more, you know, there's there's competition in every position group. There's competition between everyone and themselves, but we both view it as something, you know, how can we make this offense better, this running back room better, and each other better. And we've continued to do that every day. >> It looked like you and Zach Charbonnet were talking on the way off the field. Is even though he's not playing, has he been helpful for you? >> Yeah. Yeah, that's another guy who's you know, even when he was away during OTAs like texting me like, "Hey, I I saw this on the film. You could have done this better." like that's that's a real teammate right there and um him being out but still being on the sideline and giving me tips every time I come back to the sideline like that's really helpful and just just someone who loves the game of is that's really great teammate to have. >> What about this camp maybe you didn't expect or is new to you? >> Camp is camp honestly this is everything I expected. obviously we're in the league now so it's everything's a little bit tougher and everyone's smarter and more decisive off the ball so but end of day is football. >> You're in this offensive line you turned all five starters obviously you're new to play with them but can you sense kind of that cohesion that unit has when you run behind them? >> I can for sure especially when you see guys with their secret little handshakes before the balls while we're in the huddle so hopefully I'll get a little handshake in with them once I get more comfortable with the with the offense so. >> Anything else? >> Thanks appreciate it man.
