Just reminds me why I'm not a rancher, so uh it was good. I mean, but at the end of the day it was I was excited to get out here, and it just made that much more enjoyable to fly out to the Pacific Northwest. >> Can you remind me where the the farm is? What county is it? >> Yeah, Mount City, South Dakota. The metropolitan of 71 population, Mount City, so um yeah, that's where it's at. >> Who takes care of the farm when you're back here? >> Um my head agronomist, also known as my father, so uh he's a one of one. He allows me to come out here and and play this game of football, and uh he kind of holds down the fort back there, so it's it's a pleasure. >> Does he give you reports during the season? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah, like yesterday he was up there. I got about 20 different pictures and videos of the crops and and all that stuff, so it's it's good to get a kind of a piece of home um as you're out here playing, so it uh it also just reminds me like there's more things in life than football if you have a bad day, so uh it's good to kind of get that, and then at the end of the day come out and have as much fun as possible out here on the grass. >> Have you found that you've got more farming fans now than you do football fans? >> Uh I'm not that good of yet, so um let's just stick to football. >> What's the closest kind of big city to that? >> I mean Pierre is about an hour and a half or hour and a half south and then Bismarck, North Dakota is about an hour and 15 minutes north, so kind of right in the middle there. >> Great Blue Angels, we're here a little bit earlier today. What stuck with you about what they had to say? >> They were remarkable. Just the attention to detail, the the I would didn't really know that much about them and then they played a video and stuff and it was so cool to see kind of what they do, how they perform, how they travel, the new obstacles and challenges that they have for every single show and it's yeah, it's what I watched some YouTube videos on them last night. It's pretty sweet. Yeah, they're definitely pretty high in my book for sure. >> Would you ever go up in one of those if they invited you? >> Yeah, I just don't think I'd fit in a fighter pilot. just yeah, I think I'd be too too tall, too wide. Be super cool. Top Gun's like my favorite movie of all time, so yeah, I'd absolutely if they had a cockpit big enough. >> With the high winds they canceled the show today. So earlier this week they were flying over you guys. >> Yeah, we noticed for sure. Sam still probably hates me as I'm asking to repeat play like every other time they flew over, so yeah, you could definitely notice them it's a win-loss situation. I mean it sucks that they couldn't fly over today, but at the same time it's pretty nice having a breeze out at practice for 2 and 1/2 hours, so we take what we can get around here. >> Garrett, you've gotten a couple padded practices in now. Who do you look forward to going up against in one-on-ones the most? >> Nobody. Nobody on our defense line. I don't know. It's one-on-ones is just tough. It's I don't know how realistic it is for an offensive lineman. It's just we're all working on our own thing and and trying new stuff and all that. And I mean, at the end of the day like I say Byron Murphy as he whoops me every single time we go one-on-one, but um just having a pass rusher like that to get you better and he's a he's a good enough pass rusher where any weakness that you have in a set, if you go too lateral or or too vertical or don't punch early enough, he just exposes it. So then as you watch that film, it just continues to have you work on something day in and day out. Um same thing with the guy like Riley Mills is is the same exact way. Um and you just you go across the line, I mean it's not fun when our defense has like eight guys that can consistently get home in in a pass rush. So makes our jobs really hard during the week and then on Sundays it it's our greatest blessing. Yeah. How long do you got and where do I start? Um I think well, he wins the leverage battle right away. Um he's got the strength to bull rush. He's got the quickness to go side to side. He's got the ability to bend if he needs to get to an edge or bend a corner. And so you allow him to really kind of get outside of that A gap and plays like a three tech. You give him a two-way go or three-way go with his strength if he wants to bull rush. It's it's a guy that I don't think there's a ceiling on what he can do. and I think last year was so cool to see what he did was he was really just kind of in the A gap for most of the time and you have Leo rushing as a three. So to have those numbers being an A gap nose tackle is is pretty remarkable. I think it just shows you his his ability, his kind of floor of what he has. And now it's It's you set the baseline, you set the floor, and now it's just up from here. >> He seems to frustrate blockers with that with that knee drop. There aren't a lot of guys that specialize in that. As a lineman, if you go against somebody like that that can get on a knee like that and then hold you up and get them to make plays, like how difficult is that having to just deal with somebody that does that? >> Yeah, I mean just get the Icy Hot ready to put on your lower back cuz it's you're just your body's going to be bending and cranking the entire game. Um and he he does it to perfection. I mean, to drop on a knee like that and crank, like it puts us both offense lineman in a hard place and then allows a linebacker to free up cuz we have to spend two on a on one guy like Murph, so uh if you can master it, it's to it's a pretty useful skill in the National Football League. >> Anything else, guys? >> Thanks, guys. >> Got So, you finally got your photo with Richard Sherman. What did you appreciate most about your conversation with him? >> Uh I feel like he was real about everything I asked, you know, like you know, I was on mic and everything like that, but I feel like we talked outside outside of that. He ended up giving me his number and different things like that, so we got to chat. I loved it. >> You got some reps uh with the ones today. Uh what how did that feel? >> Uh it felt amazing, you know, it was moving fast and I feel like I was moving fast with it, so it adapted to pretty well. >> Have you had a moment yet that made you feel like, "Oh, I'm in the NFL"? >> Uh not not yet, you know, cuz I feel like everything's still moving fast, but not I'm slowing everything down still, so I haven't had anything like that. >> Blue Angels were here a little bit earlier today. What did you take away from that? And what do you take away from Mike bringing in speakers like >> Uh I feel like they they do a lot of things like we do just in a different aspect. You know, they fly planes, but we playing football and they practice just the same the way same way we do, you know, they go over different things they have to do uh just flying. So, I feel like it's pretty good. They practice a lot. >> What about other speakers like that having somebody come in day after day and giving some sort of message? >> I feel like everybody that came in that they had a message that kind of it all tied back to football whether it been like, you know, that wasn't a direct message but uh it all tied back to football and it was amazing actually. >> Now that you're here for a little while, can you see why this team won a Super Bowl last year? >> Uh actually I can. I feel like you know, it's a great a great brotherhood but it's all when it's time to work, you know, we had this thing where we call it loose and focus and I feel like we're very loose and focus focus. When it's time to focus, we're we're focused but when it's time to have fun, we have fun. >> What do you see from Elijah Royal so far? >> Uh I feel like he's a great route runner. He's actually, you know, he blocks does everything that he's needed to do honestly plus more. >> So, if they're playing you both deep safety and then sometimes kind of that third safety role, how is that adjustment kind of learning both of those? >> Uh it's been pretty it's been pretty pretty different honestly, you know, cuz I played down a little bit but in the dime spot, I've always played the strong. So, uh being in the dime has been pretty pretty well for me. I feel like I'm learning more, expanding my knowledge and it's helping me. >> What's the toughest part of the adjustment >> Uh I don't think it's that I don't think it's that hard cuz in college I ran something similar to this. Yeah. >> What does the loose look like for you? We know what the focus looks like. What does the loose look >> Uh you know, I'm just out I'll having fun with the with the guys with my boys my back half being with Spoon, being loud with Spoon or or sitting there just talking to Julian, talking to President Julian and different things like that, you know, so that's what I try to do. >> How is the mayor did he get promoted? >> Sorry. >> They were calling him the mayor, did he get promoted? >> Yeah, he's he's a president now. He's he's a president. >> [laughter] >> What do you what do you learn from him from a guy like Julian? >> Uh pretty much, you know, cuz I have a son. He had he has two sons. So, I feel like just learning how to be a football player how to be a pro but also be a father at the same time. He's helped me a lot. >> How's your family liking the Pacific Northwest so far? >> Absolutely. They I absolutely a lot. It it is crazy. Every time they get a chance they want to go on a walk, do different things, just come out here, enjoy it. So, I feel like they loving adapting well. >> When was the first time you saw them out running out? Did you >> I was on a I was on a plane when I first came in and I was like, "Oh, wow, that that's cool." >> Are you planning to watch our dogs? >> Our dogs are the show. Are you going to watch our dogs? >> Oh, I didn't hear Oh, I am. Oh, yeah, I am. I am, very much so. Oh, yeah. >> I am. And then I got miked up, so I feel like it was very good for So, I know I'm on there for sure. You know, so I'm going to be watching it. >> Promoted they used that to promote it already. We saw that or >> Oh, so I'm going to You don't think I'll be on there? >> I'm just kidding. I'm just kidding. >> He said he like making noise out there with Spoon. Who's louder? >> Spoon. Uh I'd say Spoon. >> Thank you. >> Mhm.

title: How The Energy at Seahawks Training Camp Shifted Early On
text: Um, but it's fun. That's why I'm excited to talk to Brian. I have tons of questions, so. >> Yeah, Brian, we're all kind of relying on you and and you even hear from one of your own really showing the importance of the guys who get to be boots on the ground. So, how are the energy levels the first few days of training camp? >> Well, first I I I've got to make the dad joke and say if if Rob was in Hungary recently, I am there right now. Um, it's it's I'm I'm ready for dinner, so so just so you know. But I I will say this, to be honest AB, the first two days of camp, I thought one of the emerging storylines was going to be like, why is the energy so low? Like it is it's kind of boring. The crowds that were there also were not high energy. It wasn't like a team thing necessarily. There wasn't a lot going on. It was the same players pretty much from last year doing kind of the same things. There's just what it was like nondescript and then yesterday happened. Uh, they ramped things up considerably. The intensity was ramped up. They started 1 V 1 drills, which for people that don't know, it's when the offensive linemen go against the defensive linemen. They do it with usually typically they've done it in padded practices, but last year they started doing them without pads uh uh at times and this year they started without pads um yesterday. That always is an intense drill as Mike knows, a lot of fights come come out of that drill. And started working with some of the individuals more um in certain certain drills. Like it just started to come to life a little bit more. And then today I thought it was a really good follow-up to yesterday and uh they they they roll into a players' day off tomorrow and then pads come on Thursday and that's really when football starts. So, um I thought the last two days have been a notable uptick. I thought the crowd actually was also energetic today. So, kudos to them, but um the player of the day uh to me was Jaylen Milroe today. Um I I I don't say that lightly cuz everyone kind of overreacts one way or another to Jaylen Milroe news, but he had I think he had the best throws yesterday. And I thought he had the best throws today. Um and a variety of throws down the field, down the seams, you know, with anticipation, off bootlegs, in structure, out of structure. Uh I thought it was a really nice day for Jaylen Milroe. So, uh that was that was nice to see. >> Well, Rob, correct me if I'm wrong, but I believe it was one of the first two days that was Jaylen Milroe maybe getting some different press, not not like Brian was saying for maybe an interception that he had had. So, that's really interesting just seeing the turnaround also and and then Brian, that was probably the last guy that I thought you'd say just because of all the potential breakout players that we would see. >> Yeah, I mean, um I kind of go where the the players take me and it wasn't he wasn't the only player at Stetson today. I think Montrell Foster Jr. had a really nice day. Um I thought that um Jaylen Gaines has had a nice couple of days. Uh these guys are toward the end of the roster, but they still deserve to be called out when they're they're having uh kind of super days and um one of the guys that that also, you know, probably won't get much cuz he's such a quiet guy. Charles Cross, from what I've seen, is pitching a shutout so far. I don't think anyone's beaten him. Uh Dante Fowler's tried uh multiple days, no luck. Other players have tried, no luck. Uh he looks like he's in in rare form. And I mean, I could keep going on. Like there there Byron Murphy looks like an absolute wrecking ball. Um there's there's like there's definitely you could feel certain players have come to camp with a point to prove and it's been nice to see that show up. >> That's awesome. That's exactly what you want coming out hot out of the gates and you know, 12s if you're listening Brian Nemhauser is not only a scout in the team but he's scouting the crowd. He's scouting how much you all show up. So I'd be prepared next time you go to start the next training camp but I I do want to open the questions up to the chat. So if you have any questions I know Rob and Mike will have questions for Brian and vice versa. So please use this time to talk to them. They are the Seahawks insiders and we'll try to get to them all tonight. But I do want to start with some news that we learned yesterday the Seahawks waving running back Kenny McIntosh. He was in rehabbing a ACL injury all of last season was listed on the pup list to start camp but the Seahawks have parted ways with him. So really wasn't something that we even talked about like even projecting really in any of our conversation. So Rob are you surprised at this move or could you potentially have seen this coming for the Seahawks running back room? >> I don't think it's a big shock just because of the the extent of the injury and they spent a first round pick on a running back and they every time Mike McDonald is given an opportunity to to discuss Zach Charbonnet it's it's when the gushing praise begins. So he has been a couple of times and I've watched the interviews when he's just been going like almost over the top really to to praise Charbonnet and there was a I think that it was Albert Breer who who reported either today or yesterday that there's at least you know and maybe a small chance that he could be back for the start of the season. You know, if it's not week one then quite early and I I always kind of felt that that was going to be likely just because you know, I've been spoken to so many people in the football over here over the years. They've often said that technology with ACL recovery is is quite advanced now and that the the one injury that you really want to avoid is Achilles. That's the that the the death knell really for you know, coming back anytime within the next year. Uh but an ACL is, you know, the technology's moved on so much since that was like the injury that you wanted to avoid. And he and Kosi, you know, I'm I think there was another there was another player. I can't remember who it is now. There was another player who got injured at a similar time. Might have been Jordan Brooks actually from the Seahawks. There was somebody that had a similar injury at then the same time of the year and came back for the start of the year. So, even if he's not here for week one, there's a chance that he'll be back, you know, relatively early. You've got a first-round running back. They seem to love Zach Charbonnet. It's a numbers game, isn't it? Where does he fit in? And uh if he's not quite been able to recover from this injury, you might as well have somebody else out there who is going to contribute, who is going to be on the field, who is going to be pushing for a potential roster spot or provide and those who are going to make it a bit more competition. So, not not a huge shock. >> Well, Zach Charbonnet is certainly huge and I think nationally when you look at what people might remember from last season is Kenneth Walker, the Super Bowl MVP, but a huge part of that load in that weight that was taken on was Zach Charbonnet and the impact that he had for this team. So, Mike, when you look at this running back room now that they have, it's really Zach Charbonnet, Price, Emmanuel Wilson, and Zach Charbonnet. Where do you see Zach Charbonnet fitting in and and how confident they might be to to have that group be as it is? >> Yeah, I mean, from the football aspect of it, not not a ton changes. And Rob's right. Jordan Brooks tore his ACL. See if I get these dates right. I want to say New Year's Day uh in 2023. So, January 1st, 2023. I'm pretty sure he was starting week one of that same season if I if I got my years right. Um so, it but it just depends on on your knee, all right? It depends on the surgeon that does it as well. Uh I think it was Bruce Irvin who smoked his ACL and I think he had to get it done twice or go to someone differently. Didn't go well. Rashad Penny took pretty much a whole year to come back. Um ACL. I don't know if we ever saw Was that Brian Mone? I think he tore his. Uh and we we didn't see him again. So, it can just depend. I will say this on Kenny though. I was just kind of sad to see the news. Surprised or not, it's kind of whatever. But if you guys remember, Kenny's Kenny's draft call is probably one of my favorites ever. Uh and I I That was my I think I've been on 10 drafts now or something like that. Uh and heard other calls uh outside of that too. But that one right there, I'll never forget just how emotional Kenny was, how great it was. I'm texting other people about it. That one and probably uh both Griffin twins um were great as well. There's some other ones that were good too. But those three off the top of my head. Maybe it's just I like Florida kids. Uh I think about it.

title: Byron Murphy Could Be Defensive Player of the Year
text: If you have one thought on Byron Murphy, cuz he's a guy who I I heard him himself say, you know, I'm trying to get double-digit sacks. Where do you see him and what have you seen from him early on uh this training camp? >> Yeah, a couple quick things. One, I do feel like Byron Murph Byron Murphy and Charles Cross are in different places. I I think Byron Murphy absolutely should have been an All-Pro and a Pro Bowler last year. I don't think Charles Cross should have been a Pro Bowler or All-Pro so far in his career. Um so, I think where he fits in that overall hierarchy is different. I think Byron Murphy's ceiling of where he can fit in the overall defensive player uh in the NFL, I think is higher than where Charles Cross can get. I think he he has the potential. He His body has always been like a bowling ball, right? Like he's a short, compact, powerful dude. Used to play linebacker, used to play running back, like and now he's playing nose tackle. It's a crazy thing. He is so rocked up. He is so intense. I talked to him today. He is I think he could be the Defensive Player of the Year. I I think that's the That's a a big projection. It would need like a massive jump. I think he's got that. >> a face. Rob's making a face. >> I like that. >> I think I think he has I think he has that level of talent. Whether he realizes it, different. I thought DK Metcalf could have been the best receiver in Seahawks history. He definitely did not become the best Seahawks receiver in history. So, potential versus reality is different. The other thing I'll just say on the Jalen Carter thing is I put out a tweet today that a lot of people, especially Eagles fans, did not like, which is like, "Good luck with that contract. I get Albert Haynesworth vibes." And everyone's like, "Albert Haynesworth, what a terrible comp." I'm like, "Albert Haynesworth was the best defensive tackle in football." He was maybe the best defensive player in football when he was with Tennessee and then signed with Washington and he stunk after that. He went in the tank because he was not motivated anymore to be the best player. And the question with Jalen Carter from the very get-go that Pete Carroll and John Schneider decided the answer was negative was can Jalen Carter realize his talent when he's already been paid? And I think the answer is going to be no. I think this guy's going to be a problem. I don't think he's going to live up to that contract. And people can hate that if they're a Eagles fan now, but I'm right there with Rob. If I'm going to put money of that caliber into a player at that position, 100% out of 100, I want it to be Byron Murphy and not Jalen Carter. >> Can I just say one other thing as well? I know I know it's starting to go back to Leonard Williams, but I I remember when Marshawn Lynch was coming towards the end of the year, a couple of games against the Raiders and the Giants in 2014. I remember thinking after that game, when this when he retires, when he or he leaves the Seahawks, I don't think you can replace this guy. Like he's just that impactful. There's just he's just kind of that it's just very rare to find a player like Lynch. And I I feel that way about Leonard Williams. I think when the Seahawks lose Byron Murphy's got is on the great trajectory, but I think William different type of player. And I think whenever he is no longer with the Seahawks, that's going to leave a void that you can only replace that kind of a player if you're picking very early in the draft, like top eight in the draft. And those players don't hit free agency and they're very rarely traded for second-round picks.

title: The Witherspoon Contract Has a Hidden Wrinkle
text: It is notable because today the Cleveland Browns extended Denzel Ward, signed him to a 2-year $62 million extension. We do know also that Christian Gonzalez, the Patriots star corner, has the same agent as Devon Witherspoon, which is some really interesting information. So, we're all just kind of waiting for these pieces to fall. But Rob, what is the impact of this and and where do you think the Seahawks and when do you think the Seahawks will choose to extend Devon Witherspoon? >> Well, it's most unusual, isn't it? Cuz you typically when you have a player of this kind of status who is in a position to get a contract and be paid extremely well, they are either holding out or they're holding in or there's there's kind of constant talk like the agents will go to the to the journalists and start complaining and you'll see the kind of things that that the reporters report when there's stuff going on like that. It's not that long ago that Christian Gonzalez apparently doesn't tackle well enough, according to one of the radio stations in New England. And you know, where does that report come from? That comes from the team. A team source will just dangle that out and that gets out the thrown into the ether and then that trying to can maybe helps the team a little bit with some kind of leverage cuz that's what people are talking about. These are the kind of battles that go on through the media when there's a contract negotiation. And there's absolutely none of that with Devon Witherspoon. And he would with Witherspoon, it's 100% expected to get done. It's a matter of time. You know, the team's got a lot of club control with him. So, there's there's not really anything that he can do to force the issue aside from take himself out of games and cost himself money. It doesn't feel like he's got any interest in that. The guy just looks like he loves playing for the Seahawks and and can't think of anything worse than not playing for the Seahawks. So, I imagine that this is just one of those things that we're waiting on Christian Gonzalez and the agents of both players to come up with an arrangement with the Patriots, with the Seahawks. Who gets paid first? Who's going to get paid second and therefore get a little bit more. There's not It's never felt like there's anything to worry about with this. So, whether it gets done next week, next month, or on Christmas Day before the Rams game, I don't think it really matters. It's going to get done eventually. >> I loved what Mike McDonald was saying about him just how nothing's changed. He's the same guy practicing his tail off and I think it was Brady Henderson who might have reported that Mike McDonald's son Jack was wearing a Witherspoon jersey, which I thought was kind of a great little thing to see, but but also when you think about just holistically with this team and other how other teams go about some of these contract discussions, you probably wouldn't really know if you weren't digging into it. And so, just Mike for you have been around the team for for many years now, I'm curious like how does this kind of reflect just the attitude and the culture that the Seahawks have during discussions like these? >> I was just thinking now Mike hasn't dealt with a a hold-in or holdout, right? You got that right? I know he didn't last year. So, it would have been first year? No one held out? >> The closest thing you got was maybe the Geno Smith questionable was he really hurt when he he wouldn't play those few days? You know, like >> Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. >> Maybe the closest. >> Forget where I was, but yeah. Um yeah, that would probably be be it. So, I'm kind of fascinated by that because is that has has Mike and the new staff or somehow is that communicated among the agents and the players like, "Hey, we not we not going for that." Uh cuz he just hasn't had it. And we're seeing it around, you know, the league, the hold-ins, the holdouts. Uh so, I'm I'm actually kind of is that like intentional? If so, that's a good thing. Um but ultimately, I always look at the contract stuff from the player point of view. I'm very happy for Devon Witherspoon cuz the longer they wait and if Christian Gonzalez goes first, are there more Denzel Wards? What's Denzel Wards APY? Like 32, 33, or something like that? Keep waiting, number goes up. So, good for good for Spoon. And I don't know if he'd be a holding guy anyway. He just seems like it would kill him to show up and not do the stuff. Like [snorts] uh DK was the same way for what it's worth even though he he eventually kind of sat, but uh so I am glad that they're not, you know, going through that. That probably is like a culture thing or a reflection of the staff this regime being like, "Yeah, show up and we'll, you know, we'll get this thing done. We don't need to make this bigger um than it is." Getting Jackson done as early as they did probably reflects that as well. But, I do think it'll it'll get done. I just think I thought about this last time, too, that that the same agent thing is so wonky cuz you just you just have dueling interests there. Like, yeah, let's say Jack Christian signs for 141 million. Like, if you give Devin 142 if you're his agent, he's like, "Hey, dude, you just shorted me a million bucks." And it's like, yeah, we're talking about 141 versus 142 million. Like, ah, boo-hoo, cry-cry for the millionaires. But, like, if I'm the player, like, "Yo, you you you work for me." Like, I know you work for the other guy, too, but you you legitimately work for me and not the other way around. So, it's the small thing that's not like the hugest thing in the world, but it is funky when it comes up and I think I mentioned it last time that was the belief with DK's agent as well. He has like all the receivers. Uh and it was the same thing with Deebo, A.J. Brown, they had Chris Godwin, Mike Williams, a bunch of guys who all got paid. Some of them got the exact same deal. I think Chris Godwin and Mike Evans did or excuse me, Mike Williams did. So, it's just a funky thing, but I do think it gets done. But, I am curious how they how he's balanced with that agency, maybe not just one guy, is balancing Chris their their duties and their obligations to the guy paying them in in Boston, which is Christian, and the guy cutting their checks here, which is which is Spoon. Like, that's always a funky thing for me. >> Well, Spoon is a guy that a lot of people have said they're excited to see potentially be the breakout star of Hard Knocks. But, Brian, you've been around him the last couple days. What have you seen from Spoon and the energy that he's bringing on the field. >> I mean, Mike's nailed it in the sense that I don't think anybody could control Devon Witherspoon and keep him off a football field if he's healthy and able to play. And he's the same guy he always is, you know, he he's always bringing energy, he's hyping up the crowd, he's, you know, he's Spoon. And so, like I don't I I guess for me I don't have a lot of I don't know if patience is the right word, but to me this is a non-story. I I know it is I know it is, but he's he's going to be a Seahawk. Like he's just going to be. It's a matter of when. And the fact that he is reported that he is playing and going full speed is credit to him. Uh so, I have a lot of respect for the fact that he's doing that. I'm sure the team and the and the organization do as well. And that's why it'll probably get done pretty soon. And then we don't have to talk about it anymore. Cuz it'll be done. And and uh like it I don't know, it's like it's like talking about, "Oh my god, is there going to be a first game this season on September 7th?" And it's like, "Yeah." >> On a Wednesday though. On a Wednesday. >> be on a Wednesday, too. It's true, Abby. And I hope you don't take this as any shade towards you asking the question, cuz you're not the only one. Everyone's asking about it. I just uh man, it seems it seems like the the the most predictable outcome I can ever think of. Uh he will be a Seahawk. He will sign a an extension. It's just a matter of when it happens. >> There we go. Well, to talk about maybe some not very predictable outcomes. So, guys, what do you think in here? Who wants to take the first shot at what they would be picking? Mike really trying to look at it. There is no zoom button, Mike. I'm sorry. >> Are we talking about over/under on people that Puka Nacua bites, or is this I can't see it? Is Is that on there? >> We're going individuals, individuals. Keeping it to ourselves for this one. >> Actually, it's how many drunken tweets is he going to send if the Seahawks win the Super Bowl? >> Sam Darnold. Yeah, okay. So, I mean, Bijan Robinson 1,100 yd rushing for the season. I I'd taken more on that. I I I think Bijan Robinson's best running back in in the sport, so I think I think I I am the guy that continually thinks Atlanta is going to be better than they are cuz I love I love some of their skill position players. They never are. >> Did I get it right or wrong, Brian, that you said you love traveling there? Did I make that up? Somebody likes it. >> I do like Atlanta. I don't think I love traveling to Atlanta, but the food's excellent, the people are great, you got some southern hospitality. Yeah, I like Atlanta. >> Can Can we not Can we not talk about Atlanta?

title: Will Levis, Calvin Ridley & JC Latham at Titans Training Camp
text: How do you feel like things have gone so far since been back out here from the show? >> I'm loving it. I'm having so much fun. It's been awesome being in the room with the guys. I mean, feel like we have a really tight-knit group. Dave just keeps it, you know, serious but fun at the same time. Shay as well. I'm just, you know, so blessed to be back playing the game I love and throwing it how I, you know, want to throw it again. So, just it's been awesome. How are you keeping yourself impressed of knowing, you know, the competition that you have and the opportunities? >> I'm just focused on having fun. I mean, not playing last year, like at first it was tough. I realized how much I needed that time, not just physically, but just mentally, too, to just calm the nervous system, get away from ball for the first time since second grade, I think. And I was able to make a lot of strides physically, mentally, emotionally, spiritually, and I'm just focused on having fun. And I feel like if as long as I do that, then I'm going to be playing my best ball. So, >> you had mentioned rewiring before. Um I think it was your your second your first year as a starter. You had mentioned like how you had to rewire yourself. Is that something that that you were able to do like mentally mental rewire? I don't Yeah, I probably was talking about it before, but I didn't know what I meant by that. And I feel like I figured out kind of what I needed uh from a mental side and uh took as many steps as I could to take that into account throughout my time away. And I feel like I'm feeling the dividends of it. And just got to make sure that I'm being self-conscious and self-aware of all my thoughts and feelings and being honest with myself and revisiting things of the past that I might not have been able to fully get through at that time and place and um addressing why and and finally getting past them. So, I just feel like the overall just calming of my central nervous system and where I'm at mentally is in a much healthier place than it's ever been. >> Well, how do you feel about your opportunity with this team now? What's kind of been their message to you about that opportunity? >> I mean, I'm just trying to make the most of every opportunity that I get. Uh, I can't control the reps that I get and uh I'm I'm trying to keep this or make this time or take this time to obviously work on myself, but bring along others with me. Um, you know, obviously the reps I've taken before with mainly the ones and twos and, you know, I have the opportunity to work with guys that are really fighting for a roster position now and um trying to bring them along and make as many opportunities for them as much as I'm making opportunities for me. So, uh, I'm not worried about the, you know, competition per se or, uh, the amount of opportunities that they're going to give me. I just got to make sure that I'm ready for when they are given to me and, uh, just preparing to be the best at that as possible. >> How beneficial is the table? I know it's >> Yeah. No, he's been great. I love his just mentality he takes with coaching the quarterback position. um not as not as much black and white I think as um other coaches I've had in the past and allowing us to play a little more free and trusting us and what we see in our decision-m even though if it's not you know what's said on on the paper per se um and I love it uh he has us take control even though I was learning the offense just along with everyone else earlier in the spring like right off the jump I felt comfortable with you know if I was confident I knew something well even though I didn't have like the hey if this we get this look during on this play like think this like I was it was coming more naturally to me to be able to get us into other looks that we might not have even discussed about but I can trust my guys to get in the right spots. So stuff like that and just the uh the energy he brings and he's already uh warned us that he could definitely get emotional like on game days and stuff like that. But hey, I love that. Like you know you guys have seen for me like I'm an emotional guy too. Like I I like having fun. I like celebrating when we're up. um trying to bring each other back around when we're down and uh he seems like the guy that you want to fight for and we've already felt that. >> How do you believe this is year four? Uh how much you feel like you've grown as a as a person maybe and as a player? >> A lot. I was thinking [laughter] about that the other day I was like, "Dang, this is this is really year four. I'm a true vet at this point." Um getting that letter from the PA getting vested like I didn't even know like being on IR like that counts as a vested season. And to get that like that was like wow. Um, definitely grown a lot. Feel like I was a kid when I got here. I've definitely turned into a man and there's still a lot of growing that I need to do and uh but I think what I talked touched on earlier just on the the mental side um being able to not care as much about what other people say or what other people think. I feel like I worked a lot for other people's approval in the in the beginning of my of my career and whereas I'm, you know, I'm just trying to be the best version of me uh at this point and I have more confidence than I've ever had because of that. Uh, I don't need to go out there and win x amount of games before I can feel the confidence. Like, I have the confidence right now. I I know I've put the tape out there already that I'm a, you know, a dang good quarterback in this league. And, um, I'm even better than I ever have been. So, um, >> the faith that you have a future as a starter% 100%. I I I know I'm, you know, I think I'm there there are not 32 quarterbacks in this league better than me. I know that for sure. How do you reconcile that faith with the just wanting to have fun and just taking the reps that are given to you? It seems like you have both. >> You have that confidence, but that's not what I'm thinking about when I'm stepping on the field. I mean, maybe at one point in my career, I was thinking about trying to prove that to people, but um I have that belief in myself while still not trying to make that one of my main points of emphasis of of proving that. Um, I know that as long as I just play the way that, um, you know, I'm blessed to with the abilities that I'm blessed to have and the capabilities that I have and I've learned to develop as a quarterback, like that's just going to come. And when I get the opportunities, I know that it's going to I'm going to make the most of it and I'm going to shine. >> Where did this change in your mindset come from during the time off? Was it soularching or what really was it? >> I think it was just truly trying to be honest with myself with a lot of things that happened, whether it was on the field, off the field. I think I've suppressed a lot of emotions I've had in the past just to like, you know, be the person to not care about it. But sometimes that's not healthy. And addressing things that uh I felt that came up uh from the past that I I wasn't able to truly move on from and just sometimes it's uncomfortable to have those conversations and that's why that I like avoided it in the past. But um being able to have them and have that time off and didn't address them was was really helpful. >> Blame yourself or what happened to this team? >> Absolutely not. No, I think I mean there's no one person to blame. Like I definitely could have played better. Um >> Yeah. No, >> he had mentioned how the key to a relationship with with you guys is seeing the game through the eyes of the quarterback. What does that mean to you? And do you have any examples of how he's been able to do that with >> Yeah, I'd actually point to uh Ju, our receivers's coach, yesterday. He did a good job of just I mean he was doing a presentation on just like securing the football at the catch, but it turned into a presentation on just like how hard the quarterback position is and how everyone needs to understand that and how the more grace you give the quarterback and understand that it's not just on him, it's on everybody as a whole. The more more obviously responsibility we take on ourselves, but taking the more just team approach of how it takes all of us and you know we got to do our job sometimes. We are known, we know that in those c certain situations at the end of the game, like some fourth downs, like we got to be able to make those plays, but um if we keep the onus on everybody as a group opposed to just one specific player, um then we're going to go far as a team. And I think Dable understands that as much as anybody else. Uh he's he's obviously been able to work with a lot of really talented quarterbacks and uh he's got a lot of experience and he knows just how hard this position is. And I think because of that, he's he's able to coach us really well. He had mentioned the three pillars of quarterbacking. Red zone, two minute, third down. What's your take on that? Do you agree with that? >> That's that's where you make your money. Like that's what you know, obviously you got to be efficient on first and second down. That was the team competition today. Just efficiency overall. Um, but you know, those are the situations that one are the most fun and two are the most crucial if you want to, you know, be remembered and and stay a consistent quarterback in this league. And I've been be able to have a lot of great moments in in all those moments. And maybe not as consistent in others as I would have liked, but um there's no better feeling than getting that two-minute drive done and and leading the team to a victory and coming off that field knowing that what you did, you're you're backed against the wall. The odds are not in your favor and you're still able to come out on top. So those are what the special ones are able to do and I'm I'm looking forward to my next opportunities. >> Jim, last one. >> Yeah, I was going to ask you just what it's like being back with Dell again, reunited with him. >> He's awesome. He's he's a special player. Um, you know, we brought him here for a reason because he can definitely be a huge asset for us. It's been fun to spend some time with him off the field and uh just seeing him and Cam's relationship develop has been really cool cuz he's a special type of player, but you also got to learn, you know, uh his abilities and and how you can best help him with with the ball. And um I'm just excited to have him and it's cool to be able to share the field with him again. So, Calvin, feel sorry. Feeling better now. And And how rough was that to have that hit just before camp? >> The hit? >> Stomach bug? >> Oh, yeah. Hell. Oh, sorry. >> Yeah. No, man. That that that hurts. Um, I actually had that a couple times in my life. Maybe three or four times. Um, it's not a good thing. It's like a 24-hour thing, but it can really put you down pretty good. I ate Chipotle and and sorry Chipotle. I like y'all but by the time man by the time the night hit um it was coming from everywhere. So I I got I got better pretty quick though. >> I heard you lost maybe over 15 lbs. >> Yeah, man. I was I was I was throwing up until everything was gone. >> You got it back on. >> Yeah, I got I got a good I got most of it back. Yes. >> They seem to have a particular focus as far as that as a staff. How beneficial has it been to work with them as far as your strength and conditioning, especially as you as you get older? >> Yeah, I mean, yeah, as you get older, I mean, you know, things are not like you you don't snap back as fast as you're younger, but uh um I mean, I pick up the phone anytime I'm in trouble and they they come to my aid, it no matter what time it is to and help me out and get me back, right? So, I appreciate the them the most. Kevin, I know last couple years probably not what you would have wanted individual or the team. What's the motivation like for you this year? >> Um, I just want to win, man. I just want to be a a good help to the team, to my teammates, to my room, to the young guys, and um, encourage them and uh, just win, man. We can if we can, you know, win games, that'll be the best thing for me. I don't really care about individual success as long as we win. >> Sorry. How much are these taller quarterbacks changing your life going against this defense and how much will they change before teams go against this? >> Oh, I mean, I've been going against tall quarterbacks for a while, but yeah, it's it's really good to see that we got a couple out here and um they give us a challenge and it's good to, you know, get a go against them before we go against some real other guys. >> Change how teams and receivers are going to have to play against you guys. >> Oh, yeah. I think it's going to be a lot harder to come here and um go against our DBs. They're they're big, physical, and um but it's going to also help us when we got to go against some of the bigger DBs. Now, >> Cam had talked about third down, how he learned that like that's when quarterback really that's when you so to speak. >> What's your what's your take to that? Have you seen like >> something change within him when when you guys are working on third down? >> Uh I mean, you know, Cam's I mean, a confident guy. He really thinks, you know, we going to get every third down, but uh you know, D ball is here. you know, put them in a great position to put us in a great position to get most of the third downs and we just need to be on time with each other and we should be fine. >> That a lot of the the quick passing and quick progressions for him. Like how much does that change you and how you got to get open quicker and just approach the problem? >> Uh it really doesn't change me. I just got to be be on I just got to win. That's the down that we need the most. You got to win your rep. I mean that goes for you know every receiver out there. Um you got to win. We need that down and uh you got to do your job. Ale has been able to make some plays early on, I guess. What kind of growth have you seen from him last season? >> Um, to me, Eric is a star. Uh, hard worker. Um, yeah, man. The kids the kids are stud. Uh, he's going to continue to get better, and I'm I'm going to be right there to help him, root for him. Um, but, uh, I don't know. The kids are stood to me. What about the whole room from from Cardell to everybody? >> This is uh one of the deepest rooms I've been in like um I mean three, four, five, six, it's about seven guys. I I really really think it's is really deep. Um and if we do what we got to do, get on the same page as our quarterback, um we could push, we could push. K, you had the injury last year and you know there was some question as to whether or not you'd stay around, but you ended up redoing the contract and all. What What was it about here that kind of made it a win-win for you to come back and try to help this team? >> Uh, man, I want to win some games with these guys, the young guys. I mean, they like my little brothers, man. They, you know, and uh I like this I like living in Nashville. It's a very nice place to live, but uh I want to have fun and win some games right here. you know, this is where I came and we need to get a good win the season before I check out. >> What do you like working with with Greg Lewis? He played in the league before. Uh >> yeah, definitely feel that Greg's a uh he was a former player for sure. Um fun um fun coach, man. Um I definitely, you know, we work, we work, but uh he's fun and I can relate to him. >> You said you said you would feel that he played in the game. What do you mean by that? >> Yeah, I mean just the way he talks. I mean, you know, sometimes we're not going to win every rep. I mean, you know, a receiver knows that. Um, and we know how to line. Uh, it's just the way he runs the meetings, man. You could just tell he was a former player and, you know, you know, the the receiver mind. That's the thing. >> Such a deep room. What are some things you want to see yourself personally? >> Um, I just want to see myself stay healthy. I stay healthy, I'm going to be a good player on this team. I'm going to contribute to this team. just strengthen my body. I think that's all I got to do. >> How do you like how do you like option routes? How does that mean? >> I'll run any route that my coaches my team don't want me to run period. >> But how did how does that differ maybe than what you've been doing? And >> I always ran all the routes. Um I like deep routes, but uh I run whatever they want me to run. >> This is year eight. Year eight for you. You still feel as fast as you? >> Oh, I mean I'm Yeah, I'm faster than most of them. I'm faster than most of them. >> I mean, you feel still I mean, you still feel like you're as fast as you've ever been and can contribute as much as you ever have. >> Yeah. Yeah. Hell yeah. I'm still Yeah. >> Still can beat all of them. Still fast as all of them. Yeah. >> It's been a couple years since you've been together, but what do you most like about kind of reuniting? >> Um, he's just cool, man. It just I just when I look at him, I just remember, you know, sitting at his house, man. He might cook me a steak. Um, yeah, he always get on to me talking about some in my hair and uh, you know, he just remember Young Red, so I just like him and it just feels like feels like I know somebody that you know that I'm playing for for real. For real. >> You feel like Cam, you took Cam under your wing right out of the gate. Where have you seen him make a strides in the past year? >> Um, man, honestly, this kid is just he's a he's a he's a he's just confident, man. and he's always he's kind of been the same so far, but uh I think he's just taken more charge of the team. You know, he wants to win. He wants to to do really good. He wants the offense to move the ball and you know, this organization to go somewhere. So, >> Austin, >> yeah, Carell is another guy coming in the in the league out of the draft that is asked, "Hey, who did you watch?" And it seems like your name pops up a lot for these guys. What is it like for you to feel that role and for them to be your teammate, especially as you keep getting older and have to >> Yeah, man. And um I definitely, you know, heard a lot of young guys say my name. That's cuz I used to kick ass for sure and I still can. But man, I I know that I used to really whoop whoop and especially in one-on-one situations. But uh um Tate is very very special kid, man. I love watching him and I appreciate that he said that about a >> lot that the game is 90% mental and uh 10% physical. Um, you know, we have I have these debates with my teammates about, you know, how true that is. I think it's I think it holds a lot of truth to it, though. Um, just to be able to process the game at at a high level, see the whole picture of uh what it is and execute it completely. I mean, you you get the answers to the test every single day. You know, what the defense is going to do, how they're going to play, what type of player they are. I mean, it's very seldomly going to change. You know, a guy's not going to be a power rusher all one game and then decide, hey, I'm just going to speed rush this whole game. you know, unless the tackle, you know, maybe struggling with that, whatever it might be. Um, the player is true to himself, you know, so you can learn a lot about the player or the style of the defense, whatever it is. So, um, just by watching the film and just by, you know, being a student of the game. So, showing up with the answers, um, and preparation, you know, confidence is, um, how you prepare. So, that's where you came from. >> You said at the end of last season you were going to be really focused on the mental part of your game through the offseason. How so far removed from actual games does a guy work on on his mental game here at Austin? >> I think it's um it's a amazing coincidence that you know having coach Karm here, one of the things he talks about is building the neural pathways. Um you know we're installing a lot he speaks extremely fast and uh he expects you to keep up and the thing that he says consistently is that um if we go over it one time it's it's live at any given point. So, you know, we have a script every single day that we go out and look to execute, but um he can call and we they have called something. I remember um we installed wham probably the second week and by like the seventh week of OTAAS um we called it. It wasn't on the sheet. It wasn't anything like that. And um you know, he he told us he was like, "Hey, like you know, I know we've only went over it the one time, but you know, you're part of part of being an athlete, part of being in the game is knowing what you're supposed to do." So, um, you know, just building those neural pathways, just really trying to expand the mental capacity to retain the information and execute at a high level. That's something that adds to that, um, ability to not only retain the information, but to build the mental fortitude it is to compete at a high level. >> Training on that neuropathway stuff, or is it something you've looked into beyond what what's here? >> Yeah, I mean, I've I've done my own I mean, you know, I got a mental coach um probably I think I want to say it was the Browns week of last year or maybe the week before that, but um so we we've talked about a lot of different things such as like, you know, just um being able to um mentally re-engage and refocus. You know, considering that a skill, you know, a lot of people um can start focused on one task, but being able to continuously stay focused through it is a is a skill, especially with distractions of the highs and lows, especially in a sport like this. Um and just a multitude of other things. you know, I try to do things that really attack the mind, whether it's um um reaction training or just reading, you know, reading different things about um how to better mentally prepare for certain things. So, um just I mean, as as my coach said it coincidentally, just building those neuropathways just to keep expanding my mind. >> Peter said that uh you know, last year he wanted to play himself into their plans, took a big step. How important do you feel like it is for you to take that big step this year? >> Uh it should be important. I mean, you know, this is year three for me. Um, you know, a thing that we say in the O line room is that there's there's no sympathy um given um you know, like you said, there's a lot going to be thrown at us. You know, we're installing a lot of plays. Uh it's a lot of new players, coaches. I mean, you see around the facility, everything changed. So, um you know, we're not going to allow that to be excuse of why anything is kind of um laxidasical. You know, we're all professional um athletes and coaches at the end of the day. So, um, uh, that as far as attacking it as such, that's what we're expected to do. You >> experimented with different things from a, I guess, a body standpoint to be prepared for the season, I guess, as far as weight and what you want to do to be best prepared. What where are you heading into this year as far as how you feel? >> I guess you're playing weight now. >> Yeah. >> How you feel like that'll go as the season starts? uh keep curiosity. >> I remember last year you you talked about how much weight you had lost going the season and working on ways to maximize your ability where you think you are heading into year three as far as where you want to be physically and uh how you can perform at the best >> Yeah, I mean I just think it's uh it's more about just being consistent with it. Um last year I was hit with an injury that um it was very very unique. I wasn't allowed to do any type of lower body workout. So I was only able to do upper body workouts. So, um it was really hard to, you know, get conditioning in or get footwork in, whatever it might have been, just because, um the specific injury they said you couldn't stretch it cuz it needed to heal. You need to scab back up and heal. So, um I know like just with my weight, one thing I learned is like add room in there for, you know, I don't want to say, uh injuries are part of the game, nagging injuries, whatever it's a small little ankle sprain or something big like that or even, you know, god forbid worse. um just add room in there to where if you're not able to move, you know, um your your diet, your nutritional um way of life is going to be consistent no matter what it is. So, you're not having to worry about adding weight on or, you know, losing too much weight. So, >> going back to the mental aspect, you said the Browns week, that's when you first >> I want to say either Browns the week before, >> right around there. So, in that time up until now, knowing how much football could humble you at times, how has that helped you work through those humbling moments? >> How's what specifically? the the mental coaching and the different >> Yeah, I mean a lot um I mean there's there's just so many different aspects of the game that u we look to attack, but we we kind of look at it like laying a foundation and just building every single day. So at that time it was um being able to mentally refocus, you know. Um I was I was having penalties um and some plays I I might have not liked and I had a tendency to think about the play while getting the next play thinking, you know, I think oh I didn't like that B block. why didn't I like the BB block uh x y and z and um you know we're getting the next play. Well, if you're thinking about the last play getting the next play, you're mentally not focused for the next play. So, just learning how to say, you know what, we'll look at it on film, let it go, u mentally re-engage into the play and learn how to execute uh because this is the biggest play, you know? So, um just those things to um at the point now to continue to lay down the foundation of what I want this year to look like and how can I handle the adversity or the successes of it. So Jason, >> as far as the way the passing game is supposed to operate with this scheme, how much can that help you guys as a unit? >> Uh, extremely. It's very, very unique, very dynamic passing game. Um, I'm excited about it. Um, I can't say too much about what it is specifically, but um, yeah, I mean, it's it's you get excited just hearing about all the nuances of it. And, uh, as I said, it's going to be a lot thrown at us as players on being able to not only retain the information, but to be able to play fast. I know you guys seen a couple times out there today where we're just calling the play and going. Um, and it's not a simplified offense by no means. So, being able to retain the high um level of information given to us and execute and play fast um that the way we want to play fast um is going to be a big factor of it. But, uh you get excited knowing like once once we get a grip of all this as a as a unit and once we know how to operate, you know, without even talking about it, we can just say one word and go. Um you get fired up for that. >> Last one. You mentioned a minute ago that you spent at least a little bit of time thinking about how you want this season to go for yourself. What does the ideal season three for JC Leam look like in your head? >> Uh I think first is team success. Um you know there's like I said there's no sympathy in it. So there's no no excuses, no uh yeah, he was hurt last year, played left tackle um rookie year, you know, there's no none of that going on. You know, I'm I'm here playing right tackle now. So um doing things, you know, our number one rule is protect the team. So, are you helping the team or are you hurting the team? And um showing up every day um you know, just doing my best um for the team so that we can have success um on the field and that we can establish ourselves as a um a team that's going to compete every single play down in down and earn the respect of the NFL and uh more. Um I think that's what a successful year is going to look like as a team. How much does a guy like Austin Slavin who's kind of experienced in Brian Babel's offense help uh not only you but the rest of the offensive line get acclimated in that scheme? >> Uh tremendous. I mean when you have a guy that's brought in that knows the offense um cuz coaches as great of a coach as you are um you're not on the field you know so um Slotman you know Slotty he he's great to kind of break it down. So, like last night, I think we spent like 30 40 minutes together just going over um all the the NASCARs that we've installed so far. I think it was like three two or 30 hundred of it or whatever it was. Um but just going over all of that and just he's letting me know, you know, he's a center, so you know, for me, I just got to know um where where the source's going to, what's our point, and you know, everything else. But for him, he has to know, you know, um where the mic um strong, weak, you know, four down, three down, call it all out, diamond, what the whole O line has, communicate it to the quarterback. And I mean that's the high level of information that he has to play on a consistent basis. Um and then be able to, you know, drive drive the ship, drive the train. Um so a guy like that, you know, just having in our corner that we can kind of communicate to and ask like, hey, coach said it's like this. What how do you see it? You know, um that's extremely important. So, um you know, I'm so excited he's here and I continue to just learn. I look to learn and develop with them. >> Thanks, JC.

title: Robert Saleh on Fans at Camp, Calvin Ridley & Pads Coming Monday | Press Conference
text: Robert Saleh, you got the fans out for the first time this morning. What does that bring you find the kids to you know, you got training camp vibes going. Now you have the fans. >> No, it's it's always great to get the fans out. You know, they're the the fans are the lifeblood of the entire NFL and um uh you know, I know the players feed off their energy and uh to have them out here just to to create a new stimulus for practice in the um I think I think the players and the coaching staff uh for that matter enjoy it. >> As far as uh not having practice Friday, kind of what went into that decision for you guys and what were you able to get done? >> Uh it's so it's part of the NFL mandated uh acclimation period. Um some teams go three in a row with an off day. We chose to go two with uh and I I wouldn't call it an off day. We we still kept them at a simmer. Uh had a really really big lift uh and regen session with two walk-throughs for the guys. So, it was a big-time mental day and a big-time physical day to uh we're trying to avoid having to maintain throughout training camp. We want to actually get stronger, add more armor. Uh so, the the idea behind yesterday was to give me the opportunity to lift heavy when normally you can't during the season. >> You got your guys getting bigger at corner. Longer. Obviously, people want that, but does it take anything away and how does it fit with your overall defensive philosophy? >> Yeah, um you know, there you could I guess you could argue that the bigger and longer you are, the less foot speed you have and the shorter you know, like um and it's really it's really the cat and mouse game, you know, if you're playing teams that have normal spacing and you want to get up there and press and they're not really doing anything to to allow receivers off the ball. Those big long corners will eat all day. Then you've got teams like uh Kyle Shanahan who are going to play in a box uh where you can't get your hands on receivers and they're going to make you play off coverage where foot speed's needed. So, you're still looking for the best corners possible. It's not like it used to be where we were exclusively uh corners. There's we're looking for the best corners that we can find and uh and uh try to put them in the best positions to be successful. Yeah, for for all the rookies really it's it's to understand what it is to be a professional with regards to their workout program, their meals, and all that stuff and I I thought he did a really really nice job since he's gotten here. I think he's shed about 4% body fat. He's been able been able to maintain his weight in the range that we want. Um and now it's it's the mental part. That's always going to be evolving from now till he retires. Um and so he needs to continue to grab hold of the the accomplishments he had, build on it uh as he gets older and as he lifts more he'll become more of a man and fill out his fill out his body more but but really like the the mindset that he operates with. Um you know, you saw a young guy that's willing to compete, stick his face in the fan, and do whatever's necessary to be successful. You just talking to him in the off season, very very smart. Uh instinctual, he's hair trigger, you could see it on tape. So he's got all the skills that you look for out of a nickel. Um he's a he's a for a nickel he is a bigger bodied bigger body guy so you like that and uh uh got all the confidence in the world that he's going to do a really nice job for us. Uh shoot, man. It's it's it's it's really no different for him. He's I know he's the veteran in the room. He's he's had success in this league. He's been around a while and he's had a really nice career but um he just needs to be him. Share you know, share information that he thinks is necessary for those young guys. Help pull guys along with them, but at the end of the day, the challenge for him will always find a way, even at this age, to find a way to get better and find a way to contribute in different ways. >> Skill-wise, what have you seen? >> He looks He looks youthful. You know, he's he's He's pushed through all the elements that he had throughout OTAs from last year. He's going to be full today. He looks really good. So, I'm looking forward to seeing how he acclimates and integrates into the [music] offense. >> You said back in the spring that you told Levis to go have his best off-season, come back, compete, and see where it falls. Where have you seen areas of growth and improvement in him? >> Yeah, he's He's been growing every day. You know, it's it's a new system. All the quarterbacks, even Cam, were They're They're all going through with the new terminology. It's It's different than what Will's been exposed to. But, I think he's doing a really nice job. You know, he's competing his butt off. He's asking the right questions in meetings. And so, I'm Like I said, I'm looking forward We We haven't scratched the surface. We have two practices. But, he's He's trending in the right direction. >> When your communication device, Dakota or whoever, cuts off, in effect, is that where things start? And how much do offenses do from there that he's helping everybody get set up? >> You're talking about uh >> So, Cody gets the call and his involvement from there? >> It It's >> Especially once you can >> Yeah, the the Mike linebacker is cuz really I I try my best not to overload the Mike linebacker. So, I give him the call. I mean, if it's pertinent information, I might say something, but we cut off at I think it's like 18 seconds or something. I have no idea, but I just know that I give him the call. I I want him to play free of mind. And the Mike linebacker, and you see it now, he does a really nice job with communication, getting guys lined up. He doesn't flinch. Offenses move all the time, and he's quick to communicate, get people around him lined up. I mean, and but it helps that you have Hooker and and K Dub flanking them at safety with communication and um so it's a really really good group in terms of the interior that back seven. >> Most offenses hold at least something significant until after you're out of the picture. >> No, they they once they get their personnel, offenses have to get their call in. Um if they're a no-huddle team and they're at the line of scrimmage and they're trying to see where you're at, that's probably a little bit different, but teams that huddle up, get their guys in and all that stuff, you're you're you're not worried about what they do at the line of scrimmage. >> What sort of communication does there have to be between the offense and the defensive staff when you go 11 on 11 on maybe what Brian wants Cam to see defensively? >> That that's all the time. Even in walk-through, we're trying to script. So, the scripted portions of practice, which you guys if you haven't caught on yet, is the beginning of practice, the first couple of periods. The second two periods are usually off-script where we're calling it and we're just we're letting it rip. Um and those periods along with the walk-through are completely designed one for the offense to make sure they're getting what they need and then defensively getting what they need. And so there's there's a lot of communication to make sure that the scripted portions of practice and walk-through are coordinated in a way that that maximizes the players' time. >> What what is still for money to be the first practice in pads and how much does that change things from the evaluation standpoint? >> On Monday, pads come on. >> Right. >> That's when the fun starts. >> Yeah. >> Um it the the reality is it gets a lot faster, a lot lot faster cuz the D-line and O-line aren't really protecting they're still protecting one another, but they're not operating at the speed they are now. It it becomes much more violent, it becomes much faster, the reads for the back end is a lot cleaner, the receivers getting involved in the run game and the violence in that regard. So, everything picks up and then on top of it you're adding I think it'll be the fifth install at that point. So, you're the mental load along with the pads and the new stimulus and the speed. So, you know, usually the first couple of days are always a big dud of pads because you're expecting fireworks, but there's a lot on these guys' plate starting Monday. >> A couple more guys. Are you saving one-on-one drills for when the pads come on and philosophically are you guys doing >> Yeah, that's So, we will operate differently with one-on-ones and how how it goes. You know, we've developed a a way of doing it. We'll still do one-on-ones here and there, but we we only do one-on-ones with pads to answer your question and that'll be our version of one-on-ones will show up on Tuesday and I'll give you guys a little bit more elaborate detail on that later. >> Robert, we hear a lot from the D-line and say they know they need to be the the leaders of the defense. Do you think that's a function of who you have in that unit or a function of how important they are in your defensive structure? >> Uh probably a little bit of both. You know, the you know, I always tell the D-line to whom much is given, much is required and you know, there's there's a lot of alphas in that room. Some really good football players and you know, to the the responsibility they have to to not only uphold the standard of the way we operate because we ask a lot out of our D-line. It is taxing our techniques and what we ask out of them. Um but to do things the right way and making sure that everyone is being held at the same exact standard. So, um you know, our our D-line, you know, we I I I do say it. I am vocal. We go as they go on defense. Um if they're humming and that quarterback's on his back, I can play DB and and be effective. >> Robert, >> We got to see that. We got to see that. We got to see that.

title: Coach Mike McCarthy Press Conference (August 1) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Give us a highlight of what you expect Monday to be like when you're in pads for the first time. >> Oh, shoot. Won't we talk about that Monday? I'm uh we got a lot of work to do today. Yeah, well, I mean, I think everybody's looking forward to Monday. Um you know, today is really, you know, trying to really put a lid on what we accomplished in the spring. You know, we had we had some review. Um you know, as far as the concepts and things like that at the end of the game, emphasis the last 2 days, you know, uh actually last 3 days I've been been very pleased with. So, I just want to wrap that up today and then put a bow on it. And then, you know, then the players will be off tomorrow. And then then then we'll get going. You know, then we'll jump up really right back into what I would I would call normal flow. You know, third down will be the big emphasis. You know, come Monday. You Monday's not a full practice. You know, we're still on a limited time frame. But in you know, we'll be it'll be good to get the pads on and get into some more realistic football. >> Mike, you've been running some of those 11 on 11 periods two different groups side by side on the field. What's kind of the process and the method between having those groups running concurrently during practice? >> Well, I mean, really my methodology goes back to, you know, '06 through 2010. Um I would say, you know, during the pre, you know, CBA um 2011, you know, do you were able to practice uh you know, longer. You know, you didn't have limits. Uh so, um you know, it was a it was a great experience for me as a as a first-time head coach. You know, had some great mentors, you know, as far as putting together a a program and uh you know, Marty Schottenheimer, Paul Hackett, you know, Ray Rhodes and you know, and and then I think just going into your first season, you know, you just really pay attention to the numbers. And it really what I'm going to long is but really what I'm going to this is you know, I used to do the number 3,000 was something that it was always in my mind uh because you could get, you know, 1,000 reps in the in the in the um off-season program. You know, once again, the basis is more from my years as a quarterback coach um because, you know, you you look at your opportunities, how many reps you can get, how you're going to dissect that, cut that down, and put, you know, apply that through the off-season, grow that into the training camp. And then, if you look at it, you know, it's the offense and defense usually average around 1,100, you know, plays a year. So, I've always uh looked at the ratios of, you know, how much red zone do you work on versus how much you actually use during the season. Don't have a great year on red zone, then maybe you're going to we're going to, you know, do some more of that the next year. You know, you know, rob from Peter to pay Paul. So, it's just, you know, it's it's a it's a game of numbers, you know, football is numbers. Mathematics is, I think, very important to is to pay attention to. I always have. Um you know, Dan, you know, 2011 was kind of a wash. You didn't have the off-season. So, then from '12 on, you know, I had a standard, a goal of what I was trying to get done with the football team, and worked out pretty good in 2010. So, I mean, I I tried to really try to use that as a a standard of training and and just adjusting with that through the changes in uh the CBA. So, uh with that is how do you get more reps? You know, how do you utilize the sports science? And we we can play the GPS into it. So, and and and every lot of people do it. I'm sure it it was very big in college football way back when I was when I was in college football. They call it two-spot. You know, you have two, you know, two offenses going through a defense or so forth. And you know, trying to maximize the you know, the opportunity for the young players. So, uh so, with those mock games are in two-spot. Um but the most important thing about that is the quality of those reps. I mean, frankly, reviewed it again today in the team meeting. How, you know, those reps count. I mean, they're they're counting. I I have a a goal that I'm trying to hit. You know, we're just not out there correcting some things, going through the motions. So, that those those reps are very important. And and frankly, that's why I'm with the younger players. I'm trying to get as much time with the young players and and getting them ready for the preseason game cuz those young guys are going to play for us. You know, that's in and it's it happens every year. And you preferably you hope they don't play till November, December, but guess what? Those are really important games. So, that's the facts of the of the matter of of how you train your team, the things you look about looking around the corners and trying to make sure it goes, but you know, the two spot gives us a chance to you know, to get the numbers up where they where I feel they need to be. Long answer. Is that what you want? Sorry. >> [laughter] >> A little filibuster there. >> But where do you feel that the offense is right now as far as picking up the offense? Do you feel that they're right where you thought they should be or farther ahead? >> Yeah, mentally I mentally I think we're in a a good place, solid place. You know, we're we're not you know, we're not ready to take the exam yet. Um but you know, we're definitely in a in a good place. So. Um you know, to and and to be honest, you know, it's it's about knowing what to do, you know, when to do it, but the you know, the real real challenge starts you know, starts Monday. You know, when the DBs and then you know, the set the the perimeter players can really put their hands on each other. You know, the line of scrimmage has to be established whether it's the run blocking unit, the pass rush or pass protection unit, pass rush and so forth. So, that's you know, those were when the time clocks really get you know, established and and and then we're close closer to the fire of of real football. >> Mike, we've asked you a lot about the we've asked you about the QB school. I'm just curious about the origin of it. You know, how did you develop your methodology of training quarterbacks and some of the drills and things along those lines? >> I mean really the credit goes to Paul Hackett. Um you know, I learned it from Paul, you know, '89 through '92 to University of Pittsburgh. You know, we obviously did it in a in a collegian, you know, college setting, but um you know, when we when we when we went to Kansas City, I was able to you know, Paul was the offensive coordinator and then I was uh you know, hired as a quality control coach. And you know, we started at that year in in '93 and then it was you know, it was just it was a really a great group of guys, you know, so um you know, with Joe Montana, Dave Krieg, you know, Matt Blundin. So, it's a it's it's something I've I've always believed in, you know, the CBA kind of you know, wiped out some of the opportunity for the you know, cuz the old days, you know, you would start that in the middle of March and you were able to get 4 weeks of quarterback school um before before the off-season program started, you know, um I think it was legal back then if but if it isn't, I think the statute of limitations I think I'm safe.
