But no, it was a so that's kind of how I grew up, you know, and that's that's that's what I believe in and um you know, and Aaron and I think Aaron would share cuz I've seen him talk to the younger players all the time cuz he's he's last guy that I coached that went through it, you know, cuz 2011 is when that off-season, you know, um opportunity kind of went away. So, it was just a really a a great time to really have the you know, the day to to break down, you know, everything for the quarterback cuz you know, let's be honest you you go to practice every day that you we're trying to squeeze in time in the beginning in between periods and you know, every position the O-line they get plenty of individual time to do their thing and go through all their drills and so forth and but once you know, and all the other positions do too but the quarterback always has to work with the running backs they always have to work with so, you know, where's their time to really work on their specific you know, details of fundamentals so we you know, we kind of squeeze it in there in the beginning of practice and then you know, kind of squeeze it in as we can as special teams. >> What did you see in Tannehill that made you want to bring him here and >> I'm sorry. >> What attracted you to Tannehill to bring him here and how has he how has he helped some of the young quarterbacks? He seems to be a security blanket for them already. >> No, Robert's a hell of a player, you know, just haven't been around him as a rookie um so and just I've I've always watched his career, you know, after my time with him in Green Bay, but um you know, he's you know, he and he had it right away. You know, he's very instinctive player, you know, he's very very natural in the passing game. You can see the particularly how he attacks the you know, the middle reads, the post routes, you know, the the alley routes and and uh you know, so much of that is uh is about, you know, the timing, the body the body language, you know, in ti- in tune with the clock of the quarterback. So, um you know, I I I think we're extremely fort- tunate to to have Robert here. Um Bobby, I think the guys like to call him, but uh he's uh you know, he he's a really good fit for how we want to play. >> Mike, with you being the offensive play caller, how how do you decide how much time in practice needs to be you with your head in the play sheet, your voice in Aaron's ear versus you work with the younger quarterbacks looking at the defense or things like >> Little bit of a moving target. I think you can understand that. I mean, I'm I'm I'm trying to you know, you got a number of things like all head coaches do and I'm sure it was here the same in the past. You're trying to watch young guys and and individual drills and and so forth. But in this you know, same breath, you know, um I have an accent, so I got to make sure they they hear my voice, you know, through the headset. I'm enjoying my accent. Now, I don't have to worry about it. You know, I can just let it I can just let it go, you know, so you know, but just make sure you get the mechanics cuz I'm I'm always worried about the next game. So, communication boundary communication those things are important, but I also have you know, the job of a head coach, too. I'm I'm you know, especially early you want to practice, you know, you make sure the flow of it, the the drills and so just keeping an eye on all that, so um you know, may vary a little bit practice to practice. >> Mike, how would you describe the the attitude of the the young quarterbacks you historically with your quarterback school? I mean, you know, they come in they got to this level the opportunity because they're good at what they do. And then you spend a I mean, obviously judging by rookie mini camp, you just spend a very a lot of time meticulously sort of breaking them down. How is Are they sort of like, "What are you doing here?" Or is it more of a, "Hey, they're open to coaching and obviously they want to stick around." >> Well, I I I think the you know, the reality of it is, you know, we all started somewhere at sometime and you know, you have a foundation of what you believe in. Um I've watched the development of quarterbacks change. You know, the external training and and opportunities uh that quarterbacks have is is is definitely a lot different today than it was 30 30 years ago. I mean, you know, just the things they're doing with these kids in high school is is pretty remarkable, frankly. Uh the training opportunities that they have. Uh so, being in tune with that and there's some there's some outstanding quarterback um [snorts] you know, programs out there that they're training them, you know, away from the schools and it's become a pretty profitable business, you know, so with that, but I think just being in tune with you know, how people are teaching, you know, the throwing profile, the footwork profile and and and just being able to communicate um you know, with with the quarterbacks when they get here cuz you know, everybody's it's just like anything in You know, everybody doesn't teach the exact same footwork um as a pass rusher in their stance, you know, everybody doesn't teach the same footwork as a defensive back, you know, it's it's you know, some people have you know, a certain training they believe in. Uh it's no different for for myself and and how we're doing it here and it's and it's uh you know, we're very fortunate just from a pure quarterback training standpoint and and obviously other things to have Aaron here um because you know, going back to reps, you know, this is what, 19, 18, 19 years as a starter. I mean, he you're talking about a guy that has 20,000 live reps, you know, on top of the off-season programs and so forth. So, his his ability to communicate uh to the young guys and and they're they've been I've been impressed. I mean, he made a comment to Drew yesterday in the morning meeting and Drew went went right out there and tried the footwork and the technique with his eyes. So, it's a you know, you know, I'm I'm the old that says, "Hey, don't do too much." You know, but it's it's good to see him pushing and giving these guys an education of a lifetime. >> We got time for one more. >> We saw Dontae Cannon working off to the side yesterday. Are any of those guys on pup uh close to returning next week? >> Not today. Yeah, not today. Um we'll see how the we'll see how, you know, tomorrow and everything goes, but yeah, I don't really have anything to report on those guys.

title: Alex Highsmith, Nick Herbig & Eli Heidenreich Press Conference (July 31) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: For the past couple years, I haven't started the season healthy, so for me, it's it's starting the year healthy and playing the full year healthy, you know? So, like I said, I'm just continuing to do whatever I can to make sure of that, whether it's modalities, mobility, stretching, whatever I got to do, you know, to just do whatever I can to be out there to help my team. >> How's the plan to do We already asked this, but Mike Mike said today's kind of like a mock game day. Take me through kind of what that like was what that was like for you. >> Yeah, it was basically just, you know, coming out here, you know, we obviously you know, wearing the helmets or doing contact or anything like that, but it was a very very good mental day. You know, a lot of team reps, you know, I think that's something that, you know, is really going to pay off for us, you know, guys coming out and you know, when guys are tired, you know, because you're in the middle of camp, back-to-back days, especially when we get into camp next week, you know, it's going to be back-to-back padded days and whatnot. So, being able to come out here and execute play after play after play, it was a lot of plays, but they being able to be mentally strong and execute a lot of plays, you know, I think it's just really going to help us grow as a team. Yeah, it's definitely different. You know, like I said, you know, I feel like I've kind of had the same process you know, since I've been in college, you know, in the past with with with Coach T as well. But like I said, I think just being out here and having this this mental day, guys are really just taking advantage of it in regards of just getting mental reps and and throughout the plays and just really taking the most advantage of team a lot of team reps, you know, cuz the first couple practices, you know, have been a lot of indie skill development and coming out here and getting a lot of team reps, I think was a really huge, you know, got a lot of guys that benefited from it. >> What are some of the things that you really really like about Lance's defense and the way he's utilizing and putting so much emphasis on the defensive line? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, he's he's he's a he's a he's a front guy, you know, he's coached D-line, linebackers and whatnot. So, you know, for him, I just really like I do like the scheme, you know, I think we got a lot of good things cooking up, you know, putting putting a lot of guys in great positions to make plays and so I think for us it's just about playing fast, playing physical. I think we've grown a lot as a defense throughout OTAs, this first week of camp. Guys are still learning the system, so I'm just really excited to see how he continues to put us in position to make plays, you know, cuz that's at the end of the day, you know, you got to go out there and produce. >> Do you see yourself in the long-term Steelers plans? Obviously, the next contract will be huge. >> Build it. >> Sign something next year as well? Will that be your priority? >> That's my That's my That's my, you know, dream goal. I do want to be a Steeler for life, so for me, I just want to go out there and do whatever I can to to help bring in another Super Bowl to this team, another Super Bowl to this city, so but you know, I do want to be a Steeler for life, and so for me, I'm just excited for for this year and and just to go out there and like you said, our group, you know, we're the we're the best group in the league, you know, edge-wise, and so the the three of us and Jack, so I'm I'm just really really excited for for for the group that we have, and I think it's going to be we're going to really do some special things. >> Nick, how do you like the earlier schedule with Coach Tomlin this year? What do you think of the everything that he has done so far? So far? >> Um yeah, I mean, it's obviously different, but you know, it's it's what it is. It's a system, it's what the head man wants, so you know, we're buying into it, and I like it. >> What are the biggest adjustments you have to make as a player at training camp? You got sort of in your routine when you're out here at camp. >> Uh I feel like it you kind of have to re-get into that routine every year regardless of what the schedule's like. You know, Latrobe's always a battle, but it's fun. You know, it's it's a blessing to be out here, it's a blessing to be able to wake up and have that routine. So, I think every year you grow not just as a player, as a person, your role on the team. So, I think your routines and everything leading up to that always is always evolving and changing. >> Nick, how different was it today to have kind of a mock game day, really focus on the mental side of things today? >> Yeah, that was good, especially with the new plays in, some new faces out there, and playing new positions, playing new roles in the defense, and just having that uh communication with each other um and learning the plays uh in a more slow down pace. >> How beneficial is that? I guess also, too, how different is this process compared to what you've been used to, not even last year, but, you know, going back to college up to this point? >> Yeah, um I mean, it's a different approach uh and, you know, that's what you expect when you have a new staff uh and McCarthy is a very well-respected coach. He's a He's done it for a long time in this league. He's won a Super Bowl. He's produced many MVPs and all-pro players, so he he obviously knows what he's doing. >> Nick, what really sticks out to you about Patrick Graham? >> Uh his energy. His energy's is doesn't matter if it's 6:00 a.m. or 6:00 p.m. That guy's always got energy. >> How much does that transfer to you guys? >> Oh, you know, you love to see that um not just out of coach who's just talking about it, but he's actually, you know, in tune with you and he's showing you that he's just as passionate about it as you are. >> What is a practice like today like where you guys it's not kind of I don't know the word for it, but you guys are out there like in hats, no helmets. Like, how's that feel to have a bit of a a lighter practice? >> I think it's more so just um with this new staff, with the new plays and everything, just kind of getting our feet under ourself, uh learning the plays uh and you know, uh quality over quantity sometimes, and uh I think we had some quality reps out there today. >> Practices seem to be uh quicker. Uh the tempo is faster. Do you notice a difference between this year and past years as far as how the practices are operating? >> Uh not necessarily. I mean, I don't really, you know, you kind of just get ready for practice and you don't really know what's what's going to unfold as the day goes on, so uh I don't really keep track of time, uh but it it we definitely got some good work in. >> When did you guys start doing >> mornings when, you know, did you find out this morning that hey, today's going to be a little bit more of an elevated walk-through, or do you kind of know ahead like, well, >> Yeah, I mean, coach kind of lays out the plan for us every day uh in the team meeting, so uh you kind of get a sense of what you're going into to mentally and physically prepare yourself. >> We always ask about the bonding aspect of camp always. How have things been like? I know it's been just a few days since you guys have been here. How have things been off the field for >> Oh, awesome. Awesome. Uh you know, I love being up here with the boys. Uh you know, I really get to disconnect kind of from the rest of the world and just be in our own little world and not just on the defense, but with the offense guys, with the special teams guys, so it's a great time. >> Next, you guys started the three-outside-linebacker look last year. What's the comfort level when you guys are in that situation? >> Yeah, I think that uh having T.J. and Alex out there in general is just they're the two best in the league. And then add in me to the mix, I think it's going to be exciting. >> Alex, do or do you think that Alex, like last season, may be in the best ball of his since you've been with him in his career these last five, six games? >> Uh it's hard to argue against that. Hard to argue against that. That guy's a baller. >> Did you do the three OLBs two years ago? >> Uh I think we dabbled in it, but it wasn't anything too prevalent. >> [cheering] >> Want to dabble this year? >> I guess we'll just have to find out. >> It's been really exciting. I've actually never had the chance to come out here in all my years living in Pittsburgh. I've you know, football is always starting up and never had the chance, but you know, you see pictures and videos of it, so to be out here, um you know, it it really is an honor to you know, share this field with so many Pittsburgh legends that have come here before me. Um and I'm just ready to get after it. >> You guys played at a very high level in college, but up here the talent level is as high as you can get. What's it been like being out on the field with you know, future Hall of Famers and NFL legends? >> Yeah, I mean, you said it. There's an incredible amount of talent and knowledge. I think that's the second thing that not a lot of people think about is, you know, how many years these guys have put in on this field and you know, all the things that they picked up in that time. And you you really want to pick their brain as much as you can and try and just be a sponge and absorb knowledge. >> You know, how much do you think that you played maybe and do you think that's your path to the team more so than you do with the ball in the air? >> Yeah, I uh I played all four phases at at Navy throughout my uh three years playing there. Um you know, special teams is something I take pride in and I really enjoy doing. I don't get to tackle anymore and I'm playing defense, so getting out there and tackling a little bit on special teams is it's a blast and that's absolutely um you know, a way that I see myself contributing to this team. >> All right, has there been one moment so far and it's only been a few days in, but has there been one moment where you kind of felt like you were a Steeler? Set in, I'm a Steeler and I'm in my home town. >> Here at camp? >> Yeah. >> Um you know, I I think the the first day getting here, I I pulled up that hill right behind us and just kind of overlooking the field. It was right around like sunset time, so it was very like picturesque and you just took a moment and really thought about you know, all the time and effort I put in and where I'm at and I'm just excited to you know, have this opportunity. >> What's the coolest or craziest thing you've heard from a fan or signed for a fan or the sign that you've seen in anything like that? >> That's a That's a good question. So, it was today. I was walking down the ramp over there and someone from Mount Lebanon had a printed out picture of me in like sixth grade. >> [laughter] >> So, I >> this person? >> No, I did not know them. >> They just did their research. >> I think they they went to the same middle school or they go to the same middle school that that I attended, so I absolutely went over there and signed that for them. That was pretty funny. >> Eli, are you getting used to this? >> Um I I think to an extent, it definitely just takes time. Um but it's pretty awesome. Just you know, I try to stay after and you know, give back to you know, all the all the kids and people that that took the time to come out here. You know, I was once in their shoes, so um it just means a lot to them. >> Do you have any service commitments at all or is that on hold indefinitely while you do this? >> Yeah, so my main priority right now is football. I I won't have anything taking me away from football. Um I'm currently in the reserves in the United States Marine Corps, so um I don't have any actual uh commitments while I'm in the reserves and then um you know, down the line whenever I'm done playing, I'll have the ability to go back active duty. >> It looked like you got a little more involved in passing today. Got a couple balls in the end zone. How did that feel to kind of show off those skills that you know you have? >> Yeah. I mean, it's exciting. Um and honestly, it felt natural. I did a lot of that at Navy, so um that's something I'm just, you know, trying to continue to do. Just be that versatile guy and help them out any way I can. >> Logistically, you know, more autographs you sign, I guess you miss out on a little free time at lunch or just sit there and relax a little bit after practice. Is that what you're sacrificing? >> Yeah, I mean, we we don't have anything right after. We'll have lunch, so you know, we we have time. And if some just want to get back. >> What did you notice about Mike McCarthy in terms of I guess his attention to you? >> Yeah, um that's absolutely something I've noticed. Um you know, I I think obviously every you see the details on the field. That's kind of a given. Um but you know, he gets to know his players and he cares about the details about his players. And I think that's something that you know, really resonates with with us as a team. Um you know, it's something I really appreciate is how much he cares about us and gets to know us. >> Do you have any experience with outfits that stress the detail? >> And what did you say? >> Do you have any experience with organizations or outfits that stress detail? >> Oh, okay. Uh you could say a little bit. Yeah, absolutely. You know, that's the whole premise of the military is being detail oriented. So, absolutely. >> Are there any parallels there or >> Yeah, I mean, just the the way you carry yourself. Um details matter. You could argue in the military that, you know, you you let you miss a little detail that could you know, get someone injured or you know, even even worse than that. So, it's the same thing out on the football field is, you know, stress those little details. >> Did you grow up uh you you I'm sure you wore a lot of Steelers gear. Do you ever kind of like catch yourself when you're putting on a jersey, putting on the cleats, and go, "Wow, I'm I'm actually a Steeler. I'm putting on this gear that I used to that I grew up with." >> Yeah, that's that's a good question. Um yeah, I have some some pretty cool jerseys back home that I was looking through the other day as I I was leaving packing up for camp. I have my Troy Polamalu jersey and I have a Rod Woodson jersey, too. So, just looking at those and thinking, you know, out there there's there's kids that, you know, might have my jersey. It's pretty special to think about. >> You guys are the last of 10 draft picks and a few undrafted guys. I don't know if you know like who your sweetmates are or anything, but how much are you guys bonding through this experience out here? >> Yeah, we've had a a ton of time, I feel like, spent together. And I think naturally you're going to spend more time with the rookies, you know, you have more meetings together and then, you know, guys your age and you just spend the most time with them, so you know them the best, but um, we've had a ton of time to just get to know each other over meals, in between meetings, whatever. So, and we've definitely been bonding. >> Who are your sweetmates? What do you expect here? >> Sorry? >> Who are your sweetmates? >> I actually don't know who lives right next to me. Um, we don't I don't actually share a room with anyone, we just share a bathroom, so um, we haven't run into each other there yet. Which is probably a good thing. >> You know, after what you've experienced in mini camp, OTAs, and out here, how do you feel your skillset translates to >> Yeah, um, you know, I think the NFL, especially at the running back position, is they value that versatility and the ability to you have to be a runner first and, you know, a protector first, but now nowadays you really have to go uh, catch the football and, you know, be able to you know, make some things happen in space in the passing game. So, I think that's something that I'll be able to carry over. >> You talked about being a protector. Do you look forward to getting pads on because of that? It's such a big part of the goal is that pass protection. >> Absolutely. Um, yeah, I mean, the the running back position is is pretty different to play when you don't have pads on, you're not hitting, so, you know, I'm kind of jumping out the bit a little bit to to put pads on and and get playing some real football.

title: Coach Mike McCarthy Press Conference (July 31) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Speaking with quarterbacks for a second, just in the short time you've had to work with them in the off-season, where have they begun to show some progress and what more will be the points of emphasis during the training camp here? >> Well, that's fundamentals. It's an everyday all day uh deal. I mean, just being in the meetings, I think Aaron is doing an exceptional job just sharing the past experiences and and as as we're able to go through the quarterback school and so, you know, just all the little tidbits and you know, the guys are definitely soaking it up. So, that that's an ongoing you know, you know, that's the never-ends, you know, so I mean, that's why you do it. It's the baseline of everything we do as far as playing from the pocket. Um so, you know, the young guys are doing a good job there, but they need reps, you know, they need seven-on-sevens, they need the group work. You know, just the progression of the drill work showing up into the competitive work. So, I mean, this is obviously a critical time of year for them and you know, the preseason will be big for the young guys. >> Mike, you mentioned Mike, you mentioned mock game, is that what you said today? What does that really entail? >> Uh it's just trying to hit all the different situations that occur throughout the game, you know, it's you have a primary emphasis, um for instance, it's kind of it's cut into two two phases, you know, the first phase is game management and special teams. You know, one of the things throughout the years is just, you know, through through experience, you know, you get down to the first preseason game and you know, your boundary your boundary communication, your boundary management is something that, you know, you usually just work on right before you go out. So, um you know, it's a 90-man roster, so we're my point is we're hitting those things now, you know, I don't think you can do enough situational um work, the awareness of it. Um the importance of stressing the defense with the personnel group having the right right personnel groups. Just all the little things that go into the make up of a game, you know, then you get into the second part of it and, you know, it like today's second part is really re-review of the last two days. So, we kind of It's a format I've always tried to kind of go one or two you want do two installs review. Two installs review. So, it's it kind of matches the workload capacity of what you're looking for as far as like next week we have two padded practices review. Then we'll have three padded practices. This will be the biggest stress point in this more going into the Saturday night uh scrimmage in downtown. So, um so, just you know, it's a flow that really works physically, mentally and it really gives you a chance to to hit all the situations. >> Mike, uh Spencer Anderson and Dylan Cook have played a lot of roles here through OTAs, mini camp, first couple of days. I understand they haven't been pads on yet. What have you seen from those two on the right side? >> Well, I just like to recognize your first point. I mean, it's it's a an excellent example of what I think we talked about the other day. I mean, you talk about position flex. You know, those guys define that very well and that's a real credit to to them what they've done in the past and and how we view them. Their ability to to play multiple positions, but also give them a chance to compete to win a job. You know, win a starting job. So, been very impressed with their work and you know, the O-line and D-line I'm sure they're you know, they're looking forward to getting past tomorrow's practice cuz you know, then you can get in the pads and you know, things can get you know, get get into the real stuff for them. But, I think both those guys have done a done an excellent job so far. >> Um Mike, so far um Roman's gotten a lot of work. He's gotten a lot of passes. Aaron's gone his way a lot. How have you kind of seen Roman uh kind of evolve throughout just the short time you've had with him and how's he taken uh to these opportunities? >> You know, I just look back to you know, Roman and like like a lot of things in life, you know, I look at him with the first impression. Um frankly, him and I were walking up from the meeting or or driving back from the meeting yesterday and we're talking about the Michigan workout. You know, when he's you know, he came out I was at the workout and we're talking about you know, the Harbaugh family and just what an impressive team it was and what how impressive um that whole workout was and you know, him coming out of college and and then, you know, and going back to when when I arrived here, we had a conversation on the phone. Um you know, he wanted to introduce himself and you know, talked about you know, his his first year and and um and really and and it's really hasn't changed since then. I said, "I need you to be a multiple position player." I said, "I want to be able to line you up both inside and outside." He's done a hell of a job inside. Frankly, I want to you know, I haven't even talked to him yet about this, but I think we can start working a little bit more outside, too, cuz you know, his vertical his vertical speed and and his ability to, you know, we call it the Autobahn out there on the numbers. I think he's he's an an excellent has an excellent skill set for that, also, too. So, um but he's done a really nice job. I mean, he can line up at X, Z, and F and you know, so so far, he's done exactly what we asked. >> Anyone else? >> Mike, Travis Homer uh it looks like he's has a lot of leadership duties on special teams so far. >> [clears throat] >> What did you know about him from his special teams work in the past to kind of hand him the personal protector job right now in the first half? >> Well, I mean, we're you know, we're working reps and so forth. I think it obviously his history is he's a veteran special teams player, but um yeah, I'm once again, I'm looking forward to getting into the padded work you know, that that personal protector is important cuz obviously the identification responsibility and and you do want a experienced player in there, you know, but we got some good young guys. We got some young guys that have that that uh you know, will have an opportunity in there, also. >> Mike, I know pads aren't on yet, but how do you anticipate the guys in in your previous experience being able to bring some of that physicality without full tackle? >> Yeah, I I think um I must have done a bad job with the the our our our practice will be physical. You know, I mean, the only thing that's different is we don't want to go to the ground and and risk injury, but I think everything else will look will look the same. >> Mike, there's been some opportunities for Asante Samuel Jr. in camp and he's been noticeable. What what's jumped out to you about him and could he be a, you know, a guy that could work into the mix during the season? >> I I know personally I'm counting on him. You know, it's just like anything in this league, you know, you come into a new job, new situation, especially as a head coach. Uh there's individuals that, you know, obviously competing against his father, you know, but um he's he's he's frankly been one of my favorite players, you know, since I arrived here. I just love the way he works. He's extremely physical. His his ball skills are off the charts, you know, that's a big thing I've um you know, that's that's something I really look for in defensive backs. You want to take the ball away, catch the flash of the ball. And uh he has all that and he's done you know, he's he's been here every single day uh off season program. Uh he's had two really good practices so far. You know, he really had did his first day. He had a did did a, you know, really nice job. So, I think the I think the young man's a hell of a football player. >> What's it like working with him after you said competing against his dad? That happened How often is that happened to you? >> Well, you know, you know, you know where they are cuz they're going to pick the ball off. So, you know, his father was the same way. So, uh you definitely conscious of it. Uh we're uh I think I was talking to Art about, you know, we were talking about the flag football candidates and and and I I think his name was one of the names that come up. I mean, he'd be on my flag football team, too. So, I mean, he could play, you know, hell, I'd play him on offense just cuz of his skill set, but he's uh he's a very talented young man. >> Who else do you have on that flag football candidate list? >> I think we got to go now, right? That's >> Last one. You got two years. You got some time. >> Mike, you you've talked to us about things like GPS monitoring and um you know, some sports science type of stuff. Is that something that you've always kind of leaned into or is there a point in your coaching journey that you started to, you know, explore those kinds of topics a little bit more? >> Uh very fortunate to come up in some excellent programs, you know, I've worked for, you know, great organizations, I've been around people you know, my whole career that you know, were forthcoming, you know, and been exposed to a lot. Uh but it, you know, as a head coach, you know, it's I I frankly look at this part, you know, part of your job responsibility. Those are tools. A GPS is a tool, sports science is a tool. Um they're but still it's a people's game. I think we got to be conscious of that. I'm I'm not going to you know, GPS is is part of the is is part of the evaluation. It's not going to drive every decision that we make. That's that's not realistic, you know, the human human part of this is uh you know, I think we want to refer more to the steel mill operation than we do it to the GPS. So, uh that that won't change here. Uh never never will, but those are really good tools that I've been exposed to and just have used them and have history and I'll be able to do it in three places, you know, so you got you have criteria that uh you're able to interact with both the, you know, trainers and the and the strength and conditioning coaches, and and it's it has served us well, you know, I think we've clearly I know uh first using it, I'm going to say 20% was a number that kind of jumps out at me. Um just when you look at practice and you try to reduce the fatigue injuries, you know, we were higher in my earlier days as a head coach, I but I think it was probably more of a product of how you trained back then, too. You know, you practiced a lot more. You had more team meetings and so forth. You can see that just in the practice reps. So, um blessed to coach in that in that era as a head coach, cuz you know, you know how many reps um you know, you say if you get 1,100 reps as an offense during the season, you try to emulate that in your training camp. So, um and now that's opportunity does not exist, you know, because of the the limits, you know, But, where do you get those reps? And that's where the mock game is important. You know, that's these mock games and the quarterbacks are critical and and the offensive line are critical in these mock game situations because they control the tempo and the pace and the, you know, the pre-snap part of it. So, these are really quality reps uh that we get in these uh mock games. And it still keeps me hitting the totals that I'm I'm comfortable and used to training a football team. So, uh so, just been fortunate to be part of the old age, you know, in the '90s, uh 15 days in a row of two days in pads. You know, um I'd go to jail today if I if I tried to do that. But, you know, but just have the understanding of what that looks like and how you how you do that and just try to, you know, practice safer. >> Mike, you've given Last one. You've given D'Wayne Eskridge some challenging assignments all the way back to OTAs. Obviously, DK kind of got him yesterday. What do you look for in a young player in in terms of response to a moment like that? >> Exactly what he did. I mean, that's what you want. It's a, you know, it's a seven-route. He's holding his leverage. And you got two, you know, extraordinary athletes going to keep competing, you know, making plays on the ball. And that's that's, you know, to me, that's that's a high-quality rep uh because of the big play importance in our game. You know, you have to make those plays and, you know, obviously, you can see the trust there in how he and DK did where he put the ball and and, you know, DK won that battle. So, um you can't get enough of those reps, you know, for all of our guys. But, um yeah, he's, you know, he doesn't look like a rookie. I'm I'm been impressed with him.

title: Pat Freiermuth SHINES, RB rotation, starting RG steps up, surprising cut looms? | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on, everybody? Welcome back to the Steelers Rewind here on pennlive.com. Nick Farabaugh here with you all. The Pittsburgh Steelers wrap up their first week of training camp, really the acclimation period, if you will. It is now done for the Pittsburgh Steelers. Padded practice on Monday. They are off tomorrow. So, I'll be here with a little bit of a recap of week one tomorrow. We'll have a podcast. We'll do all that great jazz. Tomorrow, I'll be back home. I'll be back in the studio. It'll be great. But, let's talk about today. The Steelers did not really do a walk-through today. It was a little bit more like the first two days. Obviously, the last two days were walk-through style. Um but, today the Pittsburgh Steelers did some good things. Um you know, did some 7-on-7 and some 11-on-11. We saw some two-minute drills. There were two two-minute drills to end uh the session. Uh we saw Aaron Rodgers drive the team right down the football field and really finish it off with a nice back-shoulder throw to Pat Freiermuth. I thought this was Pat Freiermuth's best day, and I think it's kind of exemplary of what I expect from Pat Freiermuth in the Pittsburgh Steelers offense this year. Seen balls, working the middle of the field, making really tough grabs in that area of the field. And it seems like he and Aaron Rodgers have a natural connection. I also think he and Aaron Rodgers you know, this idea that it was those two that had the disconnect and maybe not what Arthur Smith thought. I think that is clearly not the case. These two very much have a connection. And I think he's going to be very active. Roman Wilson continues to have a strong uh training camp. He made a few nice plays today. Drag routes, over routes. The Steelers continue to utilize him. He's also been doing some punt return stuff. Um but, he continues to do a lot of good things. Um also, Anthony McFarland and Jaylen Warren, I've heard some people say like it's 70-30. I think it's probably more like 55-45 towards McFarland. We see Warren out there a lot in receiving drills. We also saw Lu Nichols, the you know, the practice squad running back from last year get some first team reps today. We saw Caleb Johnson yesterday. We're seeing them kind of mix that rotation up a little bit in that running back room. Darnell Savage and DeShawn Elliott both didn't do 11-on-11 drills today, so that allowed Robert Spillane Jennings, a seventh-round rookie out of Oklahoma, to get his first team opportunities. Um did okay with them. He's been a little bit up and down, honestly. So, that's been one thing to watch. He's clearly athletic. Struggles a little bit moving side to side, but he's great downhill. He's got a nose for the football. So, there are some really positive things there. I think we saw today the first spice of Patrick Graham really show off. There was a play where they brought the slot corner blitz, but it was disguised. T.J. Watt dropped out into the middle of the field. Aaron Rodgers tried to hit the hot route behind it, and T.J. Watt was right there and picked it off. Little bit of a different blitz look, um and that led to a turnover. That's the type of stuff from Patrick Graham I think we see a little bit. We're starting to see the stamps of that. That was T.J. Watt on the right side, not the left side. We usually see him on the left side. He's moving around, playing a little bit over the middle, dropping into coverage, doing some different stuff. They're getting a little tricky with him. Um and that is allowing I think some of these guys to make some plays, and they're really excited about it. Um it's it's nice to see. In terms of the inside linebacker room, Malik Harrison has not played much uh with the third with anything but the third team. Carson Bruno has left him. Um we have seen Cole Holcomb mix in with the first team on early downs and the second team uh otherwise. Payton Wilson's playing a lot of with the first team next to Patrick Queen, but not a lot of Malik Harrison. Is he really a roster lock? I have questions. Um the second nose tackle behind Y A Black appears to be Gabriel Rubio, the sixth-round rookie out of Notre Dame. That's been interesting. We were looking to see who that would be. Didn't know, but seems like that. The corner room continues to get a lot of praise. I feel like Asante Samuel makes a play every day. He made another one today. Brandon Echols made a great uh pass breakup on a slot fade to DK Metcalf. Uh and Daylen Everett continues to show out as well. So much praise for the rookie. I had someone tell me today that he is the best rookie they have. Uh just so much. He's got a mentorship going on with DK Metcalf. Lot of positives there. And then the last thing I want to talk about, Spencer Anderson seems pretty entrenched in that right guard spot. I have not seen a single player outside of Spencer Anderson play at right guard with the first team. I've seen them switch right tackle and left tackle. I've seen, you know, Hjalte Froholdt and Cook and others kind of mix in and out. I have not seen anyone mix in with with Spencer Anderson. It's just been him. James Daniels has been with the third team. Brock Hoffman's been an interior swing man. Looks like right now Spencer Anderson, the easy favorite to be the starting right guard week one for the Pittsburgh Steelers. All right, folks. Make sure to like, comment, subscribe, turn the notification bell for more, and thanks for watching.

title: Daylen Everette IMPRESSES, Germie Bernard gets run, Kaleb Johnson steps up | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to another episode of Steelers training camp preview on Nick Farabaugh here with you guys. Pittsburgh Steelers took the field today for their third training camp practice in Latrobe under Mike McCarthy and we are continuing to see the differences between Mike McCarthy and Mike Tomlin. Certainly not the same uh training camp whatsoever. Today was essentially a spirited walk-through. I don't think it was much more than that. They were not in shells. They were not in helmets. They just came out in their jerseys and shorts. Did a lot of recall. Did some new stuff. Um there was a long, you know, 40-minute period where they were doing a lot of recall from yesterday and a little bit of a mock game putting themselves in a different situations, doing different things. It was a really kind of interesting to watch the philosophy honestly behind uh what the Steelers wanted to do um today. But, you know, you saw Drew Allar and Will Howard on one side in team drills and you saw Rudolph and and Rodgers running on one side. McCarthy actually went off with the young guys and and the third team there just to get those young guys up to speed and kind of going. We did see some different pairings today. Jeremy McNichols played a lot more um with the first team. We actually saw a lot today where they actually had four wide receiver sets where McNichols and Roman Wilson were on the field with Pittman and Metcalf and there wouldn't wouldn't be a running back on the football field. I thought that was fairly interesting. Um Roman Wilson starting to take some reps outside. Um he has continued to impress and and Mike McCarthy talked about that today talking about just how good Roman Wilson has been. That he's been so good on the inside, it's time to get him some reps on the outside because of his vertical speed. They're searching for explosiveness in this offense. If they're going to look at one place, the speed and explosiveness that Roman Wilson has, the potential he has there is a really really kind of big one for that. Also, the YAC ability of Jeremy McNichols. But, McNichols was playing inside outside. They motioned him inside to the running back position a little bit more. We saw that. when they were lining up in formations, we saw different combinations on the defensive line. Isaiah Black continues to only play nose tackle. Benton is out at end, but we also saw, you know, one where it was Benton, Black, and Harmon, no Cam Heyward. We We saw T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith flipping sides with with Nick Herbig over the middle and and no down lineman. You know, that amoeba defense that has existed for about a decade now or a little bit longer than that. It's a little bit of a different look uh the Steelers are giving. Um so we we saw a lot of different things and people kind of switching into different roles. Caleb Johnson got, you know, some first team reps on some third down plays. You know, Rogers moving them around the formation, kind of pointing out fronts to him, making sure that he can pick up blitzes. There were a few times where he got some really good praise from Aaron Rodgers today because it seems like he recognized the blitzes and picked them up. And so that's a really good thing for Caleb Johnson. He's also a wing on punt team. It seems like he's taking on these roles. I talked about if Caleb Johnson, you know, wants to be one snap away from getting on the football field cuz Jaylen Warren gets hurt, he needs to diversify his game. He can't just be an early down bruiser. He needs to be a special teamer or a pass pro guy. It seems like he has taken to that. So a really good start for Caleb Johnson. Travis Homer is the personal protector. I think he's going to make this football team. But they can keep four running backs. They have enough roster room to do that. So that will be something to kind of watch as we get you deeper into this. It also seemed like Robert Spillane, the rookie out of Oklahoma, running ahead of Sebastian Joseph right now. So if you're kind of looking at guys that can make that safety room, that is one to look at. Asante Samuel Jr. got a lot of praise today from Mike McCarthy about how good he's been, ball hawk nature of his game, all these different things that he brings to the table. He's a small player that plays bigger than he really is. I think that's a really big plus and that's a compliment in every way possible. Daylan Everett also somebody the Steelers really like and that they have talked about just extensively. Um you know, Mike McCarthy said Daylan Everett hasn't looked like a rookie and he hasn't and he's taken on a lot of different roles and I I think it's been a really big plus. All right, folks. Make sure to like, comment, subscribe, turn on the notification bell for more and thanks for watching.

So, I like to compete, I like to to put my best foot forward and you know, that's just what I'm going to continue to do and you know, I like to ask questions, I like, you know, I like to chop it up with Mike, chop it up with Christian Kirk and [music] you know, these are vets who have done it for a long time and so, I like to pick their brains too and add add things to my game that you know, I see with them and see what I can do to get myself better as well. >> Yeah. Anything specific you've gotten from Mike or Christian that you're taking and adding to your game? >> I would say definitely just speed and like releases. Like a release was a big thing for me that I asked them and and how they can just create separation. That was the big thing I've noticed with them that they create separation a lot and [music] from the from the jump from their careers and up until now and they're still doing creating separation, which is something I admire from those guys. So, I just want to take that advice from them and apply it to my game and see what I can do. >> Yeah. And we've noticed you stay late every now and then you're putting in that extra work, you're staying late after practice, getting a few more reps in. What's one part of your game? Like you mentioned separation, but something else that you are specifically working on. I would say special teams, punt return, being able to track the ball, looking at coverages, how guys fly down the field and and how they pursue and stuff like that. So, I'm trying to add that too and get better at that and I'm trying to make something shake. So, I heard that, you know, punt return hasn't happened here in quite some time. So, I'm trying to be the first one to do it. Let's do it. Let's make that history. [music] So, you're entering year three, first few years in the NFL. What's one thing about yourself that you've learned throughout these last few years. >> Uh about myself, um >> [music] >> being patient. I think that's the number one thing I've learned about myself. Um Last year was like like again, um I learned that being patient within myself and not trying to rush into anything and not trying to be someone else, just be myself. And um you know, just have love for myself as well, too, and understand in what I do, put in like the work and stuff like that, [music] and it's just uh one of those things, you know, just love yourself and uh just continue to work. >> Love that. Love that [music] mantra for yourself. And come this season, obviously training camp, we're getting through it, then we're getting into week one down in Australia, a lot of travel come up coming up for us. What's one thing at the end of the season, if we're sitting here, that you want people to say about Jacob Cowing? >> Uh he's a great guy. He's a great competitor. Um you know, he loves the Bay Area fans. He loves the faithful. Um uh I'm a great teammate as well, too. And he just likes to have fun. >> catch up with Jacob and just hear from his perspective, his journey, and um everything that he has been through and and you know, the hard work it takes to get back to this spot and confidence that he's building every single day. >> Um it also was really funny. I love that he mentioned he's got a little bit of personality. So, if you guys are ever around him, he said listen for a joke or two. >> Yeah. One of my first interactions with actually Isaac Guerendo was him hyping up Jacob Cowing. Isaac is a big Cowing fan. >> I was I was about to say that. The fact that you just said that. So, when I came up to them at practice, it was them two >> They're they're besties. >> They're besties. Yeah. >> So, catch both of them together. >> So, maybe they're funny together. Yeah. >> Exactly. Exactly. So, definitely stay tuned for that. But, closing out, what's to come, we have the first episode of The Build coming to you guys shortly. And also, first day of pads are soon to come. >> Yeah. Now, The Build. The Build is super, super exciting because we get to kind of follow the team up until um, regular season. Our studios team works so hard on that. If you have probably if you're ever at training camp, you'll see three cameras out there. So, it is going to be really exciting. Um, we're, you know, we're getting a little some snippets of it and it's um, I once it gets released to the faithful, they're going to love it. >> No, super cool. Super cool things to come, especially pads on Friday. >> So, super excited to see that. Super excited to see the faithful back here to watch the boys in the pads. Aubrey and I will bring you guys more content coverage on the rest of training camp to come. We've been posting articles on 49ers.com. We had a collabed article today. So, that was always fun to do together. Thank you for joining us on today's episode of the saloon presented by Cisco. Make sure you subscribe on YouTube, SiriusXM, and all your favorite podcast platforms. >> And make sure you have your notifications turned on for the saloon so you don't miss an episode. >> Yes, go Niners.

title: Odighizuwa, Evans Talk Team Chemistry, Competition at Training Camp | 49ers
text: the the biggest obstacles or the biggest challenges in in coming to your first training camp here >> moving my stuff. >> It's football, you know what I mean? Uh schedule's a little different, but they do a good job taking care of our bodies. So, really the logistics of getting my stuff over here is most difficult part. >> Last year, you led the NFL in quarterback hits among defensive tackles. What what do you feel like you still need to work on in your game? >> Um feel like most of my career just having a lot of pass rush production just turning that into more sacks, you know, just taking that next step. >> How did you feel about the the atmosphere today? First day of PR uh pads. How does that compare to first days that you've had uh in Dallas elsewhere? I feel like just in general as a lineman, everything feels a little bit more natural when you have pads on. >> You've been a Cowboy your whole career. You've had really tough battles with the Niners in the past. Did you have to sort of forget some of those rivalries and uh matchups against the Niners when you joined this team? >> Um, I mean, a little bit, but at the same time, I feel like that's just what what happens when you come to a new team. you know, your loyalty changes and and now anyone in a different jersey is the enemy. So, that's how it is. >> Were there specific niners offensively that you always weren't happy to have to face off against? >> I mean, it's definitely cool having Trent on my side now versus being on the other side. So, it's cool to be able to pick his brain. I was actually uh we had an off day yesterday. We're both cold tubbing and stuff. Got to chop it up with him a little bit, talk about some of the things that he's seen in his career. just get a little wisdom from him. So, it's cool to have him as a resource now as opposed to having him as opponent. >> Oh, so you said turning quarterback hits into sacks. It sounds like that's something the whole defense could have applied, you know, in terms of improving in 2026. Have you guys talked about that? Um, ways to improve uh here into the season. >> Definitely. That's something that uh I don't know if you guys have just talked to any of the other guys, but like when when we came in in OTAAS's, coach sat down with everybody in the room and individually and just went over things that everybody can improve on. So that's conversations that we've had with coach individually and everyone is sharpening themselves through camp and just working on these things and just the three get betters that we've had since OTAAS. your pedigree as a pass rusher in your career in practice, a padded practice like today where you have one-on- ones. Is that something that you particularly look forward to? >> Um, I like one-on- ones for sure. It kind of helps warm me up for the team periods. Obviously, the most game-like reps you get is the team period, but I feel like having one-on- ones is like a good prep and primer for the rushes that you're going to get during team. So, I enjoy them. I know it's very early on, but with Ricky Morris and kind of what's he's trying to instill upon you, do you get a sense of how he's going to call a game? >> Um, a little bit. The we had a move the ball period today, so got to kind of get a feel for how things are going to be called. >> How would you describe kind of his philosophy that he's tried to impart on you guys? >> Um, I mean, I'm still learning that a little bit. I got to go like review the tape, get a feel for it. But, you know, um he's I know he's trying to make it very simple, make sure we have good communication so we can play fast. >> You describe the energy and sounds you hear of Fred Warner and Dre Green Law behind you. >> Oh man, Fred just I feel like has a menacing aura. Him and Green Law for sure. So, having them on the field behind me just adds just a little bit of confidence for sure. Having two of the best linebackers in the league. Were you at all surprised? They both had took turns throwing people to the ground today. >> Not at all. >> They're teammates, but that still didn't surprise you. >> I mean, obviously talk about protect the team and stuff like that, but I just know when it comes to guys like that, they just have one speed. So, it's definitely hard to And obviously smart stuff like that. I don't think anyone's getting hurt, but like it's football. They got one speed. The way they practice is the way they play. So, you can't really argue with what they do and what they put on tape because it's very consistent, doesn't change. >> Puts a lot of emotion into coaching you guys. What are your takeaways from just working with him for a short amount of time? >> Um, I appreciate the intensity. He's very consistent. Don't think he's changed a day since I've been here, been the same guy. So, the way he's coaching is the way he's been coaching. And if he's getting on you, you probably deserve it. As far as coming together as a defense, what have been sort of the coaching point that Raheem has impressed upon you guys? >> Um, I feel like just making sure we're on the same page, getting communication, stuff like that. The play style is the biggest thing. So, if we are playing at the style that we need to, playing nasty defense, making sure we're going for the ball, stuff like that, running to the ball, bringing that energy, everything is going to come together from front to back. A couple more. Vinnie, >> also we asked you about the uh earlier during the OTAAS about the Cowboy game and that seemed to be like a big game to you. Um, how did you did you feel like you parted ways with them on bad terms or do you just excited to go against them and kind of knock heads against them? >> I mean, I love playing good teams in general. You know what I mean? I know that's one of the best offenses in the league. So, just going into the game, it's not really any bad blood. Still got a lot of love for the guys. everyone on the team don't love loss at all, but it's a great team and I'm a competitor, so just looking forward to it. >> How's your chemistry been with Brock and how's the adjustment been with him? >> I'll say it's been pretty good so far. We've gotten a lot of work in in the short amount of time that, you know, we've been teammates, but uh it's been good. It's getting better every day. >> People here would say this was hot today. Do you laugh at that and say >> I swear Coach Hank said it was a hot day? Oh, hell no. It's a perfect day. I'll take this day every day. >> Maybe this is a stupid question. Um, I don't mean to like, oh, you're an old man or anything, but I mean, at this point in your career, I mean, is it nice to get out of that humidity? I mean, is there anything to that of not, you know, spending? >> Absolutely. I mean, it's a it's definitely a bonus in being here. Um, I didn't really think about it too much until I got out here during OTAAS and I felt the the weather and it's it's a big difference. So, it's a it's a huge bonus for me to be here in this in this type of weather. >> In that same vein, in the spring, George said that when when he was kind of pitching you, one of the things that that you lit up at was the the lie flat seats on on traveling. Uh, was that was that something that actually I mean I I know it's not that the the thing that's going to swing, but like was that something that was an issue for you and how much >> the plane situation wasn't like a big selling thing for me? Um, but I'm excited for that and you know when we travel I'm sure that'll help, you know, our backs out and and our our legs for sure. >> As a tall guy, has that is that is that an issue for you? >> I love the planes that that lay back and you get to relax and sleep on them. I love those type of planes for sure. Do you know >> weather and travel aside, being with one team your whole career and now starting here? What is the biggest adjustment of coming to work? >> Just getting to know everybody. Honestly, in Tampa, I knew everybody in the front office, in the building, kitchen staff. I knew everybody. And now I'm trying to I like that environment at work, knowing everybody that I'm I come in contact with. So, just getting used to everybody and and knowing their names and stuff like that. Mike, >> it's a young room with a lot of young receivers. Are any of those young guys standing out to you? I mean, Strip Strib's having a he had a really good off seasonason OTAAS and he's he's continued that during training camp, but all of them are really getting after it. I mean, this is a hungry group of guys. We look forward to showing that we're one of the best receiver rooms in the league. you get a sense that a lot of the guys not only in your room but the guys you're going up against the the DBs have wanted to talk to you and kind of get a sense for your tricks and like just kind of >> a lot of guys have been you know picking my brain on you know how my longevity you know how I've been able to make plays consistently and things like that and in turn I I asked the other guys older guys the same thing like Trent Juice KD all those guys that have been in the league a long time um how that What do they do to, you know, stay fresh and and play so long? >> Do you know Debo from before at all? And have you seen him in here? Because what what does that mean to a team to bring him back? >> Yeah, Debo's my guy. I've been knowing Debo for met him at the Pro Bowl in 2021, I think 2022 or something like that. And we hit it off, man. We were hanging out all week. Uh really cool guy. I love the way he plays the game. I [snorts] think he's going to bring uh what he brung before to the team. That energy, that, you know, versatility. Um, hell of a pickup for us. >> Different team, but same outcome. You throw the ball up high, you go [clears throat] and get it. >> Yeah. >> Take us through that catch. And is that some How much of that do you work on with quarterbacks? Is it a timing thing or is it hey? >> It's a I mean I mean I'm I'm I'm 6'5 you know I got ability and uh you know I've done it throughout my career but it's a thing you just talk talk to the quarterbacks about like when I'm covered I'm still you know pretty open if you throw throw the ball up with some air and uh you know Brock threw a great ball. So I mean that's that's what I'm that's one of my biggest things in my in my game. >> Does he finding it hard to overthrow you? >> No I mean he he Brock is super accurate. He's a super accurate quarterback, so he he hasn't overthrown me yet. Um, it happens, but I mean, he's just super accurate. >> Couple more. >> Has anyone specifically like really bonded with you off the field so far since moving here? >> It's a It's a few guys. I mean, obviously Trent, but I've known Trent for so long now. Um, Dro Dro's cool. me and him actually, you know, we're close in age, played in the SEC, we have similar interests, so and then Christian Kirk, you know, I knew him since he was at&m. So, but there's a lot of guys that I've gotten to know and get along with. >> Mike, you talked about Brock's accuracy. What has stood out to you outside of his accuracy in these practices so far about his game that maybe you didn't know before you got here? >> Um, his attention to detail, his consistency, the way he comes to work, his first one on the field. Um he he's super smart. Um and he's quiet, but he he's a fun guy like to to be around. Like he likes talking about sports and life and you know movies and all the all those other things that I like. So that's been pretty cool. >> Mark, when you say you're covered, you're open. Obviously, >> now people believe you because you're Mike Evans, but I mean did it take a while? Like were you saying that as a rookie and people are like no that doesn't work? >> No. Um, I when I was in college, I I made a a living off of, you know, getting open, but, you know, just Johnny Manzel, me and him had a really great connection. He'll th give me jump balls and even when I'm covered, he'll throw it to me. And I've always used my frame. I think it comes from my basketball background. Like, I love to to box defenders out. And I love competing. So, competing for the ball, that's number one in my mind. Well, winning is number one in my mind, but then if I'm covered, there's elite DBs in the league. So, you got to be able to make contested grabs. Thanks, Mike. >> All right. Thank you. [music]

title: Raheem Morris and 49ers Players Address the Media Following Day 5 of Camp | 49ers
text: Mhm. >> Mhm. >> Afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. How you guys doing? >> William, what what um what happens in practice like today when you kind of run out of one specific position? >> You just keep going. And uh you do what you do in a game. You know, stuff happens in the game, you got to switch personnel groupings. Uh you got to be able to deviate off the schedule and off the script and plan and um be able to get the other guys out there and give them opportunities. Like nothing better than like that happening in these type of environments. You want to strain these guys into the point of uh where they can go, you know, take ourselves into deep water a little bit and find a way um to swim. And I think those are the things that we had to do today. Um I love this style of practice. I love the physicality of it all. I love the guys being able to fight through it and get all stuff that you want to get done today. Uh couldn't be more proud of how we accomplished that today. >> Early on in practice, it looked like you and Deebo were catching a having a nice conversation. Obviously, you probably can't get the details of it, but what is it like to have him there? If you can get the details. >> I've hated him so long. Um and it's so nice to to have him back in in the friendly atmosphere. But um you know, he's been one of those guys that's been a highly competitive guy in the National Football League that you got to deal with um no matter what the circumstances of the game is, what the situation is of the game, you got to be aware. Um he's the ultimate piece that can move around and um you have to game plan around because his ability to run the football, his ability to line up at receiver, his ability to take uh screens, his ability to do a bunch of different things on special teams, whether it be return man or whatever the case may be. Um he's so versatile and and we've used him so well in the Bay for so long um that you know, we were kind of catching up. Caught up yesterday, but it's always good to see him. You know, a face that's um familiar around this building and getting him back is uh is really cool. >> What are your memories of of facing him in two really kind of consequential games and at the end of the >> Let's just sum it up in this. I I don't know. I think it was 22. Um and uh he he caught this pass on us that we should have picked off and I think he took it for about 60. Uh and I think he was a free agent and he played every day that summer. I couldn't watch ESPN for the the entire summer cuz I'd get watching Deebo score a 60-yard touchdown on us. So, those are the biggest memories I got of him making big-time plays on us. And them finding ways to get him the ball on unique situations and um getting him the ball in space and we know what he can do in space. >> Raheem, the the rookie defensive tackles Thompson and Eason showing power and quickness and speed and all that in the one-on-ones. How do you see the D-tackle rotation behind Osa? Is it competitive? >> You know what? It is really is, you know. You got to go even. One of our guys is out right now. And then Haloti you know, he started off really well. You got C.J. West out there. You got a bunch of different guys. You know, got big AC coming back and then some of even the young guys, they really stepped up and did some really good things. So, it's nice to see those guys getting reps, getting opportunities. Um seeing them have to fight through days like this, you know, that's what the that's what uh the league is about, you know, fighting through days like this, finding a way to contribute. And those guys are all finding ways to be significant contributors in that room. And it'll play out you know, as we go further and further in the camp. >> Raheem, what is what is the level of concern when you have so few edge rushers available at the moment? >> It's hard to say level of concern. You know, you got Bosa out there. You got Ronald Hight. You know, Mycheal Williams coming back off injury. You know, they're going to all come back at some point. You know, you got you got Keion White out there. You got a bunch of different guys that can give you such a presence. And then you got different people that can provide different type of rushing mechanisms. When you're talking about Fred, you're talking about Greenlaw. You're talking about even the safety position with the guy like Tarik finding utilizing finding different ways to mix it up to get rush you know, pressure and things that you're able to do. Um it's hard to say concern. You know, it's it's more for me like you know, the chess pieces that can move around and and give you different tools and different things that can happen and how you work them. >> Does the film from practice capture the Trent Bosa doing their one-on-one thing on the side and do you get a chance to to watch them? >> You know, that's their one-person thing, you know, they those guys Bosa goes and gets them and he does his own work. You know, a lot of times he pulls Trent, he gets his one-on-one reps and things that he has to do and then he goes over with Bosa and kind of helps those guys and you know, when you see two vets like that working together, you kind of want to get away, you know, like let those guys do do what they do. Um that's what they great, whatever the the greatness that they're searching and the little intricate details that they're trying to get down over there, you know, let those guys go and do those things. So, those little private moments, I know they're right in front of you guys so they're not that private, but um >> [snorts] >> that's the things that they do. I kind of walk away when I see that kind of stuff. >> You mentioned that Teague, what are your impressions of him so far? >> You know, Teague and a lot a lot of the other safeties have been really impressive, you know, they've gotten hands on the balls, you know, having a chance to knock some passes down, doing much different things as far as covering, you know, watching these guys really gain grasp of the defense and really communicated at a very high level with Fred, you know, it's hard not to when you got those guys out there at the linebacker position doing what they do. Um to be able to read it right call and be able to communicate with those guys is really easy. So, I'm very impressed with the guys being able to pick it up and how much they love football. That that's that's the real cool part about this place. >> What about Deebo Samuel? He's known to be like very competitive. >> say that again. >> Deebo >> Deebo, okay. Everybody says his real name is so long, go ahead. >> Oh, yeah. Deebo, uh he's always he's known to be very competitive around the league, but then you see him out there really excited to go up against guys like Mike Evans a little bit today against Deebo Samuel. What have you seen from him, you know, especially in 11-on-11 drills but from the competitor that he is? >> You know, um Deebo's one of those guys that you talk about being highly competitive. So, when he's playing against Mike, you know, you know, gold jacket type of guy in practice and then you get back Deebo and we know what Deebo brings with the competitive as far as the competitive standpoint, you know, along with the D Rob, so along with the you know, all the other wide outs that we got, the young strimblings. So, it's a bunch of different guys out there that provide different challenges and like I really love how he's accepting it and he's going out there trying to find out his spots, you know, picking his spots to play really aggressive, picking his spots to play, you know, really smart, picking his spots to be able to utilize his help, uh being able to understand a defense at a very high level. I mean, is is all really competitive for him on the grass, but it's just as competitive for him inside the grass, you know, like it it seems simple for those guys, but they got little moments that they can pick. And I love how they're picking those moments, you know, him and Ronaldo has really, you know, stood out in that way, um to be able to go find him and Jack Jack Jack as well, being able to go find those moments. I mean, Luder, I mean, a bunch of different guys have made some plays. So, it's like they're finding those moments and those places where they can make plays, and it's really cool to watch. >> Raheem, given your history and background, uh if Aaron Donald does come back, would you say he could be Aaron Donald again? >> Um you know, it's Aaron Donald. Those kind of guys are what they are, and they can do whatever they put their mind to. You know, they got those different mentalities, those different people. Uh we all know those people in sports, you know, I think we talk about all the time like Kobe Bryant, you know, those Michael Jordans, those Aaron Donalds, those those people like that, you know. That's a different conversation. >> Did you counsel him to stay retired if you could? >> You know, I'm not going to counsel him to do anything, you know, you can counsel him to stay retired, and he may come back just to spite you. So, um you know, I'm sure Aaron's a he is a grown man, and he's going to make a grown man decision, whatever it is, um whatever he decides to make it. >> How was I said to you guys he was acclimation back to the defense? >> He's been fun to watch, you know, it's been fun to watch him come in and then really, um the first thing I noticed is was his routine, you know, his daily routine and how hard he works and how much he does for himself to keep himself ready to go. Um so, those are the nosy moments you have as a coach where you can ask those things, man. When did it start, you know, and he just talked about his history and, you know, growing up and, you know, having a brother that played as well and being able to adapt some of those things from different people in the place that he's been and watching him go through his process and how long he's able to be in the building. Um his mental stamina to to stay within the framework of what we're doing and to figure out how good he can be. Um I really appreciate that about him. So, like his presence being graced upon us in the building with um you know great smile, great energy. Person that loves football and really comfortable with himself. Like that those are all really great qualities to bring to a different team. >> Coach, how would you evaluate Jaylen D'Aguilar so far through camp and where is he at in his development? >> He's doing great. Young man has really stepped up on special teams, you know, showing his ability to contribute immediately, you know, you know, everybody special teams kind of a proving ground. And when you go out there and you show physicality out there that really helps us. So like, you know, when Bryant and Kittle and those guys give those guys kind of those kind of credits and then that gives them the ability to get out there and play even more defense and get more confidence, you know, watching them grow every single day and learn from every single, you know, I can't say mistake but correction, you know, like whatever that correction is I think it's always something that's fun when you talk about those younger players and he's, you know, within his room there's not a lot of talking I have to do to him, you know, he's got Fred and Greenlaw who are players in that room along with guys like Warner and Tatum that have been in this system and been been in this system and been around those guys and how to prepare. And then the coaches in that room, talking about Johnny Holland and K.J. Wright, you know, guys played a long time, they both played in the league, they both coached a long time. Well, Johnny's coached a long time and he's got a bunch of knowledge that he's able to get and acquire every single day and he's eating it all up. >> How would you make Renardo was was saying the other day that Renardo was saying the other day he felt like you have done a good job of kind of stripping things down to to so that they can play fast, simplifying things enough that it's more digestible. Can you just explain like what what he what he might mean by that? Like what what are some of the methods you use to to try to do that to make >> It's hard to say without giving away all Renardo's secrets but it's like uh you know, like having such a DB background it's like you able to relate to those guys and and what's important and then it's like trying to find ways that they can take shots and have opportunities to make plays. You know, this whole league is based on those guys making plays, you know, like nobody cares if you go out there and cover a guy and they don't get a catch, they care about what the significance of the plays that you made were. And he's found ways to make significant plays throughout camp and throughout the off-season and like he's growing every single day as he learn and his communication with his safeties and what he should be and how he should be and what he should look like. I think those things have all gotten better for him and like uh you know, that's probably what he's talking about, you know, and it's like being able to give him those details and be able to talk to him and coach those guys and again, he has another big-time veteran in his room and Jerry Gray that's played a lot of football. He's caught a lot of interceptions in this league. Um he's coached a lot of really great DBs and he's able to get it from, you know, everybody, all walks of life from within this building. You know, Ray Brown, he's got I mean he's got a ton of coaches in there and and and I'm only a contributor to be able to help those guys. >> Was there something you you saw with him either either on tape or even in your conversations with him where maybe he was he was overthinking or there's something that did need to to strip it down a little bit? >> less about that. It was more about my evaluation from college, what I knew about him and who he could be. Um it was kind of a relationship that he had with Jalen Ramsey, obviously being a Florida State guy. Um it was obviously one of those immediate relationships that was able to help me, you know, really, you know, get in with him. Um before even going dark about anything that went wrong um within the past year. I mean that's the corners position, right? There's only two positions in the National Football League that get all the criticisms, tackles and corners. It is what it is. That's the life we chose. And it's like you got to find a way to ignore the noise and find a way to be the best version of yourself every day. >> Raheem, yesterday in practice, Fred and Jalen had aggressive moments. Um given the fact they're veterans and and they've done this all the time, is it necessary to like give them a protect your teammates message or do you like a bit of that edge or or like how do you handle situations like that? >> That's that's a part of that's a part of us, right? We always talk about protecting the team. That's something that we talk about every single day, whether it's in the defensive unit rooms, whether it's in our team meetings, whether it's in our position rooms, that's a major part of what we do. And and you always get tempers to flare and when you're talking to those adults, it's easy to be really critical and hard on those guys about what it we want it to look like. And they know what we want it to look like. They you could tell by their body language after we even when it happens.
