I told Fred the other day, you know, he's starting to fight in practice and he's walking off the field and he's kissing every baby that's in sight. I'm like, you are the ultimate guy. Um and then they're very correctable moments that gives your your head coach an opportunity to go in there talk to the very best players in your football team every day and correct those things. And when people see that, um that gives great examples. So, like it's always good. You don't want them. You you you wish they would do it right away, but if that was the case, they wouldn't need us. And that's what we're here for. >> You You There's a lot of players in this league that really like playing for you. And when you when you lose a defensive end, does a guy like Leonard Floyd blow up your phone? And you've had him a couple times. What has he done for your defense in the past? >> Um Leonard Floyd is a is a phenomenal football player. He's a great He's He's even a better human. Um and he's the kind of high-quality guy that you always want to be around. Um but, you know, it's not that he blows up my phone. That mean the the those things all happen within the the workings of of our group upstairs. And you know, obviously, um you're always going to have the input. You're always going to have a say. You know, they're always going to come to you and be very, you know, ask the questions, ask the things. And Leonard's been here, so we know what he's about. Uh we know what those kind of guys are about. So, like it's, you know, those things could possibly happen. You never know. Like you always keep guys that are on short lists. There's things that happen all the time. We got great people in place to do those things, R.J. and, you know, Josh and all those guys in that personnel department that are constantly looking every single day. You You got a lot of credit and a lot of lot of respect for those guys. >> How was uh Nick Martin doing? And you're talking about Fred and and Dre as being on the field, not just in that room, but on the field as the third linebacker with them, something that's really speed up his development. >> the pads came on yesterday and he really showed up, you know. Had one of his better days yesterday with his pads. You know, you could see the the ability to run around and be physical and hit. Um you can see on his explosion. You can see the things where he drives. You see a lot of the traits. And he's continued to grow every single day. So, being out there with those two guys won't hurt. I can tell you that much. Um so, having the ability to get him out there and compete at a very high level. Um that's what you want. You want highly competitive spots, highly competitive people at all those spots going out there competing at a a big-time level. >> Anything else guys? All right. >> All right, guys. >> Welcome back. When you when you're when you're going through the process of kind of figuring out what was next for you, how would how much was a a return here kind of on your mind and what made it happen? >> Um you know, ever since last year like I said me, Kyle, John, we always had those conversations whether I was here, whether I was there, but the bond never left for sure. >> You were chatting all season. A lot of people made comments about how good you looked in the off season workouts. Was there anything different, any attention to detail or something different coming back this season or how was that off season training for you? >> Uh it was a little different. As I stated I I started a YouTube or whatever, but um it's just like different. It was my first time being a free agent, so it was just like a long process. It was frustrating, it was hard, but I had good people in my corner for us the guys that I grew up with, a couple other people, but you know, it's like head down and just get to work and just whatever happens, happens. >> Given that is there any different different feeling being back in the building after that type of stuff? >> Um I wouldn't say it was different. It kind of felt like I I didn't even go nowhere to be honest. When I when I got back I was just like, well, I know what's going on. I know the people here. Staff still the same, so it's kind of like the same for real. >> How did you enjoy your year in Washington and and how would the organizations differ from one another? >> I'm not going to compare organizations, but I had a good time over there. >> Did did Kyle reach out to you after his accident? How did you hear about it and just what was it like seeing him again when he got back? >> heard about it as soon as you guys did. But you know when it came out I kind of talked to him and he was kind of normal with me. >> I saw you chatting with Mike Evans today. What are those conversations like and what is it like coming back into a room that looks a little bit different? >> It was kind of different. You know when I left the guys that was here. But I met Mike and at Pro Bowl and you know he was in Tampa doing his thing. He'd been doing it for a long time but the conversations we was having out there was just like you know just regular conversation really not about balls just getting ready for practice. >> Lynch mentioned that he'd been talking with you and your representation for about a month. What was it that tipped the scales to bring you back? [clears throat] >> You know you know my agent and John do a good job and the side conversations with me John and Kyle is just like always kind of been the same. It was just a matter of time before it happened. >> You're You've been You're pretty tight with Ricky when Ricky came in as a rookie. Just your thoughts on on him right now as he's heading out to surgery and >> Yeah kind of been tight with him. He was in Arizona I was in Arizona. Kind of haven't lost a beat since since last year when I left. We still stayed in communication and I kind of talked to him the night whenever he got the news and he was a little frustrated. I was like bro just keep your head up man your time's coming. It's just like he's kind of had bad luck right now. It's like really nothing he can do about it but overall you know he's shown what he's capable of when he's healthy and you know wish him well in surgery and a quick recovery for sure. >> He said that he hated going up against you. I saw you guys having a conversation out there. What was that conversation like and now that you guys are I guess on the same side what's different about that? >> You know he got a really good scheme. He was joking yesterday. He was like man I'm so glad I ain't got to go against you this that and the third. I was like you know I'm kind of glad you one of my coaches as well. So it's kind of like that that kind of relationship is going to build. We was always been opponents but now we on the same side, so we will continue to build from there. >> You know, what was the reaction like from your teammates when you finally showed up in the locker room? >> Um I was in the locker room yesterday, so I kind of seen them all. kind of like I stated before is like felt like I never left. Um they was happy, I was happy, we just ready to get the ball rolling. >> Is there is there like a part of you that has feels like you have something to prove still? I know you always kind of carry a chip on your shoulder anyway, but given the way maybe the last few years have gone for you, do you feel like you have an additional motivation? >> I mean I'm continue to be myself whenever the opportunity presents itself, I'm ready for it. >> Did you volunteer the number or was there a transaction there? >> That was a you know, it was a little transaction, you know, we made it happen. >> You know, this is somewhat unique situation. I know I mean you were you twice requested trades to leave here. Um but obviously whatever happened, you know, there was it didn't create bad blood or you know, bad feelings. How is it that you guys, you, John, Kyle still have maintained such a strong relationship through everything? >> I mean contract negotiations is contract negotiations and then those are conversations for John, Kyle, and my agent to have, but our relationship has never um changed or had a fallout. So I mean that was just like contract negotiations that I'm not in control of. >> You were involved really quickly in the offense today. Was that the plan? Were you ready for that? yesterday it was like let's see where you at, let's see you know, how you feel. So I did a workout yesterday um yesterday night or whatever and then they was like all right, we're going to give you eight to 10 plays today and just see how it goes and just going to keep building from there. >> You had a few teammates who said they were offered up their guest houses for you on social media. Any Did you take them up on any yet? >> Uh no. >> Do you feel like your role in this offense will be similar to your first six seasons with the Niners? >> I have no idea. We're just going to roll with the punches. >> On a not so serious you and Trent, usually the two guys up front with the blue boxes, are they coming back? >> Um, they used it when I was gone, so I mean, hey, we we still got to rock out. >> All right, guy. Appreciate you both. >> Yep. >> [sighs] >> How we doing? >> Dre, we asked you this in the off season, but now that you're in training camp, Fred talked about it earlier this week. How good does it kind of feel back out there? And it kind of seems like you guys set the tone for the energy level, especially in that group. >> Yeah, man, it just feels unbelievable, honestly. Like, just being next to Ford, uh, 5-4, uh, you know he going control the defense, you know he going to have you in the right place, and you know, uh, yeah, it just feels like old times, man. Just you just running around having fun, just enjoying every day, just bringing that juice, and getting the best out of each other, and I mean, yeah, it just it it feels great. >> Dre, in the spring you you talked about just kind of what what made you want to come back here. With Deebo coming back now, too, I know it's only been like 24 hours right? Have you guys had a chance to to talk about like, "Hey, you know, the pull of of coming back and playing for this organization again?" >> Uh, yeah, I mean, I reached out to him a little bit, you know, during his free agency time, and just, you know, just kind of say, "Hey, man, you know, come on back, man. Like, you know what I'm saying? Like, let's have a reunion. Let's let's let's do this thing together, bro." I mean, he he knows like it ain't no place like San Fran. I mean, you can go, I mean, just talking to a bunch of different guys, and, you know, getting their experience at different places, uh, and then just, you know, for myself, uh, just the coaches, the the people in the building, uh, the the players, the leadership that we got on this team, uh, just that that warm feeling that you get that it's just it's time for battle, and that's the only thing that matters, and, uh, this place is just about football, and I mean, if you're a football player, you love that. And, uh, and just to have the the right group of guys around you, uh, that that wants the same thing, and that that that got that same motivation, man, uh, it's it's a just unbelievable feeling, unbelievable place, and, uh, I know that's what he he wants, too. I know Deebo's a football player as well, and, uh, you know, sometimes you got to go and you know, see you know, what's out there, but you know, once you go, you realize, hey, ain't nothing like ain't nothing like San Fran. >> What's the reaction like in the locker room when when Deebo comes back in? >> Oh, man, it's huge. I mean, he's he's the juice of the offense. He's the He's the thing that keep that the offense going, you know, when they need a spark. So, just knowing that he's going to be back on our side, man, it just give you all the confidence in the world that, you know, that we can get this done this year, and uh yeah, I mean, I'm excited for him. >> We asked Deebo about you and you coming back, and he's like, "We got our bully back." How when you hear that, how does that make you feel? >> Man, I just I'm just happy to be accepted by the guys, really, honestly. Uh you know, just leaving and coming back, you don't know how, you know, things are going to be, but, you know, the to to hear some of the guys and to hear that how they accept you back, and you know, they just want you to be you. I mean, that's all I could ask for. I mean, I remember telling you guys, I'm not going to be you know, more than what I am, you know, what I bring to the table, which is just being me, you know what I mean, having fun and go out there and play play football the way that I do. So, you know, just to get that type of, you know, respect and you know, from your teammates, and you know, that that type of welcome, man, it just it makes you makes you feel good. >> You were here You were here when the defense was, you know, pretty similar as it has been over the last few years, and then you have Raheem Morris coming in adding some versatility. What has that transition been like, those adjustments he's made, and what do you like about this? >> Yeah, I think it's going to be great for us. It'll kind of allows us to, you know, just tighten things up and just not give the offense, you know, something to look at every time and know, you know, kind of where we're at a little bit. Uh although, you know, in the past, you know, we've played our defense, and uh it's bread and butter, you know, like the back of our hand, but uh it's going to be a good change-up to kind of, you know, keep teams guessing, and then, you know, uh just being able to interchange between those two, I mean, it's going to be you just don't know where it's going to be coming from. And you know, it kind of reminds me a lot of the Denver defense in a way uh with the five down stuff, but you know, we still got our bread and butter on what we like to do with our four four down. >> Dre, after the little bit of scrimmage yesterday, was there any self-regulating talk amongst the defense, or did anyone talk to you guys, or you just have to >> Oh, no, we ain't got to talk. No, it's uh man, one thing about us, like this team is just like it's all love. Like, you know what I mean? Like tempers rise, this and that and that, and things flare up, but it's all love in the building. Like, you know, I respect more 23 more than anybody, man. I told him when we first came in, bro, like, you know, you my favorite player. Like, I told him that. Like, he he knows that. And uh you know, obviously all the guys that he didn't play with, Luke Kuechly and Thomas Davis and all them. So, I was telling him like, bro, I've been watching you since you came in. So, you know, just to get that honor, you know, back in what, '21, '22, '21 when he came? Uh but yeah, no, like sometimes you got to get get it going a little bit, man. You got to get them juiced up, man. So, uh yeah, man, if you know, you want to throw a ball to get them going or whatever you got to do, hey, do it. So, you know, whatever whatever we got to do to get things rolling, man. So, I mean, it's it's all love. It's just football at the end of the day. >> What's your thought process in that moment, though? Like, you cuz you didn't retaliate. Was it just like, oh, you got one, I got one, we're good here? What what what's your What are you thinking? >> honestly, my process was like, you better not touch 23. >> [laughter] >> Or you might not be on this team. So, uh but you know, I think it was a play before where he kind of I kind of got rolled up on him a little bit. And I was like, damn. So, you know, but then naturally, they catch the ball. He caught a ball on me, the five-yard ball, and I and I pushed him out of bounds. Think he thought it was worse than what it was, but I mean, at the end of the day, um yeah, my first initial reaction was I mean, I was happy he did it because it just shows like he got that fire in him. And that's what I like. I mean, I don't like that fire. So, uh yeah, like it just gets everything and everybody going, man. So, but yeah, I knew I knew don't touch 23. >> To be clear, to be clear, you and Fred were not sent to the principal's office after practice. >> Oh, no, no, no, no, no, no. But yeah, you still lesson learned though, you know, it's it's it's you know, it's just lesson learned at the end of the day. But no, no, I mean no. >> Is that Is that fully labeled that Lenoir talked about? Is that accurate? Do you find that accurate or do you find T takes exception to it? >> A bully? I don't think I'm a bully. I mean, you can call it whatever you want on the field, but uh I don't know. I just when I I don't know what to call it, you know, if that's what they want to call it, but I'm definitely not a bully like off the field though. I don't try to like be that try to give that like representation of who I am as a person cuz that's not me at all. I love everybody. I love everybody to better love. Just coming in the building and working and getting a chance to be with my teammates. Uh but when them pads come on, uh I mean, ain't whoever on the other side of the ball got to get it, so. >> Fred, they say game recognizes game. What do you think of Nick Martin so far? >> Yeah, baller for sure. Uh just got all tools that he need, the speed, um just the instincts, uh playmaking ability, uh you know, just young and still, you know, need reps and just need, you know, time to just continue to grow, but he definitely is going to be a person that I feel like that's going to make a impact in this league sooner or later. And uh yeah, it's been great to work beside him, to work uh to see how he gotten better, you know, just from his last year to this year. And uh just to see his growth and how it's going to take off. I mean, it's like I mean, he's going to be that linebacker that we're going to be counting on, you know, to come in and you know, maybe be the fever backer to be on the edge or he may, you know, be dropping or whatever it may be, but we're going to count on him a lot of ways uh to help contribute. And I know he's going to make a impact for us. >> John Lynch compared Nick Martin to you last year when they when they drafted him. Do you see any similarities at all between the two of you either in style or character? Like anything that's that's stood out? >> Uh you know, for sure. I think that you know, he's kind of more of a uh he's just more quiet and conservative to himself a little bit and I mean I think I might that in a way. It depends on you know, if you get me riled up or not, but I haven't seen him too riled up. Yesterday he was talking after a couple of hits and I was hearing him and I was loving it. And I was like, "Okay, I hear you out there 45, you know what I'm saying?" And he was getting juiced up. So, I think it's going to come with time the more he plays here and make them more confident he get, the more you going to hear from 45. So, yeah, I do see myself in a lot of ways just you know, the way he played. You know, he's he's a fast player uh and then once he knows that he's he's very instinctive. So, uh he's going he's going to make a big impact for us. >> It seems like the uh defensive backs are off to a good start this camp. What are your impressions of the guys behind you so far? >> Oh yeah, man. They look good back there. You know, just coming in, it's a lot more guys that are just just ready all across the board. You know, young guys, you know, obviously having Jayir and uh singles back there. You know, he's he's still young as well, but uh you know, and Mustapha he's a little down right now, but uh yeah, I mean it's just a bunch of guys depth at all across the board. You know what I mean? Now you don't I feel you know, the last few past years, you know, you get one guy in the back end down then you know, it was it was a struggle especially I remember that 20 what 2020 year. I mean it was struggle. The deep balls everywhere, but now you know, you just got confidence that you know, the guys the backup guys going to come in and they going to hold it down and you know, these young guys that's getting these vital reps and got those reps last year, they going to be just that much better than they were. So, uh I mean it's only going to get better for the back end. >> What have you seen from K.J. Wright as your coach this year? >> Yeah, I mean, KJ he's he's he's an alpha dog for sure. Uh you know, just he brings good juice to the team, man. He he uh he just let us be ourselves, too. You know what I mean? He he knows how to play football. He know what it, you know, what it feels like to be on that field between those lines and, you know, how things can get carried away. We was actually just watching some tape with him, you know, and just being up on the Sea- uh it wasn't Seattle, it was Green Bay. Uh uh but we that's what you don't do though. He's telling us what you don't do, but he uh right. But uh yeah, I mean, it's just, you know, he's one of the guys, honestly. He's one of the guys, but he's a he's a leader, too, as well, and uh just got so much respect for him, even, you know, obviously as he being my coach, but even before he was my coach, like you know what I mean? But him and Bobby, like watching them go to work and then like yeah, just those battles that we had with Seattle and then, you know, now he's the coach, so he just knows that he know we know that he know what he doing and yeah, I mean, the more every day he come in, he just gets you can just tell his confidence is just growing and uh he's understanding the game plan. Just we all picking up, you know, a little bit of a new game plan, so, you know, the more you understand it, he's understanding it more and more and we all are together. And that's what makes it so special and so fun is that, you know, we just we're all in this thing together. >> You know, you've been through so much, you know, health-wise since the Super Bowl. is right now I mean, everyone's like, you know, is the healthiest I've ever felt, right? But you know, is there something to that with you? Like where you are as as far as your body? I mean, have you felt this good in a in a while? >> Uh I haven't, actually. That's funny, man. I haven't felt this good since uh about a month before the Super Bowl, you know, even that whole time I was dealing with Achilles, Achilles, Achilles. Then you finally get a little healthy last or the year after the Super Bowl, you know, just enough to play and then second game you do your calf and go in the off-season, go into the Broncos, you thinking, "Okay, this is the year that I'm going to, you you make it happen." And the second day you go and you pull your quad off the bone. So, I mean, it's been just after one after another, one after another another. And I just been playing catch up the whole time. But now, um you know, I just feel like I'm where I need to be now as far as just, you know, body health-wise, everything. Uh and I know I got the best people in the world going to take care of me. And, you know, I ain't got to go out there and do more. I ain't got to go prove it to nobody. I ain't got to do this. I got to go play football still. But, uh I don't have to go out there and and and overdo it to try to, you know, to prove to them that I'm a football player or who I am as a person. You know what I'm saying? So, uh I think that's going That's going to help a lot. >> Given the quad injury you have >> experience and having to recover from so many in a short amount of time, I mean, you would think that somebody like Ricky could learn a lot from someone like you. Is Is Is that a conversation that maybe has been had or maybe you reached out and talked to him or a conversation that you guys are planning on having given, you know, him maybe being a little down on his circumstances right now. >> No, for sure. I definitely have talked to Ricky uh plenty of times, you know, since, you know, everything came out about the knee and stuff like that. And I'm just let him know like like, "Bro, like you he got hell of talent. Like he he he can play ball. Like bro can run. He can run routes. Like he Ricky is that guy." Uh it's just going to take Ricky some time. Like he got to give him some time to heal and, you know, to take care of his body and do what's best for Ricky. And uh Ricky going to play for this in this league for a long time. And uh I know it sucks just not being able to get going. I kind of like the way it's kind of starting for him. It's kind of how the last 2 years has been for me. But, uh man, at the end of the day, you got to enjoy it as much as possible. Enjoy every day. You never know when your last day is going to be on on this field. You know what I mean? So, every day you go out, you got to bring just that juice, that that gratitude, man. Everything because you just you just never know, man. So, you know, I I I've talked to him and just encouraged him like, "Hey, man, like bro, this it sucks now, but I'm trying to tell you, bro, just like keep doing what you're doing, keep, you know, just keep pushing yourself, keep getting better, you know, obviously you got to heal up, but, you know, just keep doing the little things right, man, and uh and most importantly, man, stay faithful to God, man, and all that it's going it's going to take care of itself. It always has, so and I believe that. >> When you mentioned that the quad injury, was that a particularly low moment? I mean, just being in a team, you want to prove yourself and um reward their trust and all that stuff. Uh I guess when you think about the last 2 years, I mean, where where does that fit as far as kind of Sorry, not a cheery question, but what low moments for you? >> No, it definitely was a real, real low moment, man, because you just, you know, you you're just excited to go and and prove to them what you can do and all the things that, you know, who they say you are that you are and um I mean, it just once it once I hit got the quad, you know, it was just and they tried their best to support me uh through the process and stuff, but uh you know, it just wasn't healing the right way. Like normally pretty easy with healing. Like my body heals pretty fast and uh I just remember with this quad like sitting there working every day and grinding and like soon as I go out and take off super fast, like it'd pop again. So, I'm just dealing with it, you know, even when we came here for training camp, uh and yeah, I mean, I remember coming here for training camp, but just obviously feeling just shitty because I and then uh yeah, I mean, went out there before the game started and got running and ended up messing it up again. So, it just it was just an ongoing thing that I just really needed rest from and uh but yeah, it was it was definitely a low moment, man, because you just know that you were just like just not hurting the team, but, you know, you're just giving them the narrative the narrative that they want, you know what I mean? That, you know, he injury prone and can't do this and can't do that. So, uh yeah, it sucks, man. Went definitely through a depression, man, but yeah, like I'm thankful for the guys here though. Like, you know, Fred, talking to Fred, talking to Z, those were the guys that they really helped me get out of that situation and that depression for sure. >> Last one. >> Were you as curious as anyone about this power plant conspiracy theory on the injuries? >> Yeah, I was. I was like, "Man, what the heck going on over here?" >> yeah, I mean, I don't I mean, I don't really know. Like, I grew up playing ball football on concrete. So, I mean, I don't I don't I don't look into that. I don't even look into the field situation. Like, you know, as long as we got a field to play on, I don't care if it's grass or turf. So, I'm not really the one to kind of like yeah. But, I was interested. I was like, "Shit, you got to look into it now. It's maybe something there." But, hey, you never know. >> Thanks, Dre.

title: Chris Foerster and 49ers Players Address the Media Following Day 4 of Camp | 49ers
text: Uh very happy with both guys. They really are out there working hard. They're doing a good good job. Um you know, we drafted Cruz to be able to compete inside the way things are. He's staying at tackle right now, which he's doing a nice job at tackle, but he's always going to have that tackle guard flex. We just haven't gone there yet. Uh and and and Carver Willis has done a really nice job. We're training him at cross trainin him at center as well. Uh so he'll have some good competition here at left guard and center uh or backup center type position right now. So I'm real happy with both their development. They're both very, very good rookies. They work really hard. They pick things up very well. You could tell when they weren't here, they studied a lot. Very professional, hardworking guys. >> What do you like about the addition of Josiah Dwara? >> The what? >> Josiah Dwara. The addition there. >> I I missed the question. >> Oh, the new tight end. Yeah. Just seeing him just first impressions are solid. He's doing a good job. >> Your evaluation on the one-on-one line drills and how that went, whether you guys got the better of the defense today or >> Well, defense always gets the better. I'm going to give them the credit. They always get the better of the offensive line. First day of one-on- ones is great. It's a great drill. People say it's unrealistic and to a degree it is, but it really is. It's hard drill for the offensive lineman. Um, a lot of guys, like I've said before, it's a it gets evaluated heavily. And the problem is a lot of times offensive lineman, defensive line are working on things. There's things this is the best time to work on it because there's not the risk when if somebody's working on an inside move, you're not worried about running into the rest of the offensive line in a team period. So, they'll work on inside move. Or if I have an offensive lineman, he tries something and misses every time to us. Oh, shoot. He missed three one-on- ones. Yeah. He's he's working on something that he really needs to work on and that's the best place to work on it. But defensive line did a wonderful job today. We had a couple good good reps in there. But always were if we win a day it's far and few between. >> You can al see Trent Bosa off to the side doing their own thing for a few. >> Yeah, Nick needed to get some work not in the live setting. So yeah, they looked good over there. They're working hard. Do >> you have any sense uh how long Jordan James will be out with that rib injury? >> I I don't do we have a a total time on it? We said we haven't given the time on it yet. So he'll be back as soon as he can with the rib. A lot of times it's tolerate. Sometimes it heals faster or slower. So I think it's hard to put a definite time frame on it. >> Result of a a punch out. >> It was it was a combination of the punch out isn't going to do it. There's a punch out with a spin. It's one of those perfect storms. You punch out, you hit the ball. They don't miss the ball very much. But if all of a sudden when he goes to hit the ball, you move all of a sudden something else is there. And I think he saw the punch coming. There was time to see it. So he tried to do something to make it miss. I think that's what caused the punch. I think that's what caused it to happen. Chris, I heard you the other day say that Kyle told you, "Hey, if you want to do something, do it. Otherwise, delegate." How often have you found yourself kind of doing kind of the things [snorts] as you wanted? How much have you delegated? How's that gone? >> There's little things here and there. Today, we had a team meeting. I ran a team meeting. Um, I was on, you know, protect the team, don't get in fights. I did a great job with that one. Right. Okay, [laughter] Joe. But yeah, but we're definitely doing but but for the most part like postpractice like the other day I let um let special teams coach take a breakdown and he gave an outstanding 30 minute 30 second speech just 30 seconds on leadership and and commitment and things like it was outstanding to let somebody else talk and you know usually Cal breaks him down and picks a player to say something. So I'm just alternating between me pulling up and saying hey practice was good it could be a little bit better tomorrow let's stay off the ground hey demo break us down let somebody else have a chance they probably won't get that chance again to say it. So, we've been doing that and when when it's appropriate to have the team meeting, which there's often times like I feel it will be maybe maybe tomorrow we'll be or maybe we it's better handled individually. Um, so that it's a little bit of freedom that way, but I've been doing um a little bit of both. Just a little bit of both still. >> You know, you say you don't like fights, but I mean the whole thing is a fight. Would would you would you rather have a team that fights too much or a team that doesn't fight at all? >> Some of the most physical teams I've been on never fought fought in practice. some of the the greatest defenses in Tampa, there was no fighting allowed or if you fight, you're thrown out of a game. So, it's an to me, you don't need to prove you're a tough guy. You want to prove you're tough guy, block better, play the play the defense better. Play your tech techniques better. When somebody talks crap, wait till the next play to make them pay for it within the within the structure of the rules of the game. Stepping outside the rules of the game to do anything, whether it be holding, fighting, pass interferences, all those things. They're not there's no place for them because you got to practice the practice like you're going to play the games. If I have a drill that doesn't match game, what am I doing? I'm wasting time. If I'm practicing, unlike game reps, that I'm wasting time. Fights are a waste of time and energy. Absolute waste of time or energy. One of my favorite fight stories. Did I tell you a fight story? My favorite fight stories was there's a there's a guy over a rookie left guard got a fight over here. They're fighting over by this. They get to fight him and a a linebacker in a fight over here. Pretty soon, like we saw today, the whole team's down there, right? And I'm running the film back and stand over by the water jug. He's the only guy over there by himself was the guy that started the fight. The whole team's fighting over there and he stand over there drinking water. I'm thinking to myself, "Hey, what are you doing? You started fight me. Jonathan Ogden was in there throwing blows with Ray Lewis and this slap rookie over here drinking water." I said, "You started the whole fight in practice." And uh so that fighting can get out of hand, right? Like I say, he's not even fighting anymore and everybody else is invested in it. >> Think that's a good place to stop. >> Thanks, guys. How's your chemistry been with Rock and how's the adjustment been with I'll say it's been pretty good so far. We've gotten a lot of work in in the short amount of time that, you know, we've been teammates, but uh it's been good. It's getting better every day. >> People here would say this was hot today. Do you laugh at that and say, >> I swear Coach Hank said it was a hot day. Oh, hell no. It's a perfect day. I'll take this day every day. >> Great. >> Maybe this is a stupid question. Um, I don't mean to like, oh, you're an old man or anything, but I mean at this point in your career, I mean, is it nice to get out [clears throat] of that humidity? I mean, is there anything to that of not, you know, spending? >> Absolutely. I mean, it's a it's definitely a bonus in being here. Um, I didn't really think about it too much until I got out here during OTAAS and I felt the the weather and it's it's a big difference. So, it's a it's a huge bonus for me to be here in this in this type of weather. In that same vein, in the spring, George said that when when he was kind of pitching you, one of the things that that you lit up at was the lie flat seats on on traveling. Uh, was that was that something that actually I mean, I I know it's not that the thing that's going to swing, but like was that something that was an issue for you? And how much >> the plane situation wasn't like a big selling thing for me? Um, >> but I'm excited for that. And, you know, when we travel, I'm sure that'll help, you know, our backs out and and our our legs for sure. As a tall guy, has that is that is that an issue for you? >> I love the planes that that lay back and you get to relax and sleep on them. I love those type of planes for sure. >> Weather and travel aside, being with one team your whole career and now starting here, what is the biggest adjustment of coming to work? >> Just getting to know everybody. Honestly, in Tampa, I knew everybody in the front office, in the building, kitchen staff. I knew everybody. And now I'm trying to I like that environment at work, knowing everybody that I'm I come in contact with. So, just getting used to everybody and and knowing their names and stuff like that. >> Mike, it's a young room with a lot of young receivers. Are any of those young guys standing out to you? >> I mean, Stri Strib's having a he had a really good off season at OTAAS and he's he's continued that during training camp, but all of them are really getting after it. I mean, this is a hungry group of guys. We look forward to showing that we're one of the best receiver rooms in the league. you get a sense that a lot of the guys not only in your room but the guys you're going up against the the DBs have wanted to talk to you and kind of get a sense for your tricks and like just kind of >> a lot of guys have been you know picking my brain on you know how my longevity you know how I've been able to make plays consistently and things like that and in turn I I asked the other guys older guys the same thing Trent Juice KD all those guys that have been in the league a long time um how that How what do they do to, you know, stay fresh and and play so long? >> Do you know Debo from before at all? And have you seen him in here? Just what what does that mean to a team to bring him back? >> Yeah, Debo's my guy. I've been knowing Debo for met him at the Pro Bowl in 2021, I think 2022 or something like that. And we hit it off, man. We were hanging out all week. Uh really cool guy. I love the way he plays the game. I think he's going to bring uh what he brung before to the team. That energy, that, you know, versatility. Um, hell of a pickup for us. >> Different team, but same outcome. Throw the ball up high, you go and get it. >> Yeah. >> Take us through that catch. And is that some How much of that do you work on with quarterbacks? Is it a timing thing or is it hey? >> It's a I mean I mean I'm I'm 6'5 you know I got ability and u you know I've done it throughout my career but it's a thing you just talk talk to the quarterbacks about like when I'm covered I'm still you know pretty open if you throw throw the ball up with some air and uh you know Brock threw a great ball. So I mean that's that's what I'm that's one of my biggest things in my in my game. >> Is he finding it hard to overthrow you? >> No I mean he he Brock is super accurate. He's a super accurate quarterback, so he he hasn't overthrown me yet. Um, it happens, but I mean, he's just super accurate. >> Couple more. >> Has anyone specifically like really bonded with you off the field so far since moving here? >> It's it's a few guys. I mean, obviously Trent, but I've known Trent for so long now. Um, Dro Dro's cool. Well, me and him actually, you know, we're close in age, played in the SEC, we have similar interests. So, and then Christian Kirk, you know, I knew him since he was at&m. So, but there's a lot of guys that I've gotten to know and get along with. >> Mike, you talked about Brock's accuracy. What has stood out to you outside of his accuracy in these practices so far about his game that maybe you didn't know before you got here? >> Um, his attention to detail, his consistency, the way he comes to work, his first one on the field. Um he he's super smart. Um and he's quiet, but he he's a fun guy like to to be around. Like he likes talking about sports and life and you know movies and all the all those other things that I like. So that's been pretty cool. >> Mark, when you say you're covered, you're open. Obviously people believe you because you're Mike Evans, but I mean did it take a while? Like were you saying that as a rookie and people are like no that doesn't work? >> No. Um, I when I was in college, I I made a a living off of, you know, getting open, but you know, just Johnny Manzel, me and him had a really great connection. He'll th give me jump balls and even when I'm covered, he'll throw it to me. And I've always used my frame. I think it comes from my basketball background. Like, I love to to box defenders out. And I love competing. So, competing for the ball, that's number one in my mind. Well, winning is number one in my mind, but then if I'm covered, there's elite DBs in the league. So, you got to be able to make contested grabs. Thank you. found to be kind of the biggest obstacles or the biggest challenges in coming to your first training camp here? >> Moving my stuff. It's football, you know what I mean? Uh, schedule's a little different, but they do a good job taking care of our bodies. So, really, the logistics of getting my stuff over here is most difficult part. >> Last year, you led the NFL in in quarterback hits among defensive tackles. What What do you feel like you still need to work on in your game? Um, feel like most of my career just having a lot of pass rush production, just turning that into more sacks, you know, just taking that next step. >> How did you feel about the the atmosphere today? First day of PR uh pads. How does that compare to first days that you've had uh in Dallas elsewhere? >> I feel like just in general as a lineman, everything feels a little bit more natural when you have pads on. You've been a Cowboy your whole career. You've had really tough battles with the NerS in the past. Did you have to sort of forget some of those rivalries and uh matchups against the NerS when you joined this team? >> Um I mean a little bit, but at the same time I feel like that's just what what happens when you come to a new team. You know, your loyalty changes and and now anyone in a different jersey is the enemy. So that's how it is. Were there specific Ners offensively that you always weren't happy to have to face off against? >> I mean, it's definitely cool having Trent on my side now versus being on the other side. So, it's cool to be able to pick his brain. I was actually uh we had an off day yesterday. We're both cold tubbing and stuff. Got to chop it up with him a little bit, talk about some of the things that he's seen in his career. Just get a little wisdom from him. So, it's cool to have him as a resource now as opposed to having him as opponent. Oh, so you said turning quarterback hits into sacks. It sounds like that's something the whole defense could have applied, you know, in terms of improving in 2026. Have you guys talked about that? Um, ways to improve uh here into the season. >> Definitely. That's something that uh I don't know if you guys have just talked to any of the other guys, but like when when we came in at OTAAS, coach sat down with everybody in the room and individually and just went over things that everybody can improve on. So that's conversations that we've had with coach individually and everyone is sharpening themselves through camp and just working on these things and just the three get betters that we've had since OTAAS >> your pedigree as a pass rusher in your career in practice a padded practice like today where you have one-on- ones. Is that something that you particularly look forward to? >> Um I like one-on- ones for sure. It kind of helps warm me up for the team periods. Obviously, the most game-like reps you get is the team period, but I feel like having one-on- ones is like a good prep and primer for the rushes that you're going to get during team. So, I enjoy them. >> I know it's very early on, but with Ricky Morris and kind of what's he's trying to instill upon you, do you get a sense of how he's going to call a game? >> Um, a little bit. The we had a move the ball period today, so got to kind of get a feel for how things are going to be called. How would you describe kind of his philosophy that he's trying to impart on you guys? >> Um, I mean, I'm still learning that a little bit. I got to go like review the tape, get a feel for it. But, you know, um, he's I know he's trying to make it very simple, make sure we have good communication so we can play fast. >> You describe the energy and sounds you hear of Fred Warner and Greg Greenlaw behind you. >> Oh, man. Fred just I feel like has a menacing aura. Him and Green Law for sure. So having them on the field behind me just adds just a little bit of confidence for sure. Having two of the best linebackers in the league. >> Were you at all surprised that they both had took turns throwing people to the ground today? >> Not at all. >> They're teammates, but that still didn't surprise you. >> I mean, obviously talk about protect the team and stuff like that, but I just know when it comes to guys like that, they have one speed. So, it's definitely hard to and obviously that smart stuff like that. I don't think anyone's getting hurt, but like it's football. They got one speed. The way they practice is the way they play. So, you can't really argue with what they do and what they put on tape because it's very consistent. Doesn't change. >> Puts a lot of emotion into coaching you guys. What are your takeaways from just working with him for a short amount of time? >> Um, I appreciate the intensity. He's very consistent. Don't think he's changed the day since I've been here. been the same guy. So, the way he's coaching is the way he's been coaching. And if he's getting on you, you probably deserve it. >> As far as coming together as a defense, what have been sort of the coaching point that Raheem has impressed upon you guys? >> Um, I feel like just making sure we're on the same page, getting communication, stuff like that. The play style is the biggest thing. So, if we are playing at the style that we need to, playing nasty defense, making sure we're going for the ball, stuff like that, running to the ball, bringing that energy, everything is going to come together from front to back. >> A couple more. Vinnie, >> we asked you about the uh earlier during the OTAAS about the Cowboy game and that seemed to be like a big game to you. Um, how did you did you feel like you parted ways with them on bad terms or do you just excited to go against them and kind of knock heads against them? >> I mean, I love playing good teams in general. You know what I mean? I know that's one of the best offenses in the league. So, just going to the game. It's not really any bad blood. Still got a lot of love for the guys. Everyone on the team, no love loss at all, but it's a great team and I'm a competitor, so just looking forward to it. >> What rookies have stood out to you so far on the defense? Uh, definitely like what I'm seeing from Romelo and Bryson. >> Thoughts on Kayon Black? >> One more time. >> What are your thoughts on Kayn Black? >> Is that running back? Sorry. >> Next question. >> All good, guys.

title: Why the 49ers Should Start De'Zhaun Stribling Over Deebo Samuel
text: So, let's talk Stribling. Stribling missed his first practice today, hamstring tightness, could miss a week or two, I don't know. Shouldn't be too serious, but anytime a rookie misses time, he's he's dead to Kyle Shanahan. And, you know, some 30-year-old's going to take his spot. So, um, I think he should start though. Like, here's here's what I I watched this Stribling real close, and in one-on-ones, he did it yesterday, he's not that great of a route runner one-on-one against man-to-man coverage. But, neither is Deebo. He's better than Deebo. He's better than Deebo at running routes and getting open on his own. His route tree is limited, but it's bigger than Deebo's. His his, uh, catch radius is bigger than Deebo's. Everything. Faster, stronger, taller. Younger. And, it seems to me that even though, again, he's not going to be killing people in the one-on-ones the way Aiyuk did, um, he's going to produce in 11-on-11s because defenses play zone the vast majority of the time, and zone defenses are going to be focused on Mike Evans and Christian McCaffrey, and you got this guy with free releases running through the defense, um, full speed. He's a he's a handful. And, I think you've seen it like even though, again, he's not this man-to-man beater like Ricky is, he produces in practice every day. Last Yesterday, he had like five catches. Day before that, he had like four. He's open. Defenses are focused on him. He's big and fast. He's a big play waiting to happen. He's not perfect, but he's promising. And, now Deebo's back. Deebo should have to be the number three or four receiver. Is Deebo better than DeMarcus Robinson right now? Maybe in certain situations. Like, if it's third and seven, you get man-to-man coverage across the board, take Deebo out and put in Robinson or Kittle. If it's first and 10, and you want some gadget stuff, hand the ball to him, throw a screen. Yeah, sure. Get him in there. But I feel like Deebo's kind of like Juszczyk, where like when they're in the game, you kind of know how they're going to be used. With Juszczyk, he's going to go in motion eight times. And if he gets the ball, it's going to be in like one or two ways. Deebo, same thing. He's going to go in motion eight times, and if he gets the ball, it's going to be in one or two ways. We all seen it. There's There's no more, um, air of mystery around those guys in this offense. There is with Stribling. You have no idea how Kyle's going to use Stribling. And now you won't, cuz Stribling is going to miss two weeks of training camp, and Deebo's back. It's a shame. And this is why I felt like I knew this was going to happen. When they drafted Stribling, I'm like, "What's the point, man? You're just going to sign Deebo in a few months. What is the point? You take this 24-year-old wide receiver and redshirt him for a year. How's that going to help him?" But yo, maybe the substation just zapped his hamstring anyway. He can't even play. Who knows, man? This team is silly in that way. But I think he he played really well for the first week. We haven't even seen him block yet. He actually can run clear out routes in ways that Deebo Samuel can't and has no interest in doing. And, uh, now you can forget about him. Because he's not 30. Like Kyle is on a mission to have the first offense ever with a bunch of skill position players who are over 30. Although, does Kyle Juszczyk count as a skill position player? Does he have skill? Is he skilled? I don't know about that. But he's 35. Christian Kirk, 30. Christian McCaffrey, 30. Deebo Samuel, 30. Deebo Samuel, 30. Marcus Robinson, 32. Um, Evan's 33. Kittle, 33. Oldest offense ever. What could go wrong? Not much. >> [music]

title: Why the 49ers Didn't Make Ricky Pearsall Have Surgery Last Year
text: Okay, Ricky Pearsall. So, he's out for the year. Going to have surgery soon. 9 to 12 months recovery, maybe 6 months, probably more like 12 months. And the question is why didn't he have surgery sooner? John Lynch came out today and had an explanation for that. Very defensive. Had a He's like, "Look, PCL injuries usually take care of themselves. I had a PCL injury, Mac Jones had a PCL injury. I didn't need surgery, Mac didn't need surgery, but turns out that Ricky does. And so, he's going to have surgery now." I don't know. It just feels like what the 9ers say and what they It's like, "Look, this is how the injury should uh play out most of the time. We're not going to do anything special for you. We're not going to examine this on an individual basis. It's a PCL injury, so we're going to do what we do with everyone and and and just let you rest." Didn't work. I'm sorry, just because most PCL injuries work themselves out doesn't mean that all do and you're spending so much money on your team doctor, team physician, team trainer. Like, maybe he could do a little bit of like maybe he could figure out last year what this knee needs. Like, if it's going to work itself out. Cuz you didn't know and you got it wrong and now you wasted a year of Ricky Pearsall's prime. It cost him money. Probably not going to pick up his fifth-year option. I'd be really pissed if I was Ricky Pearsall. He did what you told him to do and it didn't work. It didn't work. In retrospect, if he'd had surgery, if they The 9ers had shut him down last year right after he injured his PCL, he'd be healthy right now. But, no, they wouldn't put even put him on IR with the designation to return. It was clear they felt like, "Hey, man, walk it off. Rub some dirt on it and get back on the freaking field." And when he couldn't play in week 18 and the divisional round against the Eagles, they they kind of acted like there was something wrong with him. Like, "What is your deal?" Fred Warner is going to play on a broken ankle, dude. You need to get out there. So, he did play against the Seahawks and he was He shouldn't have been out there. Go back and watch the film. He was like limping around the field with a messed up PCL. And even after that, the 9ers were like, "Yo, just put some ice on it, bro." Rest it. And it didn't work. So, that's why the 9ers They You could blame the substation. You could blame the trainer. Either one, pick. The team doctor, the team trainer, the team facility, the Pick whatever. But Stripling never had a chance Excuse me. He didn't have a chance. Pearsall never had a chance. Never had a chance. Out for the year. Feel for him, man. Should have had the surgery last year. Now he has to have the surgery this year and it seems like the 9ers don't even care. I mean, I'm sure they care, but it's like, "Well, Deebo's here. So, good luck, Ricky. Sorry." It worked out for Mack. I don't know what to tell you. Mhm. >> [snorts] >> It would be cool if Ricky could go somewhere else and stay healthy. That would really prove that there was something specific going on with the 49ers and their facility or their training staff or something. But I want to put something on Ricky as well. It's not all the 49ers' fault. I know you expect me to blame the 9ers 100% every time something bad goes wrong. But what about Ricky? What about Ricky, right? So, Ricky, you're in your body. You know your knee's messed up. You tried to be the good teammate and gut it out last year. Fine. I get that. They wanted you to. You tried. Good for you. It didn't work. You felt it. It wasn't right. And then this offseason, it was important for you to, I don't know, find a solution to this. And you spent all offseason not just posting workout videos for clout on Instagram showing how recovered you were, but you also traveled around the world. As Ashley Ariana's pointing out, she's great. We did a a show yesterday. She DM'd me this or texted me this today. But, like what about Ricky? You You got major swelling in your knee. You're trying to fix this messed up PCL without surgery. How did flying to Japan help that? You took some really long flights halfway around the world. And you were living it up and having like a an enriching experience and I get it, dude, but like if you have a serious injury and your career's on the line, maybe you just chill in Arizona for the for the off-season. And figure out what your knee can actually do cuz all we saw was you running around in Central Park or in Japan. Uh and it looked like the scenery was nice. We noticed the sleeve on your knee. It didn't seem like you were 100% healthy, but you kept putting out these videos like you were doing everything right. In retrospect, you know who didn't go to Japan this off-season? Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Deebo, Trent. No, the the dudes who went to Japan were Ricky and Isaac Guerendo and Jacob Cowing. Anytime you find yourself on a vacation with Jacob Cowing and Isaac Guerendo, something went wrong. Turn around, go back. That's not the group. So, it's not all the Niners' fault, man. I'm sorry. Like this is your career. You're almost 26 years old and you can't afford to lose your 26 year season. You can't. And instead of doing everything within your power to make sure you were healthy or you knew what the status of your knee, you you traveled the world. And you know, you uh I mean, it was just a few weeks ago that he was in what Central Park running around, Fort Lauderdale running around. You wanted to show us how hard you were working, but you weren't working smart. And with despite all that hard work, as soon as you actually kicked it into football mode, it it it gave out. So, what was the point of all that running around in Central Park? Was it to impress us or to find out what your knee could handle? Cuz as soon as I saw you run around with that knee with that sleeve on your knee, I figured, "Eh, that's not recovered yet." And then in OTAs, that was 2 months ago. You didn't participate in in in in week two. That was a problem. That was I mean, it's not like he's Mike Evans. Mike Evans participated in week two of OTAs, but Ricky didn't. Well, he had the the veteran week off? No, no, no. He's hurt. So, Niners messed up. Ricky messed up. And this is another reason why the Niners should be thinking about bringing in a general manager. They could they could, you know, promote John Lynch. I'm not saying fire John Lynch. He's good for the organization. They could promote him and then bring in a general manager who wouldn't draft Ricky Pearsall in round one. The reason Ricky Pearsall is so controversial cuz the Niners took him in round one when they didn't give him a first-round grade. And no one gave him a first-round grade. They did. They took him there. Even though they didn't give him a first-round grade, they put all this pressure and expectations on him. If he had been a second-round pick, people wouldn't be worried about his knee as much, but he was a first-round And I don't know. They they can say, "Well, you know, we tried. We thought we did the right thing." And most times PC I don't care. He's a first-round pick. He was supposed to be a starter this year. He's better than Deebo Samuel. He's out for the year. Your team just got worse. Every time something bad happens, the Niners are like, "Yeah, yeah, you know, there's nothing we could have done differently. We did everything right. With Brandon, we did everything right. With Ricky, we did everything right." Sure. I'm so glad you believe that. Maybe the Yorks do. Maybe they don't. Maybe it's why Paraag Marathe is gone because the last time he was negotiating contracts, he gave Brandon Aiyuk $30 a year. That's what he did. That didn't work out. Someone had to get fired for that. Maybe that's why he got Maybe that's why he's out. He tried to get the void the guarantees back. All right. >> [music]

title: Chris Foerster Has High Praise for 49ers Rookie RB Kaelon Black
text: That's right. Okay, let's talk about Chris Foerster. You were watching Chris Foerster spoke today the interim head coach of this team and he was asked about Kaelan Black. He was asked about the the new tight end. Never heard of him. But he was asked about the running back. I would imagine that Chris Foerster had a big hand in drafting uh Kaelan Black. He's been the run game coordinator before Chris Foerster. He's um he has a lot to say about running backs. >> Yes. >> And you know, when they when they asked him today like what do you like about him? He's like, "Well, um when I watched his film in college, I always felt like he had the most NFL style runs of anyone I watched. And people are like, "Well, what does that mean?" He's like, "Well, in college a lot of times there's a lot of space or you make one cut or you don't have to be super decisive. Things don't happen that fast. Like things were happening really fast for in Indiana and it seemed like he was making a lot of split-second decisions that were good." That's essentially what he said. And I think Colt McKivitz said yesterday like or 2 days ago like this guy's really decisive for a rookie. He seems to cuz a lot of times they see with his with his zone plays, there isn't one hole you're supposed to hit. You got to have to use your vision. Some rookies are like, "I don't know where to go." and there's a lot of like hesitation behind the line of scrimmage when really you're supposed to just make one cut and go. >> Who who is that that guy that they got in the in the third round a year or two ago? Trey something. >> Trey Sermon, Trey Sermon. Oh my god. >> he was like always running into the back of people's feet. >> Yep. Yep. Yep. So like you either have it or you don't. You have the vision, you have the one cut ability to find daylight and like Raheem Mostert had it. Right? He wasn't the most like he wasn't going to string together eight cuts and and a and a jump cut and a spin move, but he'd make that one cut very decisively, get upfield, and find a way to get 6 yards before he even got touched. And I think like that's sort of what we're seeing with Kaelan Black. No hesitation. Um just get it and go. I like him. I really freaking hope Deebo Samuel doesn't cut into his workload cuz come on, man. Come on. He's on my team. >> In your fantasy team? Is he um is there any similarities to him and and Elijah Mitchell? We know that Kyle ended up really liking Elijah Mitchell. Maybe because he was very durable. >> Good question.
