But, I do think that Toth, who played really well at left guard for the Eagles last year at both guard and center, he might be a break glass in case of emergency option at that guard position in case neither Connor Colby nor Robert Jones make the 49ers all too comfortable at left guard when it comes to pass protection. I mean, we've heard from Chris Foerster, the O-line coach, on Jones. He's straight up said that Jones is a better run blocker than he is a pass protector and he's going to have to work on his pass protection. And uh we know that Connor Colby struggled big time, probably in both phases of the game last year. We know that he's had a good off season, but still today, as I go through some of my notes, I even thought that James Thompson Jr., who's the rookie defensive tackle out of Illinois, beat Connor Colby. I also thought that Osa Odighizuwa beat Connor Colby and it's not a shock that Osa Odighizuwa, who is the 49ers best interior rusher, the trade acquisition from the Dallas Cowboys, would have a leg up. But, I did notice that on the inside, Brett Toth looked like the best 49ers option on day one of pads, on day one of one-on-ones. Chris Foerster pointed out after, too, that a lot of times guys are going to use these one-on-ones to get better in certain areas. So, they're going to work on one specific skill, so it may not be representative of how good [clears throat] of an overall blocker he is. And you don't get team help, right? It is just a one-on-one rush. It's not a five-on-five rush. Trent Williams makes the left guard whoever is there better because Trent Williams is Trent Williams at left tackle. So, he's going to be able to pick some things up. He's going to be able to help in two-on-two situations that make a one-on-one match-up more favorable for the left guard. We saw whenever Trent wasn't at full health last year, left guard suffered. Early in the season, I think that Trent actually because he had a lot to clean up when Colton McKivitz had to fill in for the 49ers at left guard following the Ben Bartch injury, you saw that Trent's tackle numbers dropped just because there is an interconnectedness between the left tackle and left guard position. So, the 49ers know that they have a future Hall of Famer at left tackle. He can mask some of the issues at left guard, but they still have to make sure that they can raise the pass protection level from that position to at least solid. I thought Jake Brendel was solid at center today. I thought Puni held his own really well in those one-on-ones and then there's Colton McKivitz who intensified the fight later on when he sprinted in back up for Jake Tonges against Fred Warner. But, nobody's worrying about Colton McKivitz. He's a player who's graduated, I think, to the upper echelons of this league in right tackle. Every single year he's gotten better. For the 49ers, it's that left guard position that they're really going to have to figure out. And then, of course, you've got to make sure that you have depth as well because linemen are going to go down. I always say that Super Bowl caliber team needs to have at least seven, preferably eight, very, very competent linemen. Today, Nick Zakelj really struggled. It'd be surprising to me if if he made this team. I know that he's a familiar face, so maybe maybe the practice squad for Nick Zakelj, but they have deepened that offensive line. Carver Willis, the rookie, up and down today. And as I said, Enrique Cruz, there's going to be a lot of polishing that needs to happen for his pass protection to be up to par. Romello Height absolutely blew by him on that one snap. I mean, the get off it was reminiscent of D. Ford's and you know, that's what you have to be really excited about regarding Romello Height. He is very, very quick off the ball. Also, you know, I talk a lot about these five-man fronts. They're using them to drop a little bit in coverage. That's interesting to me just from the schematic perspective of Raheem Morris's defense. How quickly is he going to learn how to play in space in the NFL? Because that's going to be different than it is in college, but he's a big guy, super athletic, and definitely of the body type that that can shift between a 4-3 defensive end and a 3-4 outside linebacker. Stribling, Stribling, Stribling. DeShawn Stribling is absolutely everywhere for the 49ers, whether it's with the ones, Brock Purdy being the quarterback, the twos, Mac Jones being the QB, or Adrian Martinez {slash} Kurtis Rourke, the threes, Stribling is making catches. He's making the most plays out of anybody at this 49ers training camp. Obviously, very, very exciting for San Francisco. I would say even needed for the 49ers because you know, they've obviously got an old offense. It's the oldest in the league. Deebo will be joining this team at age 30, Mike Evans at age 33, George Kittle 32 coming off the Achilles, Christian McCaffrey just turned 30 years old. This is a 49ers offense that has needed a youth infusion and more specifically a speedy youth infusion. And DeShawn Stribling is the type of player that can give it that. I mean, just an easy, easy strider, breaks in and out of his cuts with real smoothness for somebody who's 6'3. Has won with height, has won with separation, and he only dropped one pass last year at Ole Miss, so he wins by catching everything that is thrown to him. I I say it every show. I'm very, very impressed to with De'Shawn Stripling. Brock Purdy in red zone work today threw an out pass touchdown to Luke Farrell, blocking tight end who obviously would like to work on the receiving aspect of his game. Nice pass from Purdy. And then there was Mike Evans catching that football over Updike's route. Now, Mike Evans had the press conference today and he was awesome. I mean, this guy you you talk about him and you talk about the fact that it he's been doing this for well over a decade at this point. And the way that he shares information with the media, I mean, you learn a lot from Mike Evans. You know who else is learning from Mike Evans? The 49ers defensive backs. They are picking his brain. Have a listen to this. >> A lot of guys have been, you know, picking my brain on, you know, how my longevity, you know, how I've been able to make plays consistently and things like that. And in turn, I I ask the other guys, older guys, the same thing. Trent, Juice, Kittle, you know, all those guys that have been in the league a long time. Um how did they What do they do to, you know, stay fresh and and play so long? >> One more note on De'Shawn Stripling, and then I promise I'll move on to other players, but he's just making so many plays out there that that I feel that I have to mention him. Brock Purdy flushed out to his left, so opposite side of where a right-handed quarterback would be most comfortable. And he dropped one in the bucket for De'Shawn Stripling who had gotten open on the secondary action down field. It really, really made Raheem Morris mad. Raheem was standing next to Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch, and both of those guys were calm. Shanahan and Lynch, Morris got angry and started walking over toward his DBs. They weren't able to hold the coverage for the extra 2 seconds that Purdy had bought against De'Shawn Shrubling as he was rolling to his left. Now, speaking of Shanahan, today was his longest stretch out here at practice. So, the concussion symptoms are likely subsiding. Previously, he'd been out for about 20 to 30 minutes. I would estimate about an hour for Kyle Shanahan today. In fact, at one point, he was even standing right in front of the speaker, which was blaring AC/DC. So, Shanahan, when I was in in his office the other day, he said that the noise was bothering him more than the bright light. Today, he was even joking around with the 49ers quarterbacks, dapped up Adrian Martinez over a break. It really does seem that Kyle Shanahan is feeling better. Good timing on this first day of pads. Christian McCaffrey, speaking of him, it wasn't just the little scuffle shoving match with Dre Greenlaw. He had a long maybe touchdown run. Not sure if he would have made it to the end zone. They blew the play dead before, but he was able to dart out. He's got a lot of juice this camp, by the way, but he was able to dart out from the line of scrimmage, got to the second level, and about 40 yards downfield, he gave Deommodore Lenoir a very healthy stiff arm. So, as you might be able to tell, this 49ers camp, nice and competitive, nice and physical, and things do get real once the pads do come on. Purdy almost threw an interception today that Jair Brown Brown had a pick of Purdy early, I think, on day one or two of camp. Today, was not able to hold on to it. I've got Shrubling again in my notes. I I just can't get away from this guy. Caught one from Mac Jones. As I said, he's catching passes from all the quarterbacks. Mac feathered one over Luke Gifford, the linebacker. Funny moment with Mac Jones. He went deep to Malik Turner, one of the 49ers backup receivers, one of their top gunners. The The was slightly underthrown, but it was complete to Malik Turner who won a jump ball against Darrell Luter Jr. and then I looked back at Mack and he was dancing back behind the line of scrimmage happy about the deep ball. Mack is infusing this camp with energy every single day. And then before all the fight started, I saw Curtis Rourke rip a deep out to Jordan Watkins and I'll say this because tomorrow is going to be Deebo day, I would assume. Today he's going to sign, tomorrow I would expect him to be back out at practice and maybe even hold a press conference. But Deebo's going to play the Z. As I've been telling you about Deebo Samuel, I don't think that this is going to be full-time Z setup. I don't think he's going to be asked to do the same thing, the same role as he had when he was with the 49ers last, especially in 2024 when he was the focal point. I think the more the 49ers can free things up around Deebo, the better chance he's going to have to just pick up a full head of steam and barrel guys over. And one major key is Jordan Watkins. I think he can be a standard Z receiver in this league, a flanker. And who knows with Ricky Pearsall, too, right? We're going to have to wait for another update on Ricky Pearsall, but assuming that he's out of the picture for the time being, Jordan Watkins is making a few plays at this practice and he can, along with De'Shawn Stripling and Mike Evans, take some of that pressure off of Deebo Samuel, open up space to let Deebo be Deebo a couple times a game. It's not going to be 2021 Deebo, but you can certainly let the bowling ball who people are afraid to tackle when he's at 220 lb with a full head of steam, you can certainly let him go to work when he's got space. Anyway, that Watkins deep out that I saw late in practice today, beautiful throw from Curtis Rourke. Competing to be QB3, Rourke is the most physically imposing of the 49ers quarterbacks and he rips that deep out with a lot of precision. I mean, he that that is a rope that he's able to throw out there toward the sideline. 49ers waived the tight end Tanner McLaughlin, who they signed just a few days ago, with an injury designation. Josiah Deguara, the tight end who I told you about yesterday, the Santa Rosa native, Sacramento local, signed with the 49ers. So, he was out there in the jersey number 47 today. And they also waived the defensive back Derrick Cantine. So, they added the tight end Deguara, they added the receiver Trenton Irwin. They're going to have to make one more roster move tomorrow so that they can officially add Deebo Samuel. But, that's the update from the helmet. We'll talk to you soon.

title: Sonny Styles' First Training Camp: Exclusive Interview | Next Man Up | Washington Commanders | NFL
text: Command this family. We are here training camp, our first training camp with the best fans in the NFL. And we got our first round pick, Sunny Styles, man. First training camp, bro. First time being able to practice in front of these fans, man. How are you feeling? >> Excited. Uh I think the fans brought a lot of energy today. Practice was fun. Got to fly around a little bit. So, uh it was good to go out here in front of the fans. >> Yeah, man. You've had a couple practices now where the fans aren't here, right? Where it's just media watching you guys and things are different. How do the fans and their presence turn things up for you guys? >> Uh I mean, I think the energy is just a little higher when you get fans around. Um kind of starts to feel a little bit more game-like. Uh but I think you got to get to a point in your mind where you when you're at practice, like you're already in the mode the mindset of being in the game. Mhm. Um but just being in front of the game the fans just fun. It's a fun experience. They bring a bunch of energy, so it's good. >> Did you know what to expect? Did you know it was going to be like this? You got fans over there. You got stands over there. You got fans everywhere. Did you know it was going to be quite like this? >> No, I didn't really know, honestly, until I saw the stands like a few days few days ago set up. So, I was like, "Oh, wow. It's going to be like real." Like, so you know, when I was in college, we didn't do nothing like this. So, this is this is pretty cool to see. >> And last time we spoke, I think you would only done one day of rookie mini camp. Since then, so much has happened, man. OTAs, training camp, bro. What has it been like for you adjusting to this new pace that is the NFL? >> Yeah, just trying to soak in all the information, learn from the guys around me, learn from the coaches around me. Learn from mistakes and just keep playing, having fun. And I think the biggest thing as a rookie, you got to gain your confidence. You know, make plays, keep making more plays, get more comfortable and comfortable. And then you start to feel like just how you did in college. I mean, that's how it's supposed to be. >> You got to be feeling pretty lucky to be able to learn in a room that you're in now with all of this different talent. And then with a linebacker coach, Ken Norton Jr. That's all video of him turning y'all up, pushing y'all. And what is it like to have a coach like that that not only has that energy, but has done everything that you aspire to do? >> Yeah, I mean, Coach Norton is awesome. Like you said, he played the game, played for a long time, was awesome, won won some big games, Super Bowls, was a great player. Um he's coached a lot of great players, a lot of great linebackers, so I'm in a lucky situation. You know, I got him. I got Frankie in the room with me, another linebacker who's been doing it for a minute. I got Leo in the room, another guy who's been in the year about 4 or 5 years, playing at a good level. And we got a bunch of other guys in the room. We're all feeding off each other. So, you know, I think we got a really good room, a lot of talent, a lot of good people, and uh we just feed off each other's energy. >> What are some of those questions you find yourself asking during these times when you are talking to Frankie, when you are talking to Leo? I mean, Leo got a Super Bowl. What are those questions you find yourself asking during this process? >> Uh probably more so their process. Like, whether it's their process of taking care of their body, their process of preparing for practice, their process of preparing for an opponent. Um just trying to figure out, you know, what they do. You know, a lot of people say success leaves crumbs. >> Mhm. I like that. >> So, like, you know, Frankie, he's been doing it for so long. There's a reason he's been able to do it for so long, play at a high level. Uh like you said, Leo's been been to a Super Bowl. Like, so all the success they've had it leaves crumbs. I'm just trying to pick up all those crumbs. >> Mhm. And I mean, you're not just picking up crumbs, too. You're also adding value, right? Like, I mean, you a first-round pick for a reason. You were on the field for a reason, man. How do you feel you've been able to improve this linebacker room in just a short time that you've been here? >> Yeah, I mean, I think I'm another talented guy I bring brought into the room. Um you know, I think we put a bunch of talented guys around each other, we raise the playing level for all of us. Um you know, we're all teammates at the end of the day, but we're competing, too. We want to all be on the field. You know, I think we compete at a high level, we're all making each other better. >> Mhm. And one thing we know about De'Vondre Campbell, he loves versatile players like you, right? Former safety, now playing linebacker. Have you gotten any spots where he's moved you around, had you in different places where you're like, "Okay, man, I see why this guy is where he's at"? >> Uh none none too crazy right now, you know, but I can see I can see the vision. You know, we have so many different personnels, and I think we have so many talented guys on the defense, and he's putting all these different guys in different positions to be successful. It's not like we're trying to all fit into his defense, and it's these two personnels. Like, we're a bunch of different personnels for a bunch of different guys. So, uh I think everyone's going to get to get to eat. >> Anything surprise you so far? >> Nah, nothing really surprising, honestly. >> That's a good thing. >> Yeah. >> [laughter] >> Well, Sonny man, we appreciate you, bro. We're going to let you get going cuz your family's here. My last question is about your family, man. They pulled up here to show you love, man. How was it to be able to share this with them, be on that field with them, and just share this moment? >> Yeah, it was good. I was out there with my my girl was here. Uh some of my close friends and family was out here today, so it's good to see everybody. Uh first time seeing me in a burgundy gold in live in the flesh, I guess you could say, with all the fans. So, it was a cool experience. You know, I know we got a few more open practices coming up the next few weeks, so I'm excited for those. >> Hey, Sonny man, we're excited to see you, man. We appreciate you taking the time. And I also want to show you love, man, because you took the time to sign autographs for all these fans, man. You a rookie, you locked in, you living your dream, but you taking the time to show the fans love, man. And we really appreciate that, brother. Thank you for sitting down, brother. Good luck, man. >> Appreciate it.

title: Team-First Approach | Raiders 2026 Training Camp Highlights
text: Welcome in, everybody. It is day one of Raiders training camp practices. I'm >> Yeah, you know, team first approach is the number one thing that we're going to talk about. You know, removing the word I from our verbage as much as possible and thinking about the team, uh how we can make the team better. >> You know, we had our summer break and now it's time to get to work. I think every day we go out there, we all try to work together, raise the standard every day for one another. >> It's it's just really important that come game one that our players are doing what they do best on game day. >> Players understand what we're looking for, being [music] very intentional, being very deliberate in where we're asking to asking to get better in each guy. >> [music] >> Said it in the spring, I'll say it again, it's it's it's style of play. That's the red blinking meter. No scheme will save you in this league. If you're having ME's, if you're not playing hard, [music] if you're not taking the ball away, those are like the red blinking meter that something's not right. And so, as long as the execution and the effort and the fundamentals are right, then you know you're headed in the right direction. locked in. We make a choice right now, man. Do it for your brothers. LET'S GET IT. >> THE BEST PLAYER HAS HAS TO PLAY. And that's not just what I'm going to see, you guys are going to see it in the preseason games. >> Play ball. We're just not here to mess around. We're here to get work in. Like there's no extra stuff and you know, I think that's what that's going to go a long way. Like it might not mean [music] a lot to some people right now, but you know, come November, come October, it's going to be the same message.

text: All right All right How's everybody doing? Awesome What do we got? Your thoughts on Germad as a punt returner He's so quick. Uh yeah no question You know uh hopefully we we can get that Um we didn't see that in spring because he wasn't able to practice as much He did have one today that uh looked good in that drill So hopefully we can get him going cuz he's he's definitely going to be a plus if we can get him out on the field For sure.
